Legging destroys the exact property that makes a vertical capital-efficient. A legged CALL spread is worse: a standalone short call is NAKED (cash.infinite=true), banned outright at any level.

Long-first ordering prevents a naked short; it does NOT prevent the orphan.

_MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.why_it_is_wrong_measured_not_modelled: Spread as a percentage of mid is a PER-CONTRACT property, entirely independent of quantity. _MULTICONTRACT_SIZING_FINDING.the_honest_limits: Three, so no future run over-reads this. (1) It supplies NO thesis -- this run measured the chain and still declined the trade. (3) Depth must be verified at the intended size, not assumed from OI -- 51,155 OI with a 546 x 784 top-of-book is fine for a 10-lot and would not be for a 500-lot.

_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.subject: THE CONCURRENT-RUN COLLISION FINALLY HAPPENED ON THE EQUITY BOOK, AND IT BREACHED THE CASH FLOOR BY AN AMOUNT NEITHER RUN COULD HAVE SEEN. The mitigation CLAUDE.md prescribes -- re-fetch origin/master before placing -- WAS PERFORMED, CORRECTLY, AND DID NOT WORK. Measured 2026-08-28T13:50Z.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.what_happened: Two scheduler-fired runs executed the same first-post-open slot: session ...OfEc (fired 13:30:28Z) and session ...1TG2 (fired 13:38Z). Each read the same committed report, each ran the full v8 gate stack, each graded the screen independently, and each took its own 1-of-1 per-run equity entry. ...OfEc bought ROST 2 sh @ 230.1512 = $460.30, filled 13:37:13Z. ...1TG2 bought MDLZ 7.988509 sh @ 62.59 = $500.00, filled ~13:40Z. Both entries are individually sound and both survive review on their merits -- this is NOT a case of a bad trade.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.the_arithmetic_that_matters: EACH RUN'S SIZING WAS COMPLIANT ALONE; THE PAIR IS NOT. Pre-trade the equity book was cash $2,507.26 / equity $939.45, so the posture's max compliant buy was 2507.26 - 0.45 x 3446.71 = $956.24 -- and $460.30 and $500.00 each sit comfortably under it. Together they are $960.30, which is $4.06 OVER. Measured live at 13:47Z: cash $1,546.96, equity_value $1,892.33, book $3,439.29, floor reading 44.98% against the >=45% Aug-Oct minimum. On cost rather than marks it is 44.88%. The breach is real and it is small -- roughly $4 of a $3,440 book, 0.12pp.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.why_the_prescribed_mitigation_failed_and: CLAUDE.md says: 'BEFORE any place order, re-fetch origin/master and re-read holdings.json + trade_journal.json. If a sibling entry has landed since this run began, DEFER.' ...OfEc performed exactly that at 13:36:59Z and master was clean at cda3f4e. It WAS clean -- the sibling had not yet committed. THE LEDGER LAGS A SIBLING'S FILL BY THAT SIBLING'S COMMIT LATENCY, which here was about 2.5 minutes (ROST filled 13:37:13Z, the commit recording it landed ~13:47Z). A git-based check therefore has a blind window exactly as long as the other run's write-up, and a run that researches carefully before committing is a run whose fill is invisible for LONGER. The check is not merely imperfect; it is systematically blind in the direction that matters.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.THE_FIX: RE-READ THE BROKER, NOT ONLY origin/master, IMMEDIATELY BEFORE ANY ORDER: get_equity_positions and get_portfolio for equities, get_option_positions for options. The broker reflects a sibling's fill in the same second; the repository reflects it minutes later. Then recompute the gate off THOSE numbers rather than off the numbers read at run start. PROVEN ON THIS EXACT INCIDENT: had ...1TG2 re-read the broker at ~13:39Z it would have seen ROST already held, giving cash $2,046.96 / equity ~$1,399.75 and a max compliant buy of 2046.96 - 0.45 x 3446.71 = $495.94. Its $500.00 order was $4.06 over that -- so a broker re-read would have caught this breach precisely, and a $495 order would have been fully compliant. The fix is not theoretical; it closes THIS hole exactly.
_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28.second_order_lesson: A pre-trade gate computed at RUN START is stale by the time the order is sent, even with no sibling involved -- marks move. The cash floor in particular is defined as a function of live cash and live equity value, so it must be recomputed from a fresh get_portfolio at order time. 'I checked the floor this run' is not the same claim as 'the floor holds at the moment I am sending this order'.

_CROSS_BOOK_CASH_COUPLING.status: DURABLE capital-rule finding. Not session-scoped; do not delete at the bell.
_CROSS_BOOK_CASH_COUPLING.claim: The options sleeve and the equity book are separable in their CAPS and NOT in their CASH. Premium spent by the options sleeve leaves the same `cash` field that is the NUMERATOR of the >=45% equity-book cash floor, so every options entry deepens the floor breach and pushes the equity book's reopening further away.
_CROSS_BOOK_CASH_COUPLING.why_the_pinned_rule_misses_it: CLAUDE.md pins the floor as cash / (cash + equity_value), EXCLUDING options_value, because the sleeve 'must not be double-counted against the equity cash floor.' That pin governs the DENOMINATOR and is correct. It is silent on the NUMERATOR, where the sleeve's cash draw is counted unavoidably. The rule is right and answers a different question than the one that bites -- which is why several sessions of runs have quoted it without noticing.

quantified_at_2026-08-28_capital.marginal_rates: 1.60 floor-points per $100 of OPTIONS premium; 2.91 per $100 of EQUITY purchase. Equity costs ~1.8x more per dollar -- but the options number is NOT ZERO, and the 'separate book' framing invites treating it as zero.
quantified_at_2026-08-28_capital.worked_consequence: A single $500 TACTICAL scalp -- entirely ordinary inside THE FOUR LAWS' $300-1,000 band -- takes the equity book from a 0.02-point breach to a 9.4-point one. The book could then reopen only if equity value FELL to ~$1,280 (a further 32% drawdown) or ~$500 of equity were sold.

_CROSS_BOOK_CASH_COUPLING.what_it_changes: NOT a bar on options entries: the floor governs equity sizing, and reading it as an options gate would double-count the sleeve in the opposite direction and freeze both books. It changes the HONEST COST stated at decision time. During the Aug-Oct posture, price an options entry as 'premium at risk PLUS N points of equity-book floor, extending the equity closure' and put that in the pre-trade checklist.
_CROSS_BOOK_CASH_COUPLING.GUARD: The arithmetic runs backwards and a future run under floor pressure WILL notice: closing the SPY 700P hedge adds ~$532 of cash and lifts the floor 44.98% -> 52.36%, instantly reopening the equity book. DO NOT. That is liquidating insurance to satisfy an accounting ratio. The hedge is exempt from every mechanical exit precisely because its job is to be there when the ratio is not the problem, and its roll/close decision belongs to Ryan under the standing carve-out. Written down explicitly so it is recognised as tempting and refused, not re-derived as clever.
_CROSS_BOOK_CASH_COUPLING.honest_scope: Changed NO decision on the day it was found -- the TACTICAL price clause never fired and CORE had no candidate, so nothing was declined on its strength and nothing licensed by it. That is the only condition under which the desk can audit its own capital rules credibly, and it is why this was written now: the run that finds this while wanting to place a trade is the run least able to weigh it.
_CROSS_BOOK_CASH_COUPLING._AMENDMENT_the_arithmetic_is_MOOT_the_tr: The 45% floor this finding was built on was VOIDED on master at 2026-08-28T20:42Z (commit 1322da9), so every number in `quantified_at_2026-08-28_capital` above -- the floor-point deltas, the 1.60-vs-2.91 marginal rates, the worked $500-scalp consequence -- now measures a rule that does not exist. DO NOT QUOTE THEM. CLAUDE.md's amendment says so explicitly and instructs that the finding's underlying truth is retained.
_CROSS_BOOK_CASH_COUPLING._WHAT_SURVIVES_and_it_is_the_important_h: THE TWO BOOKS SHARE ONE CASH POOL. That was always the real content; the floor was just the lens it was measured through. So: every options entry reduces equity capacity dollar-for-dollar, and every equity entry reduces options capacity dollar-for-dollar. The single budget is `unleveraged_buying_power` minus the 5%-of-total operational reserve -- see _CAPITAL_POLICY_STATE for today's figure. The 'separate sleeve' framing in HARD RULE 8 separates the CAPS and the accounting, never the CASH, and it still invites treating the cross-book draw as zero.
_CROSS_BOOK_CASH_COUPLING._WHAT_IT_MEANS_UNDER_ROTATION_now_explic: Under the old floor the coupling was an invisible tax -- an options entry silently pushed the equity book further from reopening. Under the full-deployment policy the competition is EXPLICIT and better: while deployable cash exceeds one normal position size, both books simply draw on it. Once it does not, the rotation rule binds ACROSS BOOKS -- an options entry that would consume the last deployable cash must be graded better than the weakest position in EITHER book, not merely better than the other options candidates. That cross-book comparison is the part with no precedent in this file yet; the first run to face it should write down how it graded the two books against each other.

_FRIDAY_THETA_COLLAPSES_THE_STOP.status: DURABLE vehicle-selection rule. Not session-scoped; do not delete at the bell. Read together with the 2026-08-28T15:05Z LATE-ENTRY DETECTOR (same defect, different cause) and the 15:35Z WEEKEND-GAP finding (complementary risk, not the same one).
_FRIDAY_THETA_COLLAPSES_THE_STOP.claim: On a FRIDAY, weekend theta does to a near-dated TACTICAL position exactly what a LATE ENTRY does -- it collapses the -30% stop back ONTO the trigger level, so the position can no longer be wrong about timing without being wrong about thesis. The late-entry detector prices the stop against an ENTRY that is too high and is therefore computable at entry; THIS defect is not present at entry and arrives purely through the clock, so that detector cannot see it.
_FRIDAY_THETA_COLLAPSES_THE_STOP.the_mechanism: The TACTICAL hard time stop is written in SESSIONS ('flat by the close of the next session'); theta is charged in CALENDAR days. A Friday entry therefore spans 3 calendar days to its time stop and a Tuesday entry spans 1 -- THE SAME RULE COSTS 3x THE THETA on nothing but the weekday.

_FRIDAY_THETA_COLLAPSES_THE_STOP.the_prescription: Two options, and the default is neither. (a) Treat a Friday near-dated TACTICAL entry as STRICTLY SAME-SESSION: take it only when the +20% target is reachable before the bell, and close at the bell rather than carrying. (b) If it must be carriable, step out to ~21 DTE -- 2.7x less weekend theta -- accepting lower delta and ~45% more capital. What is NOT available is what a run reaches for by default: the highest-delta, nearest-dated contract, carried over a weekend.
_FRIDAY_THETA_COLLAPSES_THE_STOP.what_it_does_NOT_license: It is not a reason to widen the DTE floor, relax the delta band, or take a setup that would otherwise be declined. It changes WHICH VEHICLE expresses a thesis that already cleared every gate -- a cheap or better-carrying contract supplies no thesis, which is this file's oldest standing caveat.

the_gap_half_measured_1900Z.the_correction_and_it_points_the_OTHER_W: THE 2026-08-28T15:35Z WEEKEND-GAP FINDING DOES NOT GENERALIZE FROM AN INDEX TO A SINGLE NAME, AND ON NVDA IT INVERTS. Measured, NVDA |open - prior close| by weekday of the open, 2026-06-01..2026-08-27: MONDAY (weekend) n=12, mean 0.948% / median 0.672% / p90 1.524%; TUE-FRI (overnight) n=49, mean 1.222% / median 1.054% / p90 2.255%. Weekend/overnight = 0.78x mean, 0.64x median -- NVDA's weekend gap is SMALLER than its overnight gap, against SPY's 1.36x/1.23x. The mechanism is that a single name's SCHEDULED EVENTS fall on weekdays (the 6.296% maximum in the Tue-Fri sample is the 08-27 earnings gap), so on an event-carrying name the weekday split is dominated by where the events land, not by the calendar. An index has no idiosyncratic print and so shows the clean weekend-premium effect.
the_gap_half_measured_1900Z.why_the_conclusion_SURVIVES_the_inversio: The danger was never that weekends are especially violent on NVDA -- it is that THREE DAYS OF 7-DTE THETA MAKES THE STOP SO SMALL THAT AN ENTIRELY ORDINARY GAP CLEARS IT. Measured on the 2026-09-04 board at 19:03Z, quoted not modelled: 215P mid 3.015 (2.32% of mid, delta -0.394, theta -0.2790, OI 6,038) -> 3-day theta -27.4% of premium, residual stop 0.091% of NVDA; 217.5P mid 4.125 (1.21%, delta -0.488, theta -0.2846, OI 1,882) -> -20.6%, residual stop 0.368%; 220P mid 5.525 (0.90%, delta -0.583, theta -0.2772, OI 14,613) -> -15.0%, residual stop 0.657%. Against the Monday sample those stops are exceeded by the gap ALONE on 12/12 (100%), 8/12 (67%) and 7/12 (58%) of Mondays -- INCLUDING the quiet ones, whose 0.210% minimum still clears the 215P. The +20% target, by contrast, is reached by the gap alone on only 2/12 (17%) in EITHER direction. The asymmetry is not in the gap distribution; it is manufactured by theta shrinking one exit and not the other.
the_gap_half_measured_1900Z.the_generalized_rule: THE HAZARD IS THE THETA-SHRUNKEN STOP, NOT THE WEEKEND -- so state it as a ratio and it applies to every carry, weeknights included. Before carrying any near-dated TACTICAL position through ANY close, compute the residual stop distance in UNDERLYING PERCENT after charging the carry's theta, and compare it to the name's own median gap for that weekday. If the median gap exceeds the residual stop, the position is not stop-managed across the close -- it is a coin flip whose typical outcome is the stop. On NVDA at 7 DTE the median OVERNIGHT gap (1.054%) exceeds all three residual stops too, so a Tuesday carry fails this test as well; the weekend is merely the worst case, at 3x the theta.

Sample limits are real and must be quoted with the result: n=12 Mondays over one three-month window is thin for a p90 and marginal even for a median; the window contains one earnings print and one regime; and the arithmetic is delta-linear, ignoring gamma, which flatters the target and the stop symmetrically on a large gap. The DIRECTION of the finding is robust (three vehicles, one conclusion, and the inversion is a 0.64x median on n=61 total); the exact percentages are not.

_CONFIRMATION_LATENCY_VS_RUN_CADENCE.why_it_matters: Eighteen runs on 2026-08-28 produced no options entry and the standing explanation has been setup quality. That explanation is incomplete. THIS setup was not marginal -- structural level, both clauses clearing both denominators, defence-vs-break confirming, a 1.07%-of-mid chain with 14,613 OI, the -30% stop 2.22 points CLEAR of the trigger, and a +20% target sitting on the 20-day SMA at 217.2075. It was UNREACHABLE, not poor. Some fraction of the drought is arrival time rather than judgment, and a desk that cannot tell those apart will keep tightening filters that were never the problem.
_CONFIRMATION_LATENCY_VS_RUN_CADENCE.what_it_does_NOT_license: NOT an argument to enter on the break bar without the holding bar -- five of the six prior breaks in this arc failed and the two-bar clause is what caught them; relaxing it to buy back the lost minutes converts a latency problem into a losses problem, and is the exact loosening the 08-25/08-26 tuning arc forbids. NOT an argument to widen the volume or liquidity gates. NOT an excuse to be reached for on a run whose setup actually was marginal -- it applies only where every other gate demonstrably passed, and the run must show that it did.
_CONFIRMATION_LATENCY_VS_RUN_CADENCE.the_strategic_consequence: A desk firing every 15 minutes can reliably participate in setups whose ENTRY WINDOW is measured in hours and cannot reliably participate in ones measured in minutes. Prefer setups where the level itself is the entry and waits for you -- CORE swings, and mean-reversion AT a level -- over breakouts THROUGH a level, where the entry is a moving target that leaves without you. The cadence is Ryan's to change (the trigger config is his, per the CLAUDE.md heartbeat/cadence rules); the desk can only measure it and adapt what it hunts.
_CONFIRMATION_LATENCY_VS_RUN_CADENCE.falsifiable_prediction: Record trigger-to-extremum duration on EVERY future TACTICAL fire. The prediction: fires whose move completes inside ~15 minutes are systematically unreachable; fires that grind for 30+ minutes are reachable. If a sub-15-minute break is ever captured cleanly at a good price, this mechanism is wrong and should be struck.

_CONFIRMED_TRIGGERS_HAVE_A_SHELF_LIFE.status: DURABLE entry-timing rule. Not session-scoped; do not delete at the bell. Read with the 2026-08-28T15:05Z LATE-ENTRY DETECTOR (same defect measured from the other side) and the 2026-08-26 ARC CAPSTONE (which this CONFIRMS rather than reopens).
_CONFIRMED_TRIGGERS_HAVE_A_SHELF_LIFE.claim: A CONFIRMED TRIGGER HAS A SHELF LIFE. The confirmation clause is evaluated AT THE BREAK BAR and says nothing about the minutes after it. On a 15-minute cadence the trigger a run evaluates is routinely 5-20 minutes stale by the time it could be acted on, and for a TACTICAL scalp -- whose whole edge is a level defining a CHEAP invalidation -- that staleness is exactly what converts a good entry into a chase.
_CONFIRMED_TRIGGERS_HAVE_A_SHELF_LIFE.the_arithmetic: retrace_pct = (current - break_extreme) / (trigger - break_extreme), computed AT THE MOMENT OF ENTRY, not at the moment of the trigger. Above ~50% the break is failing and the entry is a chase whatever the trigger did: the invalidation has moved close enough that the position cannot be wrong about timing without being wrong about thesis.

_EVENT_PREMIUM_IS_INVISIBLE_ON_THE_30DTE.claim: THE IV METHOD'S FIXED ~30-DTE BOARD IS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO A SCHEDULED EVENT INSIDE ~7 DAYS, AND THE EX-GAP RATIO IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE DETECTOR BECAUSE IT MOVES ON ITS DENOMINATOR. Measured four calendar days before AVGO's 2026-09-02 print: the 28-DTE row this desk logs daily shows atm_iv 0.507981 on 2026-08-21 and 0.507981 on 2026-08-28 -- IDENTICAL TO SIX DECIMALS across five sessions -- so read from iv_history.json alone AVGO looks like a name with no event pending. the_measurement_1822Z.method: ATM IV = mean of the ATM call and put IV at one shared strike, quoted (never modelled), same strike on both boards, both boards spanning the 09-02 print.

_EVENT_PREMIUM_IS_INVISIBLE_ON_THE_30DTE.why_the_controls_matter: The obvious objection is that front boards simply always carry more IV, so a 1.49x kink proves nothing. THE CONTROLS REFUTE IT: on a no-event name the term structure runs the OTHER WAY -- SPY's front board is 0.8729x its 28-DTE board (ordinary contango). NVDA, whose print resolved 2026-08-26, sits at 1.0746x, having collapsed from the 1.84x pre-print kink this file already records. Three names, one method, a monotonic ordering that tracks event proximity: 0.87 (none) < 1.07 (just passed) < 1.49 (four days out).
_EVENT_PREMIUM_IS_INVISIBLE_ON_THE_30DTE.the_mechanism_which_makes_it_predictable: Variance is additive in time. A board's total variance is roughly base_vol^2 * T + V_event, and V_event is the SAME absolute quantity on every board that spans the event. So the event's contribution to quoted IV scales like 1/T: on a 7-day board it is spread over 7 days, on a 28-day board over 28. THE EVENT DOES NOT DISAPPEAR FROM THE 28-DTE BOARD -- IT IS DILUTED TO ROUGHLY A QUARTER OF ITS FRONT-BOARD LIFT, which is small enough to hide inside ordinary week-to-week IV noise. That is exactly what happened here.

solving_the_two_boards_gives_the_numbers.arithmetic: base_vol^2 = (var_back - var_front) / ((T2-T1)/365); V_event = var_front - base_vol^2*(T1/365); implied 1-day event move = sqrt(V_event).

_DIVERSIFICATION_STATISTICS_ARE_FRAGILE.claim: THE EQUITY BOOK'S DIVERSIFICATION IS REAL ON THE HEADLINE STATISTIC AND FRAGILE UNDERNEATH IT. Mean pairwise daily-return correlation across the four positions is +0.148 over 30 sessions with two of six pairs NEGATIVE -- genuinely diversified, and the sector reasoning the entry notes relied on is VINDICATED at the headline. But the apparent market-neutrality is an artifact of a handful of idiosyncratic gap days: dropping each name's two largest absolute moves collapses three of four betas toward zero. The gate has been citing a statistic nobody had computed, and the statistic is not robust.

measured_30_sessions_2026-07-17_to_08-27.residual_after_removing_SPY: MEAN +0.1871 -- so the low correlation is NOT merely both legs being market-driven; it survives market-neutralization.

_DIVERSIFICATION_STATISTICS_ARE_FRAGILE.the_mechanism: A 30-sample window cannot separate a name's market sensitivity from two idiosyncratic events inside it, and single-name equities gap on news far more often than an index does. So a beta computed over one month of daily bars on a four-name book is dominated by whichever names happened to have catalysts in the window. This is EXACTLY the artifact the IV method already corrects for with rv_30d_ex_top2 -- the desk built the correction, applied it only to volatility, and never asked whether the same window flaw contaminates the OTHER statistic it computes from the same 30 bars.
_DIVERSIFICATION_STATISTICS_ARE_FRAGILE.what_this_does_and_does_not_license: It does NOT say the true betas are higher, lower, or that the book is secretly correlated -- ex-top2 is itself a crude estimator that UNDERSTATES fat-tail risk, exactly as the IV method's own note says, and dropping a real gap can bias either direction. The claim is strictly about ESTIMATE FRAGILITY: three of four numbers move by more than half their magnitude on the removal of two observations, so neither the raw nor the trimmed figure should be quoted as though it were known. Read them as a PAIR, the same way the IV ratios are read.
_DIVERSIFICATION_STATISTICS_ARE_FRAGILE.the_operational_consequence: The equity entry gate's diversification reasoning is qualitative ('uncorrelated with the existing PNC (bank) and LLY (pharma) book' -- the MDLZ entry note, 2026-08-28T13:38Z). That prose was RIGHT on the numbers, which is the uncomfortable part: it reached a correct conclusion without the measurement, so a future run cannot tell from the record whether the reasoning or the luck did the work. Any future entry citing diversification should quote BOTH the raw and ex-top2 pairwise correlation against the existing book, or say plainly that it is arguing from sector labels rather than from data.
_DIVERSIFICATION_STATISTICS_ARE_FRAGILE.a_caveat_recorded_against_myself: The tempting extra number here is a 'today-implied beta' -- all four names are down 0.40-0.66% against SPY -0.215%, giving implied betas of +1.84 to +3.05, every one far above both its raw and its trimmed estimate. DO NOT CITE THAT. The denominator is a 0.215% index move, so ordinary idiosyncratic drift of 0.4% mechanically reads as beta ~1.9 whatever the true sensitivity. It is the same too-small-denominator error this file has now recorded four times against volume baselines, arriving against a beta baseline; it looked like the most striking finding of the run and it is an artifact.

_EX_GAP_IS_AN_UPPER_BOUND_NOT_A_FORECAST.status: DURABLE calibration finding on this desk's own IV method. Read with the 2026-08-20 iv_rv_ratio finding, which it refines rather than replaces. _EX_GAP_IS_AN_UPPER_BOUND_NOT_A_FORECAST.claim: This file reads `iv_rv_ratio` and `iv_rv_ratio_ex_top2` as a PAIR and treats the ex-gap number as the honest gauge for a contract expiring before the next print. Correct. But nobody had ever asked what the raw ratio actually converges to once the offending gap ROLLS OUT of the trailing window -- and it is NOT the ex-gap number. Ex-top2 drops the two largest moves; roll-off removes only the one. So EX-GAP SYSTEMATICALLY OVERSHOOTS: it is an UPPER BOUND on the post-roll-off raw ratio, not an estimate of it.

_EX_GAP_IS_AN_UPPER_BOUND_NOT_A_FORECAST.the_rule: When quoting the pair, say which question each answers: RAW = what a buyer bears on a contract SPANNING the print; EX-GAP = a deliberately conservative floor on realized, hence an UPPER bound on the ratio; PROJECTED POST-ROLL-OFF RAW = where the headline number is actually heading, and the only one of the three that is a forecast. Compute the third when a gap is within a few sessions of exiting the window -- it is three lines of arithmetic off bars you already have.

the_rule_was_inverted_in_practice_2026-0.headline: the_rule above says RAW is the gauge for a contract SPANNING a print and EX-GAP is a deliberately conservative UPPER bound. Four consecutive runs today declined the CORE track citing the EX-GAP number on candidates that all span two macro prints. The rule existed, was correct, and was applied backwards -- the decline is right, its stated ground is measured on the wrong leg of the pair.
the_rule_was_inverted_in_practice_2026-0.the_instances: 2026-09-09 journal entries at 14:02Z, 14:15Z, 14:30Z and 15:00Z each record CORE declined on 'IV sanity ... SPY ex-gap IV/RV 1.302, 80th pct'. No entry cites the raw ratio.

the_rule_was_inverted_in_practice_2026-0.why_raw_governs_today: CORE is DTE 21-45, so a contract opened 2026-09-09 expires 2026-09-30..10-24. PPI 2026-09-10 and CPI 2026-09-11 both fall inside every one of those. The buyer genuinely bears both gaps, which is precisely the condition the_rule assigns to RAW.
the_rule_was_inverted_in_practice_2026-0.the_sharper_form_this_earns: On a session with a macro print one or two days out, NO contract in EITHER track can expire before it -- TACTICAL takes the nearest liquid expiry above the DTE-7 floor, which also spans. So on a day like today ex-gap cannot be the governing gauge for ANY candidate the desk is able to buy, and citing it is wrong by construction rather than by a close judgement call.
the_rule_was_inverted_in_practice_2026-0.the_mechanism_and_why_it_is_easy_to_miss: iv_history.json writes ONE row per name per day and both tracks read that same row. The row cannot know which track will read it, so it correctly carries both ratios -- gauge selection is a property of the CONTRACT's expiry versus the event, not of the row. A reader who takes 'the' ratio off a shared row takes whichever one is listed second. Same shape as the 2026-08-28 per-track catalyst rule: each track must screen its own window, and a number is not portable between them.
the_rule_was_inverted_in_practice_2026-0.direction_of_the_error: CONSERVATIVE, which is why it survived four runs unnoticed: ex-gap reads richer than raw, so the mistake can only suppress an entry, never license one. Harmless today; it would matter on a day where 1.09 clears IV sanity and 1.30 does not, and the desk would decline a setup it had actually graded A.
the_rule_was_inverted_in_practice_2026-0.honest_scope: CHANGED NO DECISION. A past-tense measurement bound to a timestamp is correct history and is LEFT ALONE; a present-tense assertion of current state is residue and is struck. Applied here it also correctly ACQUITTED three things a keyword sweep would have flagged: market_brief.json.capital ('~$1,757 after the $250 reserve' -- a timestamped 13:35Z computation, history, kept), docs/options-automation-setup.md lines 80-81 (describing the v9 fix, i.e. the repeal itself, correct as written), and latest_morning.md line 27 (a literal false positive -- MDLZ's 60.45 price matching the '0.45' pattern).

_VOID_FLOOR_RESIDUE_CLASS.THE_TRANSFERABLE_LESSON: A repeal has THREE dimensions, not the two this key previously named: every FILE that asserts current state, every CONSTANT the repeal retired, and every ENCODING those constants can take -- prose, numeric literal, FIELD NAME, and a status string in any capitalisation. A structured artifact does not spell its rules the way a document does, so a sweep written for prose is systematically blind to exactly the machine-readable copies that a machine will actually act on. Practical form: for a repealed rule, grep the SCHEMA (field names containing floor/cap/min/max/compliant) and the bare NUMERAL alongside the prose, and in a JSON artifact enumerate the top-level KEYS rather than trusting a full-text search of the file. The meta-lesson is the one this key keeps re-learning from a new angle each time: every sweep so far has widened the query along whichever axis the last failure exposed, then declared completion. Do not declare completion -- state the axes actually searched and let the next run find the next one.
_VOID_FLOOR_RESIDUE_CLASS.materiality: HIGHER THAN INSTANCES 8-9, AND IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION TO WHAT THE STALE TEXT SUGGESTS. Instances 8-9 sat in reference documents; this one sat in the live state file, under the key a run consults to answer 'how much can the equity book take'. And the dead arithmetic now reads WORSE than when it was written: cash is 30.60% of the equity book ($1,046.96 against $2,374.28) versus the void 45% minimum, so the repealed rule would compute a negative max-compliant-buy and freeze all remaining entry slots for the rest of the posture. The repeal is precisely what makes today's $796.96 deployable. It changed no decision today only because this run declined both books on merit and no earlier run happened to read this key -- that is luck, not a control.
_VOID_FLOOR_RESIDUE_CLASS.instance_10_holdings_json_book_concentra: The key literally named _book_concentration, INSIDE holdings.json -- the file this key's own corpus list names as SWEPT, and the file every run reads first. It carried, present-tense and unqualified: "cash_floor_pct": 44.9648, "floor_minimum_pct": 45.0, "max_compliant_buy_usd": -1.21, and "status": "BOOK CLOSED to new equity entries on the floor." Stamped 2026-08-28T15:45:00Z, i.e. written ~5 hours BEFORE the repeal and never revisited. Repaired this run against the full-deployment policy with broker-read 17:45-17:46Z numbers.
_VOID_FLOOR_RESIDUE_CLASS.WHY_NINE_SWEEPS_MISSED_IT_and_this_is_th: NOT the corpus and NOT the constant -- both of those dimensions were correct here. holdings.json was enumerated and swept; BOTH retired constants were eventually searched. The sweep missed it on a THIRD axis: ENCODING. Every query this key records was PROSE -- '0.45', '45%', 'cash floor', 'compliant buy', 'book is closed'. Instance 10 encodes the floor as JSON NUMBERS in FIELD NAMES (floor_minimum_pct: 45.0, cash_floor_pct, max_compliant_buy_usd) plus a status string in different capitalisation and without the copula. Grep '45%' does not match 45.0. Grep 'book is closed' does not match 'BOOK CLOSED'. Grep 'cash floor' does not match 'cash_floor_pct'. The residue was in plain sight, in the most-read file, and every single query was constructed to miss it.
_VOID_FLOOR_RESIDUE_CLASS.THE_DISCRIMINATOR_unchanged_and_it_worke: Still a TENSE, not a keyword, and it cleanly convicts instance 10: 'BOOK CLOSED to new equity entries' is a present-tense assertion of current state, so it is residue and was struck. Timestamped past-tense measurements elsewhere in the file were again left alone. The discriminator was never the problem -- the RETRIEVAL was.

_CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-31.cross_measurement_of_the_tape: CONCURRENT-RUN CROSS-MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-31, AND IT IS THE MOST DIRECT EVIDENCE THIS FILE HAS THAT AN OPENING-WINDOW REGIME LABEL IS NOT A LABEL. Two scheduled runs measured the same tape THREE MINUTES APART and produced OPPOSITE verdicts from CORRECT numbers. 13:36Z (sibling): AMD 475.22 +2.07%, AVGO 371.64 +0.77%, NVDA 218.75 +0.55% -> 'SEMI-LED RISK-ON UNDER A RED INDEX'. 13:38-13:40Z (this run): AMD 467.40 +0.39%, AVGO 367.005 -0.48%, NVDA 217.19 -0.17% -> 'BROAD-BASED RISK-OFF, FINANCIALS-LED'. A directional label extracted from the first ten minutes measures whichever leg happened to be running when the run fired, and a later run inheriting it will reason from a frame the tape has already withdrawn. Both labels above should be read as timestamped observations, and any run after ~14:15Z must RE-MEASURE all legs before using either. || The IV readings, by contrast, CROSS-VALIDATE cleanly across the same gap -- SPY 0.120998 vs 0.121370 (0.3% apart), QQQ 0.175312 vs 0.178442 (1.8%), NVDA 0.328571 vs 0.324473 (1.2%), on slightly different ATM strikes. _OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DECAYS_WITH_TIME.headline: THE OPENING-WINDOW ATM INFLATION IS CONFIRMED A FIFTH, SIXTH AND SEVENTH TIME IN DIRECTION -- BUT IT DECAYS WITH TIME, AND A ~20-MINUTE RE-MEASURE CAPTURES ONLY A THIRD TO A HALF OF IT. A RUN THAT RE-QUOTES EARLY HAS NOT FULLY DISCHARGED THE CAVEAT.
_OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DECAYS_WITH_TIME.method: Re-quoted the SAME strike and SAME expiry as each opening-window row, so this measures the artifact and not strike skew. SPY 767 2026-09-30, QQQ 717 2026-09-30, NVDA 220 2026-10-02; call/put averaged per the IV method.
_OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DECAYS_WITH_TIME.the_refinement: The four documented settles -- SPY -2.53%, QQQ -4.37%, NVDA -3.56%, and the 2026-08-27 audit's -4.23% -- were ALL taken 1 to 2 HOURS after the opening print. Today's three were taken ~20-25 minutes after, and came in at -0.60% to -1.95%: same direction, roughly a third to a half the magnitude. The honest mechanism is that the artifact BLEEDS OFF over the session rather than clearing at a threshold, so the size of the correction is a function of how long you waited.
_OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DECAYS_WITH_TIME.consequence: Do not treat 'I re-quoted after 14:00Z' as equivalent to 'this reading is settled'. State the GAP between the opening print and the re-measure when discharging the caveat, because that gap predicts how much of the artifact is still in the number. A row re-measured 20 minutes out is settled enough to stop being an upper bound, but a mid-session re-measure would likely read lower still.
_OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DECAYS_WITH_TIME.honest_scope: CHANGED NO DECISION -- no trade was taken in either book this run and no IV reading was load-bearing, which is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly. n=3 on one morning at one interval; the time-decay shape is inferred from two clusters of readings, not fitted. Do not convert it into a decay curve.
_OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DECAYS_WITH_TIME.what_it_does_not_license: Nothing. All three names read fair-to-cheap on the raw ratio and SPY reads RICH ex-gap at 1.2024. IV sanity is a NECESSARY condition and never a thesis -- fair vol supplies no reason whatsoever to own anything, and CORE still declines on the print cluster.

_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN.headline: THE EQUITY REPORT'S FIRST FIRE OF THE DAY IS 30 MINUTES AFTER THE BELL, SO THE AUTOMATION'S FIRST-POST-OPEN RUN -- THE ONE THAT TAKES THE DAY'S FIRST AUTONOMOUS EQUITY ENTRY -- ALWAYS ACTS ON THE PREVIOUS SESSION'S REPORT. THIS IS A SCHEDULE MISALIGNMENT, NOT A BUG IN EITHER SYSTEM.
_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN.evidence: stock-report.yml drives its cadence EXTERNALLY from cron-job.org via workflow_dispatch on 'a single hourly job (~9:00-14:00 CT, Mon-Fri)'. 09:00 CT = 14:00 UTC; the bell is 13:30 UTC. Today's first dispatch fired at 14:00:09Z, exactly on that schedule. The in-repo 'schedule:' entry (cron '0 13 * * 1-5') is documented in the workflow itself as a once-daily SAFETY NET only, and GitHub cron is best-effort -- Friday's scheduled run was created 2026-08-28T22:57:18Z, roughly ten hours late, which is precisely the 'minutes-to-hours late' the workflow's own comment warns about.
_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN.what_it_meant_today: The last COMPLETED report before this session was run 414, header '2026-08-28 22:59 UTC'. The automation's first-post-open run fired 13:38-13:50Z and placed MMM at 13:37:54Z off that Friday-night report. Run 415 dispatched at 14:00:09Z and its report ('2026-08-31 14:02 UTC') landed on master at ~14:15Z -- so the fresh report existed only from ~45 minutes after the bell.
_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN.is_it_a_violation: NO, AND DO NOT RETROSPECTIVELY TREAT THE MMM ENTRY AS ONE. v8 bars autonomous equity trades on a STALE report, and a report built on the last COMPLETED session's close is the correct signal basis for a Connors RSI2 daily-bar mean-reversion screen -- Monday morning has no new daily bar yet. What IS a session stale is the report's PRICE column and the entry/stop/target levels derived from it, and its [ERN] earnings annotations, which cannot see a date announced or moved over a weekend. CLAUDE.md already requires sanity-checking the earnings date on any name about to be bought, so the guard exists.
_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN.the_open_question_for_ryan: Should the first-post-open run be allowed to take an autonomous equity entry off the prior session's report at all, or should it wait for the day's first fresh report? No run has ever made that call explicitly, which is why it is being surfaced rather than decided here. AN UNATTENDED RUN CANNOT ANSWER IT -- HARD RULE 9.
_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN.the_clean_fix_which_is_RYANS_TO_MAKE: Move cron-job.org's first hourly report fire from 09:00 CT to ~08:15-08:30 CT (13:15-13:30 UTC) so a same-session report exists BEFORE the automation's first-post-open run acts. Agents cannot edit the cron-job.org job, same class as the 2026-08-18 trigger outage. A second, weaker option is to rely on the 13:00Z GitHub backstop, but Friday's ten-hour-late fire is direct evidence it cannot be relied on for timing.
_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN.detector_for_future_runs: Before any autonomous equity entry, read the report HEADER TIMESTAMP and state it explicitly against the current trading day. If the header predates today's bell, say so in the journal and treat the price/stop/target levels as one session stale even when the signal set is sound.
_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN._correction_do_not_inherit_the_hung_clai: An earlier draft of this key, written at 14:08Z, said run 415 was 'still in_progress with a frozen updated_at 8+ minutes later', implying a hung workflow. THAT WAS WRONG and is corrected here rather than left standing. The run completed normally and committed. The error came from trusting the GitHub actions list endpoint's status/updated_at fields, which were STALE -- they still read in_progress well after the workflow had finished and pushed. DETECTOR: confirm a workflow's completion by looking for its COMMIT on master, not by polling the actions API's status field. Same shape as this file's other measurement bugs -- a convenient indicator was trusted over the primary artifact.
_REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN.scope_note: The 30-minute gap is the durable finding and is UNAFFECTED by the correction above: cron-job.org's first fire is 09:00 CT = 14:00 UTC against a 13:30 UTC bell, verified from the workflow's own documented schedule and from today's 14:00:09Z dispatch. Report generation then takes ~2 minutes plus commit time.

_HOLE_CORRUPTED_THE_PRICE_CLAUSE_FLATTER.headline: A FEED HOLE HID THE BREAK LEVEL ITSELF, TURNING A BREAK THAT ROUND-TRIPPED INSIDE ITS OWN BAR INTO AN APPARENT CLEAN HOLD. This file documents holes hiding session extremes and depressing volume denominators; this is the first instance where the hidden extreme WAS the trigger level, and the distortion pointed toward taking the trade.
_HOLE_CORRUPTED_THE_PRICE_CLAUSE_FLATTER.the_hole: Cross-symbol signature per the 2026-08-27 rule: the 14:10Z 5-minute bucket was holed SIMULTANEOUSLY on all three symbols measured. NVDA reported 87,672 against a 1-minute sum of 1,057,298 (-91.71%); SPY 6,907 against 120,938 (-94.29%); QQQ 17,436 against 138,954 (-87.45%). Per the 2026-08-28 DIRECTION rule the bucket is materially BELOW its 1-minute sum in every case, so the BUCKET is the holed side and the 1-minute sum substitutes.
_HOLE_CORRUPTED_THE_PRICE_CLAUSE_FLATTER.the_new_part_price_not_volume: NVDA's holed bucket reported OHLC 220.035 / 220.200 / 220.000 / 220.190. The TRUE bucket, rebuilt from its 1-minute constituents, is 219.380 / 220.200 / 219.267 / 220.170. The reported LOW of 220.000 is wrong by 0.733 -- and the true low of 219.267 sits BELOW the 219.6195 session high the break was made through. So the 5-minute series portrayed price consolidating tightly above the level, when in fact it broke, traded back UNDER the level mid-bucket, and only reclaimed 220 in the final minute. A run reading the 5-minute series alone would have scored 'held beyond the level' as satisfied. It was not.
_HOLE_CORRUPTED_THE_PRICE_CLAUSE_FLATTER.why_it_is_the_dangerous_direction: Same reason an under-reported bucket manufactures volume confirmation: the distortion argues FOR the trade. A holed bucket shows one constituent minute's range, and on an UPSIDE break the minute that survives is disproportionately likely to be the last one -- which is the highest one. The price clause is therefore biased toward false positives on exactly the bars a breakout desk cares about.
_HOLE_CORRUPTED_THE_PRICE_CLAUSE_FLATTER.the_rule: Reconcile the bucket against the 1-minute series BEFORE testing the price clause, not only before computing a volume baseline. The existing detector is unchanged and sufficient; what is new is WHERE to apply it. 'Did it hold beyond the level' is a question about a bar's LOW (on a long) or HIGH (on a short), which is precisely the field a hole destroys.
_HOLE_CORRUPTED_THE_PRICE_CLAUSE_FLATTER.mixed_form_worth_noting: This hole is a MIXED presentation. Its OHLC is byte-for-byte the 14:14 one-minute bar (220.035/220.200/220.000, the single-constituent signature), but its VOLUME of 87,672 matches NO constituent minute (240,529 / 330,209 / 238,852 / 184,587 / 63,121) -- the partial form the 2026-08-28T15:35Z finding recorded. One bucket can be single-constituent in price and partial in volume at once, so neither signature alone is the test. The reconciliation GAP remains the test.
_HOLE_CORRUPTED_THE_PRICE_CLAUSE_FLATTER.honest_scope: Changed no decision. The trade was independently declined on index disagreement and on the volume clause, and the price clause was incomplete anyway (the holding bar had not closed). A feed-integrity finding is only creditable when the audit does not license a trade.
_HOLE_CORRUPTED_THE_PRICE_CLAUSE_FLATTER.FOLLOW_UP_2026-08-31T14:27Z_HOLES_DO_NOT: Re-fetched at 14:27Z, SEVENTEEN MINUTES after the bar closed: the 14:10Z 5-minute bucket STILL reports 87,672 against a 1,081,849 one-minute sum (-91.9%), OHLC still byte-for-byte the 14:14 minute, still hiding the true bucket low of 219.2672. THE RULE THIS ADDS: the 2026-08-26 'fetch the window twice a few minutes apart' detector catches PROVISIONAL bars, NOT holes -- a second identical read is NOT evidence a bucket is clean. Only the 1-minute reconciliation settles a hole. Control, so this is a hole and not a systematic offset: the 14:15Z bucket reads 1,185,159 vs a 1,156,642 one-minute sum (+2.5%) and the 14:20Z bucket 1,179,206 vs 1,136,656 (+3.7%), both inside tolerance. Separately the 1-MINUTE series was itself revised UP -- this run's break-bar sum 1,081,849 vs the 14:20Z run's 1,057,298 (+2.3%), the 2026-08-26 provisional-bar finding -- moving the break bar from 92.8% to 94.9% of baseline and changing nothing.

_RESERVE_IS_THE_STRICTER_OF_TWO.headline: EVERY RUN SINCE THE 2026-08-29 CAPITAL AMENDMENT HAS QUOTED DEPLOYABLE CAPITAL FROM THE 5%-OF-TOTAL RESERVE ALONE, WHILE FOUR LAWS #4's FLAT $250 SAT UNAPPLIED BESIDE IT AND IS STRICTER AT THIS ACCOUNT SIZE.
_RESERVE_IS_THE_STRICTER_OF_TWO.the_arithmetic: CLAUDE.md's full-deployment policy sets an operational reserve of 5% of total_value, recomputed each run: 0.05 x $3,973.02 = $198.65. FOUR LAWS #4 says 'Always leave >=$250 unencumbered.' The governance rule is 'where either is stricter, the stricter rule applies'. $250 > $198.65, so the binding reserve is $250 and deployable = $1,046.96 - $250 = $796.96, NOT the $848.45 the 14:05Z and 14:15Z runs quoted (they used $848.45 off a $198.51 reserve). Overstatement today: $51.35.
_RESERVE_IS_THE_STRICTER_OF_TWO.the_crossover_and_why_it_will_not_self_c: The two rules agree only at 0.05 x total = 250, i.e. a total_value of $5,000. BELOW $5,000 the flat $250 binds; above it the 5% formula does. This account has been below $5,000 for the entire life of the full-deployment policy, so the 5% formula has been the wrong number every single time it has been quoted, and will stay wrong until the account grows ~26%. It is a permanent-until-fixed error, not a transient one.
_RESERVE_IS_THE_STRICTER_OF_TWO.why_it_survived: The 5% formula is the NEW rule, it is written with emphasis ('recomputed every run, NEVER hard-coded as a dollar figure -- it scales with the account'), and applying it feels like compliance. FOUR LAWS #4's $250 is one clause in a longer law about margin, so a run checking that law reads it for 'is unleveraged_buying_power the budget?', answers yes, and moves on without noticing the reserve sentence in the same bullet. Same family as this file's most-repeated defect: a check that passes for the wrong reason.
_RESERVE_IS_THE_STRICTER_OF_TWO.the_detector: Compute BOTH reserves every run and take the max: reserve = max(0.05 * total_value, 250.00). One line. Do not quote a deployable figure derived from only one of them.
_RESERVE_IS_THE_STRICTER_OF_TWO.materiality: IMMATERIAL TODAY and stated as such -- no trade was placed, and both figures comfortably cover any entry that was contemplated. It becomes material the moment cash sits between the two numbers, when a run would authorise an entry that FOUR LAWS #4 forbids. FOUR LAWS are absolute and admit no thesis, so an overrun there is a governance breach rather than a sizing error.
_RESERVE_IS_THE_STRICTER_OF_TWO.STATUS_VOID_UNDER_v10: VOID as of the 2026-09-02 prompt v10 paste (confirmed live 2026-09-03T00:19Z). This key was CORRECT when written 2026-08-31 under prompt v8, whose FOUR LAWS #4 read 'Always leave >=$250 unencumbered' while CLAUDE.md's capital policy said 5% of total_value -- a genuine conflict that the governance tie-breaker ('where either is stricter, the stricter rule applies') correctly resolved to $250. v10's FOUR LAWS #4 now reads: 'Always leave the OPERATIONAL RESERVE unencumbered: 5% of get_portfolio total_value, recomputed every run, never a hard-coded dollar figure (it replaces the old flat $250).' The prompt NAMES AND RETIRES the $250 itself, and CLAUDE.md already said the flat $250 'is retired'. BOTH DOCUMENTS NOW SAY 5% -- the tie-breaker has nothing left to bite on. Use 5% of total_value. Do NOT re-derive the $250 from this key's body below, which is kept only so the record reads correctly.

_RESERVE_IS_THE_STRICTER_OF_TWO.why_this_one_would_have_survived_and_the: The stale rule is the STRICTER one, so applying it never errors, never overspends and never visibly blocks anything -- it just quietly understates deployable capital by $51.26. A safe-direction error is invisible to every check that only asks 'did we deploy money we do not have?', which is the only capital check this desk runs. IMMATERIAL TODAY -- $353.36 and $302.10 are both below the ~$600 minimum entry, so no decision changes either way, which is the only condition under which an audit of a capital input is creditable. _LATE_ENTRY_COST_ON_A_FLAT_UNDERLYING.headline: THE LATE-ENTRY DETECTOR MEASURED FOR THE FIRST TIME ON A MOTIONLESS UNDERLYING, WHICH ISOLATES THE COST OF MERELY WAITING: an 11-DTE ATM tactical vehicle bled -2.46% in fourteen minutes while its underlying moved -0.048%.
_LATE_ENTRY_COST_ON_A_FLAT_UNDERLYING.why_the_test_is_new: Both prior tests (2026-08-28, -11.25% and -11.19%) ran on underlyings that MOVED, so the delta term dominated and the non-delta cost could not be separated. Holding spot nearly fixed separates it.
_LATE_ENTRY_COST_ON_A_FLAT_UNDERLYING.what_it_says: Delta accounts for roughly -0.055 and theta roughly -0.002 across fourteen minutes. About HALF the loss is neither -- implied-vol bleed plus a bid/ask that DOUBLED from 0.99% to 2.02% of mid. Order of magnitude: ~1.2-1.4% of premium per quarter-hour to hold an 11-DTE ATM tactical contract with the underlying standing still, against a +20% target needing only ~+1.04% on NVDA. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: 'why NOW' is not a stylistic gate on a scalp, it is the arithmetic -- a tactical thesis that needs half an hour to be right has already spent a quarter of its target.
_LATE_ENTRY_COST_ON_A_FLAT_UNDERLYING.limits_stated_plainly: n=1. The prior run did not record this contract's IV, so the vol-versus-spread split is INFERRED from the residual, not measured -- do not quote the decomposition finer than 'roughly half'. Part of the spread widening may be quote timing rather than a real liquidity change. It changed no decision (the trade was declined on three other grounds and stays declined), which is the only condition under which a detector can be audited credibly.

_HANDOFF_CONJUNCTIONS_CLEAR_OUT_OF_ORDER.finding: A handoff that lists conditions as a conjunction invites the next run to read partial satisfaction as partial progress. It is not. Measured on the 14:35Z NVDA handoff's three conditions: condition 3 (index legs no longer printing session lows) CLEARED -- SPY's 764.721 low was set 14:25Z and QQQ's 713.160 at 14:26Z, neither renewed in ~20 minutes. Condition 1 (a completed 5-minute close above the structural level, next bar holding) FAILED OUTRIGHT: NVDA extended its session high to 220.600 on a WICK but never closed a bucket above 220.360, the highest completed close being 220.175. The volume condition was never reached.
_HANDOFF_CONJUNCTIONS_CLEAR_OUT_OF_ORDER.the_mechanism: The three gates have wildly different costs to clear. An index leg ceasing to make new lows is satisfied by ordinary mean reversion and demands nothing whatsoever of the setup; a completed close through a level on real participation is the only one carrying information. So the cheap gate cleared, the decisive one did not, and a run counting satisfied gates would feel two-thirds of the way to a trade while being no closer at all.
_HANDOFF_CONJUNCTIONS_CLEAR_OUT_OF_ORDER.the_rule: WHEN HANDING FORWARD A CONJUNCTION, RANK THE CONDITIONS BY WHAT THEY COST TO CLEAR AND NAME WHICH IS DECISIVE. Otherwise the COUNT of satisfied gates gets mistaken for PROXIMITY to a setup -- and the count rises fastest on the gates that mean least.
_HANDOFF_CONJUNCTIONS_CLEAR_OUT_OF_ORDER.robustness: Measured on BOTH bar constructions: the broker's 5-minute buckets and an independent rebuild from the 1-minute series agree on every close to within 0.015 and both place the 220.600 high inside the 14:35 bucket. Two constructions, one answer.
_HANDOFF_CONJUNCTIONS_CLEAR_OUT_OF_ORDER.honest_scope: Changed no decision -- the trade was declined on the price clause alone and would have been whatever the index legs did. A gate-ordering audit is only creditable on a run where it does not license a trade.

_OVERSOLD_COHORT_IS_MEASURABLE_BEFORE_AN.claim: MEASURE THE REPORT'S OVERSOLD LIST AS A COHORT BEFORE GRADING ITS MEMBERS ONE AT A TIME. The trend-maturity gate's clause (c) -- does the PRESENT tape confirm or diverge -- has been applied name-by-name for nine runs of this session. It is computable across the whole candidate set in one get_equity_quotes call, before any thesis workup, and it answers a question no individual grade can: am I looking for a stabilizing name inside a stabilizing group, or hunting the single exception?
_OVERSOLD_COHORT_IS_MEASURABLE_BEFORE_AN.measured_2026-08-31T15_27Z: 15 non-held RSI2 / oversold-uptrend candidates vs prior close: REGN +0.222 (the ONLY green) | AEHR -0.588 | KLAC -0.644 | IWM -0.872 | COF -0.902 | CAT -1.192 | AMAT -1.224 | RTX -1.445 | TSEM -1.808 | GE -1.870 | MRVL -2.006 | GEV -2.139 | MAR -2.227 | GD -2.291 | BE -2.799. _OVERSOLD_COHORT_IS_MEASURABLE_BEFORE_AN.the_reasoning: An RSI2 mean-reversion entry is a bet that an oversold name STOPS going down. A cohort being distributed at 3.2x the index rate is that bet failing across the class on the day you would take it -- and it explains, in two lines, nine consecutive name-by-name declines.
_OVERSOLD_COHORT_IS_MEASURABLE_BEFORE_AN.the_honest_caveat_which_limits_the_claim: An oversold cohort underperforming on a down day is PARTLY EXPECTED BY CONSTRUCTION: the screen selects names already being sold, skewing the sample toward weakness and high beta. This does NOT prove the setup class is broken and a run reading it that way has over-claimed. What it establishes is narrower and sufficient -- today shows DISTRIBUTION where the entry needs STABILIZATION. Note also that the cohort is not merely high-beta: GD, RTX, CAT and MAR are low-beta names and all four fell 1.2-2.3% against an index down 0.45%.
_OVERSOLD_COHORT_IS_MEASURABLE_BEFORE_AN.how_to_read_the_exception: The single green name is the one worth working -- but relative strength for ONE SESSION is one data point, and it does not repair a weak setup. REGN was that name today and was still declined: spot 795.95 sits only -0.84% below its own 20-day (802.69), so its RSI2 4.6 print comes from five small down days rather than a washout, with very little to revert. Compare the cohort's real washouts: KLAC -9.0%, AMAT -10.3%, GEV -9.8% below their 20-days. Depth of pullback and relative strength are SEPARATE tests and a candidate needs both.
_OVERSOLD_COHORT_IS_MEASURABLE_BEFORE_AN.the_shape_of_the_lesson: Same family as the denominator findings: a statistic every run needed was cheaply computable and nobody computed it, so nine runs re-derived a worse version of it one name at a time. When a gate is being applied repeatedly to members of a set, check whether it can be applied to the SET.

_THE_200DAY_GATE_CERTIFIES_DOWNTRENDS.headline: THE EQUITY REPORT'S 'OVERSOLD WITHIN A RISING 200-DAY UPTREND' GATE PASSED A NAME SITTING BELOW ITS 20-, 50- AND 130-DAY AVERAGES, 16% OFF ITS HIGH, SIX SESSIONS INTO LOWER CLOSES. THE 200-DAY LAGS TOO MUCH TO CERTIFY 'DIP IN AN UPTREND'. ADD THE 50-DAY AS THE DISCRIMINATOR.
_THE_200DAY_GATE_CERTIFIES_DOWNTRENDS.the_demonstration_not_an_inference: MAR was today's best-looking tradeable RSI2 candidate -- RSI2 2.4, the deepest oversold on the list after AEHR, a tight -3.6% suggested stop, no earnings in the window, no sector overlap with the book, non-oil, non-spec. Measured off daily closes: spot 344.03 against 20SMA 354.86, 50SMA 366.86 and a 130-session SMA of 359.17 -- BELOW ALL THREE, with the 50-day sitting ABOVE the 20-day (the classic downtrend stack). 16.3% off the 410.98 window high. Closes 356.39 -> 360.20 -> 357.77 -> 358.67 -> 353.87 -> 351.08 -> 344.03. That is a falling knife the screen certified as a dip in an uptrend.
_THE_200DAY_GATE_CERTIFIES_DOWNTRENDS.the_mechanism: A 200-day SMA averages a full year, so it keeps rising for months after the intermediate trend has rolled over. An RSI2 screen CANNOT fire unless price is stretched below its short-term averages -- that is what oversold means -- so 'below the 20-day' carries no information and every candidate has it. The 50-day is the first average that distinguishes the two cases: above it, there is an established mean above spot for price to revert TOWARD; below it, mean reversion has no mean, and the trade is a bet against an intermediate downtrend.
_THE_200DAY_GATE_CERTIFIES_DOWNTRENDS.applied_to_todays_list: MAR below 20/50/130 -> REJECT. GD spot 371.25 below 20SMA 387.56 AND 50SMA 375.98 -> REJECT on the same test. RTX 208.57 below 20SMA 218.12 but ABOVE 50SMA 205.85 by only 0.64% -> passes narrowly. REGN 793.53 below 20SMA 802.69, above 50SMA 716.62 by 10.7% -> passes clearly. _RSI2_SCREEN_TREND_FAILURE_IS_SYSTEMATIC.mechanism: A 200-day average is still rising on year-ago data long after price has broken down. A name 40% off its high can sit above a rising 200-day for months. So the gate as written admits deep downtrends and calls them dips. Connors' RSI(2) mean-reversion is specified for names ABOVE their long-term average and in an intact uptrend; the report's gate does not enforce that in any usable form, and the RSI2 print itself is trend-blind by construction.
_RSI2_SCREEN_TREND_FAILURE_IS_SYSTEMATIC.detector: BEFORE grading any RSI2 name, compute SMA20 / SMA50 / SMA130 and % off high. Below all three = DOWNTREND, decline it -- do not spend a thesis workup on it. This is one get_equity_historicals call for up to 10 names and it disqualified five of eight candidates in a single pass, which is far cheaper than the per-name news-and-analyst workup the gate stack would otherwise demand.
_RSI2_SCREEN_TREND_FAILURE_IS_SYSTEMATIC.the_inversion_that_makes_this_hard: THE TREND FILTER AND THE MEAN-REVERSION EDGE POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, AND THIS IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN A QUIRK OF TODAY. BLK passes the trend test BECAUSE it is only 1.6% off its high -- and that same fact is what makes it the WEAKEST reversion candidate on the screen: there is almost nothing to revert into. Its RSI2 of 5.9 was generated by FOUR CONSECUTIVE SMALL DOWN DAYS (a sequence), not by any magnitude of decline; RSI2 is a 2-day oscillator and prints single digits on a 0.2% slide if the slide is consistent. The report's own numbers say it: stop 1120.52 (-2.65%) against target 1182.84 (+2.77%), roughly 1:1. So 'best trend on the screen' and 'best setup on the screen' are NOT the same name, and a run that finds the only trend-passing name must still ask what it is being paid to take the trade. Pairs with _TAPE_CONFIRMATION_AND_THE_RSI2_SCREEN_ARE_IN_TENSION (2026-08-31T16:00Z), which found the same tension from the opposite end -- there, the tape confirmation that validated REGN lifted its RSI2 out of the gate.

Neither filter is wrong; a run must resolve them on merits rather than let whichever it applies second do all the work.

(1) MAGNITUDE: quote the complex ETF, the index, and the ratio -- below ~2x the index it is beta, not a de-rate. (2) DISPERSION: quote the MEMBERS and the best-to-worst spread. If one member is a multi-sigma outlier or any member is GREEN, the ETF number is a weighted average and not a regime, and 'the complex is de-rating' is the wrong description of it. The magnitude test alone cannot tell a de-rating complex from a complex containing one blowup -- both print the same ETF number.
_COMPLEX_VETOES_NEED_A_MAGNITUDE_TEST.why_this_matters_more_than_the_first_tes: The 16:16Z run built the magnitude test precisely to stop a correct veto from being reused by analogy, and it worked -- it caught the financials and power-complex over-extensions. But it REAFFIRMED the defense veto on the strength of ITA -2.10% = 4.4x SPY, and that reaffirmation is what this measurement corrects. The magnitude test PASSED on a tape where LHX was green and the ETF reading was being carried by an outlier. A test that catches the analogies but certifies the original is the more dangerous half, because it launders the original into settled fact.

'The complex veto was mis-specified' does NOT mean the vetoed names are un-vetoed. It means the reason changes -- and for GD the corrected reason is STRONGER. A complex-wide de-rate is beta a mean-reversion entry can fade; an idiosyncratic decline against a flat-to-green complex is the market marking down THIS name. _A_BLOCK_PRINT_INFLATES_THE_BASELINE_AND.the_detector: A 1-minute bar that is a large multiple of BOTH neighbours WITH A PRICE RANGE NEAR ZERO is a block cross, not participation -- exclude it from any trailing baseline used as a confirmation denominator. This is the exact mirror of the existing recognition rule ('a 1-minute bar whose volume is a tiny fraction of both neighbours is provisional'). The discriminator is RANGE, not size: participation moves price, a cross does not.

THE DANGEROUS CASE IS THE SAME PRINT LANDING ON THE BREAK BAR ITSELF: a block cross inside the two-bar confirmation window would supply the participation the clause is looking for, on a trade that expressed no view at all. _ENTRY_DAY_BAR_IS_NOT_THE_POSITIONS_BAR.claim: ON THE ENTRY DAY, THE DAILY BAR'S HIGH AND LOW BOUND THE STOCK, NOT THE TRADE. _RSI2_REVERSION_AND_PROFIT_NEED_NOT_COIN.what_it_says_about_the_08_26_gate: It VINDICATES the gate at near-zero opportunity cost, which is the strongest form the evidence could take. Had the ungated reading been applied, the RSI2 print that fired on 08-26 would have banked a LOSS. Had the gated version somehow fired at the best moment available (08-24 high, RSI2 37), it would have banked +$1.11 before spread. There was no profitable exit anywhere in this cycle to be missed. The gate cost nothing and prevented a realized loss.
_RSI2_REVERSION_AND_PROFIT_NEED_NOT_COIN.the_transferable_mechanism: RSI2 is a RELATIVE oscillator normalized to recent range, so it re-baselines to wherever price has settled. An entry taken before price bottoms means the whole subsequent reversion is measured against a LOWER base: the oscillator can traverse its entire range while price merely chops sideways. PNC ran 1.6 -> 66 while price stayed inside a 241.30-247.08 band the entire time. THEREFORE: 'the RSI2 signal reverted' and 'the trade is profitable' are independent events, and a swing thesis that treats the first as implying the second is unfalsifiable in exactly the tape where it fails.
_RSI2_REVERSION_AND_PROFIT_NEED_NOT_COIN.HONEST_SCOPE_n_equals_1: One name, one cycle. This does NOT condemn the RSI2 screen and must not be cited as though it did. Four of the book's five positions (LLY 2 sessions, MDLZ 1, ROST 1, MMM 0) are far too young for their signal to have had its chance -- only PNC has been held long enough to judge, and judging the strategy off its single oldest position is precisely the selection-on-the-outcome error the 18:18Z run recorded today. What it establishes is narrower and firm: a completed reversion is not a guaranteed exit, so the desk should not model RSI2 entries as self-liquidating.

THE RUN IS BUYING THE OPENING BOUNCE OF THE VERY DIP ITS SIGNAL TOLD IT TO BUY.

The 13:36:10Z fill at 374.4437 caught 82% of that opening pop and the whole move round-tripped inside eleven minutes. _OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_E.THE_MECHANISM_and_it_is_the_transferable: The signal and the execution are fighting each other. The autonomous entry is sourced from an RSI2 MEAN-REVERSION screen computed on the PREVIOUS SESSION'S CLOSE (see _REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN: the fresh report does not land on master until ~14:15Z, so the first-post-open run always acts on yesterday's report). The opening ten minutes is precisely when yesterday's oversold names get their reflexive bounce. So the run reads 'this name is oversold as of last night' and then executes into the exact window where that oversold condition is being relieved. It buys the bounce it meant to buy the dip of.
_OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_E.WHY_NOBODY_CAUGHT_IT: This file already carries the rule 'NEVER price a decision off the opening auction print -- re-quote at least ~5 minutes after 13:30Z', and runs have obeyed it. But that rule was written about MARKS and DECISIONS (the 2026-08-21 QQQ 680P incident, where an opening print flipped the SIGN of a P/L reported to Ryan). Nobody applied it to EXECUTION. Re-quoting before deciding and then filling into the same window satisfies the letter of the rule and gets the artifact anyway -- this file's most-repeated defect, a check that passes for the wrong reason. It is also the execution-layer sibling of the documented first-hour volume inflation: the opening bar carried 5.2x the next bar's volume on ROST and 2.3x on MDLZ, which is the same auction imbalance seen from the fill side instead of the denominator side.
_OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_E.THE_FIX_and_it_repairs_TWO_findings_with: PREFER to take the trading day's autonomous equity entry on the first run at or after ~14:15Z, once the fresh report has landed on master, rather than on the first-post-open run. Nothing in the thesis decays in 40 minutes: the hold is 1-3 weeks and the signal is already a day old. The same deferral ALSO retires _REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN's standing problem, because the run would then be acting on the CURRENT session's report instead of the prior one. Two known defects, one change, no gate loosened.
_OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_E.SCOPE_AND_LIMITS_stated_because_overclai: n=4 and the total measured cost is ~$14. This is a process refinement, NOT a crisis, and it must not be written up as one. Three caveats: (1) buying lower is not automatically better for a mean-reversion entry -- if a name keeps falling the later fill wins, if it reverts immediately the earlier fill wins; what is notable is that the improvement was available in 4 of 4 cases, not that it is guaranteed. (2) ROST filled at 44.3% of its range, so 'the run always buys the top' would be false. (3) GD's session is incomplete. The deferral is a PREFERENCE, not a bar: a genuinely time-critical signal still trades when it fires, and the entry must never be delayed past the point where the setup is gone.
_OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_E.what_it_does_NOT_change: No gate is loosened or tightened by this. The full HARD RULE 6 stack -- HARD RULE 7 thesis check, A-grade-only bar, capital policy, sector steer, [ERN] rule, per-name and spec caps, HARD RULE 3 market-order mechanics, HARD RULE 5's no-stops policy, 1/run and 3/day throttles -- applies unchanged. This is about WHEN in the session a cleared entry is executed, never about WHETHER it clears.
