_RSI2_EXIT_TRIGGER_SITS_AT_THE_ENTRY_PRI.the_mechanism_which_is_the_transferable_: A 2-period RSI's full traverse from oversold to overbought spans only the last few sessions' range. The ENTRY is taken when RSI2 is near its floor -- i.e. at a point inside that range -- and the EXIT fires when RSI2 reaches 70, which requires only that price recover to roughly the same range. Both prices are drawn from the SAME short window, so they coincide. This is why the trigger tracks the recent range rather than the entry: on names that have drifted down since entry (PNC -1.8%, LLY -1.2%) the trigger has drifted BELOW the entry with them; on names entered nearer their low (MMM, GD) it sits slightly above. THE TRIGGER PRICE IS ALWAYS 'ROUGHLY WHERE THE STOCK HAS RECENTLY BEEN', NEVER 'ENTRY PLUS A PROFIT'.
_RSI2_EXIT_TRIGGER_SITS_AT_THE_ENTRY_PRI.what_this_does_to_the_18_05Z_FLAG_and_it: The 18:05Z flag's core objection was that the magnitude floor's DENOMINATOR is a number the report itself labels an ESTIMATE, so eleven exits had been declined against a benchmark the source disclaims. That objection is now MOOT: the trigger sits at the entry price by construction, so the mechanical exit banks ~0-1% of position value WHATEVER the target is. The floor does not need the target to justify itself, and the argument no longer rests on an advisory number. The floor is not an ad-hoc override the desk keeps reaching for -- it is correcting a STRUCTURAL property of pairing an RSI2 entry screen with an RSI2 exit trigger, and it will therefore fire on essentially every position this book ever takes.
_RSI2_EXIT_TRIGGER_SITS_AT_THE_ENTRY_PRI.the_honest_counter_argument_and_it_is_st: CONNORS' OWN RSI(2) METHOD USES THE CROSS BACK ABOVE ~70 AS THE DESIGNED EXIT AND PROMISES NO TARGET. Under the pure method, 'exit at approximately breakeven-to-small-gain, frequently' is not a defect -- it is the strategy: you compound via a high hit rate on many small gains, not via large per-trade objectives. So this measurement does NOT establish that the mechanical exit is wrong. It establishes something narrower and more useful, below.
_RSI2_EXIT_TRIGGER_SITS_AT_THE_ENTRY_PRI.THE_ACTUAL_GOVERNANCE_QUESTION_restated_: THIS BOOK IS RUNNING TWO DIFFERENT EXIT SYSTEMS AT ONCE AND THEY DISAGREE BY CONSTRUCTION. The ledger records a TARGET for every swing (ROST 244.66, MDLZ 64.70, ...) and the report prints it; the automation executes the RSI2>=70 CROSS. Measured above, those two exits are ~0.8% and ~6% apart in price terms and 5x-35x apart in payoff. Pick ONE: (a) TARGET-BASED -- the RSI2>=70 print is advisory, exits happen on the target, the trailing stop, or a thesis break, and the magnitude floor becomes redundant because it is just 'the target has not been hit'; or (b) CONNORS-PURE -- the RSI2 cross IS the exit, targets come out of the ledger entirely, the magnitude floor is DROPPED, and the book accepts many ~breakeven round trips for a high hit rate (note this costs two spreads per trip and would have banked $0.64 net on ROST at 15:01Z). WHAT SHOULD NOT CONTINUE IS RUNNING BOTH, which is what twelve consecutive declines actually are. _TARGET_BRANCH_DECIDES_THE_MAGNITUDE_FLO.the_construction: report.py:98 -- target = round(max(ma20, min(price * (1 + 1.5 * stop_dist), hi20)), 2), with stop_dist = STOP_SIGMA_MULT(2.5) * sigma, sigma = pstdev of the last 20 close-to-close returns, hi20 = max of the last 20 closes. The target is CLAMPED BETWEEN TWO STRUCTURAL LEVELS -- the 20-day mean below, the 20-day high above -- with a volatility extrapolation in between. It is not the free-floating guess that 'Entry/stop/target are ESTIMATES' reads like at a glance.

ROST: sigma 0.017162, ma20 244.3117, hi20 255.23, 1.5R raw 229.87 x 1.064365 = 244.6641 -> target 244.66, matching the ledger to the cent via the MIDDLE (1.5R) branch, which beat the ma20 floor by only $0.35 (0.14%) -- so ROST's target is effectively its 20-DAY MEAN. MDLZ: sigma 0.012517, ma20 62.8715, hi20 64.70, 1.5R raw 62.43 x 1.046935 = 65.3605, CAPPED by hi20 -> target 64.70, also exact. MDLZ's target IS the 20-day HIGH (the 2026-08-24 close).

_TARGET_BRANCH_DECIDES_THE_MAGNITUDE_FLO.the_half_that_survives_and_is_the_reason: The two denominators are DIFFERENT KINDS OF DISTANCE, and nothing in the sibling finding covers this. Reverting to the 20-day MEAN is what a Connors mean-reversion entry is designed to do; reaching the 20-day HIGH is a strictly stronger demand, imposed only when volatility would have carried the 1.5R extrapolation past it. A position hovering within pennies of entry crosses that threshold back and forth on noise, so the SAME print is a mandatory autonomous take-profit and a policy-default hold within the same hour, with nothing about the trade having changed. That is not a knife-edge the floor introduced; the floor is what makes it visible. Whatever Ryan decides, the threshold should be a distance, not zero.

_CALIBRATION_ENGINE_AND_THE_IN_REGIME_BU.what_it_measures: The margin over the BREAKEVEN win rate implied by the payoff ratio -- never a raw win rate against a fixed number. At payoff 1.0 you need 50%; at payoff 2.0 only 33%. Comparing a win rate to a fixed threshold is the standard way to misread a strategy's health.
_CALIBRATION_ENGINE_AND_THE_IN_REGIME_BU.it_is_not_a_forecaster: It does not classify the regime or predict anything. The primary signal is the strategy's OWN trailing edge -- a direct measurement of whether the edge is present, not a proxy for it. The RSI(2) book is a mean-reversion engine that works in range-bound tapes and degrades in trending ones; measuring the edge catches that without needing to name the regime.
_CALIBRATION_ENGINE_AND_THE_IN_REGIME_BU.THE_BUG_IT_CAUGHT_ON_ITS_FIRST_RUN: Fed the live book's 53 closes, the calibration returned HEALTHY (+22.3 pts) and proposed loosening swing_time_stop_days 14 -> 16. EVERY ONE OF THOSE 53 TRADES CLOSED BEFORE THE TIME STOP EXISTED -- it was dead code until this same commit. The sample contained exactly ZERO evidence about the parameter it wanted to change. Fixed by adding the in_regime_trades argument: a parameter may only be tuned on trades that closed UNDER IT, and after any parameter change that parameter's evidence resets to zero.
_CALIBRATION_ENGINE_AND_THE_IN_REGIME_BU.why_that_bug_matters_beyond_this_instanc: Tuning a parameter on data that predates it is superstition, and it is INDISTINGUISHABLE from real calibration unless you count the in-regime trades -- the output looks identical, well-reasoned and well-evidenced. Same family as this file's most-repeated defect: a check that passes for the wrong reason. A self-optimizing system is exactly where that failure is most dangerous, because nobody is reading the intermediate step.
_CALIBRATION_ENGINE_AND_THE_IN_REGIME_BU.the_kill_branch_is_deliberately_exempt: Margin <= 0 -> halve size, pause new entries, escalate -- and this branch SKIPS the in-regime gate. If the book is losing money, 'these trades predate the current settings' is not a reason to keep sizing into it. RISK-OFF NEVER WAITS FOR A CLEAN SAMPLE.
_CALIBRATION_ENGINE_AND_THE_IN_REGIME_BU.asymmetry_on_purpose: A degraded edge tightens the entry trigger; a healthy edge does NOT loosen it, and may only earn a slightly longer time stop. A working strategy is not an invitation to take worse setups.

Cheap: six positions, one pass. The test for each hit is not 'does this mention the old rule' -- historical findings legitimately do -- but 'does this INSTRUCT a future run', i.e. is it phrased as a standing direction rather than a dated measurement. REFINED 2026-09-03T13:05Z, BY THE DETECTOR FAILING ON ITS OWN REPAIR MINUTES AFTER BEING WRITTEN: a post-merge verification grepping positions[] for the literal string 'DECLINED ON THE MAGNITUDE FLOOR' reported MDLZ and ROST as STILL LIVE. The bullet above had already stated the correct test ('does this INSTRUCT a future run', not 'does this mention the old rule') and the verification then implemented the wrong one. So state the check EXECUTABLY rather than as a principle: a hit is live residue ONLY IF its field carries no void/superseded marker (IS VOID, SUPERSEDED, overwritten here) and the surviving sentence is phrased as a standing direction. A naive string grep will flag every correctly-repaired record forever, and a later run trusting it would 're-fix' records that are already right -- or, worse, conclude the repair never landed. Same family as everything else in this file: a check that fails for the wrong reason is the mirror of a check that passes for one, and writing the principle down is not the same as encoding it.

A stale report cannot make it stale, cannot make it wrong, and cannot certify it either way. The stale-report bar exists to stop the desk acting on decayed TECHNICALS; the time stop has none. It is also the book's ONLY mechanical loss discipline (HARD RULE 5 forbids price stops) and prompt v10 states mechanical exits are NEVER throttled, with FOUR LAWS #2 adding that a cap never delays or blocks an exit. Blocking it is not the 'stricter' branch of the governance tie-breaker -- it is the removal of the only floor the equity book has.
_TIME_STOP_NEEDS_NO_REPORT_BUT_THE_RSI2_.half_two_the_rsi2_exit_does_depend_on_a_: The RSI2>=70 branch reads s['rsi2'], which a day-old report cannot certify. The obvious fix -- compute RSI2 live via get_equity_technical_indicators(type='rsi', period=2, interval='day') -- WORKS, but the two implementations are NOT the same number. Measured against the SAME 2026-09-02 close: MMM report 1.1 vs live 0.8236 (gap 0.28); GD report 1.9 vs live 1.9442 (gap 0.04); ROST report 83.2 vs live 73.1276 (gap 10.07).
_TIME_STOP_NEEDS_NO_REPORT_BUT_THE_RSI2_.the_asymmetry_and_why_it_is_mechanical: The agreement is excellent at the oversold extreme and poor at the overbought one. RSI is bounded [0,100] and a 2-period RSI pinned by two hard down closes collapses to ~0 under ANY smoothing convention, so competing implementations (Wilder vs simple averaging of gains/losses) cannot disagree there. They diverge where up and down closes mix -- the mid and upper range. CONSEQUENCE, and it inverts the intuition: the ENTRY screen (RSI2 < 10) sits in the region where the sources agree to a fraction of a point, and the EXIT trigger (RSI2 >= 70) sits in the region where they differ by ~10 points. A live RSI2 is a safe substitute for the screen and an UNSAFE one for the exit -- backwards from the assumption that an exit is the simpler call.
_TIME_STOP_NEEDS_NO_REPORT_BUT_THE_RSI2_.what_it_licenses_and_what_it_does_not: LICENSED: the first market-hours run may execute PNC's TIME STOP without waiting for the 14:15Z report -- re-quote >=5 min past 13:30Z per the opening-auction rule, confirm placed_agent 'agentic' against the broker, sell, notify Ryan ONCE with evidence. NOT LICENSED: treating a live RSI2 as interchangeable with the report's near the 70 line. Where a live reading lands within ~10 points of 70 and the report disagrees or is silent, WAIT for the fresh report rather than banking or declining off the substitute.
_TIME_STOP_NEEDS_NO_REPORT_BUT_THE_RSI2_.does_it_change_todays_decision: NO, and that is what makes it citable. ROST reads 73.13 live and 83.2 on the report -- both clear 70, so its take-profit fires on either source and the 10-point gap is not load-bearing today. PNC's time stop needs no RSI2 whatsoever. The finding is recorded on a run where it licenses nothing, which is the only condition under which a measurement of the desk's own inputs is credible.
_TIME_STOP_NEEDS_NO_REPORT_BUT_THE_RSI2_.honest_scope: n=3, and only ONE observation sits in the overbought region. Do NOT carry forward '~10 points' as the typical overbought gap -- that is a single measurement. What IS established: the two sources are demonstrably not interchangeable at the threshold that decides an exit, while being interchangeable at the one that decides an entry. Re-measure before leaning on either.
_TIME_STOP_NEEDS_NO_REPORT_BUT_THE_RSI2_.family: Same shape as this file's most-repeated defect -- a check that passes for the wrong reason. A run that substitutes the live RSI2 and finds it above 70 would report 'exit confirmed against a live technical' and be right by luck; the same substitution on a name reading report-72 would silently decline an exit the policy fires.
_TIME_STOP_NEEDS_NO_REPORT_BUT_THE_RSI2_.GAP_SIZED_WITH_DATA_2026-09-09T14-15Z: The key above reasons about 'the ~45 minutes between the bell and the report landing' from a single day's observation. MEASURED over the last 11 trading days via the GitHub commit API (08-24..09-09, Labor Day 09-07 excluded), first report of ANY kind on master per day: 13:56, 13:55, 13:59, 14:01, 15:01, 14:02, 14:02, 14:02, 14:01, 14:02, 14:01Z -- ten of eleven land 25-32 min after the 13:30Z bell, so the routine gap is ~30 min, not 45. THE OUTLIER IS THE POINT: on 2026-08-28 the first report of the session was an INTRADAY at 15:01Z, 91 minutes after the bell, and that day's MORNING report did not land until 22:59Z -- almost three hours AFTER the close. So the morning job can fail for an entire session while intraday fires normally. CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST DRAFT, recorded because the overclaim is the instructive part: I initially read 08-28 as 'no report all session' from latest_morning.md alone and was about to write that down; checking latest_intraday.md in the same window refuted it. Same shape as the file's standing rule -- measure before you remediate, and one file is not the session's report history. WHAT IT ADDS: the delay a report-gated time stop would have cost is bounded by DATA at ~30 min typical / 91 min worst-observed, with no upper bound in principle since the dispatch is an external cron. It does not change the key's conclusion (the time stop reads no market data, so it is not report-gated at all) -- it sizes the cost of getting that conclusion wrong. _OPENING_AUCTION_RULE_APPLIES_TO_EXITS_T.the_mechanism_which_is_the_transferable_: The rule was written in the record as an ENTRY-side price-protection rule (opening auction prints are wide and non-informative). It is symmetric: an exit priced off the same wide auction leg sells low or buys high just as an entry does. The rule's stated purpose in _current_state and CLAUDE.md is 'never PRICE a decision off the opening auction print' -- 'price a decision' covers both sides. A run that reads the rule as entry-only will fire an exit inside the window and collect the artifact.
_OPENING_AUCTION_RULE_APPLIES_TO_EXITS_T.does_it_change_the_decision_to_have_sold: NO. Both exits fire mechanically the moment the market opens: the time stop is calendar-only (15d >= 14d) and the RSI2>=70 print is on yesterday's completed close -- neither is a function of the intraday tape. The rule is about WHEN to price, not WHETHER to trade. Fill quality is the whole cost measured here.
_OPENING_AUCTION_RULE_APPLIES_TO_EXITS_T.the_correction_for_the_next_run: Any run that executes ANY mechanical order (entry OR exit) inside the first 5 minutes past 13:30Z should re-quote and re-check between minutes 5 and 10 unless the position or the sizing would materially decay in that window. For a mechanical exit off yesterday's close there is no such decay -- the rule binds. NOT LICENSED: waiting past the opening window to hunt for a better price -- that is timing the exit, which HARD RULE 5 forbids in reverse. Wait to price honestly, then execute; never wait to price favourably.
_OPENING_AUCTION_RULE_APPLIES_TO_EXITS_T.why_it_survived_previously: The rule was written into every position's _current_state as 'the executing run must re-quote at least ~5 min after 13:30Z per the opening-auction rule' -- clear enough. The failure mode was two runs racing: the 13:33Z run saw the trigger, fetched a live quote (>0Z past bell), and fired. From its own vantage it was following the letter of a rule ('a live quote was taken'); it missed the '>=5 min' clause. Second occurrence of this file's most-repeated defect this session, arriving on an execution instead of a filter -- a check that passes for the wrong reason.
_OPENING_AUCTION_RULE_APPLIES_TO_EXITS_T.honest_scope: n=2, both fills in one collision. The magnitudes are small (-$3.76 = 0.09% of total account value) and one leg (ROST) barely mattered. The finding is that the RULE binds symmetrically, not that the sibling was reckless -- both runs correctly waited on the auction, and one just waited less.

_NO_DENOMINATOR_EXISTS_IN_THE_FIRST_THIR.status: DURABLE. The SYMMETRIC SIBLING of _CLOSING_WINDOW_IS_FORTY_MINUTES_NOT_TWENTY, and a FIFTH denominator mode that is different in KIND from the other four. Read with _PARTICIPATION_IS_A_VETO_NOT_A_GREEN_LIGHT and the 2026-08-26 arc capstone.
_NO_DENOMINATOR_EXISTS_IN_THE_FIRST_THIR.claim: The four known denominator defects are all MIS-CALIBRATIONS -- a baseline that is too strict (session-average inflated by the opening hour, 08-25; trailing window inflated by an event flush, 08-28), too easy (trailing-local drained in a decaying tape, 08-26; closing-auction flow in absolute terms, 08-27/08-28). This one is an ABSENCE. In roughly the first 20-30 minutes of a session there is NO ADMISSIBLE DENOMINATOR AT ALL, because every baseline the clause could use is either the opening auction itself -- which this file's own rules forbid as a denominator -- or the candidate bars being tested, which is circular. A clause with no denominator is not strict or lenient; it is UNEVALUABLE, and an unevaluable confirmation clause means the break is UNCONFIRMED, which means no trade.

_THE_SWING_BOOK_IS_ONE_LOW_BETA_BET_EXPR.the_mechanism_and_it_is_the_transferable: Connors RSI2 selects the most oversold names in a universe. In a persistent melt-up the oversold set IS the funding source for the rally -- the money buying the index is coming OUT of exactly these names. So the screen assembles a short-the-rotation book without ever DECIDING to take that bet, and it does so one name at a time, each of which passes its own gate cleanly. This is the book-level form of _THE_RSI2_SCREEN_IS_BLIND_TO_THE_BOOK: that key found the screen cannot see what is already held; this one finds that even a perfectly diversified-by-sector set of its picks is a single factor exposure.
_THE_SWING_BOOK_IS_ONE_LOW_BETA_BET_EXPR.what_it_does_NOT_license_and_this_is_loa: IT IS NOT A SELL SIGNAL AND MUST NEVER BE READ AS ONE. HARD RULE 5 permits an equity sale on exactly three things -- the RSI2>=70 cross while green, the 14-day time stop, and a HARD RULE 7 thesis break. Relative underperformance is none of them, and the whole point of the no-price-stop policy is that an underwater swing with an intact thesis is HELD. The 14-day time stop is already the mechanism that recycles these if they stall (LLY 09-10, MDLZ 09-11, MMM 09-14, GD 09-15). A run that reads this key as authority to liquidate has inverted it.
_THE_SWING_BOOK_IS_ONE_LOW_BETA_BET_EXPR.what_it_DOES_bear_on: The ENTRY side, and it tightens rather than loosens: adding a FIFTH name off the same oversold screen adds correlated exposure the per-name cap cannot see. Today's three candidates all show the same signature on the same tape -- AMAT -0.77%, LRCX +0.11%, RTX +0.29% against SPY +1.15% / QQQ +1.35%. That is corroboration of the existing B/B+ grades, not a new veto. THE_SECOND_FINDING_a_news_articles_perce.what_happened: The 13:47 ET Benzinga market wrap -- a good, specific, correctly-attributed piece -- recorded 'Hewlett Packard Enterprise dropped 4.5% after its results fell short.' THE_SECOND_FINDING_a_news_articles_perce.why_it_is_a_new_sub_class: This file already forbids inheriting a mid-event DIRECTIONAL READ (2026-08-28, the Warsh keynote, where every leg of a cross-asset tell flipped in ten minutes) and already has a four-instance family of 'a modelled estimate is never a substitute for a quote' (spot price, ATM strike, wrong expiry board, modelled premium). This is neither. The number was not modelled and not stale-by-inheritance from another run -- it was PUBLISHED, by a human, with attribution and a timestamp, which is exactly what makes it read as authoritative rather than as provisional.
THE_SECOND_FINDING_a_news_articles_perce.the_detector: Re-quote every percentage taken from an article before it enters a grade. The article's own published_at is the tell: a market-wrap percentage is a snapshot of the moment it was written, and an intraday session routinely moves several points past it. Cite the article for the WHY (what management guided, what the analyst said) and the broker for the WHAT (where the stock actually is). Those are different questions and the article is only authoritative on the first.
THE_SECOND_FINDING_a_news_articles_perce.honest_scope: This changed no decision -- AMAT was declined on the reporters-vs-non-reporters split, which holds with or without HPE (2 reporters at -6.87% vs 7 non-reporters at +0.62%). _THIS_WEEKS_ENTRIES_PREDATE_THE_SIZING_P.WHY_IT_MATTERS_the_in_regime_gate_bites_: The calibration duty may only tune a parameter on trades that closed UNDER IT, and after any parameter change that parameter's evidence RESETS TO ZERO. A calibration run that reaches for the live book's 53-close history to tune the new sizing or time-stop numbers is committing the exact bug calibrate.py caught on its own first run -- tuning a parameter on data that predates it, which is superstition and is indistinguishable from real calibration unless you count.
_THIS_WEEKS_ENTRIES_PREDATE_THE_SIZING_P.THE_ONE_BRANCH_THAT_MAY_STILL_FIRE: The KILL branch is EXEMPT from the in-regime gate by design -- risk-off never waits for a clean sample. _A_VERIFIED_MACRO_FIGURE_WAS_WRONG_BY_AN.headline: The August Employment Situation printed at 12:30Z today: NONFARM PAYROLLS +162,000 vs a Dow Jones consensus of +53,000, UNEMPLOYMENT 4.1% STEADY, July revised UP to +21,000, strongest monthly gain since March. The 2026-09-03T17:50Z key _NFP_IS_INSIDE_EVERY_TACTICAL_WINDOW_OPENED_TODAY recorded the expectation as 'consensus ~475k vs 235k prior, u-rate 5.1% vs 5.2%' -- WRONG BY ROUGHLY AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE ON PAYROLLS AND A FULL POINT ON THE UNEMPLOYMENT RATE. A run inheriting those numbers reads 162k against a remembered 475k as a CATASTROPHIC MISS; against the real 53k it is a 3x BEAT. THE SIGN OF THE SURPRISE INVERTS, which is the single input a post-print regime label is built from.

_A_VERIFIED_MACRO_FIGURE_WAS_WRONG_BY_AN.why_it_survived_and_this_is_the_transfer: THE 09-03 KEY LABELLED ITSELF 'VERIFIED, not assumed' AND CITED THREE SOURCES. That provenance line is exactly what invites the next run to trust it without re-checking -- a confidently-sourced wrong number is more dangerous than an admittedly-uncertain one, which is this file's standing rule that a bullet asserting a hard figure deserves MORE scrutiny, not less. Worse, NOTHING COULD HAVE FLAGGED IT: the 09-03 conclusion (TACTICAL barred into an unresolved print) depended ONLY on the print's TIMING, not on its expected magnitude, so the finding was RIGHT for reasons entirely independent of the numbers it got wrong. A check that passes for the wrong reason -- this file's most-repeated defect -- here arriving as a correct conclusion resting on fabricated inputs.
_A_VERIFIED_MACRO_FIGURE_WAS_WRONG_BY_AN.detector: A macro consensus figure is load-bearing ONLY at the moment the print lands, and that is the moment nobody re-derives it. RE-QUOTE THE CONSENSUS FROM A LIVE SOURCE AT PRINT TIME, never from an inherited watchpoint -- the surprise is actual-minus-consensus and an inherited consensus silently sets the sign. Cheap sanity check that would have caught this one for free: 2026 NFP has been running 20-160k all year, so a '475k consensus' is outside the plausible range of the series and a 5.1% u-rate contradicts the 4.1% that has been printing. AN OUT-OF-RANGE MACRO FIGURE IS A MEASUREMENT BUG UNTIL A PRIMARY SOURCE SAYS OTHERWISE.

_QUOTE_FEED_LAG_MEANS_WALL_CLOCK_CANNOT_.status: DURABLE. Corrects the REMEDY of the 2026-08-21T13:32Z opening-print rule, not its diagnosis.
_QUOTE_FEED_LAG_MEANS_WALL_CLOCK_CANNOT_.headline: THE STANDING FIX -- 'RE-QUOTE AT LEAST ~5 MINUTES AFTER 13:30Z' -- IS CALIBRATED ON WALL-CLOCK TIME, BUT THE ARTIFACT IT GUARDS AGAINST IS A PROPERTY OF THE DATA'S VENUE TIMESTAMP. THE CONNECTOR'S QUOTE FEED LAGS WALL CLOCK BY AN AMOUNT THAT IS NEITHER ZERO NOR CONSTANT, SO WAITING FIVE MINUTES AND RE-QUOTING RETURNED A PRINT FROM INSIDE THE OPENING AUCTION WINDOW -- TWICE.

measurement.fetch_A: wall clock ~13:37:00Z -> SPY venue_last_trade_time 13:31:40.523Z. Lag ~5.4 min.
measurement.fetch_B: wall clock ~13:42:00Z -> SPY venue_last_trade_time 13:33:40.248Z. Lag ~8.3 min.
measurement.the_damning_ratio: Between the two fetches wall clock advanced ~5.0 min while venue time advanced 2.0 min -- the feed progressed at ~40% of real time, i.e. it FELL FURTHER BEHIND. Re-fetching is therefore not guaranteed to walk you out of the opening window; it can walk you deeper into the lag.
measurement.uniform_across_symbols: All 8 symbols in fetch A carried 13:31:34-13:31:40Z venue times (SPY, QQQ, LLY, MDLZ, MMM, GD, NVDA, XLF). A single lagged symbol would be a per-instrument quirk; eight at one timestamp is the feed.
measurement.materiality: Not cosmetic. MMM marked 167.92 in fetch A and 167.5504 in fetch B -- -0.37, -0.22% -- and GD 361.2199 -> 361.295. Position marks and any percentage computed off them move between two reads that a wall-clock rule would call equally settled.

_QUOTE_FEED_LAG_MEANS_WALL_CLOCK_CANNOT_.the_detector: READ venue_last_trade_time ON THE QUOTE, NOT YOUR OWN CLOCK. A print is settled when its VENUE timestamp is at/after ~13:35Z, regardless of when you fetched it. If the venue timestamp is still inside the opening window, the quote is provisional no matter how long you waited -- re-fetch and CHECK AGAIN rather than assuming the wait did it. The same applies to get_option_quotes, which returns quote.updated_at (the SPY 700P hedge read updated_at 13:31:41.8Z in fetch A).
_QUOTE_FEED_LAG_MEANS_WALL_CLOCK_CANNOT_.why_it_survived: This file's most-repeated shape: a check that passes for the wrong reason. A run that waits past 13:35Z and re-quotes has followed the 2026-08-21 rule to the letter, reports 'settled numbers', and is holding opening-auction prints. Nothing errors. The 2026-08-21 incident itself was diagnosed correctly -- an opening print flipped the SIGN of a P/L reported to Ryan -- and the remedy was simply written in the wrong units.
_QUOTE_FEED_LAG_MEANS_WALL_CLOCK_CANNOT_.honest_scope: n=2 fetches on ONE morning, one symbol set. This may be opening-window congestion that clears later in the session rather than a standing property of the feed, and a caching layer in the connector would produce the same signature. Do NOT generalize it into 'the feed is always ~8 minutes late'. The DETECTOR is the durable half and costs nothing: the venue timestamp is returned on every quote already. A later run should re-measure the lag mid-session and record whether it decays.
_QUOTE_FEED_LAG_MEANS_WALL_CLOCK_CANNOT_.changed_no_decision: Correct by the file's own standard for an input audit. No trade was placeable in either book this run -- the equity report on master is stale so signal-sourced trades are barred, and no options trigger existed 7 minutes into the session. Both fetches agree that all four swings are underwater, so the RSI2>=70 take-profit was unavailable on either read.

_THE_CONFIRMATION_CLAUSE_IS_UNREADABLE_A.headline: THE DENOMINATOR ARC HAS A FOURTH WINDOW AND IT IS THE MIRROR OF THE CLOSING ONE: FOR ROUGHLY THE FIRST HALF HOUR, BOTH KNOWN BASELINE DEFECTS ARE LIVE AT THE SAME TIME, SO A VOLUME-CONFIRMATION RATIO COMPUTED AT THE OPEN CARRIES NO INFORMATION IN EITHER DIRECTION.
_THE_CONFIRMATION_CLAUSE_IS_UNREADABLE_A.the_measurement: QQQ 1-minute volume, 2026-09-04 13:30-13:36Z: 208,349 / 104,828 / 80,496 / 53,068 / 38,854 / 77,491 / 35,781. The first bar is 5.8x the seventh, and the decay is monotonic apart from one 13:35 uptick.
_THE_CONFIRMATION_CLAUSE_IS_UNREADABLE_A.why_both_defects_are_live_simultaneously: The 2026-08-25 finding says a SESSION-AVERAGE denominator is too STRICT because the opening hour inflates it. The 2026-08-26 finding says a TRAILING-LOCAL denominator is too EASY in a decaying tape because it tracks participation downward. At the open, the session average does not meaningfully exist yet (it IS the opening bars, so a candidate bar is measured against the auction it is decaying away from), AND the trailing-local mean is collapsing at ~5.8x per six minutes -- the fastest decay any window in this file exhibits. There is no third window to fall back on: the pre-event baseline the 2026-08-28 post-flush correction prescribes requires a quiet stretch of THIS session, and at 13:36Z none has occurred yet.
_THE_CONFIRMATION_CLAUSE_IS_UNREADABLE_A.the_symmetry_that_makes_it_a_rule_rather: The 2026-08-27T19:45Z finding established that the clause is structurally unreadable in the last ~20 minutes because closing-auction flow inflates every bar for reasons unrelated to information. This is the same fact at the other end of the session, driven by the same mechanism (auction flow), and it points the same way: DO NOT let a confirmation ratio decide a TACTICAL entry inside roughly the first 30 minutes. Wait for a stretch of ordinary two-sided trade to exist before asking whether participation 'arrived'.
_THE_CONFIRMATION_CLAUSE_IS_UNREADABLE_A.what_it_does_NOT_say: It does NOT bar trading in the opening window, and it must not be read as widening or narrowing any threshold. It says one specific input -- the volume RATIO -- is uninformative there, so a trigger must stand on its PRICE and STRUCTURE clauses alone in that window, which in practice means it should wait. It is also NOT the same claim as the 2026-09-01 opening-window SLIPPAGE finding (that one is about fill quality on equity entries; this one is about whether an options trigger can be confirmed at all).
_THE_CONFIRMATION_CLAUSE_IS_UNREADABLE_A.honest_scope_it_changed_no_decision: The TACTICAL track was declined this run for a reason that never reached the volume clause: NO LEVEL WAS BREAKING. QQQ closed 09-03 four cents from its 20-day SMA (717.67 vs 717.7140), then GAPPED OVER it -- 13:30Z open 719.41, session low 718.525 -- and never traded down to it. SPY sat flat in a 0.99-point range 3.2 points above its own 20-day. So no ratio was load-bearing, which is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly. Recorded per the standing rule that an audit is creditable precisely when it does not license the trade.
_THE_CONFIRMATION_CLAUSE_IS_UNREADABLE_A.detector: Before letting any volume ratio confirm a break, ask whether the session yet contains a stretch of ORDINARY participation to serve as the denominator. If every available baseline is either the auction itself or a window still decaying away from it, report the ABSOLUTE volume and state that the ratio is unreadable -- do not pick whichever denominator is available and treat its answer as a verdict.

_FEED_LAG_IS_PER_SESSION_NOT_FEED_WIDE.status: DURABLE QUALIFIER on _QUOTE_FEED_LAG_MEANS_WALL_CLOCK_CANNOT_CLEAR_THE_OPENING_WINDOW (13:42Z, same session-day). It STRENGTHENS that finding's detector and CORRECTS its implied model. Read the two together; neither is complete alone.
_FEED_LAG_IS_PER_SESSION_NOT_FEED_WIDE.headline: TWO CONCURRENT RUNS QUOTED THE SAME EIGHT SYMBOLS ~50 SECONDS APART AND GOT VENUE TIMESTAMPS 4.5 MINUTES APART -- WITH THE *EARLIER* FETCH RETURNING THE *FRESHER* DATA. A FEED-WIDE LAG CANNOT DO THAT. THE STALENESS IS A PROPERTY OF THE CONNECTION SERVING YOU, NOT OF THE FEED AT A GIVEN MOMENT.

the_measurement.run_13_42Z_fetch_A: wall ~13:37:00Z -> all eight symbols at venue 13:31:34-13:31:40Z. LAG ~5.4 MINUTES.
the_measurement.the_contradiction: The 13:36:10Z fetch is ~50 seconds EARLIER in wall clock than the 13:37:00Z fetch, yet its data is ~4.5 minutes NEWER. Under a feed-wide lag model, venue time is a monotonic function of wall clock shared by all consumers, so a later fetch can never be staler. It was.
the_measurement.both_were_internally_consistent: Each run saw ALL EIGHT of its symbols carrying one coherent timestamp cluster -- which is exactly why the 13:42Z run correctly ruled out a per-instrument quirk and concluded 'eight at one timestamp is the feed'. That inference is sound about the SCOPE (connection-wide, not per-symbol) and wrong only about the LEVEL (connection, not global).

_FEED_LAG_IS_PER_SESSION_NOT_FEED_WIDE.why_this_matters_more_than_it_looks: The 13:42Z finding's remedy is 'a print is settled when its VENUE timestamp is at/after ~13:35Z, regardless of when you fetched it.' That remedy is CORRECT AND SURVIVES INTACT. What does not survive is any inference from one run's lag to another's -- a run must never conclude 'the feed was lagging at 13:37Z today, so my 13:36Z read was also stale', nor the reverse. Staleness is not a shared property of the clock; it is a property of YOUR quote, and only your own venue timestamp can establish it.
_FEED_LAG_IS_PER_SESSION_NOT_FEED_WIDE.consequence_for_marking_the_book: Three marks for MMM exist within six minutes of one session's open -- 168.00 (venue 13:36:09Z), 167.92 and 167.5504 (venue ~13:31:40Z and ~13:33:40Z). They differ by up to 0.45 (-0.27%). When two runs' marks disagree, DO NOT average them and do NOT prefer the later fetch: prefer the quote with the LATER VENUE TIMESTAMP, which may well be the earlier call.
_FEED_LAG_IS_PER_SESSION_NOT_FEED_WIDE.honest_scope: n=1 collision, two sessions. It CHANGED NO DECISION -- neither run traded (broker re-read at 13:45Z, both order endpoints empty), and both declined both books on grounds that never touched a quote's freshness. That is the only condition under which a data-integrity audit is creditable. The mechanism is NOT established: two sessions hitting different upstream replicas, a per-session cache warming at different rates, and connection-level throttling all fit the observation equally, and this run did not distinguish them. What IS established is the negative claim, which is the useful half: the lag is not a single global quantity, so it cannot be inherited between runs.
_FEED_LAG_IS_PER_SESSION_NOT_FEED_WIDE.detector: Read venue_last_trade_time ON YOUR OWN QUOTE, every time, and treat any print whose venue timestamp sits inside the opening window as provisional no matter how long you waited or what a sibling run observed. If a concurrent run's marks disagree with yours, compare VENUE timestamps rather than fetch times before deciding whose number is real.
_FEED_LAG_IS_PER_SESSION_NOT_FEED_WIDE.family: Fifth member of this file's 'a check that passes for the wrong reason' set applied to measurement infrastructure, after the 5-minute-bucket holes, the 1-minute revisions, the cross-symbol hole signature, and the direction rule. Same shape as the 2026-08-26 correction to the 1-minute arbiter: a rule written to stop trusting a convenient number replaced it with a different convenient number -- here, another run's freshness observation -- and treated that one as authoritative.

_QUOTE_FEED_LAG_READ_THIS_QUALIFIER_FIRS: _FEED_LAG_IS_PER_SESSION_NOT_FEED_WIDE corrects the implied model of _QUOTE_FEED_LAG_MEANS_WALL_CLOCK_CANNOT_CLEAR_THE_OPENING_WINDOW. The detector in that key stands; the phrase 'the feed' in it should be read as 'this connection'.

_THE_ERN_FLAG_IS_FORWARD_ONLY_AND_THE_RS.status: DURABLE, NEW. A structural gap in the [ERN] rule, found by the first run to grade the 2026-09-04T14:02Z report. It CHANGED THIS RUN'S DECISION -- so it is not an audit taken on a quiet day, and the honest-scope note at the bottom applies.
_THE_ERN_FLAG_IS_FORWARD_ONLY_AND_THE_RS.headline: THE [ERN <date>] BAR IS PURELY FORWARD-LOOKING -- IT ASKS WHETHER A PRINT FALLS INSIDE THE HOLD WINDOW AND IS SILENT ON A NAME THAT PRINTED LAST NIGHT. _THE_ERN_FLAG_IS_FORWARD_ONLY_AND_THE_RS.the_general_rule_and_it_is_the_transfera: The [ERN] rule's stated mechanism is 'a swing straddles a binary event the entry has no edge on, and policy forbids the stop that could protect the gap.' That mechanism has a SIBLING the rule never named: an entry taken IMMEDIATELY AFTER the same binary event, where the desk has no more edge than it would have had before, and where the oversold reading it is acting on is a mechanical artifact of the event rather than a signal. Same event, same absent edge, opposite side of the print. The flag protects against a gap you would HOLD THROUGH; it does nothing about a gap you would BUY INTO.
_THE_ERN_FLAG_IS_FORWARD_ONLY_AND_THE_RS.why_it_matters_MORE_under_the_new_sizing: The 2026-09-02 concentration policy raised the per-name cap to 30% of account value and made [ERN] an ABSOLUTE bar precisely because 'one overnight gap through a print is a ~4-5% account hit' with no price stop. Buying INTO a fresh negative re-rating at that size carries the same exposure to the same event -- the position simply starts on the far side of it. A rule tightened to an absolute bar on one side of a print should not be advisory-to-absent on the other.
_THE_ERN_FLAG_IS_FORWARD_ONLY_AND_THE_RS.THE_DETECTOR_and_it_costs_one_call: Before entering ANY RSI2 name, run get_earnings_calendar with a NEGATIVE days window (a LOOK-BACK) as well as the forward one. A report entry dated within the last 1-2 sessions with verified:true and a non-null eps.actual means the oversold print is an event artifact -- DECLINE. One call covers the whole screen at once, because the calendar is market-wide rather than per-ticker. The report's Earnings column cannot supply this: it is built from the forward calendar by design and was correctly blank.
_THE_ERN_FLAG_IS_FORWARD_ONLY_AND_THE_RS.the_corollary_that_keeps_it_from_becomin: It is a DEFERRAL, exactly like the forward [ERN] rule. A post-earnings name can become a perfectly good setup once the re-rating settles and the gap stops dominating the oscillator -- typically a few sessions, i.e. once RSI(2)'s two-bar window no longer contains the gap. What it cannot be is a MEAN-REVERSION setup on the day of the gap. Re-grade from scratch on post-event numbers; never carry the pre-event grade forward and never carry the deferral forward as though it were a thesis judgment.
_THE_ERN_FLAG_IS_FORWARD_ONLY_AND_THE_RS.honest_scope: n=1, and this one changed the decision -- which is the condition under which this file's own standard says a finding is LEAST credible. Two things carry it anyway. First, the mechanism is STRUCTURAL rather than statistical: RSI(2) is a two-period oscillator and a large gap saturates it arithmetically, so no sample size is needed to establish that a fresh gap produces a low RSI2 print. Second, the earnings date is VERIFIED from the broker's own calendar (verified:true, eps.actual populated), not inferred from the price move. What is NOT established is how often this occurs -- nobody has measured what share of RSI2 screen names printed within the prior two sessions, and a future run could compute it cheaply from the same look-back call.
_THE_ERN_FLAG_IS_FORWARD_ONLY_AND_THE_RS.what_this_does_NOT_change: Nothing about the forward [ERN] rule, which stands in full as an absolute bar. Nothing about the report, which annotated PATH correctly. This ADDS a look-back leg to an existing check; it loosens no gate.

_THE_RAW_IV_RV_RATIO_HAS_A_SCHEDULED_JUM.what_to_actually_do: Quote the pair (raw + ex-gap) as the IV method already requires, and ADD the rolloff date when the artifact is large. For a contract EXPIRING BEFORE the next print, ex-gap is the honest gauge; for one SPANNING a print, raw is, because the buyer genuinely bears that gap. The rolloff schedule matters for a third case the pair does not cover: a CORE swing held 21-45 days will still be open when the denominator jumps, so a position entered on a 'cheap vol' raw reading can find that reading gone while nothing about the position changed.
_THE_RAW_IV_RV_RATIO_HAS_A_SCHEDULED_JUM.honest_scope: This does not say premium is cheap or rich anywhere -- and IV sanity is a NECESSARY condition that never supplies a thesis. It says the raw ratio contains a scheduled, arithmetic, direction-known move that is computable today, and that treating it as new information is a mistake with a date on it. Trimming the top return is itself a crude estimator that UNDERSTATES fat-tail risk; do not swap one headline number for another.

_INDEX_AGREEMENT_IS_DECIDABLE_BY_ONE_CON.headline: The TACTICAL index-agreement clause is a CAP-WEIGHTED test wearing a BREADTH test's clothes, and today one stock decided it. SPY -0.295% RED vs QQQ +0.176% GREEN read as 'the indices disagree, stand down' -- the exact reason the 14:16Z and 14:21Z runs gave. Measured across all eleven sector SPDRs, the indices AGREE: 8 of 11 red (XLY -1.382%, XLC -1.027%, XLF -0.974%, XLV -0.952%, XLE -0.890%, XLP -0.328%, XLB -0.038%, XLRE -0.011%) against 3 green (XLK +0.713%, XLI +0.475%, XLU +0.191%). QQQ ex-semis is negative and CONFIRMS SPY. The clause was reading NVDA, not the market.
_INDEX_AGREEMENT_IS_DECIDABLE_BY_ONE_CON.the_assumption_free_arithmetic: Do NOT reach for a weight table you have not measured -- INVERT instead. Solve w = index_change / constituent_change for the weight at which one name fully explains the index: QQQ +0.176% / NVDA +2.346% = 0.075. So IF NVDA's QQQ weight is at least 7.5%, NVDA ALONE accounts for the entirety of QQQ's gain. That is a threshold, not a claim about the weight, and it needs no external data. Corroborated independently by breadth: XLC and XLY -- the other mega-cap-growth sectors inside QQQ -- are the two WEAKEST of all eleven, so QQQ's green cannot be broad tech participation.
it_cuts_BOTH_ways_and_that_is_why_it_is_: WRONGLY BARS a trade (today's case): a run with a bearish SPY thesis sees QQQ green, calls it disagreement, and stands down -- while breadth was actually CONFIRMING the short. The clause vetoed on a reading its own premise did not support.

WRONGLY LICENSES one (the mirror, and the more expensive direction): a run sees QQQ green and calls it tech leadership, entering long into a tape where 8 of 11 sectors are being sold. A cap-weighted index can stay green through a broad de-rating for as long as one mega-cap holds.
_INDEX_AGREEMENT_IS_DECIDABLE_BY_ONE_CON.the_detector_and_it_costs_one_call: Quote the sector SPDRs alongside the two indices before letting index agreement decide anything (11 names exceeds the 10-symbol cap by one -- two calls, or drop XLRE). If the SECTOR COUNT disagrees with the INDEX SIGN, the index is being carried by WEIGHT, not BREADTH, and the agreement clause is measuring a constituent. Report the count with the index prints, never the index prints alone.
_INDEX_AGREEMENT_IS_DECIDABLE_BY_ONE_CON.the_transferable_shape: This file's most-repeated defect -- a check that passes for the wrong reason -- arriving inside the confirmation clause itself rather than inside its denominator. The volume-baseline arc (2026-08-25 through 08-28) fixed WHAT the confirmation was measured AGAINST, four separate times. Nobody had asked whether the AGREEMENT half of the same trigger measures what its name claims. A test whose inputs are cap-weighted cannot answer a question about participation, however carefully its thresholds are tuned.
_INDEX_AGREEMENT_IS_DECIDABLE_BY_ONE_CON.honest_scope_the_condition_under_which_t: IT CHANGED NO DECISION. No TACTICAL trigger existed to take either way: SPY sits +0.22% ABOVE its 20-day 769.2065 with no completed 5-minute close through the 770.76 session low, participation is decaying (14:15Z 110,999 / 14:20Z 137,911 / 14:25Z 90,597 against 419,012 on the opening bar), and it is a Friday, so the 2026-08-28 weekend-gap measurement applies -- the median Monday gap 0.342% exceeds the whole -30% stop distance. The correction removes a veto that was reached for the wrong reason and leaves the trade declined on the merits. A filter's inputs can only be audited credibly on a run where the audit does not license a trade.
_INDEX_AGREEMENT_IS_DECIDABLE_BY_ONE_CON.n_is_1: One session, one pair of indices. The MECHANISM is arithmetic and general; the FREQUENCY with which a single constituent flips the clause is unmeasured. Do not carry this forward as 'the agreement clause is broken' -- carry forward the detector.

_NFP_BAR_HAS_EXPIRED_THE_PRINT_IS_OUT.note: _NFP_IS_INSIDE_EVERY_TACTICAL_WINDOW_OPENED_TODAY was written 2026-09-03T17:50Z and barred TACTICAL for the rest of THAT session because the August payrolls print fell inside the track's hold window. _A_HOLED_BUCKET_DOES_NOT_HEAL.headline: 'Wait for settled bars' defends against REVISION, not against HOLES -- and the two defects have opposite age profiles. Measured this run: the three OLDEST 5-minute buckets in the window are holed on BOTH symbols and the four NEWEST are byte-exact, which is the inverse of what 'settling' implies.
_A_HOLED_BUCKET_DOES_NOT_HEAL.measurement: QQQ buckets vs their 1-minute sums: 14:10 -37.5%, 14:15 -36.9%, 14:20 -45.2%, then 14:25 / 14:30 / 14:35 / 14:40 all +0.0% EXACT. SPY, same three timestamps: -25.7%, -39.8%, -79.7%, then the same four clean at +0.0%. All six are BUCKET-holed by the 2026-08-28 direction rule (bucket materially BELOW its 1-minute sum = the bucket is the holed side).
_A_HOLED_BUCKET_DOES_NOT_HEAL.the_persistence_result_which_is_the_new_: The 14:21Z run had ALREADY flagged QQQ's 14:10Z bucket as defective. This run re-measured it 26 minutes later from an independent fetch and it is STILL -37.5%, with the identical shape. THE HOLE IS PERMANENT -- it does not backfill, and re-fetching does not repair it. That forecloses 'wait and re-fetch' as a hole remedy and leaves per-window reconciliation as the ONLY defence, at every bar age.
_A_HOLED_BUCKET_DOES_NOT_HEAL.why_it_matters_against_the_standing_dete: The 2026-08-26 detector prescribes '(b) End the trailing baseline ~10 minutes back from now rather than at the last printed bar, so the clause is computed only on settled bars.' That is correct FOR REVISIONS, where a recently-closed bar's values are still provisional. It gives ZERO protection against a hole, and today it would actively mislead: a run ending its baseline 10 minutes back would compute it on 14:10/14:15/14:20 -- all three holed -- while discarding the four clean buckets. Waiting for settlement here selects FOR the corrupt bars.
_A_HOLED_BUCKET_DOES_NOT_HEAL.second_new_element_contiguity: The holes arrived as a CONTIGUOUS BLOCK of three consecutive buckets, simultaneously on two symbols, then stopped cleanly. Every previously recorded instance was an ISOLATED bucket (2026-08-27 at :45 across three symbols; 2026-08-28 at :05, :05 and :20). A three-bucket run means 'reconcile the candidate bucket' is insufficient -- the entire baseline window can be holed at once, so RECONCILE EVERY BUCKET YOU INTEND TO AVERAGE, not just the one being tested.
_A_HOLED_BUCKET_DOES_NOT_HEAL.quantified_in_the_dangerous_direction: Trailing-6-bucket mean, 14:15-14:40: QQQ raw 173,814 vs corrected 196,576 (raw 11.6% LOW); SPY raw 93,262 vs corrected 121,822 (raw 23.4% LOW). This is the fourth distinct way this file has recorded a volume denominator being wrong, and like the others it depresses the denominator -- manufacturing the confirmation the clause exists to withhold.
_A_HOLED_BUCKET_DOES_NOT_HEAL.honest_scope: IT CHANGED NO DECISION. No trigger existed this run -- QQQ never traded through its 20-day, so no volume clause was load-bearing. That is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly. n is also small: one window, two symbols, one session; the contiguity result should not be generalized into a claim about how long outages typically run.
_A_HOLED_BUCKET_DOES_NOT_HEAL.transferable_shape: A detector written against one failure mode (revision) inherits an implied claim of coverage over a neighbouring mode (holes) that it never had. This file's most-repeated defect -- a check that passes for the wrong reason -- arriving as a remedy applied to the wrong disease.
_A_HOLED_BUCKET_DOES_NOT_HEAL.amended_2026-09-04T16:20Z_PERSISTENCE_IS: THIS KEY'S HEADLINE ('THE HOLE IS PERMANENT -- it does not backfill') AND _A_FEED_HOLE_BACKFILLS_SO_AN_INHERITED_HOLE_FIGURE_IS_STALE'S HEADLINE ('a feed hole BACK-FILLS over time') FLATLY CONTRADICT EACH OTHER, AND A RUN GREPPING THE LEDGER INHERITS WHICHEVER IT HITS FIRST. Measured free this run from bars fetched for the routine TACTICAL check, and the contradiction resolves as BOTH-TRUE-OF-DIFFERENT-BUCKETS: the 15:30Z bucket, recorded holed by the 16:05Z run from a 16:03Z fetch, was re-fetched at 16:20Z and is BYTE-IDENTICAL on both symbols -- SPY 9,184 and QQQ 4,832, unchanged, 50 minutes after the bar closed and 17 minutes after the prior reading; the 1-minute sums are unchanged too (SPY 88,928, QQQ 112,008), so the bucket is still -89.7% / -95.7%. STATIC. Against that, the 15:47Z key measured QQQ's 15:10Z bucket revising 21,643 -> 54,428 (+151%) over 12 minutes. Same session, same feed, opposite behaviour. THE FORM DOES NOT PREDICT IT EITHER, which kills the obvious hypothesis: the two static instances are QQQ 14:10Z (a PARTIAL hole, -37.5%, static over 26 min) and the 15:30Z pair (WHOLE-BAR substitutions, static over 17 min), while the one back-filling instance, QQQ 15:10Z, is also PARTIAL. Partial holes appear in both camps. SO: n=4 buckets, no observable feature yet predicts whether a hole heals, and NEITHER headline may be relied on. This costs nothing operationally because both keys already prescribe the same defence and it is the only one that works under either behaviour: NEVER inherit a predecessor's hole figure, NEVER treat a re-fetch as the correction, and reconcile every bucket you intend to use against the 1-minute series. The measurement changed no decision -- no volume clause was load-bearing this run (TACTICAL was declined on late-entry arithmetic, not on volume).

_BOOK_CORRELATION_MEASURED_THE_FOUR_HOLD.headline: MEASURED AND REFUTED: the desk's own entry-gate reasoning has been calling this book a repeated bet on one low-beta defensive/income factor. It is not. Mean PAIRWISE daily-return correlation among LLY/MDLZ/MMM/GD over 33 sessions is 0.143, and mean correlation to SPY is 0.022 -- essentially independent.
_BOOK_CORRELATION_MEASURED_THE_FOUR_HOLD.matrix_33_sessions_0721_to_0903: LLY-MDLZ 0.24 | LLY-MMM 0.25 | LLY-GD 0.16 | MDLZ-MMM 0.03 | MDLZ-GD -0.09 | MMM-GD 0.28. To SPY: LLY -0.22, MDLZ -0.28, MMM +0.39, GD +0.20.
_BOOK_CORRELATION_MEASURED_THE_FOUR_HOLD.todays_confirmation: On a session where SPY is -0.48%, the four holdings printed LLY -1.40%, MDLZ +0.03%, MMM +0.29%, GD -1.95% -- a 2.24-point spread. Four names moving that differently on one tape are not one factor.
_BOOK_CORRELATION_MEASURED_THE_FOUR_HOLD.the_error_this_corrects: The 2026-09-04T14:32Z run declined PM as 'a FIFTH expression of the low-beta defensive/income factor the book already holds four times'. The DECLINE is correct and stands, but that particular support for it is not: nobody had measured whether the four actually co-move. They are all RED SIMULTANEOUSLY, which LOOKS like a common factor and is the thing that was reasoned from -- but simultaneous drawdown is not correlation. The correct diagnosis of -3.13% is four independent entries each modestly underwater (mistimed entries), NOT one factor breaking. Those two diagnoses imply opposite actions: a broken factor argues for reducing the whole book, mistimed entries argue for leaving sound theses alone to work.
_BOOK_CORRELATION_MEASURED_THE_FOUR_HOLD.why_it_changed_no_decision_today: PM stays declined on the CLEANEST ground available and one that does not depend on the factor claim at all: it was graded B+, and the concentration policy says a B-grade gets NO position rather than a small one. A measurement is only credible when reported on a run where it does not license the trade the desk would like to make -- this one does not.
_BOOK_CORRELATION_MEASURED_THE_FOUR_HOLD.consequence_for_the_rotation_gate: The capital policy defines 'weakest' as weakest on the ENTRY STACK, never the biggest loser. This measurement is the arithmetic reason that distinction bites here: with pairwise correlation 0.143 the four drawdowns carry almost no common information, so ranking them by P/L would be ranking them by four unrelated pieces of noise. GD is the biggest loser (-4.20%) and has the STRONGEST fresh evidence of the four.
_BOOK_CORRELATION_MEASURED_THE_FOUR_HOLD.honest_limits: 33 daily observations is a short window and correlations rise in a real risk-off event -- these are calm-tape readings and should not be quoted as a crisis estimate. The claim is narrow: on the evidence available, the four are not a single factor bet, and no run should assert that they are without re-measuring.

_THE_ENTRY_BAR_NOW_SCALES_WITH_THE_SLOT_.headline: A consequence of Ryan's 2026-09-02 concentration policy that no run has yet stated: the entry bar is no longer fixed, it SCALES WITH THE SIZE THE SLOT WOULD COMMAND. The same name can be a reasonable entry under the old band and a bad one now, with no change in the name.
_THE_ENTRY_BAR_NOW_SCALES_WITH_THE_SLOT_.the_arithmetic: The four current positions were entered under the OLD $400-500 band and are each ~$484 -- 12.4% to 12.8% of the account, and all four are BELOW the new ~$600 minimum entry. The next entry, sized per policy (deployable / remaining slots, capped at 30%), is $1,155-1,267: roughly 2.6x any position now held, and instantly the book's dominant holding.
_THE_ENTRY_BAR_NOW_SCALES_WITH_THE_SLOT_.what_it_means_in_practice: PATH is the worked example. As a ~$460 entry under the old band it was a marginal-but-arguable speculative AI-software swing. As a ~$1,155 entry it would put 30% of the account into a $15 small-cap with a 12.1% stop distance -- obviously not A-grade for a dominant position. The name did not change; the slot did. This is exactly the 'FEWER MUST MEAN MORE SELECTIVE, NEVER MERELY BIGGER' clause operationalized, and it is the clause the policy itself flags as load-bearing and easy to lose.
_THE_ENTRY_BAR_NOW_SCALES_WITH_THE_SLOT_.the_trap_it_guards_against: The inverse error is the tempting one: a desk sitting on $1,266.73 of idle cash next to four sub-minimum positions feels UNDER-deployed and reaches for the best available name to fill the slot. Full deployment raises the cost of a bad entry; it does not lower the bar for one. Idle cash is the residual of quality and being flat is a correct state.
_THE_ENTRY_BAR_NOW_SCALES_WITH_THE_SLOT_.note_on_the_current_book: The book's shape -- four small, equally-weighted positions -- is precisely what the 09-02 change was written to move away from. Nothing is to be DONE about that directly: HARD RULE 5 permits no exit here, and selling a sound thesis to re-size is churn. The four will resolve on their own exits (time stops 09-10 through 09-15) and the capital will re-deploy under the new policy then.

_A_RISING_200DAY_CAN_BE_A_WINDOW_ARTIFAC.the_detector: Measure the 200-day cushion in SESSIONS, not in percent: sessions_to_cross = (spot - sma200) / sma200_slope_per_day. LIN: price 481.37 live vs SMA200 480.1777 = +0.42%; SMA200 RISING +1.134% over 20 sessions, but SMA50 FALLING -1.94% and price -4.02% BELOW it; drawdown -11.79% from the 546.64 high of 2026-07-02; 12mo +0.91%, 12-1 +2.76%. _SECTOR_RELATIVE_MOMENTUM_SEPARATES_A_DI.the_detector: Before grading any RSI2 candidate, quote its 12-month and 12-1 return against its SECTOR ETF over the same window, and check the SMA50 slope alongside the SMA200 slope. A name whose 200-day is rising while its 50-day FALLS is a decelerating trend, not a dip; a name trailing its own sector by double digits over twelve months is being de-rated by the market for a reason the technicals do not carry. Two SMAs disagreeing is the tell -- the slow one describes the past, the fast one the present.

_SECTOR_RELATIVE_MOMENTUM_SEPARATES_A_DI.the_fundamental_trap_it_also_flags: LIN's fundamentals read fine in isolation -- Q2 EPS 4.50 vs 4.49 est, revenue 9.29B vs 9.02B est, FY26 guide narrowed UP to 17.70-17.90, consensus OVERWEIGHT, FactSet mean PT 547.09 = +13.6% above spot. A +13.6% mean target on a stock flat for twelve months is a measure of how far the targets have LAGGED, not of upside.

_THE_SLOT_DENOMINATOR_IS_AMBIGUOUS_BETWE.headline: The sizing formula 'size = deployable / remaining open slots' is UNDEFINED when the book sits at target. With 4 positions against a TARGET of 3-4, remaining slots is ZERO and the formula divides by zero; read against the BAND of 3-5 it is one slot and yields $1,155. The two readings differ by the entire decision, and no document says which denominator is meant.
_THE_SLOT_DENOMINATOR_IS_AMBIGUOUS_BETWE.the_arithmetic_today: total_value $3,850.33, cash $1,459.18 == unleveraged_buying_power, operational reserve 5% = $192.52, deployable $1,266.66, per-name cap 30% = $1,155.10. BAND reading: 1 remaining slot -> size min(1266.66, 1155.10) = $1,155.10, a compliant entry. TARGET reading: 0 remaining slots -> no compliant size exists; the book is full and today has no entry at any size.
_THE_SLOT_DENOMINATOR_IS_AMBIGUOUS_BETWE.how_it_has_been_resolved_so_far: Silently, and in the loose direction. The 2026-09-04T15:05Z run quoted a $1,155-1,267 slot without noting that it was choosing the band over the target; _THE_ENTRY_BAR_NOW_SCALES_WITH_THE_SLOT_SIZE inherits the same choice. Neither run was careless -- the ambiguity is genuinely invisible until the book actually reaches 4, which happened for the first time on 2026-09-01.
_THE_SLOT_DENOMINATOR_IS_AMBIGUOUS_BETWE.the_reading_applied_this_run_and_why: The STRICTER one, per the standing governance clause that where prompt and CLAUDE.md differ the stricter rule applies, and because 3-4 is written as the TARGET while 3-5 is written as the outer band a run may not exceed. A target the desk is already at is not a slot waiting to be filled. Practical consequence: a 5th entry is PERMITTED but must justify EXCEEDING the target, which is a higher bar than merely clearing an A-grade -- it is not automatically available just because cash is on hand.
_THE_SLOT_DENOMINATOR_IS_AMBIGUOUS_BETWE.why_it_is_not_the_void_cash_floor_return: It is a POSITION-COUNT gate, not a percentage cash target, and it does not reserve any cash: with 3 positions the formula is well-defined and the book deploys fully into the 4th. It only binds at the target count, and it binds on COUNT, which the concentration policy sets explicitly. Nothing here re-derives a cash percentage, and no cash is being held back for a better setup -- that would require the catalyst-and-expiry record the policy demands.
_THE_SLOT_DENOMINATOR_IS_AMBIGUOUS_BETWE.ESCALATED_TO_RYAN: YES -- recorded in _open_questions_for_ryan.q4_slot_denominator. An unattended run may apply the stricter reading; it may not settle which denominator Ryan meant. This will recur on every run while the book sits at 4.
_THE_SLOT_DENOMINATOR_IS_AMBIGUOUS_BETWE.changed_a_decision: PARTIALLY. PM graded A- this run on the full entry stack and was declined on the combination of this above-target gate and the size/selectivity test; under the band reading it would have been a genuinely closer call at $1,155. LIN was vetoed on trend structure and would have been declined under either denominator.

THE_AMBIGUITY_INVERTS_AT_THE_BOTTOM_OF_T.headline: This key resolved the ambiguity at the TOP of the band (4 positions) by applying the 'stricter rule' tie-breaker. THAT TIE-BREAKER HAS NO DETERMINATE MEANING AT THE BOTTOM, and the book arrives there on Monday. At 4 positions both axes agreed -- the target reading gave FEWER entries AND LESS deployed. At 2 positions they SEPARATE: the band reading (fill to 4) gives MORE entries at a SMALLER size each; the target reading (fill to 3) gives ONE entry at a LARGER size. 'Stricter' points one way on count and the opposite way on concentration.
THE_AMBIGUITY_INVERTS_AT_THE_BOTTOM_OF_T.why_it_lands_monday: MMM's time stop fires 2026-09-14 and GD's 2026-09-15. Both are pure calendar arithmetic over the ledger -- no report, no price input -- and neither can escape via take-profit, which is gated on price > entry while both sit ~-5% to -6%. The book goes 4 -> 2 inside two sessions with certainty.
THE_AMBIGUITY_INVERTS_AT_THE_BOTTOM_OF_T.the_arithmetic_at_2026-09-11T13-36Z_mark: MMM 2.884552 sh x 163.23 = $470.83; GD 1.335314 sh x 355.645 = $474.90; together $945.73 returns to cash. Cash then ~$1,161.18 against total_value ~$3,880, reserve 5% ~$194, DEPLOYABLE ~$967. Remaining book: ABNB + UNP = 2. Per-name cap 30% ~$1,164. BAND reading -> 2 slots -> $483.59 each. TARGET-BOTTOM reading -> 1 slot -> $967.00 = 24.9% of the account, inside the cap.
THE_AMBIGUITY_INVERTS_AT_THE_BOTTOM_OF_T.THE_RESOLUTION_and_it_needs_no_Ryan_turn: The BAND reading is SELF-DEFEATING, which settles it without appealing to the tie-breaker at all: $483.59 is below the ~$600 MINIMUM ENTRY, and the minimum is written as an absolute -- 'Below that, DO NOT ENTER -- wait for capital.' So the 2-slot reading does not produce two smaller entries, it produces TWO ILLEGAL ONES, i.e. no entry at all while ~$967 of A-grade funding capacity sits idle for want of arithmetic. A ruleset cannot mean that. THE MINIMUM-ENTRY CLAUSE RESOLVES THE DENOMINATOR AT THE BOTTOM OF THE BAND: size to the number of slots you can actually fund AT OR ABOVE the minimum -- here ONE entry of ~$967, leaving the book at 3, inside both the 3-4 target and the 3-5 band.
THE_AMBIGUITY_INVERTS_AT_THE_BOTTOM_OF_T.why_this_is_the_direction_the_policy_was: Same clause resolving the way it was drafted to resolve: 'more strong plays then a bunch of small ones' (Ryan, 2026-09-02). The minimum exists precisely because without it a book keeps making ever-smaller entries with whatever cash is lying around -- and the 2-slot reading is that failure mode arriving through the sizing formula rather than through drift.
THE_AMBIGUITY_INVERTS_AT_THE_BOTTOM_OF_T.WHAT_IT_DOES_NOT_RESOLVE: The TOP-of-band ambiguity is untouched and stays escalated in _open_questions_for_ryan.q4_slot_denominator. Nothing here licenses a 5th position, and nothing here re-derives a cash target: if only one A-grade name clears, the residual is the residual of quality and a 3-position book is a correct state, not an under-deployment to be corrected.
THE_AMBIGUITY_INVERTS_AT_THE_BOTTOM_OF_T.recompute_on_the_day: Every dollar figure above moves. Recompute deployable from get_portfolio on the day. The branch that changes the answer: if ABNB/UNP draw down or the exits realize materially less, deployable can fall under $600 and the correct output is NO entry rather than a sub-minimum one. THE FINDING IS THE READING, NOT THE NUMBER.
THE_AMBIGUITY_INVERTS_AT_THE_BOTTOM_OF_T.changed_a_decision: NOT TODAY -- nothing is placeable this run (deployable $21.46 against a ~$600 minimum, and master carries yesterday's boards so the stale-report clause bars an autonomous entry independently). Written now because it is decision-bearing on MONDAY and the run sizing the post-time-stop redeployment should inherit the resolution rather than derive it under a live clock.
