_THE_ATM_STRIKE_MIGRATES_WITH_SPOT_AND_T.status: DURABLE measurement rule for iv_history.json. Read WITH _IV_DAY_OVER_DAY_DIFFS_NEED_A_TIME_OFFSET (same class, ORTHOGONAL axis: that one corrects for WHEN a row was read, this one for WHICH STRIKE it was read at) and _OPENING_WINDOW_IV_DISCOUNT_IS_A_FUNCTION_OF_ELAPSED_TIME (whose measure-don't-assume rule this run followed).
_THE_ATM_STRIKE_MIGRATES_WITH_SPOT_AND_T.headline: THE IV METHOD LOGS THE **ATM** STRIKE, AND THE ATM STRIKE MOVES WITH SPOT -- SO ON ANY SESSION WITH A REAL SPOT MOVE THE DAY-OVER-DAY atm_iv DIFF IS DOMINATED BY SLIDING ALONG THE SKEW, NOT BY THE SURFACE MOVING. MEASURED AT ONE INSTANT ON TWO SYMBOLS: +4.05% (SPY) AND +3.49% (QQQ) OF RELATIVE IV PER 1% DOWN-MOVE IN SPOT. THAT IS LARGER THAN THE DOCUMENTED -2.5% TO -4.4% OPENING-WINDOW ARTIFACT AND POINTS THE OPPOSITE WAY.
_THE_ATM_STRIKE_MIGRATES_WITH_SPOT_AND_T.the_measurement: 2026-10-02 board, all four quotes at the same 15:32:34Z venue timestamp so NO time effect can contaminate the slope. SPY: 772 strike avg IV 0.113323 vs 769 strike 0.115112 = +1.578% over $3, spot 769.10 -> +4.05% per 1% of spot. QQQ: 721 strike 0.164733 vs 717 strike 0.167936 = +1.945% over $4, spot 716.95 -> +3.49% per 1% of spot. Direction is the ordinary index put skew: a down session drags the ATM strike DOWN onto a HIGHER-IV point, so the next day's logged atm_iv is mechanically INFLATED with an entirely unchanged surface.
_THE_ATM_STRIKE_MIGRATES_WITH_SPOT_AND_T.the_parity_result_that_makes_the_fixed_s: Averaging the call and put at a FIXED strike is parity-invariant, and SPY demonstrated it to six decimals across a -0.40% spot move: call 0.101402 -> 0.100955 (-0.000447) and put 0.125244 -> 0.125691 (+0.000447), an EXACT rotation, sum 0.226646 both times, average 0.113323 both times. The legs redistribute as the forward moves; the average does not. This validates the IV method's average-the-two instruction and means a same-strike re-quote is a clean surface probe. QQQ is the control that proves the probe is not merely inert: BOTH its legs fell (call 0.163540 -> 0.159070, put 0.172630 -> 0.170395) for a genuine -1.995% surface softening over the same 93 minutes.
_THE_ATM_STRIKE_MIGRATES_WITH_SPOT_AND_T.why_it_went_unnoticed: The existing time-offset finding explicitly restricted its artifact measurement to 'names whose ATM strike did NOT move so skew cannot contaminate the reading'. That was the correct control for measuring THAT artifact -- and it quarantined this effect rather than measuring it. The strike migration then kept operating unexamined on the LOGGED rows, which by construction always use the method-correct (moving) strike. A control that removes a nuisance variable does not remove it from the data the method actually records.
_THE_ATM_STRIKE_MIGRATES_WITH_SPOT_AND_T.what_it_implies_for_an_inherited_conclus: The 2026-09-01 finding's surviving reading -- 'index implied vol genuinely firmed on a -0.61% / -1.25% risk-off session' -- needs re-derivation and may partly INVERT. Applying today's slope: SPY's -0.61% session mechanically adds ~+2.4% to its +3.73% raw diff, so the firming survives at roughly half size; QQQ's -1.25% session mechanically adds ~+4.4% against a raw diff of only +1.20%, which would make QQQ's surface SOFTEN rather than firm. STATED AS A PREDICTION, NOT A CORRECTION: today's slope is a LOCAL one measured over $3-4, and extrapolating it across a full session's move is exactly the kind of unmeasured application this file's rules forbid. A future run should re-quote the 08-31 and 09-01 strike pairs directly rather than inherit either version.
_THE_ATM_STRIKE_MIGRATES_WITH_SPOT_AND_T.the_rule: Before quoting any day-over-day atm_iv diff, state the SPOT MOVE between the two readings and whether the ATM strike migrated. If it did, either (a) re-quote the PRIOR day's strike on today's board and diff THAT (one call, exact, parity-invariant), or (b) report the diff as confounded and unmeasured. Never present a moving-strike diff as a statement about the vol surface.
_THE_ATM_STRIKE_MIGRATES_WITH_SPOT_AND_T.honest_scope: n=2 symbols, one board, one instant, adjacent-strike slope only. It changed NO decision this run -- no options entry was contemplated (the QQQ level is chopping, and the standing Friday weekend-gap finding independently bars a TACTICAL scalp), which is the only condition under which a measurement rule can be audited credibly. It does NOT touch any ratio's rv leg, and today's rows were rewritten at the method-correct strike, so nothing here is a licence to log a non-ATM strike.
_THE_ATM_STRIKE_MIGRATES_WITH_SPOT_AND_T.EXTENDED_2026-09-11__THE_ARTIFACT_ALSO_B: This key's rule was applied for the first time on a real sweep (2026-09-11, post-CPI) and it WORKED -- it killed a compelling false finding before it was recorded. New half nobody had stated: because the artifact scales with each name's OWN spot move TIMES its OWN relative skew slope, it differs across names and therefore corrupts comparisons BETWEEN them, not merely each name's level. Measured: naive ranked SPY and QQQ the two most-crushed names at a 2.29x index-vs-single-name separation; corrected, they rank 3rd and 4th behind AVGO and TSM and the separation falls to 1.40x. Relative skew per 1% of moneyness is -5.47 (SPY) and -3.72 (QQQ) against -0.86/-0.29/+0.11 for MSFT/TSM/AMD, so low-vol indices are hit ~20-50x harder per unit of migration AND move most on macro days -- the two compound, making index-vs-single-name the most artifact-prone comparison in the sweep. Full write-up: _THE_MIGRATION_ARTIFACT_IS_PROPORTIONAL_TO_EACH_NAMES_OWN_SPOT_MOVE_SO_IT_FABRICATES_CROSS_SECTIONAL_STORIES_2026-09-11.

_A_FEED_HOLE_BACKFILLS_SO_AN_INHERITED_H.headline: A feed hole is NOT a fixed wrong number -- it BACK-FILLS over time, upward, and stays short for at least ~37 minutes past the bar's close. So a hole flagged by an EARLIER RUN must be RE-FETCHED, never inherited; and a second fetch proves the bar is provisional without ever giving you the right number. Only the 1-minute reconciliation does that.
_A_FEED_HOLE_BACKFILLS_SO_AN_INHERITED_H.the_revision: QQQ's 15:10Z 5-minute bucket, measured by the 15:35Z run at 21,643 and by this run at 15:47Z at 54,428 -- a +151% revision on a bucket that had been CLOSED for 20 minutes at the first reading and 32 at the second. True 1-minute sum: 145,223. So the first reading was 14.9% of true and the revised reading is still only 37.5% of true. The bar was still filling in 37 minutes after it closed.
_A_FEED_HOLE_BACKFILLS_SO_AN_INHERITED_H.why_this_is_new: The 2026-08-26 rule ('fetch the window twice a few minutes apart'; 'end the trailing baseline ~10 minutes back') is aimed at bars near NOW and treats revision as noise of unpredictable sign. This is a different object: a bucket flagged as HOLED by a prior run, inherited by a later one. Its correction has a KNOWN SIGN (upward, toward the 1-minute sum) and a horizon far longer than 10 minutes. Nothing in the file said to re-fetch an inherited hole figure, and a run that quotes a predecessor's hole number is quoting a number that has since changed by 151%.
_A_FEED_HOLE_BACKFILLS_SO_AN_INHERITED_H.cross_symbol_confirmation_free_in_one_ca: The SAME two timestamps are holed on BOTH symbols -- SPY 14:45Z -81.3% and 15:10Z -93.8%; QQQ 14:45Z -89.4% and 15:10Z -62.5% (each vs its own 1-minute sum). That is the 2026-08-27 cross-symbol agreement signature, obtained for free by carrying a second symbol in the same get_equity_historicals call. Read in ONE direction only, per that finding: agreement evidences a feed-window hole; a clean neighbour would have evidenced nothing.
_A_FEED_HOLE_BACKFILLS_SO_AN_INHERITED_H.the_signature_has_more_than_one_FORM_in_: SPY 15:10Z bucket 11,155 equals its 15:11 one-minute bar EXACTLY (whole-bar substitution) while QQQ 15:10Z bucket 54,428 matches NO constituent minute (partial hole) -- same feed window, same minute, two different presentations. QQQ 14:45Z (9,273 = its 14:49 bar) is a third instance of the exact-match form. This confirms the 2026-08-28 warning not to require the single-constituent signature before declaring a hole: THE RECONCILIATION GAP IS THE TEST, the exact match is only one of its forms.
_A_FEED_HOLE_BACKFILLS_SO_AN_INHERITED_H.direction_and_magnitude_third_confirmati: Corrected QQQ trailing-30 baseline over 15:10-15:35Z: raw 115,491 vs corrected 130,624 -- raw is 11.6% LOW, in line with the prior measurements of 13.1% and 10.1%. Un-reconciled buckets depress the DENOMINATOR of every trailing-volume baseline, so the defect manufactures the confirmation the tactical volume clause exists to withhold. Same dangerous direction, third independent instance.
_A_FEED_HOLE_BACKFILLS_SO_AN_INHERITED_H.detector: (1) Never inherit a predecessor's hole figure -- re-fetch it. (2) Never treat a second fetch as the correction: both the 21,643 and the 54,428 readings were wrong; only the 1-minute sum (145,223) was right. (3) Reconcile every bucket you intend to use, whatever the offset -- today's holes landed at :45 and :10, against :05/:05/:20 on 08-28 and :45 on 08-27, so the offset carries NO information, as the 08-28 run correctly predicted when it killed the ':05 clustering' hypothesis.
_A_FEED_HOLE_BACKFILLS_SO_AN_INHERITED_H.honest_scope_it_changed_no_decision: No volume clause was load-bearing today, so nothing turns on these numbers. There is no price trigger to confirm: QQQ crossed its 20-day SMA (717.7140) FOUR times in the 15 completed 5-minute closes from 14:30-15:40Z, and SPY (20-day 769.2065) never closed below its own on any of the 15 -- minimum close 769.25, +0.006%. A filter's inputs can only be audited credibly on a run where the audit does not benefit the desk.
_A_FEED_HOLE_BACKFILLS_SO_AN_INHERITED_H.amended_2026-09-04T16:05Z_the_substitute: CORRECTION TO THE RECOGNITION RULE AS WRITTEN IN BOTH THIS KEY AND CLAUDE.md. The file describes the whole-bar form as the bucket being 'its LAST constituent minute'. Measured at 16:03Z on the 15:30Z bucket, on BOTH symbols simultaneously, it is the SECOND: QQQ's 15:30Z bucket (volume 4,832, O 716.970 / H 717.120 / L 716.9501 / C 717.050) is byte-for-byte QQQ's 15:31 ONE-MINUTE bar; SPY's 15:30Z bucket (9,184, O 769.070 / H 769.1899 / L 769.070 / C 769.110) is byte-for-byte SPY's 15:31 one-minute bar. Not the last minute (15:34) in either case. Reconciliation gaps: QQQ 4,832 vs a 112,008 1-minute sum = -95.7%; SPY 9,184 vs 88,928 = -89.7% -- bucket-below-sum on both, so per the 2026-08-28 direction rule the BUCKET is the holed side and the 1-minute sums substitute. CONSEQUENCE: do not look for a match against the closing minute specifically. Test the bucket against EVERY constituent minute, or better, just use the reconciliation gap, which catches the partial form too.
_A_FEED_HOLE_BACKFILLS_SO_AN_INHERITED_H.the_hole_SUPPRESSED_THE_SESSION_LOW_ON_B: The 2026-08-27 rule says to report a session extreme as a FLOOR because a holed bucket shows one minute's range. Here is that happening, measured: QQQ's 15:30Z bucket low reads 716.9501, while the true interval low across its five minutes is 716.865 (in the 15:30 minute) -- understated by 0.085, and 716.865 is BELOW every other 5-minute bucket low of the session, so the true session low is at least 716.865 and no reading of the 5-minute series alone shows it. SPY the same: bucket low 769.070 against a true 769.030, understated by 0.040. Small in points and the point is not the size -- it is that BOTH symbols had their extreme suppressed in the SAME window, so a run drawing a level off the 5-minute series would have drawn it wrong on both at once, with no discrepancy between them to notice. Quote intraday extremes as 'at least X' unless the buckets bracketing them have been reconciled.

_A_LEVEL_CROSSED_REPEATEDLY_IS_NOT_A_LEV.finding: COUNT the completed closes on each side of a candidate level BEFORE doing any volume work. QQQ crossed its 20-day SMA 4 times in 15 completed 5-minute closes (14:30-15:40Z) -- a level crossed 4 times in 75 minutes is not a level, it is a pin, and no volume clause can rescue a break of it. SPY over the identical 15 bars crossed its own 20-day ZERO times (min close 769.25 = +0.006% above 769.2065).
_A_LEVEL_CROSSED_REPEATEDLY_IS_NOT_A_LEV.why_it_earns_a_name: The 14:45Z and 15:05Z runs each ran a full two-bar price clause plus a volume workup on the QQQ 20-day and declined on magnitude; the 15:35Z run was the first to COUNT (3 crossings in 12 bars) and used it correctly. Promoting that from an informal observation to a named pre-screen makes it reusable: the count is one line of arithmetic off bars already fetched, and it disqualifies the level before the expensive work -- exactly the ordering the 2026-08-14 SOURCING fix applies to liquidity.
_A_LEVEL_CROSSED_REPEATEDLY_IS_NOT_A_LEV.the_contrast_is_the_useful_part: SPY and QQQ sit at +0.006% from their respective 20-days -- IDENTICAL distance -- and are untradeable for OPPOSITE reasons. QQQ oscillates through its average (no information in a break). SPY rides just above its average without ever testing it (no break to trade). A distance reading alone cannot tell these apart; the crossing count can. Do not read 'near the 20-day' as a single state.
_A_LEVEL_CROSSED_REPEATEDLY_IS_NOT_A_LEV.threshold_stated_as_judgement_not_law: No count threshold is asserted from n=1 session. What is asserted is that the count must be COMPUTED and REPORTED alongside any level-based trigger, so the next runs accumulate the sample that would justify a threshold.
_A_LEVEL_CROSSED_REPEATEDLY_IS_NOT_A_LEV.amended_2026-09-04T16:05Z_count_extended: SAMPLE EXTENDED, SAME SESSION, AND THE CONTRAST HARDENED. Over the full 18 completed 5-minute closes 14:30-15:55Z, QQQ crossed its 20-day SMA (717.7140) FIVE times -- up from the 4-in-15 recorded at 15:47Z and the 3-in-12 at 15:35Z. Sequence of closes vs the level: above/above/above, below x4 (14:45-15:00), above x2 (15:05,15:10), below x4 (15:15-15:35), above (15:40), below x3 (15:45-15:55). SPY over the IDENTICAL 18 bars still crossed its own 20-day (769.2065) ZERO times -- min close 769.11, +0.005% above. Three consecutive measurements have found the crossing count RISING on QQQ and pinned at zero on SPY, which is what a pin looks like as it persists rather than resolves. Still no threshold asserted from one session; the sample is what is being accumulated.
_A_LEVEL_CROSSED_REPEATEDLY_IS_NOT_A_LEV.the_count_is_ROBUST_TO_FEED_HOLES_and_th: A crossing count is built from bar CLOSES, and a holed bucket's close is one constituent minute's close rather than the interval's -- so the obvious objection is that the count is an artifact of the feed. CHECKED, not asserted: three buckets in the window are holed (14:45Z, 15:10Z, 15:30Z, both symbols). Every crossing survives, because each holed bar's side of the level is independently confirmed by an ADJACENT CLEAN bar -- e.g. the 14:45Z crossing into 'below' is corroborated by the clean 14:50Z close (717.60, volume 228,843), and the 15:05Z crossing into 'above' by the clean 15:05Z close itself (717.94, volume 182,378). THE GENERAL RULE: a hole can only manufacture or erase a crossing where the holed bar is the ONLY bar on its side of the level. Check that condition -- it is one glance -- rather than either trusting or discarding the count wholesale. This is the cheap way the two findings of this session compose; neither one says it alone.

_A_FEED_HOLE_CAN_INVERT_A_STRUCTURAL_LEV.status: DURABLE, NEW SUBJECT. Every prior feed-hole finding in this file is about the VOLUME DENOMINATOR of the confirmation clause, or about a drawn level / session extreme being understated. This is the first measured instance of a hole flipping the SIGN of the PRICE clause -- the completed-close test against a moving average -- which is the half of the trigger that decides whether a break exists at all.
_A_FEED_HOLE_CAN_INVERT_A_STRUCTURAL_LEV.headline: A HOLED 5-MINUTE BUCKET REPORTS ONE CONSTITUENT MINUTE'S CLOSE AS THE BUCKET'S CLOSE. WHEN THAT MINUTE SITS ON THE OTHER SIDE OF A MOVING AVERAGE FROM THE TRUE INTERVAL CLOSE, THE HOLE MANUFACTURES OR ERASES A COMPLETED-CLOSE BREAK. THE VOLUME CLAUSE FAILING OPEN IS THE KNOWN HAZARD; THIS ONE FAILS THE PRICE CLAUSE, WHICH IS UPSTREAM OF IT.
_A_FEED_HOLE_CAN_INVERT_A_STRUCTURAL_LEV.the_measurement: SPY 20-day SMA 769.2065 (two-method cross-validated earlier today). SPY's 15:30Z 5-minute bucket is whole-bar-substituted by its 15:31 minute and therefore reports close 769.110 -- 0.0965 BELOW the 20-day, i.e. a COMPLETED 5-MINUTE CLOSE THROUGH A STRUCTURAL LEVEL, the first leg of a bearish two-bar price clause. The TRUE interval close is the 15:34 minute's 769.250 -- 0.0435 ABOVE the 20-day, i.e. no break at all. Same bar, same level, opposite verdict. QQQ's 15:30Z bucket is holed in the identical window (4,832 = its 15:31 bar) so a run checking cross-symbol agreement gets no discrepancy to notice.
_A_FEED_HOLE_CAN_INVERT_A_STRUCTURAL_LEV.why_it_is_worse_than_the_denominator_cas: A wrong denominator makes a real break easier or harder to CONFIRM. A wrong close decides whether the desk believes a break HAPPENED. Under the standing trigger construction the price clause is evaluated first and the volume clause only runs on a bar that already passed it -- so a hole here does not weaken a filter, it feeds the filter a fictional event. And it is silent: nothing errors, the bar looks ordinary, and the neighbouring symbol is holed in the same window so the 2026-08-27 cross-symbol check agrees rather than disagrees.
_A_FEED_HOLE_CAN_INVERT_A_STRUCTURAL_LEV.it_cuts_BOTH_ways_which_is_why_no_direct: Here the hole INVENTS a bearish break that did not occur. The mirror is equally available: had the substituted minute been the one printing 769.30 while the true close was 769.15, the hole would have ERASED a real break. Substituted minutes are not biased toward or away from a level, so there is no safe direction to lean and no 'holes only make us miss trades' consolation.
_A_FEED_HOLE_CAN_INVERT_A_STRUCTURAL_LEV.DETECTOR: Before testing ANY completed-close price clause against a structural level, reconcile the candidate bucket against its 1-minute constituents and take the LAST minute's close as the interval close -- never the bucket's reported close. This is the same 1-minute reconciliation the volume rules already demand, so it costs no extra call; what is new is that it must be run for the PRICE test too, and must be run even when no volume clause will be evaluated. A bucket flagged as holed for volume purposes has an untrustworthy OHLC as well: this file already knows a holed bucket's LOW understates the interval (2026-08-27 FLOOR rule, re-confirmed 16:05Z today) -- the CLOSE is corrupted by exactly the same mechanism and nobody had said so.
_A_FEED_HOLE_CAN_INVERT_A_STRUCTURAL_LEV.consequence_for_the_20day_crossing_count: The crossing count adopted at 15:47Z as a free pre-screen is computed from completed 5-minute closes, so it inherits this defect directly. The 16:05Z run extended the count to 5 and checked that it survived the holes -- correctly, and that check is now understood to have been load-bearing rather than incidental. Re-derive the count from hole-corrected closes, or it will count fictional crossings; on today's SPY series the raw 15:30Z close would have added a spurious crossing to a name that in truth never lost its 20-day all session (true minimum close 769.250, +0.006% above).
_A_FEED_HOLE_CAN_INVERT_A_STRUCTURAL_LEV.honest_scope: n=1 window, two symbols, one session, and IT CHANGED NO DECISION -- which is the condition under which this file's own standard says a filter audit is credible. TACTICAL was declined this run on the late-entry arithmetic (the SPY 20-day was never lost, so there was no reclaim to trade, and price sits 1.6 points above the level 40 minutes on), not on anything measured here. What is established is STRUCTURAL rather than statistical, like the RSI2-saturation finding: a whole-bar substitution reports a single minute's close as the interval's, and a single minute's close can sit on either side of a level, so no sample size is needed to show the verdict can invert. What is NOT established is how often the substituted minute lands across a level that matters.

_THE_QQQ_20DAY_IS_NOT_A_TRADEABLE_LEVEL_.headline: QQQ lost its 20-day SMA intraday on the FIRST volume reading of this arc that clears EVERY denominator -- and it is still not a trigger, because the LEVEL fails its own prescreen. The usual failure is inverted: normally the level looks fine and the volume clause vetoes. Here volume confirmed and the level is the thing that is meaningless.
_THE_QQQ_20DAY_IS_NOT_A_TRADEABLE_LEVEL_.the_level: 20-day SMA 717.7140, computed off the last 20 daily closes through 09-03 and matching the two-method cross-validation inherited from this morning to 4dp. Spot 717.300 at 17:31Z = 0.414 BELOW it (-0.058%).

why_it_is_not_a_level_the_free_prescreen.intraday_crossings_today: FOUR crossings of 717.7140 in one session: below at the 15:30 open (717.05), above at 15:40 (717.760), back below at 15:45 (717.340), above at 16:05 (718.075) and held there for ~80 minutes to a 719.470 high, back below at 17:25 (717.505). Two of those crossings came ten minutes apart.
why_it_is_not_a_level_the_free_prescreen.daily_context_which_is_the_damning_half: QQQ has closed on BOTH sides of this average for eight sessions and only flipped sign 3 times in 18. It closed BELOW on 08-24, 08-25, 08-26, 08-28, 08-31, 09-01, 09-02 and 09-03 -- and yesterday's close was 717.67 against an SMA of 717.7140, i.e. 0.044 BELOW. The index has been sitting ON this line for over a week.
why_it_is_not_a_level_the_free_prescreen.conclusion: Today's cross is not a level giving way. It is the index oscillating around a value it has been pinned to for eight sessions. Breaking it carries no information, and no volume reading can supply information a level does not have.

the_volume_clause_PASSED_and_that_is_the.denominators_all_three: trailing-30 local mean 132,891 -> 106.6%; early-session (15:35-16:00) baseline 66,235 -> 213.9%; session mean ex-candidate 100,717 -> 140.7%. Clears every one, including the strictest.
the_volume_clause_PASSED_and_that_is_the.feed_integrity_checked_first: All six QQQ 5-min buckets 17:00-17:25 reconcile EXACTLY against their 1-minute sums (119,053 / 120,233 / 123,785 / 134,108 / 239,168 / 141,697 -- zero discrepancy in either direction), so no holed denominator is doing this work. SPY's 17:25 bucket likewise exact (81,834).
the_volume_clause_PASSED_and_that_is_the.so_the_veto_is_not_a_volume_veto: Every prior decline in this arc rested at least partly on participation. This one cannot, and saying so is the point of recording it.

the_test_that_actually_kills_it_defence_.rule_applied: The 2026-08-28 defence-versus-break ratio: a breakdown that matters takes MORE participation to break a level than it took to defend it.
the_test_that_actually_kills_it_defence_.measured: The 17:20Z bar was the session's heaviest at 239,168 (180% of the trailing-30 mean) and it was a DOWN bar that closed at 717.740 -- 0.026 ABOVE the level, i.e. the level was DEFENDED on the day's biggest print. The 17:25Z break bar took 141,697 = 59.2% of that. Participation fell 41% between the defence and the break.
the_test_that_actually_kills_it_defence_.reading: Sellers finished at the line; what followed is drift, not distribution. Identical shape to the 2026-08-28 QQQ 716.52 case (defence 162.5%, break 91.9%/57.6%), which reverted within six minutes.

three_further_independent_grounds.price_clause_INCOMPLETE: The two-bar clause needs a completed close beyond the level AND a holding bar. 17:25Z is the FIRST completed close below (717.505); the 17:30Z bar was still forming at decision time. One bar is not the trigger, and entering on it is trading the anticipation.
three_further_independent_grounds.index_agreement_FAILS: SPY 769.590 is still +0.384 ABOVE its own 20-day (769.2065) and has not tested it. A QQQ-only break with SPY holding its level is a divergence, not a tape.
three_further_independent_grounds.friday_weekend_gap: 2026-09-04 is a Friday. A TACTICAL scalp not closed by the bell carries a weekend whose MEDIAN gap (0.342%) exceeds the entire -30% stop distance in underlying terms. Unchanged and still binding.

_THE_QQQ_20DAY_IS_NOT_A_TRADEABLE_LEVEL_.honest_scope: This changed NO decision -- the trade was declined on four independent grounds and the level prescreen alone was sufficient. That is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly. It is recorded because it is the first clean instance of the INVERSE case, and because a later run that sees a confirmed volume reading on this level must not read it as the arc's first real signal.
_THE_QQQ_20DAY_IS_NOT_A_TRADEABLE_LEVEL_.transferable: A volume clause measures whether participation arrived. It cannot measure whether the thing participation arrived AT means anything. When the volume finally confirms, that is the moment to re-audit the LEVEL -- not the moment to trust the filter. Count the crossings first: it is free, it needs no live data, and here it settled the question before any denominator was computed.

_LABOR_DAY_MAKES_THIS_A_96_HOUR_WEEKEND_.headline: Monday 2026-09-07 is Labor Day and the NYSE is shut. THREE runs today (17:35Z, 17:46Z, 18:01Z) wrote that a TACTICAL scalp opened now 'runs to Monday's close' / carries a '~72h window'. The next session is TUESDAY 2026-09-08 and the window is ~96h. The error changed no decision -- the scalp was declined on independent grounds each time -- but it was inherited verbatim three runs running, which is how a wrong constant becomes doctrine.
_LABOR_DAY_MAKES_THIS_A_96_HOUR_WEEKEND_.what_was_measured: SPY daily bars 2024-09-04..2026-09-04, 502 sessions, adjustment_type=none. Market holidays were DETECTED FROM THE DATA rather than from a calendar: any weekday with no bar in an otherwise continuous series. 20 detected, ending 2026-01-19 / 02-16 / 04-03 / 05-25 / 06-19 / 07-03 -- MLK, Presidents, Good Friday, Memorial, Juneteenth, July 4th observed. Gaps bucketed by whether a holiday falls strictly between the two sessions.
_LABOR_DAY_MAKES_THIS_A_96_HOUR_WEEKEND_.THE_HONEST_READ_and_it_is_NOT_the_one_th: A holiday weekend does NOT gap harder than an ordinary one on the MEAN -- 0.495% vs 0.550%, slightly LOWER -- so 'more calendar hours therefore more gap' is refuted by the data that was gathered to support it. What IS true: the post-holiday MEDIAN is the highest of the three buckets (0.417% vs 0.342% vs 0.264%) and a >0.5% gap happens on HALF of post-holiday opens against 39.1% of ordinary Mondays and 24.4% of overnights. So the holiday weekend is more RELIABLY large and not more EXTREME -- the ordinary-Monday mean is dragged up by a fatter tail. n=20 is thin for a p90 and cannot support a magnitude claim; it comfortably supports the frequency one.
_LABOR_DAY_MAKES_THIS_A_96_HOUR_WEEKEND_.decision_consequence_TACTICAL: The 2026-08-28 finding priced a TACTICAL -30% stop at 0.20-0.32% of SPY on the vehicle quoted that day. The post-holiday median gap of 0.417% EXCEEDS that whole distance, and clears 0.5% half the time. A scalp opened today is flat-by-Tuesday's-close with both of its exits unenforceable across ~96 hours. The Friday bar on TACTICAL entries is therefore FIRMER today than on an ordinary Friday, and it is firmer for the frequency reason, not the extra-day reason.
_LABOR_DAY_MAKES_THIS_A_96_HOUR_WEEKEND_.decision_consequence_EQUITIES: SWING_TIME_STOP_DAYS is 14 CALENDAR days (report.py computes days_held = today - entry_date, confirmed by reading it this run), so a market holiday inside the window costs the position a TRADING SESSION while the deadline does not move. Labor Day sits inside all four open windows. LLY (entry 08-27, stop 09-10) has 3 sessions left after today -- 09-08, 09-09, 09-10 -- not 4. MDLZ 09-11 has 4, MMM 09-14 has 5, GD 09-15 has 6. Each is one fewer chance for the mean reversion to pay before the capital is recycled, ~10% of the window's opportunity on a 14-day clock. This is not an argument to extend the stop: elapsed time is the point of it, and a holiday is exactly the kind of dead time it is meant to charge for.
_LABOR_DAY_MAKES_THIS_A_96_HOUR_WEEKEND_.correction_to_the_2026-08-28_STUDY_and_i: That study bucketed purely by the WEEKDAY OF THE OPEN, so post-holiday opens -- which mostly land on Tuesdays -- were counted inside its TUE-FRI 'overnight' bucket, inflating it. Its n=404 is this run's n=389 plus ~15 holiday gaps. Effect is real and immaterial: mean 0.401% -> 0.395%, median 0.279% -> 0.264%, p90 0.901% -> 0.885%. The 08-28 conclusion stands unchanged. Recorded because a contaminated control bucket is worth naming even when it does not move the answer.
_LABOR_DAY_MAKES_THIS_A_96_HOUR_WEEKEND_.the_transferable_shape: A weekday-derived constant ('the weekend is 2 days', 'the next session is Monday') is correct ~90% of the time and silently wrong on the ~10% of Fridays that precede a holiday -- the same family as every other entry here where a constant encoded an assumption about a moving thing and nothing errored. Detector, and it costs one call: derive the session calendar FROM THE BAR SERIES, never from the weekday. A weekday absent from a continuous daily series is a market holiday, which is also how the 20 holidays above were found.
_LABOR_DAY_MAKES_THIS_A_96_HOUR_WEEKEND_.honest_scope: Changed no decision. Both books were flat on independent grounds before this was measured, and the equity consequence is an observation about window quality, not a rule change. n=20 post-holiday gaps over two years, one regime, SPY only.

_THE_TWO_BOOKS_HAVE_OPPOSITE_EDGES_AND_B.source: BROKER, get_pnl_trade_history(span='3month') on 718757339 -- 73 closes. Split per the v10 calibration duty: equities = side 'sell', options = side ''. NOT from trade_journal.json.
_THE_TWO_BOOKS_HAVE_OPPOSITE_EDGES_AND_B.headline: The v10 duty to run edge_stats on EACH BOOK SEPARATELY has never actually been executed on this account, and doing it splits the two books in OPPOSITE directions. EQUITIES: n=55, +$303.23, hit 70.9%, payoff 1.04, breakeven 49.0%, MARGIN +21.9 pts, expectancy +$5.51. OPTIONS: n=18, +$60.00, hit 50.0%, payoff 0.96, breakeven 51.0%, MARGIN -1.0 pt, expectancy +$3.33. BLENDED: margin +6.7 pts.
_THE_TWO_BOOKS_HAVE_OPPOSITE_EDGES_AND_B.why_blending_is_the_dangerous_reading: The blended +6.7 pts reads as a healthy book. It is the average of a genuinely strong equity engine and an options sleeve sitting a hair BELOW its own breakeven. Neither number describes anything real: the equity book's true margin is three times the blend, and the options book's is negative. The prompt's rule that 'blending hides which one is working' is not a stylistic preference -- on this account it is the difference between +21.9 and -1.0.
_THE_TWO_BOOKS_HAVE_OPPOSITE_EDGES_AND_B.the_options_+$60_is_two_trades: The options book's positive dollar total is carried entirely by QQQ +$226 (08-24) and WULF +$208 (08-03). Strip those two and the remaining 16 closes are roughly -$374. A 50% hit rate at payoff 0.96 is a coin flip that pays slightly less than it costs -- which is precisely what the margin figure says and what the dollar total conceals.
_THE_TWO_BOOKS_HAVE_OPPOSITE_EDGES_AND_B.NO_ACTION_TAKEN_AND_WHY: n=18 is BELOW MIN_TRADES_FOR_ACTION=20, and the n<20 guard is a SEPARATE guard from the in-regime gate: the KILL branch's exemption is written against the in-regime gate only, not against the sample-size floor. So this is REPORTED, never adjusted. It is also not this run's duty -- the weekly calibration falls on the week's first trading day, which is TUESDAY 2026-09-08 because Monday is Labor Day.
_THE_TWO_BOOKS_HAVE_OPPOSITE_EDGES_AND_B.and_the_in_regime_caveat_cuts_hardest_he: These 73 closes span several policy regimes (the $1,500-per-trade sizing amendment, the dual-track split, the concentration rewrite, the time stop going live). In-regime n for the CURRENT parameters is approximately zero on both books -- see _THIS_WEEKS_ENTRIES_PREDATE_THE_SIZING_POLICY_SO_CALIBRATION_HAS_NO_IN_REGIME_SAMPLE. So this is a DESCRIPTIVE measurement of what the account has done, not an actionable calibration input. Do not tune anything off it.
_THE_TWO_BOOKS_HAVE_OPPOSITE_EDGES_AND_B.what_the_next_run_should_do: Tuesday 2026-09-08 owns the weekly calibration. Run the split again then, state both margins separately in the daily report, and if the options book has reached n>=20 still at margin <=0, the KILL branch applies to THAT BOOK ALONE -- halve options size, pause new options entries, escalate to Ryan. It must not be netted against the equity book's health.
_THE_TWO_BOOKS_HAVE_OPPOSITE_EDGES_AND_B.honest_scope: This changed no decision today: both books were flat on their own merits before the statistic was computed, and no calibration was due. A measurement is only creditable when it does not license what the desk already wanted to do.

_A_REPORT_GENERATED_ON_A_MARKET_HOLIDAY_.headline: Both committed reports on master are stamped 2026-09-07 -- LABOR DAY, a session that never happened. The MORNING file (18:12Z) carries LLY at 1149.36, the exact official settled close. The INTRADAY file (19:02Z), 50 minutes later on the same closed market, carries LLY at 1148.20 -- a price that matches NO settled close, NO last regular trade, and NO extended print. The price source DRIFTED between two runs of a non-session, and the drift PROPAGATED INTO THE SIGNAL. Prompt v10 and CLAUDE.md both say to read 'latest_morning.md / latest_intraday.md, WHICHEVER IS NEWER'. On a holiday-generated pair that rule selects the WRONG file: newer is LESS trustworthy, because it is further from the last settled close.

how_the_holiday_was_established_from_DAT.historicals: get_equity_historicals(day, adjustment_type=none, 5 symbols, 08-31..09-08) returns bars for 08-31, 09-01, 09-02, 09-03, 09-04 and NO 09-07 bar, in an otherwise continuous series.
how_the_holiday_was_established_from_DAT.broker_confirms: get_equity_quotes returns previous_close_date = 2026-09-04 for all five names, and close.source = 'sip-list-exchange-close', close.interpolated = false.
how_the_holiday_was_established_from_DAT.calendar_agrees: 2026-09-07 is the first Monday of September 2026 = Labor Day. The data was checked FIRST; the calendar only corroborates.

the_measurement.verdict: 1148.20 reconciles to NOTHING the broker reports. It is a thin holiday quote from the report's upstream feed, not any settled or observable print.

_A_REPORT_GENERATED_ON_A_MARKET_HOLIDAY_.THE_CONTROL_that_makes_this_a_finding_an: Of the six RSI2 setup rows, FIVE are byte-identical across the two holiday reports -- PM 182.53, PATH 15.19, CL 88.77, SBUX 104.47, GD 359.39 -- and all five match their official settled closes exactly. GD's RSI2 is 9.8 in BOTH files. Only LLY's price moved, and only LLY's RSI2 moved. The signal change is therefore ATTRIBUTABLE to the price drift rather than to noise in the indicator, which is the difference between a measurement and a coincidence.
_A_REPORT_GENERATED_ON_A_MARKET_HOLIDAY_.THE_AMPLIFICATION_and_it_is_the_hazard: A -0.101% price change (1149.36 -> 1148.20) moved RSI2 from 3.6 to 3.0 -- a -16.7% RELATIVE move, roughly 165x amplification. A 2-period RSI is enormously sensitive near its extremes, which is exactly the region the entry screen reads. THE FAILURE THIS PREDICTS: a name sitting at RSI2 ~10.5 on the settled close can print RSI2 ~9.8 on a holiday phantom quote and appear as a fresh A-grade BUY setup that the settled data does not support. Under the 2026-09-02 concentration policy that is a ~30%-of-account entry sourced from a price nobody traded. Do NOT generalize the 165x figure -- it is measured at RSI2 ~3 where sensitivity is highest and it is not constant across the range.

THE_RULE.selection: On a report pair whose header date is a NON-SESSION, prefer the EARLIER file -- it was built closer to the settled close. Better still: verify the report's price column against get_equity_quotes[].close.price before any signal off it decides a trade. That is one call for up to 10 names and it is the arbiter.
THE_RULE.detector: Before trusting any committed report, check that its header date is a real session: a daily bar exists for that date, or get_equity_quotes.previous_close_date equals it. A header date is a CLAIM about when the report ran, never evidence that a market was open.
THE_RULE.scope: This is not confined to holidays. Any report generated while the market is shut -- a weekend backstop firing, an early-close afternoon, a pre-open run -- can carry a price field unanchored to the last settled close.

_A_REPORT_GENERATED_ON_A_MARKET_HOLIDAY_.HONEST_SCOPE_it_changed_no_decision: (1) The market is shut and nothing is placeable. (2) LLY is already HELD, so its BUY row is a [HELD] line the desk skips regardless. (3) The error is 0.10% on a position underwater ~3.5%, so no exit trigger is anywhere near. (4) A fresh 2026-09-08 report lands on master ~14:15Z and overwrites both files before the preferred entry window. _THE_UNION_MERGE_RECIPE_DEDUPES_ON_A_KEY.status: DURABLE, NEW. Caught inside this run's OWN union merge, before the write landed. No data was lost.
_THE_UNION_MERGE_RECIPE_DEDUPES_ON_A_KEY.headline: CLAUDE.md's collision rule says to resolve a same-slot conflict as a UNION and to 'keep both trade_journal.json entries (ordered by run_utc)'. Implemented the obvious way -- a dict keyed on run_utc, then sort -- it SILENTLY DELETES entries. Measured on this merge: ours 1097 + theirs 1097 with 1096 shared should give 1098; the run_utc dict returned 1091. SEVEN historical entries vanished.
_THE_UNION_MERGE_RECIPE_DEDUPES_ON_A_KEY.the_mechanism: run_utc IS NOT UNIQUE and never was. Seven timestamps already appear TWICE within a single side of this merge -- 2026-08-13T18:30Z, 2026-08-13T23:29Z, 2026-08-14T17:15Z, 2026-08-14T19:15Z, 2026-08-28T15:35Z, 2026-08-28T17:15Z and one more. Those are precisely the CONCURRENT SAME-SLOT PAIRS from earlier collisions, which prior runs correctly preserved. So the recipe destroys exactly the artifact it was written to protect, and it does so MORE aggressively the more collisions the file has already survived.
_THE_UNION_MERGE_RECIPE_DEDUPES_ON_A_KEY.why_it_is_invisible: The output is a valid, correctly-ordered journal whose tail looks exactly right -- this run's entry and the sibling's, both present, in order. The loss is seven entries buried three weeks back. Nothing errors, no diff line screams, and `git diff --stat` reports a plausible number because a merge legitimately rewrites many lines. This is the file's most-repeated shape: a check that passes for the wrong reason.
_THE_UNION_MERGE_RECIPE_DEDUPES_ON_A_KEY.THE_FIX_two_lines: Union on CONTENT identity -- json.dumps(entry, sort_keys=True) -- never on a timestamp. Then ASSERT the arithmetic before writing: len(merged) == len(ours) + len(entries unique to theirs). The assertion is what actually catches it; the content key is only what makes the assertion pass. Same discipline as the lot-count invariants and the `git diff --stat` rule -- TRUST THE CHECK, NOT YOUR READING OF THE RESULT.
_THE_UNION_MERGE_RECIPE_DEDUPES_ON_A_KEY.generalise_it_beyond_the_journal: Any 'merge as a union' instruction that names a field to key on is asserting that field is unique. Verify that before trusting it. The same trap is live for iv_history rows keyed on (ticker, date) -- overwriting today's row is the DOCUMENTED intent there, so it is correct -- and for market_brief watchlist entries. Know which of your union keys are meant to collapse and which are not.

_A_RAW_IV_RV_RATIO_LEVEL_IS_NOT_COMPARAB.occasion: Completing the day's IV sweep (TSM and AVGO, the two names the 14:14Z run left unswept) took both to n=20, the IV method's threshold for quoting a percentile. It is the first time two names crossed it in the same run, which is what made the comparison visible at all.
_A_RAW_IV_RV_RATIO_LEVEL_IS_NOT_COMPARAB.THE_FINDING: Two ratios 1.7% apart sit at opposite ends of their own distributions. AVGO's ratio is NUMERICALLY HIGHER than TSM's and is near the CHEAPEST premium it has printed; TSM's is LOWER and is near the RICHEST. A run reading 'both ~0.97, both mildly cheap, similar' -- which is exactly how a raw ratio invites being read -- gets both names backwards at once. THE RATIO'S LEVEL CARRIES NO CROSS-SECTIONAL INFORMATION; only its rank against the same name's own history does.
_A_RAW_IV_RV_RATIO_LEVEL_IS_NOT_COMPARAB.the_mechanism: iv_rv_ratio is implied divided by that name's OWN trailing realized, so the denominator is name-specific and its typical level is a property of the name's vol structure -- how much of its realized variance is gap-driven, how much event premium its chain habitually carries. Dividing by realized removes the vol LEVEL from the comparison but not the name's characteristic BIAS. AVGO habitually runs a higher ratio than TSM, so the same number means different things.
_A_RAW_IV_RV_RATIO_LEVEL_IS_NOT_COMPARAB.what_it_does_and_does_not_change: It does NOT weaken the raw-versus-ex-gap pairing rule (2026-08-20), which is about one name across time and stands unchanged -- note both names here also show the classic gap artifact, TSM raw 0.9641 vs ex-gap 1.3669 and AVGO 0.9803 vs 1.2484, so BOTH look cheap raw and rich ex-gap. It adds a second, orthogonal caution: the existing rule guards a name's ratio against its own window; this one guards one name's ratio against ANOTHER name's. Before ranking candidates on IV cheapness, rank each on its OWN percentile, and say n -- at n=20 over ~4 weeks a percentile is a rank within one regime, not a vol-of-vol estimate.
_A_RAW_IV_RV_RATIO_LEVEL_IS_NOT_COMPARAB.honest_scope: Changed no decision -- no options entry was armed in either track this run, and IV sanity is a NECESSARY condition that never supplies a thesis. Also n=20 for both names is the bare minimum the method permits; the 95th and 10th percentiles are 19-of-20 and 2-of-20 counts, not stable estimates. The finding is the DIVERGENCE at nearly equal levels, which does not depend on either percentile being precise.

_A_FEED_HOLE_IN_THE_CANDIDATE_BAR_PRODUC.headline: Every prior feed-hole finding in this repo documents the hole landing in the DENOMINATOR, depressing a trailing baseline and MANUFACTURING confirmation. Today a hole landed on the CANDIDATE BAR ITSELF and would have VETOED a break that actually participated at 148.6% of baseline. The bias direction is a property of WHERE the hole lands, not of the defect.

the_measurement.holed_bucket_1: 14:30 reported 42,373 vs 1-minute sum 60,068 -- bucket 29.4% BELOW, so per the 2026-08-28 direction rule the BUCKET is the holed side; use 60,068. the_measurement.holed_bucket_2: 14:50 reported 7,799 vs 1-minute sum 196,582 -- the bucket understates by 96.0%, a 25x error, and equals its 14:53 one-minute constituent (7,799) EXACTLY: the single-constituent signature.
the_measurement.consequence: Raw, the 14:50 candidate bar reads 7,799 = 5.9% of the trailing-30 baseline -- an emphatic volume veto. Corrected, it reads 196,582 = 148.6% of the same baseline, and with its holding bar (14:55, 138,928 = 105.0%) the two-bar window clears at 126.8%. The feed alone would have flipped a CONFIRMED break into a vetoed one.

_A_FEED_HOLE_IN_THE_CANDIDATE_BAR_PRODUC.the_transferable_lesson: The repo's framing has been 'a hole depresses the denominator and manufactures the confirmation the filter exists to withhold' -- always the dangerous, too-eager direction. That framing invites a run about to DECLINE anyway to skip the reconciliation, reasoning that the error only ever makes it too eager and it is not being eager. That reasoning is now measured to be wrong. A hole in the numerator vetoes a real break; a hole in the denominator confirms a fake one. RECONCILE ALWAYS, including on runs that expect to decline -- the direction of the bias is not knowable before the reconciliation.
_A_FEED_HOLE_IN_THE_CANDIDATE_BAR_PRODUC.honest_scope: This changed no decision. The break was declined on three independent grounds that have nothing to do with volume (IV sanity, index disagreement, magnitude), so the corrected volume clause was not load-bearing today -- which is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly. n=2 holed buckets in one 60-minute window on one symbol; the offset carries no information (14:30 and 14:50 here, :05/:05/:20 on 08-28, :45 on 08-27), so reconcile every window you intend to use.

_A_RECONCILED_BUCKET_CAN_GO_HOLED_ON_A_L.headline: The repo's feed model has two rules: a holed bucket does not heal (_A_HOLED_BUCKET_DOES_NOT_HEAL), and 1-minute bars are revised after they close (2026-08-26). Nobody had recorded the REVERSE of the first: a bucket that reconciled EXACTLY at one fetch reading as holed at a later one. Measured today on the same symbol, same session, 13 minutes apart.

the_measurement.at_15_03Z: The 15:03Z run measured it at 138,928 and recorded it among the 'clean buckets -- all EXACT matches to their 1-minute sums' in _A_FEED_HOLE_IN_THE_CANDIDATE_BAR_PRODUCES_A_FALSE_NEGATIVE. It was used as the HOLDING BAR of that run's two-bar confirmation window.
the_measurement.at_15_16Z: The same bucket reads 11,000 -- which equals its own 14:55 one-minute constituent (11,000) EXACTLY: the single-constituent signature this file teaches you to recognize as a hole.
the_measurement.and_the_other_leg_moved_too: The 1-minute sum 14:55..14:59 is now 11,000 + 21,185 + 31,074 + 27,600 + 23,241 = 114,100, against the 138,928 the earlier fetch reconciled to -- the minute series itself was revised DOWN 17.9% (-24,828). So it is not that one side went bad while the other held; BOTH legs of the reconciliation moved between fetches.
the_measurement.the_control_in_the_same_pull: The 14:50 bucket still reads 7,799 against a 1-minute sum of 196,582 -- byte-identical to the 15:03Z measurement. So _A_HOLED_BUCKET_DOES_NOT_HEAL is re-confirmed in the same window that refutes the durability of a clean reading. Holes are sticky; CLEAN readings are not.

_A_RECONCILED_BUCKET_CAN_GO_HOLED_ON_A_L.the_measured_consequence: The 15:03Z run's two-bar window read candidate 196,582 = 148.6% of a ~132,290 trailing baseline and holding bar 138,928 = 105.0%, clearing on both legs at a 126.8% two-bar mean. Recomputed on today's numbers the holding bar is 114,100 = 86.3% -- it FLIPS from pass to fail. The two-bar mean still clears at 117.4%, so the verdict direction is unchanged, but one of its two legs inverted with no new trading activity whatsoever. On a reading nearer the line, that flips the answer.
_A_RECONCILED_BUCKET_CAN_GO_HOLED_ON_A_L.THE_RULE: A RECONCILIATION IS NOT A DURABLE FACT ABOUT A BAR -- it is a measurement of two feeds agreeing at one instant. RE-RUN THE RECONCILIATION IN THE RUN THAT USES IT. Never inherit a reconciled volume figure from an earlier run's key, however carefully that run measured it, and never treat 'this bucket was verified clean' as a property the bucket now carries.
_A_RECONCILED_BUCKET_CAN_GO_HOLED_ON_A_L.why_it_matters_beyond_bookkeeping: The 15:03Z finding's whole lesson was RECONCILE ALWAYS, including on runs expecting to decline, because the bias direction is not knowable in advance. This extends it one step: reconciling once is not enough either, because the thing you reconciled can change underneath a later run that is reasoning from your written figure. The handoff is the vulnerable surface -- exactly the shape of _HANDOFF_CONJUNCTIONS_CLEAR_OUT_OF_ORDER and of the standing rule that a numbered clause must be re-derived, not quoted.
_A_RECONCILED_BUCKET_CAN_GO_HOLED_ON_A_L.honest_scope: This changed no decision. Today's QQQ 20-day reclaim was declined on three grounds that never touch volume -- the level fails its own repeated-crossing prescreen (_THE_QQQ_20DAY_IS_NOT_A_TRADEABLE_LEVEL), the index tape disagrees (SPY -0.268% and still 0.12% BELOW its own 20-day while QQQ sits +0.34% above), and the late-entry arithmetic puts the stop back on the trigger level. _A_PERCENTAGE_PREMIUM_TARGET_RIDES_UP_WI.status: DURABLE entry-timing rule. Read as the MIRROR of _CONFIRMED_TRIGGERS_HAVE_A_SHELF_LIFE (which measures a break that RETRACES) and as a PARTIAL CORRECTION to the 2026-08-28T15:05Z LATE-ENTRY DETECTOR, whose stop-half did NOT fire here. Not session-scoped; do not delete at the bell.
_A_PERCENTAGE_PREMIUM_TARGET_RIDES_UP_WI.claim: A breakout that FOLLOWS THROUGH does not become a better late entry. For a track whose target is a PERCENTAGE OF PREMIUM (+20-40% TACTICAL), the target is measured off the entry premium -- and the entry premium rises with spot. So the UNDERLYING EXTENSION still required is approximately INVARIANT to the follow-through: the target recedes at roughly the rate you advance toward it. Waiting for a break to prove itself is therefore self-defeating on a percentage-target track -- it buys confidence at no improvement in reachability.
_A_PERCENTAGE_PREMIUM_TARGET_RIDES_UP_WI.measured_on: The QQQ 20-day SMA reclaim that the 15:05Z run declined, re-measured 18 minutes later after clean follow-through. Contract QUOTED, not modelled (the repo's most-repeated bug): QQQ 2026-09-18 723C at 15:20:57Z -- bid 7.55 / ask 7.59, mid 7.570, spread 0.53% of mid, delta 0.4655, gamma 0.01838, theta -0.4548/day (-6.0%), IV 0.1793, OI 1,199, vol 175, $757.00/contract. A FLAWLESS vehicle: inside the 0.40-0.60 delta band, an order of magnitude inside the <=3%-of-mid TACTICAL gate, and squarely in the $300-1,000 band. The decline is about gates, never about the contract.

the_arithmetic.at_15_01Z: spot 718.89 (+0.198% above the 717.5105 20-day). Same contract back-priced at ~6.94. +20% = $138.80, plus one day's theta $45.48 = $184.28 needed, at ~0.48 average delta = 3.84 pts -> QQQ ~722.7, an extension of +0.53% from spot.
the_arithmetic.at_15_20Z: spot 720.24 (+0.392% above the same level). Quoted mid 7.570. +20% = $151.40, plus theta $45.48 = $196.88 at ~0.48 average delta = 4.10 pts -> QQQ ~724.3, an extension of +0.56% from spot.
the_arithmetic.the_result: The index advanced +1.35 pts (+0.19%) and the required extension went 0.53% -> 0.56%. It did NOT shrink; it grew marginally. Ten consecutive 5-minute bars of genuine follow-through (717.450 -> 720.320, +2.87 pts) bought exactly ZERO improvement in reachability.
the_arithmetic.mechanism: delta converts spot into premium in BOTH directions. A rising spot raises the premium the +20% is computed on, so the dollar target rises ~delta x (spot advance) -- the same quantity by which spot approached it. Gamma makes it slightly worse, not better, because the higher-delta contract needs a proportionally larger dollar gain. A FIXED-DOLLAR or LEVEL-BASED target would behave the opposite way; a PERCENTAGE-OF-PREMIUM target is invariant by construction.

_A_PERCENTAGE_PREMIUM_TARGET_RIDES_UP_WI.the_correction_to_the_late_entry_detecto: The 2026-08-28T15:05Z detector says: price the -30% stop in UNDERLYING terms, and if it sits at or below the trigger level the entry is too late. Measured here, that half DOES NOT FIRE. -30% = $227.10; at ~0.42 average delta net of one day's theta that is ~4.3-5.4 QQQ points, putting the stop at ~714.9-715.9 -- 1.6 to 2.6 points BELOW the 717.5105 trigger level. An ordinary retest of the 20-day costs ~16-22%, NOT the full stop. So this entry is late WITHOUT having its stop pushed onto the level. THE DETECTOR HAS TWO HALVES AND THEY FIRE INDEPENDENTLY: the stop-proximity half is about how far above the level you entered relative to the contract's risk budget, and the magnitude half is about whether the target is reachable at all. Citing 'late entry' as one undifferentiated objection would have been a check passing for the wrong reason -- the repo's most-repeated defect. Say WHICH half fired.
_A_PERCENTAGE_PREMIUM_TARGET_RIDES_UP_WI.why_it_was_still_declined: Two gates unchanged from 15:05Z and neither is about entry timing: (1) IV SANITY -- QQQ ex-gap iv_rv_ratio 1.2664, raw 0.9538 at the 100.0th percentile of the name's own 20 readings; a raw ratio under 1.0 reads as cheap premium and is simultaneously the richest relative reading QQQ has on record here. (2) INDEX DISAGREEMENT -- SPY 768.08 is still -0.127% BELOW its own 20-day (769.053) while QQQ sits +0.392% above; the divergence NARROWED (was -0.179%) but did not resolve, and breadth stayed poor (XLV -2.37%, XLF weak, strength narrow and tech-led). Plus the magnitude half above. Three gates, none of them the CPI catalyst -- 09-11 CPI is outside a Tue->Wed scalp window and importing it would be the documented category error.
_A_PERCENTAGE_PREMIUM_TARGET_RIDES_UP_WI.honest_scope: n=1: one contract, one 18-minute window, one name. The invariance is approximate, not exact -- gamma, the theta charge and the average-delta approximation each move it by a few basis points. What is firm is the SIGN: follow-through did not reduce the required extension. It changed no decision (the trade was already declined on two independent gates and remains declined), which is the only condition under which an entry-timing rule can be audited credibly.
_A_PERCENTAGE_PREMIUM_TARGET_RIDES_UP_WI.feed_note: The 14:55Z 5-minute bucket read QQQ 11,000 and SPY 9,708 against neighbours of 173,367/130,905 and 125,304/104,774 -- the cross-symbol hole signature at one timestamp, per the 2026-08-27 rule. No volume clause in this run rested on it, so nothing propagated; recorded so a later run does not read it as a quiet tape.
_A_PERCENTAGE_PREMIUM_TARGET_RIDES_UP_WI.cross_validation_and_one_CORRECTION_to_t: A concurrent same-slot run (PR #1266, broker-read 15:15-15:16Z) reached the same DECLINE independently and agreed the late-entry arithmetic worsened -- cross-validation, not conflict. But it listed among its grounds 'stop lands back on the trigger', which THIS run's QUOTED measurement REFUTES: the -30% stop sits at ~QQQ 714.9-715.9, i.e. 1.6-2.6 points BELOW the 717.5105 trigger level, so a retest costs ~16-22% and not the full stop. That claim was MODELLED; this one is quoted off a live chain (mid 7.570, delta 0.4655, theta -0.4548). The repo's most-repeated bug is exactly this substitution, and it is worth flagging even though BOTH runs declined and the outcome is identical -- a conclusion held for a reason that is not true is a check passing for the wrong reason, and the next instance would inherit it. The magnitude half fired; the stop half did not.

The 2026-09-02 change was verified on what it made the system DO -- the time stop fires -- and nobody re-read what the system SAYS. _TIME_STOPPED_NAMES_RE_PRESENT_AS_CLEAN_.headline: A sell REMOVES the position from `positions`, and the RSI(2) setup table's HELD marker is derived from OPEN positions only -- so the moment a name is exited it re-presents on the next run as a clean, unannotated BUY candidate. `_closed_positions` was read by NOTHING (grep: 0 references in report.py). First instance is DATED: LLY time-stops 2026-09-10 while sitting at RSI2 0.9, the LOWEST reading on the entire board.
_TIME_STOPPED_NAMES_RE_PRESENT_AS_CLEAN_.the_asymmetry_that_is_the_actual_finding: The exposure is NOT equal across the three equity exits, and this is the transferable half. A TAKE-PROFIT is SELF-IMMUNIZING: it fires at RSI2>=70, the opposite end of the oscillator from the RSI2<10 entry screen, so a name sold that way physically cannot appear on the setup table on its way out. A TIME STOP has NO such immunity -- it is indexed on ELAPSED TIME, which is uncorrelated with RSI2, so a time-stopped name exits at whatever RSI2 it happens to carry, including deeply oversold. The two exits look equally safe from the outside and only one of them is.

_A_PRE_EVENT_ANALYST_PRICE_TARGET_IS_A_O.THE_FINDING: A mean analyst price target published BEFORE an event does not reprice with the event -- so 'spot crossed below the mean PT' is a statement about SPOT, not about analyst opinion. The gap opened because price moved, not because anyone re-underwrote the name. That makes such a PT a ONE-DIRECTIONAL instrument: it can validly REJECT (if a structurally stale-HIGH target ALREADY sits below spot, downside is confirmed a fortiori -- which is exactly the inference the 14:14Z run drew, and it was sound) but it can NEVER CONFIRM (a target above spot merely means nobody has updated yet). Reading the crossing as restored upside treats an un-revised number as a post-event valuation.
_A_PRE_EVENT_ANALYST_PRICE_TARGET_IS_A_O.why_this_is_dangerous_rather_than_merely: The arithmetic is IDENTICAL in both directions -- one subtraction, one sign. Nothing in the comparison announces which direction is licensed, so a future run re-testing the 14:14Z rejection finds its binding fact reversed and reasonably concludes the objection is spent. Same family as the repo's cross-symbol feed-hole rule (agreement across symbols evidences a hole; a clean neighbour evidences nothing) and the min_ticks pre-screen (a coarse tick kills a chain; a fine tick proves nothing) -- a test that is real in one direction and vacuous in the other.
_A_PRE_EVENT_ANALYST_PRICE_TARGET_IS_A_O.the_detector: Before letting an analyst PT move a verdict, check its PUBLICATION TIMESTAMP against the event, and quote the PT's own change over the same window beside the spot's. If the PT moved <1% while spot moved ~10%, the PT is pre-event and may only be used to reject. A poll of ~30 analysts cannot reprice within hours regardless of how many notes cross the tape.

_TIME_STOP_EXECUTION_PATH_PREFLIGHTED_TH.WHAT_THIS_PROVES_AND_WHAT_IT_DOES_NOT: It is an ELIMINATION, not a guarantee, and the distinction is this file's own: review_option_order FALSE-GREENS a multi-leg order that the place endpoint then rejects 400, so a clean review is never proof of executability -- only a filled order is. What a clean review DOES prove is the removal of every obstacle the broker surfaces at review time, and the 2026-08-24 collateral measurement established the other half: a review that RAISES an alert is real and must be honoured. So tomorrow's exit is not blocked by anything checkable in advance; that is a genuine narrowing and it is all that is claimed.
_TIME_STOP_EXECUTION_PATH_PREFLIGHTED_TH.THE_TRAP_THIS_ACTUALLY_CAUGHT_use_quanti: HARD RULE 3 reads 'dollar-based MARKET orders, market_hours=regular_hours (fractional only works this way)'. That rule was written for ENTRIES and is correct for them. Applied literally to a full EXIT it orphans a residual sliver: a dollar_amount sell is converted to shares off last_trade_price, so any tick between conversion and fill leaves a fraction of a share behind. THE PRECEDENT IS IN THIS REPO -- on 2026-08-13 Ryan's GTC stop filled 11 of 11.810007 IREN shares and he had to place a SECOND market order to clear the 0.810007 residual. A stranded sliver on an autonomous time stop is worse than untidy: the ledger removes the position on a SELL fill, so the book and the broker would silently disagree from that moment on, and the next run's reconciliation would report drift it cannot explain.
_TIME_STOP_EXECUTION_PATH_PREFLIGHTED_TH.THE_RULE: Any FULL exit -- time stop, take-profit, thesis sell, rotation sell -- is placed with `quantity` set to the position's exact broker quantity from get_equity_positions (up to 6 decimals), NEVER with dollar_amount. Read the quantity from the BROKER immediately before sending, not from holdings.json: the broker is the arbiter, and a partial fill or a dividend-driven fractional adjustment would make the ledger figure wrong. dollar_amount remains correct for entries, where there is no exact target quantity to hit.

_HARD_PINNING_A_MODE_IS_WHAT_CAUSES_THE_.headline: The report workflow's schedule-backstop branch hard-pinned MODE=morning and carried a comment claiming that NOT consulting the clock is what makes a late fire safe. The reasoning is exactly inverted: the clock is the only thing that knows the fire was late, so refusing to read it is what GUARANTEES the mislabel. Found by asking a routine question -- why has today's report not landed yet -- and reading the workflow rather than the file.
_HARD_PINNING_A_MODE_IS_WHAT_CAUSES_THE_.the_measurement: GitHub Actions run id 34255265460, workflow stock-report.yml, event=schedule, run_started_at 2026-09-08T17:08:10Z -- 4h08m after its '0 13 * * 1-5' slot. It wrote latest_morning.md stamped 'MORNING (2026-09-08 17:10 UTC)'. 17:08:10Z is 12:08 CDT, i.e. mid-session. So a mid-session full scan was written into the file the playbook designates as the day's MORNING scan. Both properties the comment asserted are false: it DID clobber latest_morning.md mid-session, and it DID mislabel.
_HARD_PINNING_A_MODE_IS_WHAT_CAUSES_THE_.why_it_matters_and_the_ordering_inversio: The content of a mid-session scan is fine; the LABEL and the TIMESTAMP are what break. Two harms. (a) A run reasoning about WHEN the signal was computed is wrong by four hours -- and this book has a live finding (_OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_EQUITY_ENTRIES) whose whole mechanism is that the RSI2 entry is computed on the PREVIOUS session's close. (b) The worse one: every consumer reads 'latest_morning.md / latest_intraday.md, WHICHEVER IS NEWER'. On 2026-09-08 the 17:10Z MORNING file was newer than the 17:02Z intraday for about an hour. Slip the backstop a little further -- past the last cron-job.org dispatch of the day -- and latest_morning.md becomes the newest file in the repo while containing the day's LAST scan. The freshness check then passes for the wrong reason, which is this file's most-repeated defect.
_HARD_PINNING_A_MODE_IS_WHAT_CAUSES_THE_.the_fix_applied_this_run: The schedule branch now uses the SAME wall-clock test the auto branch already uses: CTHOUR < 10 -> morning, else intraday. Verified rather than assumed: an ON-TIME 13:00Z fire is 08:00 CDT and still labels morning, so the backstop's stated intent is fully preserved; the actual 17:08Z fire is 12:08 CDT and would now label intraday, landing in the correct file. Leading-zero hours ('08', '09') were checked against the -lt comparison for an octal trap -- none, and the auto branch has relied on the identical expression in production for months. YAML re-parsed clean; diff 24/9.
_HARD_PINNING_A_MODE_IS_WHAT_CAUSES_THE_.the_transferable_lesson: A safeguard justified by what it REFUSES to look at deserves the same scrutiny as one justified by what it checks. 'Delay-proof because it doesn't consult the clock' reads like robustness and is actually the failure mode stated as a feature -- the branch cannot distinguish an on-time fire from a four-hour-late one precisely BECAUSE it discarded the one input that separates them. Related to the standing rule that a confidently-written rule is not evidence: this comment asserted a hard safety property ('can never mislabel') in absolute terms and was wrong, and it survived because nobody had a reason to read a workflow comment while the reports were landing.
_HARD_PINNING_A_MODE_IS_WHAT_CAUSES_THE_.honest_scope: This changed NO trading decision. Today's equity entry was already deferred to the >=14:15Z run for an independent and sufficient reason (no report has been generated at all yet on 09-09), and the mislabelled 09-08 file was superseded by a genuine 19:01Z intraday before any run traded off it. n=1 measured occurrence, though the mechanism is deterministic rather than probabilistic: it recurs on every late fire, and GitHub cron slipping hours is documented behaviour the workflow's own header already acknowledges. Recorded and fixed now precisely because a filter's inputs can only be audited credibly on a run where the audit does not license a trade.

_AN_SMA_FORWARD_PATH_IS_A_TWO_VARIABLE_P.THE_FINDING: market_brief.json has been publishing a `sma20_fwd_path_if_flat` for SPY and QQQ as a forward view of where the 20-day average is heading. The 2026-09-08 brief's SPY path was [769.20, 769.21, 769.34, 769.37] off a 769.2065 base -- flat to slightly RISING, and its prose said so: '20-day is RISING ~+0.23/session.' MEASURED THIS RUN off settled bars: the 20-day printed 769.0530 on 09-04 and 768.6995 on 09-08. It FELL both sessions, about -0.25/session. The path was wrong in SIGN within two sessions, and so was the sentence describing the average's direction.
_AN_SMA_FORWARD_PATH_IS_A_TWO_VARIABLE_P.THE_MECHANISM_verified_arithmetically_no: A moving average changes by (what ENTERS the window - what LEAVES it) / N. The published path computes only the LEAVING leg and freezes the entering leg at 'price stays flat' -- here, flat at the 2026-09-03 close of 773.17. Actual closes came in BELOW that assumption: 09-04 at 770.19 (-2.98) and 09-08 at 765.96 (-7.21). Predicted drag from that shortfall alone is -2.98/20 = -0.149 and then -7.21/20 = -0.3605, cumulative -0.5095. OBSERVED cumulative error against the path is -0.5105 (769.21 predicted vs 768.6995 actual). The two agree to 0.001, so the entering leg accounts for essentially ALL of the miss. This is a measurement, not a story.
_AN_SMA_FORWARD_PATH_IS_A_TWO_VARIABLE_P.SO_THE_PATH_IS_NOT_WRONG__IT_IS_MISLABEL: The arithmetic is correct for what it computes. It is a SENSITIVITY to what rolls out of the window, and it is published under a name and in a position that invite reading it as a FORECAST. Those are different objects: the first is a statement about the window's HISTORY and is exactly true; the second is a claim about the FUTURE and requires the price assumption to hold. Relabel it, do not delete it -- the leaving leg is genuinely useful and is the half a run cannot compute in its head.
_AN_SMA_FORWARD_PATH_IS_A_TWO_VARIABLE_P.WHY_IT_MATTERS_TODAY_which_is_the_only_r: The 09-08 brief a run would inherit says SPY 'spot 772.74 sits +3.53 over the 20d' and calls that average RISING. At 13:37Z today SPY is 763.79, which is 4.91 BELOW a 20-day that is FALLING. BOTH legs of the inherited description have inverted. That is the difference between 'holding above a rising short-term average' and 'below a rolling-over one' -- a materially different read of the same index, available to any run that recomputes and invisible to one that inherits.
_AN_SMA_FORWARD_PATH_IS_A_TWO_VARIABLE_P.THE_TRANSFERABLE_CLASS_and_this_is_the_s: This is the 2026-08-28 IV-forecast lesson arriving on a different instrument: 'a ratio has two moving parts; a forecast that freezes one will be right about the artifact and wrong about the level -- say which leg is held fixed when stating one.' There it was implied vol held fixed while the realized window moved; here it is spot held fixed while the entering bars moved. Two independent instruments, one mechanism, and in BOTH cases the frozen leg is the one the desk cannot observe in advance. That repetition is what upgrades it from an IV quirk to a class: ANY published projection over a rolling window must name its frozen leg IN THE FIELD NAME, or the next run will read a sensitivity as a forecast.
_AN_SMA_FORWARD_PATH_IS_A_TWO_VARIABLE_P.THE_DETECTOR: Cheap and total: before inheriting any moving-average level or its direction, recompute it on settled bars -- it is one get_equity_technical_indicators call the run needs anyway. If the inherited brief states a RELATIONSHIP ('spot is above/below', 'the average is rising/falling'), that relationship is the thing to re-derive, not the number, because a relationship can invert while the number moves only fractionally. SPY's 20-day moved 0.51 -- seven hundredths of one percent -- and the sign of the spot-versus-average relationship still flipped.
_AN_SMA_FORWARD_PATH_IS_A_TWO_VARIABLE_P.ACTION_TAKEN: market_brief.json for 2026-09-09 publishes recomputed SPY/QQQ 20- and 50-day levels through 2026-09-08 and deliberately does NOT republish a forward path, pointing here instead.
_AN_SMA_FORWARD_PATH_IS_A_TWO_VARIABLE_P.HONEST_SCOPE: This changed NO decision today, which is the only condition under which this kind of audit is credible: both options tracks were declined on independent grounds (TACTICAL on the regime capstone with PPI inside its own hold window; CORE on the trend-maturity gate), and no equity entry was available on report staleness regardless of any level. n=2 sessions on one instrument, one direction. The projection error is also SMALL in absolute terms (0.51 on 769) -- what makes it worth writing down is not the magnitude but that a sub-0.1% error was enough to invert the sign of the relationship a run actually reasons from.
_AN_SMA_FORWARD_PATH_IS_A_TWO_VARIABLE_P.CONCURRENT_RUN_CROSS_VALIDATION_and_the_: A sibling run executed this same slot at 13:33Z and INDEPENDENTLY found the same slope inversion, recomputing identical values (SPY sma20 768.6995, QQQ 717.3850) by a different method. Two independent measurements agreeing is the strongest form this evidence comes in. But the two runs ATTRIBUTE it differently, and the difference is the whole finding: the 13:33Z run wrote that the rollover is caused 'purely from late-August closes ROLLING OUT of the window'. That is true of the average's FALL and does not explain the published path's ERROR -- because the path already models exactly what leaves, and it still predicted a RISE. Only the ENTERING leg can account for a sign error in a projection that computed the leaving leg correctly, and the 0.001 agreement above shows it accounts for all of it. Both runs are right about what they measured; the leaving leg explains the level, the frozen entering leg explains the miss.
_AN_SMA_FORWARD_PATH_IS_A_TWO_VARIABLE_P.STATUS_the_field_was_REPUBLISHED_the_sam: The 13:33Z run republished sma20_fwd_path_if_flat for both indices with a corrected NEGATIVE slope (SPY [768.469, 768.143, 767.547, 767.028]). So this finding is not retrospective housekeeping -- it attaches to a live field a concurrent run wrote minutes ago, and the corrected path carries the identical frozen-leg assumption. market_brief.json key_levels now carries the READ_THE_FWD_PATHS_AS_A_SENSITIVITY_NOT_A_FORECAST caveat pointing here. The paths are KEPT, per the relabel-don't-delete recommendation: the leaving leg is genuinely useful and is the half a run cannot compute in its head.

_PERCENTILE_AND_RATIO_ARE_WEAKLY_CORRELA.why_today: The IV method says '<20 readings: IV/RV only; 20+: percentile vs own history.' Today's sweep is the 21st reading for all eight core names, so percentiles became citable for the FIRST TIME. That reads like an upgrade -- a better number replacing a cruder one. IT IS NOT. It is a SECOND, WEAKLY-CORRELATED question, and the day a new statistic unlocks is exactly the day a run is most likely to over-trust it.
_PERCENTILE_AND_RATIO_ARE_WEAKLY_CORRELA.the_measurement: Across the eight names measured together on the 2026-10-09 board (30 DTE), Spearman rank correlation of PERCENTILE vs EX-GAP IV/RV ratio = +0.262; percentile vs RAW ratio = +0.333. For contrast, raw vs ex-gap ratio = +0.786 -- those two DO track each other, because both are measured against realized vol and differ only in the denominator's treatment of gaps. The percentile is measuring something else entirely.

the_disagreements_by_name.TSLA: 95th percentile (the RICHEST reading in its own 21-row history) but ex-gap ratio 1.038 -- barely above fair vs realized. Five rank places apart, the widest split on the list.
the_disagreements_by_name.TSM: 40th percentile (cheap-ish for itself) but ex-gap ratio 1.337 -- the richest-but-one reading vs realized on the whole list. Four places apart, and the two measures point in OPPOSITE directions.
the_disagreements_by_name.AVGO: 10th percentile -- the cheapest IV it has printed in its own history -- yet ex-gap ratio 1.178, still rich vs realized. Four places apart. Its IV is at a personal low BECAUSE its post-earnings realized vol collapsed; relative to that lower realized it is not cheap at all.
the_disagreements_by_name.SPY_QQQ_NVDA: 0 places apart -- the two measures agree perfectly on three of eight. The split is not universal, which is what makes it dangerous: a run that spot-checks a name where they agree will conclude they are interchangeable.

_PERCENTILE_AND_RATIO_ARE_WEAKLY_CORRELA.the_mechanism_which_is_the_transferable_: A PERCENTILE asks 'is this name's implied vol high FOR THIS NAME, historically?' A RATIO asks 'is this name's implied vol high relative to what the stock is ACTUALLY DOING right now?' Those come apart whenever REALIZED vol has moved -- which is most of the time, and always after an event. Neither is 'the' cheapness measure. A contract is cheap to OWN only if implied is low against the movement you expect to collect, which is the ratio's question; the percentile only says where this name's vol sits in its own recent range.
_PERCENTILE_AND_RATIO_ARE_WEAKLY_CORRELA.HONEST_SCOPE_and_it_is_a_real_limit: n=8 names on ONE day. A Spearman of +0.262 at n=8 is NOT statistically distinguishable from 0 nor from +0.6. So the defensible claim is 'these two are NOT interchangeable and must both be quoted', NOT 'they are uncorrelated'. Do not carry the +0.262 forward as though it were an estimated constant -- re-measure it as the series lengthens.
_PERCENTILE_AND_RATIO_ARE_WEAKLY_CORRELA.the_second_caveat_which_is_arguably_bigg: The percentile base is 20 PRIOR readings spanning only 2026-08-11..2026-09-08 -- about four weeks, one regime, one earnings cycle. The IV method's 20-reading threshold is a MINIMUM SAMPLE, not a guarantee of meaning. 'TSLA is at the 95th percentile' currently means 'higher than 19 of its 20 readings from the last four weeks', which is a much weaker statement than the phrase implies. Say it the long way when it decides anything.
_PERCENTILE_AND_RATIO_ARE_WEAKLY_CORRELA.the_rule: QUOTE BOTH, ALWAYS, AND NAME WHICH ONE IS DOING THE WORK IN A DECISION. When they disagree, the disagreement IS the finding -- it usually means realized vol has repriced recently -- and it should be investigated, not resolved by preferring whichever number is newer.
_PERCENTILE_AND_RATIO_ARE_WEAKLY_CORRELA.honest_scope_changed_no_decision: This changed NO decision today. Both options tracks were declined before the percentiles were consulted -- TACTICAL on the PPI catalyst window (structural, tape-independent), CORE on the ex-gap ratio and the pre-CPI timing. A filter's inputs can only be audited credibly on a run where the audit does not license a trade.
