_A_RUN_COMMITTED_ITS_STALE_CLONE_OVER_MA.the_mechanism_and_it_is_the_transferable: A remote session's repo is cloned ONCE at container start and never re-pulls on its own. On a repo that commits roughly every fifteen minutes, CLONE-TIME CONTENT IS NOT MASTER'S CONTENT -- by mid-session it is hours or days behind. A run that reads a file into memory at start, edits its own copy, and writes it back is not editing master's version of that file; it is REPLACING master's version with a stale one. Git raises nothing, because from git's point of view the run simply authored a large legitimate change on a correct parent. The PR merges cleanly for the same reason.
_A_RUN_COMMITTED_ITS_STALE_CLONE_OVER_MA.why_every_check_passed: This is the file's most-repeated defect -- a check that passes for the wrong reason -- arriving one artifact to the left of where the checks point. The 16:15Z run's BROKER reconciliation was genuinely correct and genuinely clean (4 equities + 1 hedge, matched on qty AND basis, both order endpoints empty), and its journal entry is accurate about the account in every particular. 'ZERO DRIFT' was measured against the BROKER. NOTHING IN THE RUN LOOP MEASURES DRIFT AGAINST MASTER. The two existing repo-side checks both miss it by construction: (a) the branch-vs-master drift check asks whether commits have PILED UP UNMERGED, and here they had not; (b) the `git diff --stat` rule exists and would have caught this instantly -- a -2,503-line stat on a re-verification run is unmissable -- but it is written up as a JSON-SERIALIZATION noise detector ("a diff far larger than the change you made means a formatting mismatch, not a content change"), so a run that reads it as an indent/ensure_ascii check has no reason to run it on report.py or a workflow yaml.

the_fix_two_halves_both_cheap.1_before_editing: Re-sync the worktree to master BEFORE touching any tracked file: `git fetch origin master && git checkout -B <branch> origin/master`. Do this at the TOP of the run, not at the end. Reading a file off disk without it reads the clone, not the repo.
the_fix_two_halves_both_cheap.2_before_committing: `git diff --stat origin/master` and read it as a WHOLE-RUN assertion, not a per-file formatting check: every file listed must be one you meant to change, and a no-op re-verification run must show exactly ONE file (trade_journal.json) at roughly +12 lines. ANY deletion count in the hundreds, or any appearance of report.py / a workflow / a report .md on a run that touched none of them, is a stale-clone overwrite -- `git checkout origin/master -- <file>` and re-apply your own change on top.

_A_RUN_COMMITTED_ITS_STALE_CLONE_OVER_MA.generalization: Name the CLASS, per this file's own standing instruction, because the sibling cases are already visible: any artifact a run reads once at start and writes back later carries the same staleness, and the window is the length of the run. The repo is only the instance that got measured. The rule is: RE-READ IMMEDIATELY BEFORE WRITING, from the authoritative source -- the broker for positions, origin/master for files -- never from the copy you took when the run began. That is the same principle the CONCURRENT-RUN COLLISION rule reached for orders on 2026-08-28 ("the broker is the arbiter"), applied to the second of the two things a run persists.
_A_RUN_COMMITTED_ITS_STALE_CLONE_OVER_MA.what_it_would_have_cost_if_unrepaired: No trade was affected THIS run -- the reverted reports are stale, and a stale report BARS signal-sourced equity trades, so the immediate failure mode was conservative. The real exposure was next-run and infrastructural: (a) the reverted _realized_options_pnl_today object reads trading_day_et 2026-09-04 with both throttles at zero, which is exactly the over-authorization hazard the ledger's own _schema_note describes -- a run believing it holds a fresh 8-entry budget breaches the limit without erroring; (b) the reverted heartbeat would have invited the next post-open run to re-stamp and re-roll daily artifacts already rolled; (c) the reverted report.py and workflow are LIVE CODE that the GitHub Actions cron executes, so every subsequent report would have regenerated with two known bugs re-armed.
_A_RUN_COMMITTED_ITS_STALE_CLONE_OVER_MA.remediation: Repaired by the 2026-09-09T16:22Z run: all ten files restored from e015108 via `git checkout e015108 -- <files>`, verified as the exact inverse of the revert (+2,503 / -403). UNION, not a side-pick, per the concurrent-run rule: the 16:15Z run's own journal entry is genuine work and was re-appended on top of the restored 1,165-entry journal, annotated. Ryan notified once.

restore_VERIFIED_COMPLETE_2026-09-09T16:.verdict: RESTORE IS SOUND. No residue, nothing still missing. A later run may stop re-checking this incident.
restore_VERIFIED_COMPLETE_2026-09-09T16:.method_and_it_is_the_reusable_half: Do NOT verify a restore by reading the restore commit's own diff -- that only shows what the restore run BELIEVED it was putting back, which is the same class of self-report that let the revert through. Compare master against the BAD COMMIT'S PARENT, which is the pre-revert truth, one file at a time: `git diff --quiet bfea3b4^ origin/master -- <file>`. Silent exit = that file is byte-identical to what existed before the revert. This costs one command per file and is independent of every claim either run made.
restore_VERIFIED_COMPLETE_2026-09-09T16:.result: Of the ten files bfea3b4 reverted, EIGHT are byte-identical to bfea3b4^: .github/workflows/stock-report.yml, report.py, automation_heartbeat.json, daily_options_report.md, iv_history.json, latest_intraday.md, latest_morning.md, market_brief.json. The two that differ do so as PURE ADDITIONS with zero deletions -- holdings.json +26/-0 and trade_journal.json +24/-0 -- which is the restore run's own new content (this finding key and its journal entry), not surviving damage. Zero deletions across all ten is the assertion that matters.
restore_VERIFIED_COMPLETE_2026-09-09T16:.why_this_was_worth_a_command: The two highest-severity items were LIVE CODE the GitHub Actions cron executes on a schedule no run controls: report.py's two 2026-09-08 fixes and the workflow's late-cron mislabel fix. A partial restore there fails SILENTLY and in the worst place -- it would poison the signal source every future run reads, while every broker reconciliation continued to pass. Confirming they are byte-identical is what closes the incident.

_A_SHALLOW_CLONE_MANUFACTURES_A_PHANTOM_.headline: `git fetch` reporting a FORCED UPDATE, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` returning NO, are BOTH artifacts of a shallow clone and are NOT evidence that master was rewritten. Master was healthy throughout. The alarm is dangerous because the obvious remediation it invites -- re-committing known-good content over master -- IS this morning's stale-clone failure.
_A_SHALLOW_CLONE_MANUFACTURES_A_PHANTOM_.what_was_observed: This run's opening `git fetch origin master` printed `+ d2a176e...881af6f master -> origin/master (forced update)`. The `+` prefix and the word 'forced' mean git could not prove a fast-forward. Follow-up `git merge-base --is-ancestor d2a176e 881af6f` exited non-zero (NOT an ancestor), and `git log origin/master --grep=#1254` plus a date-windowed log both returned EMPTY -- i.e. the merge commit for PR #1254 (2026-09-08T12:28Z), which certainly WAS on master, appeared to have been dropped from master's history.
_A_SHALLOW_CLONE_MANUFACTURES_A_PHANTOM_.what_it_actually_was: The container's clone is SHALLOW. `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` returns true; `git rev-list --count origin/master` is 98; `.git/shallow` pins the boundary at 19abe21 (2026-09-08T18:35Z). d2a176e is 2026-09-08T12:28Z, i.e. it PREDATES the shallow boundary. `git cat-file -t d2a176e` still returns 'commit' -- the object survives from the original clone -- but the commits CONNECTING it to master's tip were never fetched. With the connecting history absent, git cannot compute ancestry, so it reports the ref move as forced and --is-ancestor answers NO. Both answers are about the LOCAL CLONE's contents, not about the remote's history.
_A_SHALLOW_CLONE_MANUFACTURES_A_PHANTOM_.why_this_is_worth_a_key_and_not_a_shrug: The desk had a stale-clone incident at 16:15Z TODAY (see _A_RUN_COMMITTED_ITS_STALE_CLONE_OVER_MASTER_AND_REVERTED_TEN_FILES) in which a run reverted ten files on master by committing clone-time contents on a correct parent. The natural post-incident instinct is to verify master's integrity from inside the container on the next run. A run doing exactly that gets a LOUD false positive -- 'forced update', 'not an ancestor', 'the PR #1254 merge is missing from master' -- and the natural fix for a suspected force-push is to restore master from the content you hold locally. That is precisely the destructive action that caused the morning's incident. THE FALSE ALARM POINTS AT THE TRAP.
_A_SHALLOW_CLONE_MANUFACTURES_A_PHANTOM_.the_pair_is_the_useful_object: These two defects are mirror images and both come from the same root -- a container clone is not the repository. The stale-clone bug is SILENT: nothing errors, the parent is correct, the PR merges cleanly, and the damage is only visible in `git diff --stat origin/master`. The shallow-clone bug is LOUD: git shouts 'forced update' and means nothing by it. A desk that learns only the first lesson distrusts its clone's CONTENT while still trusting its clone's HISTORY, which is the half that just cried wolf.
detector: Before treating ANY ancestry, fast-forward or force-push signal as real, run `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`. If it is true, ancestry across the shallow boundary is UNKNOWABLE locally, and `--is-ancestor` exiting non-zero is not evidence of a rewrite.

A commit older than `.git/shallow`'s boundary will always look 'dropped' to `git log --grep` and to date-windowed logs, because those only search what was fetched. An empty search result over a shallow range is not an absence in the repo.

To actually answer the question, ASK THE REMOTE, which is the arbiter here exactly as the broker is the arbiter for positions: `git fetch --unshallow` (or a deeper --depth), or query the GitHub API for the commit. Never answer it from local refs alone.
NEVER 'restore' master on the strength of a local ancestry check. Restoration is only ever justified by a diff against a freshly-fetched origin/master, per the 16:22Z restore protocol.
_A_SHALLOW_CLONE_MANUFACTURES_A_PHANTOM_.master_verified_healthy_this_run: Working tree checked out at origin/master 881af6f via `git checkout -B <branch> origin/master`; `git diff --stat origin/master` is EMPTY. The 16:33Z run's verification of all ten restored files stands and was not redone.
_A_SHALLOW_CLONE_MANUFACTURES_A_PHANTOM_.honest_scope: This changed NO decision. No trade was gated on it, master was already verified healthy by the 16:33Z run, and this run traded nothing in either book for reasons entirely unrelated. It is recorded because it would have licensed a destructive action on some FUTURE run -- which is the only kind of near-miss worth a key. n=1: one fetch, one container. The shallow depth is set by the session harness and may differ between containers, so the boundary date is not a constant -- read `.git/shallow`, never assume it.

_BOUNCE_STRENGTH_WAS_A_SCREEN_NOT_THE_TE.subject: The 15:20Z and 15:35Z runs held MDLZ partly on the reason 'the bounce is WEAKER now (61.755 / 61.610) than when that plan was written (61.855), so there is no new argument against it.' At 18:16Z the bounce is 62.075 -- STRONGER than 61.855 and the strongest print of the session, with RSI2 75.5 vs the 74.5 that stood when the plan was written. By those runs' own stated criterion the question re-opens.
_BOUNCE_STRENGTH_WAS_A_SCREEN_NOT_THE_TE.what_the_reason_actually_was: A SCREEN, not the test. Bounce-strength is a cheap sufficient reason to DECLINE to re-open a settled question -- if the price is worse than when the decision was made, there is trivially nothing new to discuss. It was never a NECESSARY condition for holding. The load-bearing reason at 14:12Z was the THESIS: management reaffirming the 3-5% organic algorithm at the Barclays conference that day, plus cocoa supply in surplus, i.e. the bear case easing and the likely CAUSE of the bounce.
_BOUNCE_STRENGTH_WAS_A_SCREEN_NOT_THE_TE.why_the_distinction_bites: A stronger price print is not evidence against a thesis -- if anything, price confirming the cocoa-surplus / guidance-reaffirmation story is weak evidence FOR it. So the screen failing does NOT flip the answer; it only means the screen has stopped screening and the REAL test has to be run. A run that treats the screen as the test would read 'bounce stronger than when we decided' as a sell signal and realize a loss on a technical trigger -- exactly what the 2026-08-26 correction forbids.
_BOUNCE_STRENGTH_WAS_A_SCREEN_NOT_THE_TE.what_this_run_did: Re-ran the real test: HARD RULE 7 on live news (get_equity_news, 8 articles). No thesis break -- nothing adverse post-dates the 14:12Z research. VERDICT INTACT. HOLD, for the ORIGINAL reason, not the inherited one. Exit stays the 09-11 time stop, unconditional.
_BOUNCE_STRENGTH_WAS_A_SCREEN_NOT_THE_TE.the_class_this_belongs_to: This file's most-repeated defect, arriving in the mirror orientation: normally a CHECK PASSES FOR THE WRONG REASON. Here a check was about to FAIL for the wrong reason. Both have the same cause -- a cheap proxy standing in for an expensive test, with nothing recording which one is load-bearing. DETECTOR, and it is the transferable half: when a run declines to re-open a decision, it must say whether its reason is the DECISION'S reason or merely a SCREEN that made re-opening unnecessary. A screen that is not labelled as one gets inherited as doctrine, and the first run to see the screen fail will mistake that for the decision reversing.
_BOUNCE_STRENGTH_WAS_A_SCREEN_NOT_THE_TE.honest_scope: This changed NO decision -- MDLZ is held, as it was at 14:12Z, 15:20Z and 15:35Z. That is the only condition under which this kind of reasoning audit is credible: the audit did not license a trade. The stake is also small ($495.87 position, -$4.11 open, on a $3,915.88 account) and the position is condemned by the 09-11 time stop in 2 days regardless, so the entire disputed quantity is exit PRICE on a sale already scheduled, not whether to own MDLZ.

_CONCURRENT_RUNS_DIVERGED_ON_ONE_DISCRET.what_happened: Two scheduler-fired runs worked the SAME MDLZ exit-into-strength signal within seven minutes and reached OPPOSITE conclusions. The 18:15Z run re-opened the question, re-ran HARD RULE 7 on live news, found the thesis INTACT, and HELD -- writing _BOUNCE_STRENGTH_WAS_A_SCREEN_NOT_THE_TEST and merging as PR #1337. The 18:22Z run independently reached the same re-opening trigger, weighed it against the fixed 2026-09-11 time stop landing on CPI day, and SOLD -- order 6aa1a3b4-2a25-4513-a02d-4f7547e07f5a filled 18:21:40.199Z at 62.08. The fill is real and the position is flat; PR #1337's ledger, merged after the fill, still showed MDLZ open.
_CONCURRENT_RUNS_DIVERGED_ON_ONE_DISCRET.why_the_existing_safeguard_could_not_cat: The 2026-08-28 collision rule says the BROKER IS THE ARBITER and to re-read get_equity_orders immediately before acting. The 18:22Z run did exactly that, TWICE, and both reads were correctly EMPTY -- because the sibling had placed NO ORDER. That safeguard detects a sibling that ACTED; it is structurally blind to a sibling that DECIDED. A hold leaves no trace at the broker, so divergent discretion is invisible to a broker-first check by construction.
_CONCURRENT_RUNS_DIVERGED_ON_ONE_DISCRET.the_class_this_belongs_to: The documented collision hazard was always framed as DOUBLE-SPENDING -- two runs taking the same entry, breaching sizing and slot caps. This is the mirror case and it is not a capital-safety failure at all: nothing was double-spent, no cap was breached, exits are never throttled, and the book is simply flat one name. What collided was JUDGMENT on an explicitly OPTIONAL signal. The relay's whole design assumes one instance per slot, so it has no tie-breaker for two instances holding opposite views of the same discretionary call.
_CONCURRENT_RUNS_DIVERGED_ON_ONE_DISCRET.which_reasoning_was_better_answered_hone: Neither is clearly wrong; the call was genuinely two-sided and both runs did real work. The 18:22Z sell rests on three arguments that SURVIVE the sibling's write-up: the 09-11 time stop is non-discretionary so only PRICE was ever at issue; 09-11 is the CPI print date, so the mechanical sale would have executed into a macro-conditioned tape; and the warn-window rule in HARD RULE 5 / prompt v10 says a position about to be recycled is better sold into a bounce than out of one. But the sibling MEASURED something the seller did not, and it cuts against the seller: MDLZ's own-computed RSI2 on the last COMPLETED daily bar (09-08) is 54.41, so the report's 75.5 is an INTRADAY print on an incomplete bar. The seller's fourth argument -- 'RSI2 75.5 is the desk's own exit level' -- was therefore OVERSTATED and should have been checked against a completed bar before being leaned on. The sibling also made a point the seller underweighted: the freed capital has nowhere to go until the _cash_hold expires 09-14, so the exit bought a better price without buying a redeployment.
_CONCURRENT_RUNS_DIVERGED_ON_ONE_DISCRET.the_transferable_lesson: An RSI2 figure quoted from the intraday report is a LIVE-BAR print, not a completed-bar signal, and the two can differ by 20+ points. The entry side of this book already re-verifies report RSI2 against own daily bars before buying (see the MDLZ entry _note, which did exactly that). The EXIT side had no such habit, and this run leaned on an unverified 75.5 while a sibling computed 54.41 from the same data. RE-VERIFY A REPORT RSI2 AGAINST THE LAST COMPLETED BAR BEFORE IT DECIDES AN EXIT, exactly as the entry path already does -- a discretionary exit deserves the same evidentiary bar as a discretionary entry, and asymmetry between the two is how a book ends up better at buying than at selling.
_CONCURRENT_RUNS_DIVERGED_ON_ONE_DISCRET.what_is_NOT_claimed: No rule was broken by either run. Exits are never throttled, no approval was needed or claimed (HARD RULE 9 intact), the ownership gate did not apply (MDLZ was an agentic entry), and no capital was double-committed. This key exists so the relay can see that its collision doctrine covers only half the hazard.
_CONCURRENT_RUNS_DIVERGED_ON_ONE_DISCRET.resolution_applied: UNION per the standing rule, never by picking a side. The sibling's _BOUNCE_STRENGTH_WAS_A_SCREEN_NOT_THE_TEST key is preserved verbatim and its journal entry kept in full, ordered before this run's. The positions array and _closed_positions follow the BROKER, which is the arbiter: MDLZ is closed.

_A_KEY_RENAME_IN_A_TIME_SERIES_FAILS_TOW.headline: The 14:02Z IV sweep wrote all 8 core rows under NON-CANONICAL key names -- iv_rv_ratio_raw / iv_rv_ratio_ex_gap / strike -- against 20 consecutive sessions (2026-08-11..09-08) of iv_rv_ratio / iv_rv_ratio_ex_top2 / atm_strike. Measured across the file, not inferred: the rename is exactly one day wide and covers 8 of 8 core names, 3 keys each. NORMALIZED THIS RUN, labels only, no measured value altered.
_A_KEY_RENAME_IN_A_TIME_SERIES_FAILS_TOW.why_it_matters_and_it_is_the_direction_o: CLAUDE.md's standing rule is 'iv_history.json IS A TIME SERIES -- DIFF IT BEFORE QUOTING TODAY'S ROW', written after a four-session NVDA vol ramp hid in plain sight because nobody diffed. A KEY RENAME SILENTLY DEFEATS THAT DIFF, and it does so in two directions with opposite symptoms. Keying on the ESTABLISHED name returns None for today -- which reads as 'the sweep did not run', and is exactly what this run hit on its first pass. Keying on TODAY's name returns None for all 20 priors -- which reads as 'this name has no history'.
_A_KEY_RENAME_IN_A_TIME_SERIES_FAILS_TOW.the_dangerous_half: The second direction fails toward SILENCE, not error. A run computing the percentile off iv_rv_ratio_raw would find n=1, and the IV method's own rule ('<20 readings: IV/RV only; 20+: percentile') would then correctly suppress the percentile. THE DESK WOULD BELIEVE IT WAS HONOURING THE n<20 GUARD WHILE ACTUALLY HOLDING 21 READINGS IT COULD NOT SEE. That is this repo's most-repeated defect -- a check that passes for the wrong reason -- arriving through a field LABEL rather than through any run's reasoning.
_A_KEY_RENAME_IN_A_TIME_SERIES_FAILS_TOW.why_the_timing_is_the_worst_possible: The percentile capability is ONE DAY OLD. _FIRST_PERCENTILE_CAPABLE_IV_READING records 2026-09-08 as the first reading in this file's history to reach the 20-row threshold. A rename on day two would have destroyed the capability on the first day it existed, and destroyed it quietly.
_A_KEY_RENAME_IN_A_TIME_SERIES_FAILS_TOW.why_this_was_normalized_rather_than_flag: The file's own _comment sets the opposite precedent for the 2026-08-24 BOARD DISCONTINUITY: 'Flagged rather than silently corrected, because rewriting another run's measured rows is worse than recording the seam.' That precedent is correct AND does not apply here, and the distinction is the point. The board seam was a difference in WHAT WAS MEASURED (a 09-18 vs 09-25 expiry) -- rewriting it would have manufactured data. This is a difference in WHAT THE MEASUREMENT IS CALLED. Values, provenance and measured_utc are untouched; each normalized row carries a _schema_note recording the original names. Relabel a label; never relabel a measurement.
_A_KEY_RENAME_IN_A_TIME_SERIES_FAILS_TOW.honest_scope: IT CHANGED NO DECISION AND CAUSED NO WRONG NUMBER. The 14:02Z run computed its own percentile correctly (SPY pctile_vs_own_history 80.0 sits in the row), so the rename was in the OUTPUT only -- the defect was latent, aimed at future runs, and is recorded on a run where the audit licensed nothing. Cost this run: one wasted read that returned None for all 8 names and briefly looked like a missed sweep.
_A_KEY_RENAME_IN_A_TIME_SERIES_FAILS_TOW.detector: The schema lives in this file's _comment and in 20 sessions of precedent, and NOTHING IN THE REPO READS IT -- grep confirms no .py touches iv_rv_ratio / atm_strike / iv_history, so there is no parser to throw and no test to fail. An agent-only artifact has no compiler; its schema is enforced only by the next agent noticing. So: BEFORE APPENDING TODAY'S ROW, READ THE PRIOR ROW AND MATCH ITS KEY NAMES EXACTLY. Adding a field is additive and fine (today's call_spread_pct_of_mid is welcome); RENAMING one is a silent break. Same family as the indent / ensure_ascii rule -- match the file's OWN existing convention, never the one that reads better -- and the same detector applies: if a series read returns None for a stretch you believe was measured, suspect the KEY before you suspect the sweep.
_A_KEY_RENAME_IN_A_TIME_SERIES_FAILS_TOW.iv_read_after_repair: Series now continuous, n=21 and zero gaps for all 8. Read as a PAIR per the method: ex-gap is rich-to-fair almost everywhere -- SPY raw 1.0947 / ex-gap 1.3020 (80th pctile), QQQ 0.9666 / 1.2824 (55th), TSM 0.9566 / 1.3374, AVGO 0.9420 / 1.1779, MSFT 0.5236 / 1.0690, NVDA 0.8097 / 1.0330, TSLA 0.9179 / 1.0384 (95th); only AMD sits under at 0.7668 / 0.9541. Six of eight are ABOVE 1.0 ex-gap. Raw ratios rose for a third straight session on SPY (0.9927 -> 1.0920 -> 1.0947), QQQ (0.8398 -> 0.9538 -> 0.9666) and NVDA (0.7449 -> 0.7795 -> 0.8097). MSFT is the documented trap in plain view: a headline 0.5236 that is one gap, fair at 1.0690 ex-gap. This argues AGAINST opening long premium today from a direction independent of thesis -- and IV SANITY IS A NECESSARY CONDITION, NEVER A THESIS: rich vol is a reason not to buy, cheap vol would have been no reason to buy. Percentiles quoted with n=21 attached: a rank over ~4 weeks and ONE regime, not a vol-of-vol estimate.

_MMM_200DAY_IS_FLAT_NOT_RISING_THE_LEDGE.headline: A WRITTEN STRUCTURAL LEVEL CARRIES ITS DRIFT RATE IN PROSE, AND THE UNITS ARE AMBIGUOUS — READ '+X OVER THE TRAILING 7 BARS' AS A TOTAL, NOT A PER-DAY RATE. MEASURE THE LEVEL; NEVER EXTRAPOLATE A WRITTEN ONE.
_MMM_200DAY_IS_FLAT_NOT_RISING_THE_LEDGE.what_happened: MMM's setup_invalidation (3) reads: 'a close back below the RISING 200-day SMA at 160.88 (measured 2026-09-01, +0.4511 over the trailing 7 bars; spot 170.61 sits +6.0% above it)'. This run, checking whether MMM had tripped it, first read '+0.4511' as a PER-DAY rate — which extrapolates to 160.88 + 9*0.45 = ~164.9 today, placing spot 162.40 BELOW the 200-day and manufacturing a false invalidation trip on a position 4 days from its time stop. MEASURED instead via get_equity_technical_indicators(sma, period=200, interval=day): 160.8834 (09-04), 160.8920 (09-08), 160.8812 (09-09). The level is 160.88 and essentially FLAT — moving ~0.01/day, not 0.45. The written figure is a 7-BAR TOTAL (~0.064/day), and even that has since flattened to ~zero.
_MMM_200DAY_IS_FLAT_NOT_RISING_THE_LEDGE.the_error_it_would_have_caused: Not a trade — a below-200MA flag is HOLD/REVIEW and never a sell on its own (only a full HARD RULE 7 research verdict of BROKEN sells). But it would have put a false 'invalidation tripped' into the ledger and the daily report on a name whose premise is intact, and the next run would have inherited it. Spot 162.40 is +0.94% ABOVE the measured 200-day: invalidation NOT met.
_MMM_200DAY_IS_FLAT_NOT_RISING_THE_LEDGE.the_rule: Two halves, and the second is the durable one. (1) When a level's drift is written as '+X over the trailing N bars', that is a TOTAL over N bars — divide by N before using it as a rate. (2) Better: do not use it as a rate at all. This file already warns that a correctly re-derived structural level can itself be moving fast and that its value today says nothing about tomorrow; the corollary nobody wrote down is the mirror image — a level's DRIFT RATE goes stale exactly like the level does. MMM's 200-day was genuinely rising when the rate was recorded on 09-01 and is flat nine sessions later, because what LEAVES the trailing window changes. One get_equity_technical_indicators call settles it for free; an extrapolation never does.

_THE_REVIEW_GATE_CAUGHT_A_SIBLING_COLLIS.headline: THE 2026-08-28 COLLISION RULE SAYS 'THE BROKER IS THE ARBITER — RE-READ IT IMMEDIATELY BEFORE ANY ORDER.' THIS RUN DID EXACTLY THAT AND STILL MISSED A SIBLING'S FILL, BECAUSE THE COLLISION WINDOW WAS 1.4 SECONDS. THE THING THAT ACTUALLY PREVENTED THE DOUBLE-SELL WAS review_equity_order.

_THE_REVIEW_GATE_CAUGHT_A_SIBLING_COLLIS.THE_MECHANISM_which_is_the_transferable_: The 2026-08-28 finding measured a collision whose blind window was the SIBLING'S COMMIT LATENCY (~10 minutes) and correctly concluded that git cannot see a sibling's fill, so the broker must be re-read. But a broker re-read has its own blind window: the interval between YOUR read and YOUR order. That interval is normally a few seconds and is invisible until two runs land in it. Here it was 1.4 seconds and the sibling fitted inside it. NO POLLING FREQUENCY CLOSES THIS — the gap is structural, because a check and the action it authorizes cannot be simultaneous. Only a check the BROKER performs atomically at order time can.
_THE_REVIEW_GATE_CAUGHT_A_SIBLING_COLLIS.WHY_THE_REVIEW_ENDPOINT_IS_THE_RIGHT_LAS: This repo already knows review is a FALSE GREEN for multi-leg support (a clean review, then a 400 at place). That rule is specifically about a CAPABILITY the review endpoint does not check. It is NOT a general licence to disbelieve review. The 2026-08-24 collateral measurement established the other half and it governs here: a review that RAISES an alert is real and must be honoured. Share count, like collateral, is state the review endpoint genuinely evaluates. So the asymmetry is exact and stable: A CLEAN REVIEW PROVES LITTLE; A RAISED ALERT IS TRUE.
_THE_REVIEW_GATE_CAUGHT_A_SIBLING_COLLIS.the_rule: ALWAYS review_equity_order / review_option_order immediately before placing, EVEN when the trade is mechanical, unconditional and already fully gated — and treat any raised alert as authoritative over your own freshly-read position state. A time stop is exactly the kind of order a run is tempted to fire straight from the ledger, because it needs no live technical and the decision was made before the bell. That temptation is the hazard.
_THE_REVIEW_GATE_CAUGHT_A_SIBLING_COLLIS.what_this_does_NOT_claim: It does not claim the broker pre-check is useless — it remains the only way to catch a sibling that filled MINUTES earlier, which is the common case and the one 08-28 measured. It is a NARROWING: the pre-check bounds the risk, the review gate closes it. Both are required. n=1 on the sub-2-second case.
_THE_REVIEW_GATE_CAUGHT_A_SIBLING_COLLIS.outcome: Correct in the end: exactly one exit order exists, the position is flat, realized -$25.30 broker-confirmed, and the ledger carries ONE closed-position record. The two runs agreed on the decision and disagreed only on who got there first — which is cross-validation of the time-stop logic, not a conflict.

NARROWING_ADDED_2026-09-10T13:50Z_BY_A_T.THE_GAP_IN_THE_RULE_ABOVE_AND_IT_IS_LOAD: This key concludes 'the pre-check bounds the risk, THE REVIEW GATE CLOSES IT.' That is true for a SELL and FALSE for a BUY, and the difference is not a detail -- it is the entire reason the one collision that actually cost this desk money was not caught. review_equity_order raised EQUITY_MAX_SELL_SHARES_EXCEEDED because SHARE COUNT IS A BINDING CONSTRAINT the broker must enforce: you cannot sell shares you no longer hold, so a duplicate sell fails safe BY CONSTRUCTION and the review merely reports it. THERE IS NO EQUIVALENT CONSTRAINT ON A DUPLICATE BUY. A second identical buy is a perfectly valid order to the broker as long as buying power covers it, so the review returns CLEAN and both orders fill -- doubling the position and breaching the per-name cap, the sizing rule and the entry throttle at once.
NARROWING_ADDED_2026-09-10T13:50Z_BY_A_T.the_precedent_that_proves_it: 2026-08-28, _CONCURRENT_RUN_COLLISION_2026-08-28: two runs 2m50s apart bought ROST ($460.30) and MDLZ ($500.00), spending $960.30 against a $956 ceiling and breaching the then-live cash floor. BOTH WERE BUYS. A review call before either would have returned no alert, because neither order was individually invalid -- they were only invalid TOGETHER, and 'together' is precisely what no single-order review can see. So the review gate would not have prevented the one collision on record that actually did damage.
NARROWING_ADDED_2026-09-10T13:50Z_BY_A_T.the_corrected_statement_of_the_defence: SELLS: broker pre-check (bounds it) + review gate (closes it, because the broker enforces share count atomically). Genuinely safe. BUYS: broker pre-check (bounds it) + review gate (DOES NOT CLOSE IT). The residual risk is real and unmitigated by any check this desk currently performs. Treat the near-simultaneous window as genuinely open on the entry side, and note that entries are throttled to 1/run precisely because the desk cannot see a sibling's -- a throttle each run applies to ITSELF is no defence against two runs each applying it correctly.
NARROWING_ADDED_2026-09-10T13:50Z_BY_A_T.practical_consequence_for_entries_no_new: On the ENTRY side the only real mitigations are timing and reconciliation, not review: (a) the documented preference to take the day's equity entry on the first run at/after ~14:15Z is now doing double duty -- it also DE-SYNCHRONISES runs away from the first-post-open slot where all three of today's runs and both of 2026-08-28's collided; (b) re-read get_equity_orders as the LAST action before place_equity_order with nothing in between, accepting that a sub-2-second sibling still fits inside it; (c) if a fill appears that this run did not place, DEFER and recompute every gate off the fresh numbers rather than proceeding. NARROWING_ADDED_2026-09-10T13:50Z_BY_A_T.an_honest_note_on_how_this_run_reached_t: Badly, and it is worth recording because the failure mode is this file's most-repeated one. Before any sibling was visible, this run drafted a finding asserting that review_equity_order had PLACED a live order -- it had called review, never place, and an order existed. FALSE. The sibling placed it; the alert was the review WORKING. The draft explicitly considered the sibling hypothesis and dismissed it as 'weaker', partly because no 13:00Z+ branch or commit existed on origin -- while the commit-latency rule this file already teaches says git silence is only evidence a sibling HAS NOT FINISHED WRITING (the sibling pushed 13:39:19Z; the check ran ~13:37Z). It was caught by a MERGE CONFLICT, not by reasoning, and never merged. Two rules restated: GIT SILENCE IS NEVER EVIDENCE OF ABSENCE in a shared account -- the concurrent-run hypothesis is the FIRST candidate, not the fallback; and a sub-second timestamp coincidence feels decisive but is not, because runs synchronised on the same settle window collide inside one second by design. (Same draft also called LLY the book's first time stop; PNC 2026-09-03 was, a fact sitting in _closed_positions in the file it had already loaded. CHECK THE LEDGER BEFORE ANY 'FIRST-EVER' CLAIM.)
NARROWING_ADDED_2026-09-10T13:50Z_BY_A_T.and_the_window_this_run_actually_left_op: This run's own pre-order broker check ran at 13:16Z and it acted at 13:36Z -- a TWENTY MINUTE gap, not the 1.4 seconds this key measures, because it waited out the mandatory ~5-minute post-bell settle in between. The settle-wait REOPENS the window the pre-check closes. Two individually correct rules compose into a gap: 'never price off the opening auction print' makes you wait, and nothing tells you to redo the broker read afterwards. 'IMMEDIATELY BEFORE' MEANS IMMEDIATELY -- if anything made you pause after the check (a settle window, a research detour, a slow tool call), the check is stale. Measure the gap and redo it.

_A_PLACE_ERROR_CAN_BE_FALSE__400_RETURNE.recorded_by: The run that SENT order 6aa2b259 -- the third of three concurrent same-slot runs, and the only one positioned to observe this.
_A_PLACE_ERROR_CAN_BE_FALSE__400_RETURNE.severity: HIGH -- a double-trade hazard on the BUY side. No money was lost here; the hazard is the reflex, not the event.
_A_PLACE_ERROR_CAN_BE_FALSE__400_RETURNE.THE_FINDING: place_equity_order returned `API error 400: {"detail":"Not enough shares to sell."}` for the LLY time-stop exit. THE ORDER HAD ALREADY FILLED. get_equity_orders shows exactly ONE LLY order all day -- 6aa2b259-4dea-46b0-92e4-0a1c8c89c2ff, state 'filled', 0.420254 sh @ 1129.5485, placed_agent 'agentic', created 13:36:25.650672Z, executed 13:36:25.786Z. One call, one order, one fill -- and the caller was told it failed.
what_was_verified_before_sending_so_this: get_equity_positions seconds earlier: quantity 0.420254, shares_available_for_sells 0.420254, shares_held_for_sells 0.000000.
review_equity_order on the identical payload: order_checks {} -- no alerts.
A fresh ref_id UUID (ea0aae0d-12a1-4d0c-8710-43fa8b977d7d), exactly as the tool contract prescribes.
The quantity was the exact BROKER figure, not a ledger figure, per the 2026-09-09 preflight rule.
_A_PLACE_ERROR_CAN_BE_FALSE__400_RETURNE.MECHANISM_NARROWED_AND_SETTLED_BY_A_SIBL: An earlier draft of this key offered two candidates -- a gateway retry, or a SIBLING run having taken the shares. THE SIBLING TIMELINE EXCLUDES THE SECOND. _THE_REVIEW_GATE_CAUGHT_A_SIBLING_COLLISION... records to the second that order 6aa2b259 -- THE ORDER THIS RUN'S OWN CALL CREATED -- is what took the shares at 13:36:25.650Z, and that the other run never placed anything (its review gate blocked it at 13:36:38Z). So there was no third party: the shares were consumed by THIS CALL'S OWN FIRST ATTEMPT. That leaves the GATEWAY RETRY reading: the order was submitted and filled, the response was lost or timed out, the request was retried, and the retry re-validated share availability against a position its OWN predecessor had just emptied, returning 400. The ref_id did its job on the ORDER (only one exists) and not on the RESPONSE, so the caller received the retry's validation failure instead of the original fill.
_A_PLACE_ERROR_CAN_BE_FALSE__400_RETURNE.THE_RULE: AN ORDER-PLACEMENT ERROR IS NOT EVIDENCE THE ORDER DID NOT HAPPEN. Before reacting to ANY failed place_equity_order or place_option_order -- retrying, re-sizing, logging it as declined, or reporting that nothing was placed -- RE-READ THE BROKER: get_equity_orders / get_option_orders with created_at_gte=today, plus positions. A filled order matching your payload is YOUR fill: STOP. Never retry on the strength of an error string alone.
_A_PLACE_ERROR_CAN_BE_FALSE__400_RETURNE.WHY_THIS_COMPLETES_A_TAXONOMY_RATHER_THA: The repo now has all three cells of the review/place truth table, and they do not agree: (1) A CLEAN REVIEW PROVES LITTLE -- review_option_order false-greens a multi-leg order the place endpoint then rejects 400 (2026-08-24), because multi-leg SUPPORT is a capability review does not check. (2) A RAISED REVIEW ALERT IS TRUE -- the 08-24 collateral demand and the 09-10 EQUITY_MAX_SELL_SHARES_EXCEEDED were both real, because collateral and share count are state review genuinely evaluates. (3) THIS ONE, AND IT IS THE NEW CELL: A RAISED ERROR AT *PLACE* TIME CAN BE FALSE. Cells (1) and (3) are mirror images -- a clean result that is wrong, and a dirty result that is wrong -- and knowing (1) does NOT imply (3): 'a review proves nothing' and 'an error proves nothing' are separate claims about different endpoints.
_A_PLACE_ERROR_CAN_BE_FALSE__400_RETURNE.WHAT_THE_REFLEX_WOULD_HAVE_COST_and_the_: 'Not enough shares to sell' reads like a quantity problem, so the obvious repair is a retry with a smaller quantity. ON A SELL THAT IS HARMLESS -- the shares are genuinely gone, so the retry just fails again, and the sibling finding separately establishes that the review gate closes the SELL path. INVERT THE SIDE AND NOTHING CLOSES IT: the same class of false negative on a BUY, answered by a retry with a fresh ref_id, DOUBLE-SIZES the position. Review cannot catch that -- buying power for a second entry genuinely exists, so the review is clean and correct. Under the 2026-09-02 concentration policy a doubled entry is up to 60% of the account in one name, through the 30% per-name cap, with no price stop under HARD RULE 5.
_A_PLACE_ERROR_CAN_BE_FALSE__400_RETURNE.RELATION_TO_THE_TWO_ADJACENT_RULES_and_t: The 2026-08-28 collision rule says re-read the broker BEFORE placing; the 09-10 sibling narrows that to 'a broker precheck has its own blind window, so review immediately before placing and honour any raised alert'. Both govern the moment BEFORE the order. THIS ONE GOVERNS THE MOMENT AFTER IT. Before: review, and believe an alert. After: re-read the broker, and disbelieve an error until the broker agrees. Neither substitutes for the other.
_A_PLACE_ERROR_CAN_BE_FALSE__400_RETURNE.honest_scope: n=1. The retry is inferred from the error text plus the single-order record rather than observed in the gateway, though the sibling timeline removes the only competing explanation. It may be specific to fractional sells that fully close a position, where a second validation necessarily sees zero shares. What is MEASURED and needs no interpretation: a 400 was returned for an order that filled. That alone justifies the rule, which costs one read call.
_A_PLACE_ERROR_CAN_BE_FALSE__400_RETURNE.did_it_change_this_runs_decision: YES, and it was load-bearing rather than merely recorded. The next action on a 400 would ordinarily have been a retry. Checking get_equity_orders FIRST revealed the fill, prevented a second order, and produced the correct broker-confirmed -$25.30 instead of a false 'exit failed, position still open' handoff that would have made the next run's reconciliation report unexplainable drift.

_A_ZERO_OF_26_VERDICT_WAS_BUILT_FROM_A_2.why_it_is_worth_a_key: The cohort method is GOOD and should not be abandoned -- collapsing 26 names into six correlated buckets is what makes a full board gradeable inside one run's budget. Its failure mode is specific and silent: names that belong to no bucket simply do not appear, and the bucket list still LOOKS exhaustive because every name in it is accounted for. Nothing errors. The verdict reads as a strong, well-organised no-trade, which is indistinguishable from a genuine one.
_A_ZERO_OF_26_VERDICT_WAS_BUILT_FROM_A_2.the_class_not_the_instance: This is CLAUDE.md's most-repeated defect -- a check that passes for the wrong reason -- and specifically the 2026-08-25 family THE SCOPE OF A FINDING MUST MATCH THE SCOPE OF WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MEASURED, which recorded three occurrences in a single session (a five-name claim from a two-name sample, a universe claim from that five-name list, and the session-key sprawl). Every one of those was a conclusion held for the right reason on evidence that did not support it. This is the fourth, and the first where the unmeasured remainder actually contained the trade.
_A_ZERO_OF_26_VERDICT_WAS_BUILT_FROM_A_2.the_detector_and_it_costs_one_line: When a run grades a board by COHORT, sum the cohort sizes and assert the total equals the board size before writing the verdict. len(union of enumerated tickers) == len(table). If it does not reconcile, the missing names are UNGRADED -- say so explicitly rather than reporting a total. Same shape as the git diff --stat rule and the lot-invariant assertion: trust the arithmetic, not the sense of having been thorough.
_A_ZERO_OF_26_VERDICT_WAS_BUILT_FROM_A_2.corollary_for_the_relay: An inherited 'zero A-grades today' is a CONCLUSION, not data. It is cheap to re-derive the cohort arithmetic from the prior entry's own text and expensive to miss what it omits -- the asymmetry favours checking every time. A relay instance that trusts the headline never looks at the remainder, and the remainder is where an unexamined name will always be.
_A_ZERO_OF_26_VERDICT_WAS_BUILT_FROM_A_2.honest_scope: The omission was almost certainly capacity, not carelessness -- the 14:00Z run did substantial genuine work (two durable findings, a full IV sweep, worked verdicts on NVDA and TGT) and 26 names is a lot for one run. Nothing here says its declines were wrong; every one of the 23 it did reach looks correctly graded, and this run independently declined two of the three it missed. The finding is narrow: the VERDICT'S SCOPE exceeded the REASONING'S SCOPE, and that gap is mechanically detectable.
_A_ZERO_OF_26_VERDICT_WAS_BUILT_FROM_A_2.outcome_disclaimer: ABNB's entry is graded, not vindicated. Whether the trade works is unknown and irrelevant to this finding -- had ABNB graded C like its two companions, the reporting defect would be identical and equally worth recording. Do not let a fill turn a process finding into a market call.

_THE_REPORT_PIPELINE_LOSES_A_BOARD_TO_A_.headline: Today's 15:00Z intraday report was GENERATED and then LOST on a git push race. Four runs then reasoned off a 105-minute-old board, each writing 'board not reissued' without ever asking why it was not reissued.

what_was_measured.the_failure: GitHub Actions run 34492753828 (stock-report.yml, workflow_dispatch, 15:00:08Z) completed with conclusion FAILURE. The scan itself succeeded; the 'Commit the published report' step failed. Log: fetch printed 'Current branch master is up to date' at 15:03:08.99Z, then `git push` was rejected '! [rejected] master -> master (fetch first)' at 15:03:10.01Z.
what_was_measured.the_window: ONE SECOND. The step already did `git pull --rebase` before pushing -- the intent was correct and the comment above it says exactly why -- but a single pull-then-push leaves a race window between the pull completing and the push landing.
what_was_measured.why_the_window_is_now_routinely_hit: The automation merges a PR to master roughly every 15 minutes, plus concurrent sibling runs. The report scan takes ~2-3 minutes (checkout 15:00:08Z -> push 15:03:10Z), so every report run overlaps at least one desk merge by construction. This is not bad luck; it is a structural collision that gets MORE likely as run frequency rises.
what_was_measured.contrast: Yesterday's equivalent fires (15:00Z, 16:00Z, 17:00Z, 18:00Z, 19:00Z on 09-09) all succeeded. Nothing about the report code changed. The desk's own commit cadence is the variable that moved.

_THE_REPORT_PIPELINE_LOSES_A_BOARD_TO_A_.what_it_cost_today: latest_intraday.md on master is still the 2026-09-09T19:01Z board. The whole 2026-09-10 session has run off the 14:01Z morning board. Every autonomous equity signal -- RSI2 setups, momentum entries, TAKE-PROFIT fires, TIME STOP fires, THESIS-CHECK flags -- is sourced from that committed report and from nothing else, so a lost push is a blind trading session. Immaterial today only because no exit was reachable (all three swings underwater or flat, so RSI2>=70 is gated off) and the board's single A-grade name was already taken at 14:21Z.
_THE_REPORT_PIPELINE_LOSES_A_BOARD_TO_A_.why_no_run_caught_it: The runs at 14:47Z, 15:01Z, 15:16Z, 15:20Z and 15:30Z each correctly noted 'the board was not reissued' and correctly declined to re-grade a static board on fresher tape. Not one asked WHY it was not reissued. A missing artifact produces no error anywhere -- the stale file reads perfectly, the freshness check passes against the MORNING report which IS today's, and the DATA ERROR clause never fires because the report that failed was never written at all. CLAUDE.md's most-repeated shape, arriving as an ABSENCE rather than a wrong value: a check that passes for the wrong reason.
_THE_REPORT_PIPELINE_LOSES_A_BOARD_TO_A_.the_root_fix_applied: stock-report.yml 'Commit the published report' now retries the whole rebase+push cycle up to 5 times with backoff (3s, 6s, 9s, 12s) and fails loudly with ::error:: if it still cannot land. One shot was never enough against a moving ref.
_THE_REPORT_PIPELINE_LOSES_A_BOARD_TO_A_.the_detector_for_the_class: An artifact that is SUPPOSED to arrive on a schedule and does not is invisible to every check that reads the artifact -- because there is nothing to read. Assert the SCHEDULE, not the content: on any run, if the newest committed report is older than the report cadence would imply (~1 hour during 14:00-19:00Z), check the workflow's run list for a FAILED fire before reasoning off the stale board. Same family as the 2026-08-21 dead-man lesson -- a liveness check cannot detect degradation, and here it could not detect a single missing beat either.
_THE_REPORT_PIPELINE_LOSES_A_BOARD_TO_A_.honest_scope: n=1 failure. The push race is proven; the claim that it will recur is an inference from the cadence arithmetic, not a measurement. It changed no trading decision today.

UPDATE_2026-09-11T17-20Z_THE_RETRY_FIX_W.status: SUPERSEDES the 'no run asked why' framing of this key's own title. A run DID ask why, on the second occurrence, and the answer was a DIFFERENT defect wearing the same symptom. Fix pushed this run.
UPDATE_2026-09-11T17-20Z_THE_RETRY_FIX_W.the_second_loss: GitHub Actions run 34625197677 (stock-report.yml, workflow_dispatch, 17:00:08Z, head 1f23618) FAILED and lost the 17:00Z intraday board. The scan succeeded; 'Commit the published report' failed after all five attempts.
UPDATE_2026-09-11T17-20Z_THE_RETRY_FIX_W.what_the_09-10_fix_did_and_did_not_cover: The 09-10 remedy replaced a single pull-then-push with a 5-attempt rebase+push loop. That correctly handles a REJECTED PUSH -- the one-second race this key documents. It does NOT handle a CONFLICTED REBASE, and the two are different failures with different recovery paths.

the_actual_mechanism.trigger: TWO report runs generated an intraday board minutes apart: the 16:57:27Z SCHEDULED fire (run 34624946460, succeeded, landed e2ef706) and the 17:00:08Z DISPATCH fire (run 34625197677). Both write the SAME latest_intraday.md.
the_actual_mechanism.the_wedge: Once the sibling's board is on master, our replayed commit CONFLICTS on that file. From that moment the working tree holds unmerged files, and every subsequent `git pull` in the loop dies immediately with 'error: Pulling is not possible because you have unmerged files' / 'fatal: Exiting because of an unresolved conflict'. Attempts 2, 3, 4 and 5 were GUARANTEED no-ops -- the retry loop cannot make progress, it can only burn its budget.
the_actual_mechanism.why_it_looked_like_the_same_bug: The job's own error line is the generic 'push attempt N rejected (concurrent push to master); retrying', which is the loop's wording for ANY failure. The log text says conflict; the summary says push race. A retry loop that logs one cause for every failure mode hides the failure mode it cannot handle.

REPRODUCED_THEN_FIXED_THEN_VERIFIED.reproduction: Built a 3-clone scratch repo (origin + sibling + ours) and replayed the exact sequence. The old loop emitted the identical error text to the CI log and ended with the tree wedged at 'UU latest_intraday.md' -- byte-for-byte the observed failure, so the mechanism is confirmed, not inferred.
REPRODUCED_THEN_FIXED_THEN_VERIFIED.the_fix: In .github/workflows/stock-report.yml, the loop now detects a conflicted rebase (.git/rebase-merge or .git/rebase-apply present) and resolves it deterministically in favour of THIS run's freshly generated board: under `git rebase` the replayed commit is the 'theirs' side, so `git checkout --theirs -- $REPORT` is our new report; then `git add` and `rebase --continue`. If the conflict is NOT confined to that file it aborts the rebase instead, so the next attempt starts from a clean tree rather than a permanently wedged one.
REPRODUCED_THEN_FIXED_THEN_VERIFIED.verification: Same scratch scenario against the new loop: conflict resolved on attempt 1, PUSHED ON ATTEMPT 2, final tree clean, the newer board is what landed, AND the sibling's commit is preserved in history rather than clobbered. YAML parses (yaml.safe_load) and the extracted step passes `bash -n` with the workflow expression substituted.
REPRODUCED_THEN_FIXED_THEN_VERIFIED.why_OUR_board_wins_is_the_right_default: Both boards are the same-minute scan; the later one is at worst equally fresh. The cost being avoided is asymmetric and the workflow's own comment states it: 'The report is the sole source of every autonomous equity signal, so a lost push is a blind trading session.' Losing the board is far worse than either board winning.

UPDATE_2026-09-11T17-20Z_THE_RETRY_FIX_W.the_transferable_lesson: A REMEDY AIMED AT ONE FAILURE MODE CAN LEAVE A SECOND MODE THAT PRESENTS IDENTICALLY -- AND A RETRY LOOP IS THE CLASSIC PLACE FOR IT, BECAUSE RETRYING IS ONLY A FIX WHEN THE FAILURE IS TRANSIENT. A conflicted tree is not transient: it is a state the loop must CLEAR, and retrying against it is not merely useless but actively consumes the attempt budget that would otherwise have handled the race the loop was built for. Detector: when a retry loop exhausts its attempts, read whether attempts 2..N produced the SAME error as attempt 1. Identical repeated errors mean a wedged state, not contention.
UPDATE_2026-09-11T17-20Z_THE_RETRY_FIX_W.residual_risk_stated_honestly: This does NOT stop the two runs from colliding -- it makes the collision non-fatal. The redundant trigger config (cron-job.org dispatch + the native schedule backstop) is what produces same-minute duplicate scans, and only Ryan can change that. Also unverified in production: the fix is proven in a local reproduction and by static checks, but no live conflicted rebase has exercised it yet. The next duplicate-fire collision is the real test; if run 34625197677's failure mode recurs, this is where to look first.

The red X was real and the root cause was real; only the impact was imported from the previous incident because the symptom matched. _THE_UNGRADED_DELTA_RETURNED_ON_A_BOARD_.why_no_run_erred: The 18:02Z run rebased onto origin/master 16343f1, which PREDATES report commit e7296df. It graded the newest board it could see. This is the 2026-09-09 stale-clone hazard in its benign form: not a stale WRITE over master, but a stale READ of an input that master had already refreshed. The window is the gap between a run's rebase and the report cron's push, and on a ~15-minute cadence against a report that re-runs every few minutes those two will collide regularly.
_THE_UNGRADED_DELTA_RETURNED_ON_A_BOARD_.the_transferable_shape: A NEGATIVE claim about a data set is only as fresh as the fetch that produced it, and it decays SILENTLY. 'Ungraded delta NONE' reads identically whether it was re-derived one second ago or inherited from an hour-old board -- which is precisely why those four runs were right to re-assert it mechanically each time rather than quote it. The residual gap is that re-asserting against a stale COPY of the board is indistinguishable from re-asserting against the live one. Same family as the 2026-08-28 sibling-collision finding: the check was performed correctly and interrogated an artifact that had already moved.
_THE_UNGRADED_DELTA_RETURNED_ON_A_BOARD_.detector: Before asserting a board is fully graded, confirm the board you graded is the one on master RIGHT NOW: `git fetch origin master && git log origin/master --oneline -3 -- latest_intraday.md` and compare the report's own header timestamp to the file you read. If a newer report commit landed after your rebase, re-read it and diff the setup table before writing any 'delta NONE' claim. Cheap -- one fetch -- and it is the only thing separating a graded zero from an ungraded one.
_THE_UNGRADED_DELTA_RETURNED_ON_A_BOARD_.honest_scope: This is a REFINEMENT, not a fault. No run misgraded a name, no gate was skipped, and the four re-assertions were each methodologically correct on the data they held. The cost was one A-grade setup sitting ungraded for roughly 18 minutes, which is why it is filed as a detector rather than an incident.

_A_GATE_EVALUATED_AS_A_SNAPSHOT_EXPIRES_.the_class: TWO independent gates in the equity book are evaluated as a SNAPSHOT AT ENTRY while the position's own clock -- the flat 14-session SWING_TIME_STOP_DAYS -- outlives the snapshot. Nothing errors, nothing re-checks, and the ledger keeps carrying the gate as though it were still true. Both instances below were measured this run; they are the same defect aimed at different fields, and they belong to this file's most-repeated family: a check that passes for the wrong reason.

instance_1_TARGET_REACHABILITY.finding: A position's `target` and its time stop are set by INDEPENDENT mechanisms -- the target by the RSI2 screen's estimate, the time stop by a flat constant -- and nothing in report.py or prompt v10 ever asks whether the target is REACHABLE inside the remaining window. Measured on all four swings against each name's own trailing 6-month distribution (133 daily bars, 2026-03-02..2026-09-09, % of overlapping N-session windows that produced the required gain):

measurements.MMM: needs +11.21% in 4 sessions (target 180.83 vs spot 162.60, time stop 09-14). 0 of 129 windows cleared = 0.0%. Best 4-session gain in the entire sample +8.49%, i.e. the required move has NOT ONCE occurred in six months. daily_sigma 1.60%.
measurements.GD: needs +9.67% in 5 sessions (target 387.04 vs spot 352.92, time stop 09-15). 3 of 128 = 2.3%. Best in sample +11.69%. daily_sigma 1.47%.
measurements.ABNB: needs +9.25% in 14 sessions (target 183.08 vs spot 167.58, time stop 09-24). 25 of 119 = 21.0%. daily_sigma 2.49%.
measurements.UNP: needs +4.81% in 14 sessions (target 298.32 vs spot 284.6292, time stop 09-24). 41 of 119 = 34.5% -- the most reachable target in the book by a wide margin. daily_sigma 1.57%.

instance_1_TARGET_REACHABILITY.what_it_means_concretely: MMM and GD have ONE exit left each, and it is the time stop. Their target exit is arithmetically dead and has been for days, while the ledger still lists a target as if it were a live branch. A position with one possible exit should be described that way -- it changes what the position IS, from a two-sided swing into a dated liquidation.
instance_1_TARGET_REACHABILITY.and_it_settles_the_ROTATION_GATE_which_i: The book went fully deployed at 18:20Z (deployable $15.12 vs a $600 minimum), so under THE CAPITAL POLICY the only path to a new entry is ROTATION -- an A-grade idea graded better than the WEAKEST POSITION HELD, funded by selling it. Prior runs recorded the gate as 'ACTIVE but idle for want of a candidate'. The stronger and more useful statement is that IT IS DORMANT BY ARITHMETIC UNTIL 2026-09-14, because the two weakest stacks and the two nearest time stops ARE THE SAME TWO POSITIONS: (a) rotating out of MMM or GD buys only 4-5 days of ~$938 that is returning on its own, pays a full round-trip spread, and forfeits the reversion the position exists to harvest -- MMM printed RSI2 0.9 on the 19:01Z board, its most-oversold reading, which is precisely the condition the entry was taken for; (b) the two positions whose capital is genuinely locked for 14 days, ABNB and UNP, hold the book's ONLY two live targets (21.0% and 34.5% reachable) and both theses are intact, so selling either to fund a fresher signal is the exact churn HARD RULE 5 and the CAPITAL POLICY forbid. CAPACITY RETURNS 09-14 (MMM ~$469) and 09-15 (GD ~$472).
instance_1_TARGET_REACHABILITY.the_trap_it_closes: The naive rotation pick is the biggest loser -- MMM at -6.19%. The CAPITAL POLICY forbids exactly that ('Weakest = weakest on the ENTRY STACK ... NEVER simply the biggest loser'), and the reachability numbers show why the prohibition is not merely stylistic: the biggest loser here is also the position whose capital costs the least to wait for.

instance_2_THE_RISING_200DAY_GATE_EXPIRE.finding: The RSI2 screen's trend gate is 'oversold inside a RISING 200-day uptrend', tested against TODAY's average. But the average MOVES, and a 14-session hold is long enough for a rising average to climb through spot. When the cushion measured in SESSIONS is smaller than the hold window, the gate that qualified the entry EXPIRES DURING THE TRADE.

Spot 118.69 sits just +1.37 points / +1.17% above it = a cushion of 10.1 SESSIONS. The hold window is 14 sessions. Projected forward on a FLAT tape the average reaches ~119.22 by the 09-24 time stop -- ABOVE TODAY'S SPOT. The entry would spend the back third of its life failing its own entry gate with no help from the tape.

instance_2_THE_RISING_200DAY_GATE_EXPIRE.read_it_with_its_sibling_key: _A_ONE_DAY_MA_SLOPE_IS_NOT_A_FORWARD_PATH warns that a single-day slope does not project. That still holds and this does not contradict it -- the slope here is measured over 22 sessions and verified monotonic, and the conclusion does not need the projection to be accurate, only for the cushion (10.1 sessions) to be shorter than the hold (14). _A_GATE_EVALUATED_AS_A_SNAPSHOT_EXPIRES_.detector: Two lines of arithmetic, both computable at entry and neither currently required by any rule: (1) REACHABILITY -- required_move_pct / remaining_sessions, sanity-checked against the name's own distribution of N-session gains. If the required move has essentially never occurred, the target is not an exit and the time stop is the certain one; say so. (2) CUSHION IN SESSIONS -- (spot - SMA200) / SMA200_slope_per_session. If that is smaller than the hold window, the trend gate expires inside the trade and the setup is not what the screen says it is.

_A_SINGLE_SCRATCH_TRADE_FLIPPED_THE_SIGN.severity: live code that gates the risk-off branch; FIXED THIS RUN in calibrate.py
_A_SINGLE_SCRATCH_TRADE_FLIPPED_THE_SIGN.headline: calibrate.edge_stats() divided the win rate by ALL closes but derived the breakeven win rate from only the DECIDED ones, so the two sides of the margin comparison ran on different denominators. One $0 realizing leg was enough to flip the options book from a thin-positive edge into the KILL branch.

measured.source: get_pnl_trade_history span=3month, the broker — never trade_journal.json
measured.options_book_before_fix: n=17, wins 9, losses 7, win_rate 9/17 = 52.94% vs breakeven 53.29% -> MARGIN -0.35 pts = KILL ('edge gone, halve size, pause new entries, ESCALATE')
measured.options_book_after_fix: n=17 (1 scratch), win_rate 9/16 = 56.25% vs the same 53.29% breakeven -> MARGIN +2.96 pts = thin but POSITIVE
measured.the_economics_never_moved: net +$90.00 and expectancy +$5.29/trade are IDENTICAL either way. Only the statistic changed.
measured.the_scratch: SPY 2026-08-26T17:26:20Z, realized_gain exactly 0 — the long leg of the legged SPY 740/735 put vertical, bought and sold back at 3.22. A legged vertical is a multi-row close and a scratch leg is a NORMAL product of one, so this is not a one-off.
measured.equities_unaffected: 54 closes, zero scratches, margin +15.67 pts before and after.

_A_SINGLE_SCRATCH_TRADE_FLIPPED_THE_SIGN.the_mechanism: breakeven_win_rate = |mean_loss| / (mean_win + |mean_loss|) is computed ENTIRELY from the decided trades. win_rate was computed over every close. Comparing them is not like-for-like, and the error is DIRECTIONAL: a scratch sits in the denominator and in neither the wins nor the losses, so it can only ever drag the measured win rate DOWN — i.e. toward risk-off, never away from it. A defect that only ever errs toward caution is the hardest kind to notice, because every instance of it looks like prudence.
_A_SINGLE_SCRATCH_TRADE_FLIPPED_THE_SIGN.the_fix: calibrate.py edge_stats() now computes win_rate over (wins + losses) and reports a new `scratches` field; format_report surfaces it as e.g. '9W/7L/1scratch'. `n` still counts every close (it gates MIN_TRADES_FOR_ACTION, and a scratch really is a completed trade) and expectancy/net still average over everything (a scratch genuinely contributed $0). ONLY the win rate narrows, because it is the only figure compared against a decided-trades breakeven.
_A_SINGLE_SCRATCH_TRADE_FLIPPED_THE_SIGN.changed_no_decision_today: Both books return REPORT ONLY regardless: options n=17 < MIN_TRADES_FOR_ACTION 20, equities only 2 of 54 closes are in-regime. And today is FRIDAY — the calibration ritual is Monday. A filter's inputs can only be audited credibly on a run where the audit does not change the answer.
_A_SINGLE_SCRATCH_TRADE_FLIPPED_THE_SIGN.worth_knowing_and_NOT_a_defect: The n<20 guard returns BEFORE the KILL branch, so the KILL branch is exempt from the IN-REGIME gate but not from the SAMPLE-SIZE gate. That matches the prompt's own ordering ('n < 20: report, never adjust' is listed first) and is correct: the in-regime gate is about relevance, the n gate is about whether a losing streak is distinguishable from noise at all. No future run should read the options book as being under a standing KILL order.
_A_SINGLE_SCRATCH_TRADE_FLIPPED_THE_SIGN.transferable_lesson: This file's most-repeated shape, arriving inside the module written to measure the desk objectively: A RATIO'S TWO SIDES MUST BE COMPUTED OVER THE SAME POPULATION. The module already knew not to compare a win rate against a FIXED threshold (its own docstring says so); it then compared it against a correctly-derived breakeven over a different denominator. Getting the numerator's theory right does not protect the denominator — and this is now the fifth distinct denominator defect recorded in this repo, after session-average, trailing-local-in-decay, closing-auction, and post-flush-inflation.

_A_FEED_HOLE_IS_A_TRAILING_SUFFIX_OF_THE.headline: THE HOLE MECHANISM IS NOW EXACT, NOT A SIGNATURE: a holed 5-minute bucket is the AGGREGATE OF A TRAILING SUFFIX of its constituent minutes -- the leading minutes are dropped. Verified to the cent and the share on two SPY instances with DIFFERENT suffix lengths in one window. The load-bearing corollary: because the suffix always ENDS on the interval's last minute, the CLOSE IS ALWAYS PRESERVED while open/high/low/volume are corrupted.

_A_FEED_HOLE_IS_A_TRAILING_SUFFIX_OF_THE.what_this_supersedes: It does not overturn the existing hole rules -- it makes them a special case and explains the anomaly they could not. (a) The 'bucket volume equals ONE of its constituent minutes' signature is the k=1 case. (b) The 2026-08-28T15:35Z note recorded a PARTIAL hole whose 27,681 'equals none of its constituent minutes' and concluded the single-constituent signature is only one form -- correct, and the missing step was that nobody tested SUMS OF TRAILING SUFFIXES. k=2 reproduces that class exactly. (c) The direction rule (bucket BELOW 1-min sum => bucket holed, substitute the sum) is re-confirmed twice and is what a run should still act on.
_A_FEED_HOLE_IS_A_TRAILING_SUFFIX_OF_THE.THE_COROLLARY_THAT_DECIDES_WHICH_MEASURE: A suffix hole ends on the interval's true last minute, so close == true close ALWAYS. Therefore: (1) measurements built on COMPLETED CLOSES are IMMUNE -- the two-bar price clause, a close-through-a-level test, and a cross-sectional return series computed off closes all survive a hole untouched. (2) Measurements built on HIGHS/LOWS are corrupted TOWARD HIDING EXTREMES -- here the high read 0.19 and 0.28 LOW and the low read 0.30 and 0.33 HIGH, so the range read ~30-40% too NARROW. A session extreme or structural level taken off a holed bucket is a FLOOR, never a value (the 2026-08-27 'report it as at least X' rule is the right response and this is its mechanism). (3) VOLUME is corrupted DOWNWARD 87-96%, depressing any trailing-mean denominator and manufacturing the confirmation the clause exists to withhold -- the known dangerous direction.
_A_FEED_HOLE_IS_A_TRAILING_SUFFIX_OF_THE.IMPROVED_DETECTOR_same_cost: Do not test whether the bucket's volume equals ONE constituent minute -- test whether the bucket reproduces the o/c/h/l/v of ANY TRAILING SUFFIX of its minutes (k = 1..n). That catches the partial holes the single-constituent signature misses, costs the same single 1-minute fetch the direction rule already requires, and returns k, which tells you how much of the interval was dropped. The reconciliation GAP remains the trigger; the suffix test identifies the form.
_A_FEED_HOLE_IS_A_TRAILING_SUFFIX_OF_THE.honest_scope: n=2, ONE symbol, ONE window. _A_CROSS_SECTIONAL_DISPERSION_READING_IS.headline: THE 'HAND FORWARD THE NUMBERS, NOT THE VERDICT' RULE HAS A GAP: A DERIVED CROSS-SECTIONAL STATISTIC IS NOT A 'NUMBER' IN THE SAFE SENSE. Today's brief disclaimed its directional verdict from the opening prints -- explicitly, citing the 2026-08-28 finding -- and then drew a CROSS-SECTIONAL verdict from those same disclaimed prints in the same paragraph. This is a BROAD relief rally, not a sector rotation; no index-vs-index divergence to trade.' The same regime object states, correctly, that these are opening-window prints 'recorded as a baseline, not as a decision input', and withholds the directional label on exactly the right grounds.

the_measurement.method: XLF-SPY return spread vs the official 2026-09-10 closes (757.83 / 708.69 / 56.87), computed on 5-minute COMPLETED CLOSES 13:30-14:15Z. _A_CROSS_SECTIONAL_DISPERSION_READING_IS.the_two_errors_this_pins_down_and_they_a: (1) The BRIEF read the statistic at the TIGHTEST bar of the session (13:30, 5.8bp three-way) and concluded 'they move together, no divergence to trade.' (2) THIS RUN's own first pass read two point quotes (13:36Z settled vs 14:20Z live) and was drafting the opposite story -- 'the CPI rally's leader has been sold, financials are rotating out.' At 14:05Z the spread was -17.6bp, essentially back to the brief's figure. BOTH verdicts are artifacts of WHICH TIMESTAMP WAS SAMPLED. The single-timestamp sampling uncertainty (~+/-35bp) is LARGER than the 19bp the brief's conclusion rested on, so the statistic cannot support either reading.
_A_CROSS_SECTIONAL_DISPERSION_READING_IS.THE_TRANSFERABLE_RULE: The 2026-08-25/08-28 rule protects against inheriting a DIRECTION and is silent on inheriting a DISPERSION -- and the brief shows the disclaimer being applied to the direction leg while the cross-sectional leg walked straight past it, in one paragraph, by a careful author. A derived cross-sectional statistic carries the same staleness as a verdict, because its sampling error is on the order of the effect being measured. SO: a dispersion, correlation, breadth or leadership statistic must be quoted WITH ITS WINDOW and WITH ITS RANGE OVER THAT WINDOW, never as a point value; and 'the three move together' is not a finding unless the spread's own swing is smaller than the spread being claimed. One timestamp cannot establish co-movement.
_A_CROSS_SECTIONAL_DISPERSION_READING_IS.what_it_does_NOT_say: It does NOT say financials are being rotated out -- that claim is exactly what the measurement refutes, and no sector read is licensed here. It does NOT invalidate the brief's regime label (the three names are all solidly green; the POST-CPI RELIEF RALLY description survives). It is a claim about the ERROR BAR on a statistic, not about the tape.
_A_CROSS_SECTIONAL_DISPERSION_READING_IS.changed_no_decision: No entry was fundable in either book and no position action turns on XLF. Recorded because a filter's inputs can only be audited credibly on a run the audit does not benefit -- and because this run nearly committed error (2) above before measuring.

_EVENT_WOKEN_RUNS_STAMP_run_utc_AHEAD_OF.headline: A RUN WOKEN BY AN EVENT RATHER THAN BY THE SCHEDULER HAS NO FIRE TIME HANDED TO IT, AND TODAY TWO SUCH RUNS ESTIMATED run_utc FORWARD INSTEAD OF READING THE CLOCK -- STAMPING THEMSELVES 11m25s AND 17m40s AFTER THE COMMITS THAT CARRIED THEM. A journal entry cannot postdate the commit containing it; these do.

the_measurement.method: For each of today's entries, git log -S'<stamp>' -- trade_journal.json gives the commit that INTRODUCED it; compare its committer timestamp to the entry's own run_utc. The commit time is a hard upper bound on the true decision time, so any run_utc later than it is wrong by construction -- no clock-skew argument can rescue it.
readings: CONTROL, same day same file: entry 2026-09-11T17:05:00Z <- commit 8cd851a7 at 17:06:01Z => stamped 61s BEHIND, i.e. correct (decision time, committed a minute later).

The correct one is SCHEDULER-FIRED. n=3 on one day, but the split is clean and the mechanism explains it.
the_measurement.prevalence: EXACTLY 2 of 1,278 entries are stamped in the future relative to a clock reading of 17:16:47Z (corroborated by Robinhood venue timestamps of 17:16:46Z, so the container clock is correct and the entries are not). ZERO entries are out-of-order by run_utc. This is a new defect that appeared today, not a chronic one.

why_it_matters_despite_changing_no_decis: It corrupts THE ONE PRESCRIBED FIX for the dead-man's known blind spot. CLAUDE.md's cadence rule says a health check must assert a RATE by counting scheduler-fired entries per trading day, and that count keys on run_utc. Entries stamped into a future bucket are counted in the wrong bucket -- and these two are ALSO run_type 'market_hours_regular', which the rule says to COUNT, so they are not filtered out by the run_type discipline that was supposed to make cadence math safe.

It inverts the handoff. THIS run read a tail ending at '17:30Z' while its own clock said 17:16Z and nearly concluded its own clock was skewed -- i.e. a run that trusts a forward-stamped predecessor concludes it is running BEFORE work that has already landed on master. That is the precise inverse of the relay's purpose.

Honest scope: it changed no decision here. Both mis-stamped runs were non-trading (an Actions fix and a correction), the book was untouched, and nothing gated on the timestamps. Recorded because a timestamp defect is only auditable on a run where it costs nothing.
_EVENT_WOKEN_RUNS_STAMP_run_utc_AHEAD_OF.the_transferable_shape: This file's most-repeated defect arriving in the metadata rather than the measurement: a value that LOOKS like it was read was actually ESTIMATED, and nothing errors. A scheduler fire hands the run a time; an event wake does not, so the run supplies one -- and a plausible-looking round number ('17:30:00Z') is indistinguishable from a read one. Note that both wrong values are round to the minute AND to a :22/:30 cadence slot, i.e. they were reconstructed from what the run EXPECTED the schedule to be rather than from the clock.
_EVENT_WOKEN_RUNS_STAMP_run_utc_AHEAD_OF.the_detector: Read run_utc from the clock at WRITE time, never estimate it, and never round it to a cadence slot. Cheap assertion before committing any journal entry: its run_utc must be <= now, and after committing it must be <= the commit's own timestamp. One line, and it catches every variant including the ones this key does not enumerate -- same posture as the `git diff --stat` rule: trust the assertion, not your sense of having stamped it correctly.
_EVENT_WOKEN_RUNS_STAMP_run_utc_AHEAD_OF.remediation_applied: Both entries REPAIRED in trade_journal.json by this run: run_utc set to the introducing commit's timestamp (a defensible upper bound on the true decision time), with the original value and the evidence preserved in a _stamp_corrected field on each. _THE_RSI2_TRIGGER_SITS_AT_THE_ENTRY_PRIC.the_mechanism_which_is_the_transferable_: A 2-period RSI is computed off the last few sessions' range and knows NOTHING about the entry price. On a fresh position those two things coincide, because the entry was taken out of that same range -- which is exactly why the parent finding could say the exit banks ~0-1% 'by construction'. As a position drifts away from its entry, the recent range travels with the price and the entry price stays put, so the RSI2 trigger DETACHES from the entry and re-anchors to wherever the stock now trades. The coincidence was never causal; it was an artifact of recency.
_THE_RSI2_TRIGGER_SITS_AT_THE_ENTRY_PRIC.the_operational_consequence: On an aged or stalled name the RSI2>=70 print is NOT a near-breakeven round trip -- it is a DEEPLY RED exit wearing a take-profit's label. The price>entry gate is what stops it, and on this book today it is doing 4.46 and 3.70 points of work, not 0.84. That gate was added by the 2026-08-26 correction (PNC, RSI2 78.5 while 0.34% underwater) and its value scales with how stale the position is: THE OLDER THE POSITION, THE MORE THE GATE IS LOAD-BEARING. Anyone tempted to read the gate as a rounding-scale technicality should read these two numbers.
_THE_RSI2_TRIGGER_SITS_AT_THE_ENTRY_PRIC.the_watch_handed_forward: GD is 0.88 points (+0.25%) from printing RSI2 >= 70 while -4.46% underwater, and it TIME-STOPS 2026-09-15. MMM is 1.98 points (+1.20%) away and TIME-STOPS 2026-09-14. A run that sees either cross MUST NOT bank it as a take-profit: the price>entry gate fails, so under HARD RULE 5 and the 2026-08-26 correction it is an OPTIONAL exit-into-strength routed to THESIS, never a mechanical exit. Note the one way it becomes actionable: report.py annotates a bounce inside TIME_STOP_WARN_DAYS (3) because a position about to be recycled anyway is better sold INTO a bounce than out of one -- both names are inside or entering that window, so an RSI2 pop next week is a legitimate DISCRETIONARY exit-into-strength ahead of a time stop that will sell them regardless. That is a judgment call with the thesis attached, NOT the mechanical trigger firing.
_THE_RSI2_TRIGGER_SITS_AT_THE_ENTRY_PRIC.honest_scope: n=2 stalled names against n=6 fresh ones in the parent finding, one session, one book. The DIRECTION is not in doubt (the mechanism is arithmetic, not statistical) but the 5x magnitude is specific to how far these two have drifted, not a constant. Re-measure per name; do not carry '4.5%' forward as a number.

_THE_REPORT_WINDOW_IS_IN_CT_AND_THE_MARK.found_by: the 19:15Z run, auditing its own already-delivered report
_THE_REPORT_WINDOW_IS_IN_CT_AND_THE_MARK.severity: a factual error in a DELIVERED artifact; corrected by a second push at 19:30Z
_THE_REPORT_WINDOW_IS_IN_CT_AND_THE_MARK.headline: THE DAILY-REPORT THRESHOLD IS SPECIFIED IN CT AND THE MARKET CLOCK RUNS IN ET, SO THE ONE RUN THAT OWNS THE REPORT MUST HOLD TWO DIFFERENT UTC OFFSETS SIMULTANEOUSLY -- AND THE CT OFFSET GETS REUSED FOR ET, INFLATING TIME-TO-BELL BY EXACTLY ONE HOUR.
_THE_REPORT_WINDOW_IS_IN_CT_AND_THE_MARK.what_happened: The run converted the v10 threshold correctly (2:15 PM CT = 19:15Z, CDT = UTC-5) and then described the same instant in ET using the SAME -5 offset, writing '14:16 ET' and '1h45m before the bell'. Correct: EDT = UTC-4, so 19:15Z is 3:15 PM ET and the bell (20:00Z) is 45 MINUTES away, not 1h45m. The error appeared in the report header, in the report's TACTICAL reasoning, in the journal entry and in _last_entry_evaluation -- four places, one conversion.
_THE_REPORT_WINDOW_IS_IN_CT_AND_THE_MARK.why_it_is_not_a_trivial_slip: The Friday-clock argument is one of the two loadbearing reasons the TACTICAL track was declined, and time-to-bell is the variable it turns on. An hour of phantom runway is exactly the margin that would make a scalp look takeable: the corrected clock puts the run at or inside the closing-auction window where the volume-confirmation denominator is unreadable, which is an ADDITIONAL independent bar the wrong figure concealed. The error therefore pointed toward MORE trading, not less -- the dangerous direction.
_THE_REPORT_WINDOW_IS_IN_CT_AND_THE_MARK.why_this_run_was_the_one_to_make_it: Every other market-hours run reasons in ET only and gets it right (the 18:48Z run correctly wrote 'Friday 14:47 ET' for 18:47Z). ONLY the report-owning run is handed a threshold in CT, so only it is ever holding both offsets -- which makes this a latent trap that fires roughly once per trading day, on the single run that produces the artifact Ryan actually reads.
_THE_REPORT_WINDOW_IS_IN_CT_AND_THE_MARK.detector: When a run states a wall-clock time in more than one zone, compute each from UTC independently and CHECK THEM AGAINST EACH OTHER: ET and CT must differ by exactly 1 hour, and time-to-bell must equal 20:00Z minus the run's own UTC stamp. Both are one line of arithmetic. Never derive one zone from the other by reusing an offset. During US DST, ET = UTC-4 and CT = UTC-5; the market bell is 13:30Z-20:00Z.
_THE_REPORT_WINDOW_IS_IN_CT_AND_THE_MARK.the_class: Same family as this file's most-repeated defect, arriving in unit conversion rather than in a filter: a quantity was computed correctly for the purpose it was needed for (the threshold test passed, and the run DID correctly own the report), and then reused for a second purpose with a different basis. A check that passes for the wrong reason -- here, a conversion that is right in the zone it was made in and wrong in the zone it was quoted in.
_THE_REPORT_WINDOW_IS_IN_CT_AND_THE_MARK.honest_scope: CHANGED NO DECISION. _THE_RSI2_EXIT_BANKS_0_TO_1_PERCENT_BY_C.headline: THE BOOK'S MOST-QUOTED EXIT CONSTANT -- 'the RSI2>=70 take-profit sits a mean 0.84% from the ENTRY price BY CONSTRUCTION, so it banks ~0-1%' -- IS NOT A CONSTANT.
