_THE_RSI2_EXIT_BANKS_0_TO_1_PERCENT_BY_C.why_it_matters: This is not a curiosity: the 0.84% measurement is the STATED REASON the magnitude floor was voided (HARD RULE 5 and prompt v10 both argue 'the exit banks ~0-1% of position value BY CONSTRUCTION, so a floor measured against the target can never be satisfied'). THE VOIDING REMAINS CORRECT -- a target-relative floor still cannot be met, and the broker record behind it (trades under +/-$10 are 58% of closes and net +$90.48) is untouched. What is wrong is the REASON, and a reason that is an artifact of when it was measured will mislead the next run that reasons FORWARD from it: a run inheriting 'the take-profit will bank ~1%' would price ABNB's exit near 169.5 when it actually arms at 175.44, and would expect MMM's and GD's to bank a profit when they arm 3.7% and 4.5% BELOW entry, i.e. realize a LOSS while wearing a take-profit label.

The incumbent finding is confirmed, not displaced.
what_is_established_and_what_is_not.NOT ESTABLISHED -- the mechanism behind: This run proposed that recent realized volatility drives the distance and TESTED IT AGAINST THE INCUMBENT. It LOST: correlation of |distance| with 5d mean absolute daily move is r=+0.3742, against r=+0.6895 for held-days. Recorded as a refuted hypothesis rather than dropped. AT n=4 NEITHER r IS EVIDENCE and neither should ever be quoted as such -- four points across two cohorts cannot separate two collinear candidate mechanisms.
what_is_established_and_what_is_not.THE ONE ARITHMETIC FACT THAT SURVIVES TH: ABNB and UNP were entered on the SAME DAY and are the SAME AGE (1d), yet their triggers sit +3.49% and +1.03% from entry -- a 3.4x spread with the age variable held constant. So age, whatever it explains about the sign, CANNOT explain the magnitude. The natural candidate is that ABNB's RSI2 window carries 4.5x UNP's daily move (2.18% vs 0.48%) and a 2-period RSI needs a proportionally larger up-move to traverse to 70 -- a ratio that happens to match, and a match of two ratios at n=2 is a hypothesis, NOT a finding. Do not promote it without more closes.

_THE_RSI2_EXIT_BANKS_0_TO_1_PERCENT_BY_C.the_transferable_shape: A CONSTANT DERIVED FROM ONE CROSS-SECTION IS A SNAPSHOT WEARING THE WORD 'BY CONSTRUCTION'. The phrase 'by construction' is what made this durable and unexamined: it reads as a claim about the ALGEBRA of a 2-period RSI (which would be regime-free and permanent) when it is in fact a claim about one day's BOOK (four names, their ages and their realized vols on 2026-09-02). This file's most-repeated defect is a check that passes for the wrong reason; this is its sibling -- a number that is TRUE for the wrong reason, and therefore silently stops being true. Detector: when a rule quotes a measured constant to justify itself, re-solve the constant on the CURRENT book before reasoning forward from it. Here that cost one bisection per position.

_THE_CALIBRATION_OPTIONS_BUCKET_BLENDS_T.WHY_IT_IS_A_MIS_SPECIFICATION_AND_NOT_JU: CLAUDE.md defines the hedge as insurance and EXEMPTS it from every premium backstop precisely because it is 'expected to decay in a melt-up'. A directional trade that loses money is evidence the entry was wrong; an insurance leg that loses money is evidence the insured-against event did not happen. Scoring them in one bucket means THE CALIBRATION IS BIASED TOWARD 'EDGE GONE' EXACTLY IN THE TAPES WHERE THE HEDGE DID ITS JOB -- it reads a successful risk-management outcome as a trading failure. The bias is directional and systematic, not noise.
_THE_CALIBRATION_OPTIONS_BUCKET_BLENDS_T.THE_FORWARD_CONSEQUENCE_THAT_MAKES_THIS_: calibrate.recommend() checks `stats.n < MIN_TRADES_FOR_ACTION` (20) and returns REPORT ONLY BEFORE the KILL branch is ever reached -- verified by reading the source this run, and it matches the spec (the KILL branch is exempt from the IN-REGIME gate, not from the SAMPLE-SIZE gate; those are an attribution guard and a precision guard, different things). So at n=18 nothing fires. AT n=20 WITH THE HEDGE STILL IN THE BUCKET, a negative margin fires KILL: position_size_multiplier 0.5, new_entries PAUSED, escalate to Ryan. The book would halve its options size on the strength of an insurance decay. It is TWO CLOSES AWAY.
_THE_CALIBRATION_OPTIONS_BUCKET_BLENDS_T.THE_FIX: Split the options bucket before calibrating: score DIRECTIONAL option trades (the desk's own TACTICAL/CORE entries) as the edge sample, and account for hedge legs separately as a cost of carrying the defensive posture. The broker feed CANNOT do this alone -- get_pnl_trade_history returns no placed_agent and no hedge tag, so the hedge is only identifiable by cross-referencing get_option_orders and holdings.json. Any future split must be driven off the ledger, not the P&L feed.
_THE_CALIBRATION_OPTIONS_BUCKET_BLENDS_T.HONEST_SCOPE__READ_THIS_BEFORE_QUOTING_E: Do NOT carry forward '+3.0 pts' as the options book's true edge. n=17 vs n=18 are both far too small for either margin to be meaningful, and the ex-hedge figure is not a better estimate -- it is the SAME tiny sample minus one point. The claim here is narrow and structural: A SINGLE INSURANCE TRADE CAN INVERT THE VERDICT, WHICH MEANS THE BUCKET IS MIS-SPECIFIED NO MATTER WHICH SIDE IT LANDS ON. That would be true had the hedge closed at a profit.
_THE_CALIBRATION_OPTIONS_BUCKET_BLENDS_T.the_class: This file's denominator/sample family, arriving at the CALIBRATION rather than at a volume clause: a statistic is only as good as what is allowed into its sample, and a sample assembled by asset class rather than by INTENT mixes two activities with opposite success criteria. Sibling of the iv_rv_ratio earnings-gap artifact -- there one event day dominated a 30-sample stdev; here one insurance leg dominates an 18-trade edge estimate.
_THE_CALIBRATION_OPTIONS_BUCKET_BLENDS_T.detector: Before any edge statistic decides a parameter, ask what the sample is a sample OF. If it contains positions held for a purpose other than the edge being measured -- hedges, assignments, transfers, legging-test residue (the 08-26 SPY 0/-3/-13 rows are in this same bucket) -- it is measuring two things at once.

_A_BLENDED_CALIBRATION_SAMPLE_PASSES_BOT.WHY_NEITHER_GUARD_CATCHES_IT_and_this_is: The module has exactly two guards and a blended sample defeats both BY CONSTRUCTION, not by accident. (1) MIN_TRADES_FOR_ACTION=20 is a floor, so BLENDING RAISES n AND MAKES THE GUARD EASIER TO CLEAR -- each book alone is under 20 (51 equities pass, but the options bucket at 18 does not), while the blend at 69 sails through. The guard that exists to demand a big enough sample is satisfied by the very act of contaminating it. (2) recommend()'s in_regime_trades defaults to stats.n, i.e. 'the whole sample is in-regime', so a caller that does not pass the argument -- the natural thing to do when you have not split the books and have no per-book regime date -- disables the attribution gate silently. Two guards, both passed, nothing logged as skipped.
_A_BLENDED_CALIBRATION_SAMPLE_PASSES_BOT.WHY_IT_IS_A_MIS_SPECIFICATION_AND_NOT_A_: A directional trade that loses money is evidence the entry was wrong. An insurance leg that loses money is evidence the insured-against event did not happen -- CLAUDE.md defines the hedge as exempt from every premium backstop precisely because it is 'expected to decay in a melt-up'. Scoring them together biases the calibration toward 'edge gone' EXACTLY IN THE TAPES WHERE THE HEDGE DID ITS JOB. What today adds to the 09-11 finding is the BLAST RADIUS: the 09-11 run scoped the damage to the options bucket's own KILL branch and judged it two closes away. It is not confined there. Through the blend it reaches the EQUITY parameters -- a different book, with an opposite and demonstrably healthy edge -- and it is live today, not at n=20.
_A_BLENDED_CALIBRATION_SAMPLE_PASSES_BOT.THE_ROOT_FIX_APPLIED: calibrate.py: edge_stats() now inspects each trade's `side` and sets a new EdgeStats.mixed_book flag when the sample carries BOTH 'sell' (equity) and '' (option) closes; recommend() returns 'REFUSED -- blended sample' as its FIRST guard, before the n and in-regime checks, and adjusts nothing. Verified this run: EQUITIES and both OPTIONS buckets return byte-identical verdicts to the pre-fix run, and only the blended path changes -- from three applied parameter changes to REFUSED.
_A_BLENDED_CALIBRATION_SAMPLE_PASSES_BOT.why_the_guard_is_FIRST_and_why_that_does: A blended margin is not a measurement of anything, so nothing downstream of it is meaningful -- including the KILL branch, which is deliberately exempt from the in-regime gate. A blended KILL would halve the EQUITY book's size on OPTIONS losses, which is the same defect pointing the other way. Refusing does not suppress a risk-off signal: splitting the sample is one line and a real KILL survives it, arriving attributed to the book that produced it. The guard demands attribution, not delay.
_A_BLENDED_CALIBRATION_SAMPLE_PASSES_BOT.non_breaking_by_design: A per-book sample is never mixed, so every compliant call is untouched. A sample whose trades carry no `side` key at all leaves the flag False -- provenance unknown is not the same as known-bad, and silently refusing a synthetic or hand-built sample would be its own trap.
_A_BLENDED_CALIBRATION_SAMPLE_PASSES_BOT.HONEST_SCOPE: This changed NO trading decision: the market is shut, both books return REPORT ONLY on their own, and no parameter was written. It is also NOT a claim that the options book is fine -- at n=17/18 nothing about that sleeve is measurable. _CONCURRENT_RUNS_SPLIT_ON_A_DISCRETIONAR.NOT_A_RULE_VIOLATION_and_say_so_plainly: HARD RULE 5 makes the underwater RSI2 bounce an OPTIONAL exit-into-strength routed to thesis. Optional means BOTH hold and sell were permissible, so neither run broke a rule and neither is provably wrong on process. The 14:00Z run's decline was well-argued; the acting run's exit is the same class as the MDLZ 2026-09-09 exit this book already took. _CONCURRENT_RUNS_SPLIT_ON_A_DISCRETIONAR.the_structural_finding_which_is_the_tran: THE EXISTING COLLISION RULE COVERS RUNS THAT AGREE AND ACT TWICE (the 2026-08-28 double-entry: ROST + MDLZ, two runs, same trigger, two fills). This is the UNRECORDED inverse: runs that DISAGREE. And disagreement does not resolve symmetrically, because the two available actions are not symmetric in permanence. A run that DECLINES an optional exit leaves the decision open -- the next run, and the next, may each take it. A run that ACTS closes it permanently and irreversibly. So across a relay of concurrent and successive runs, an optional exit is taken if ANY run in the sequence votes to take it, while a hold requires EVERY run to keep voting hold. The aggregation is a logical OR over sell-votes, not a majority or a considered consensus. THE BOOK WILL THEREFORE TAKE OPTIONAL EXITS SYSTEMATICALLY MORE OFTEN THAN ANY SINGLE RUN'S JUDGEMENT WOULD IMPLY, and no individual run can observe this happening -- each one only ever sees its own decision.
_CONCURRENT_RUNS_SPLIT_ON_A_DISCRETIONAR.why_the_broker_precheck_does_NOT_fix_thi: Worth stating because the fix for the double-entry case looks superficially applicable. The 2026-08-28 rule (re-read the broker immediately before placing; a filled order this run did not place means DEFER) works there because both runs wanted the SAME action, so whichever checks second stands down and the outcome is correct. It cannot help here: the declining run has nothing to place, so it never reaches a pre-place check, and the acting run's own precheck correctly shows no sibling order for GD. Both prechecks pass. The mechanism is invisible to the control that was built for its sibling case -- this file's most-repeated shape, a check that passes for the wrong reason, arriving one decision-type to the left of where the check points.
_CONCURRENT_RUNS_SPLIT_ON_A_DISCRETIONAR.honest_scope: n=1 for an observed split; the ASYMMETRY ARGUMENT is structural and does not depend on n, but the claim that it materially biases results does. It is also NOT evidence the exit was bad: GD sold at 358.0976 against a 13-day-old entry at 374.4437, and whether that beat holding one more day to the 09-15 time stop is unknowable today and should be MEASURED on 09-15 rather than asserted now -- which is exactly what _THE_WARN_WINDOW_EXIT_INTO_STRENGTH_HEURISTIC_IS_UNMEASURED... asks for. This entry adds a third data point to that open measurement, and the 09-15 close is the checkable trigger.

_THE_CONFIRMATION_WINDOW_AND_THE_ENTRY_V.what_this_licenses_and_what_it_does_not: It does NOT license loosening the confirmation clause, entering un-confirmed breaks, or chasing. It does NOT license re-tuning any threshold -- the 2026-08-26 capstone's conclusion stands untouched: successive fixes to the instrument have left the result unchanged, so regime, not measurement, has been the dominant variable. What it DOES suggest, for a future run to test rather than assume: on a structural level with a live trigger, the honest question is whether the entry is viable AT the moment of confirmation, and that is answerable with two lines of arithmetic (stop distance in points vs distance above the level) BEFORE the confirming bar closes. A run that pre-computes the viability boundary when the break first prints can tell the next run exactly what price still works -- which is a handoff, not a loosening.

_AN_INDEX_LEVEL_RECOVERY_IS_NOT_EVIDENCE.the_mechanism_and_it_is_the_transferable: A veto scoped to a COMPLEX cannot be retired by a reading taken on the INDEX that contains it, because the index is mostly not that complex. QQQ's 45bp recovery is arithmetically compatible with SMH getting worse -- and on this tape it was exactly that, the non-semis majority of the Nasdaq bidding while the semis bled. A run that re-graded the semis 'on fresh numbers' and reached for the most salient fresh number (the index it had already fetched for the tape read) would have upgraded four C-grades on a denominator that contains almost no information about them. Same family as this repo's volume-denominator arc: the number is real, the question it answers is not the question being asked.
_AN_INDEX_LEVEL_RECOVERY_IS_NOT_EVIDENCE.the_honest_qualifier_which_is_load_beari: THE SEMIS WERE NOT UNIFORMLY WORSE AND SAYING SO WOULD OVERCLAIM. Internals are MIXED: NVDA +37bp and MU +39bp IMPROVED, AMAT was flat to the basis point, and only LRCX (-81bp) genuinely deteriorated; the ETF's -15bp is the cap-weighted net. So the finding is NOT 'semis kept falling' -- it is that the complex was flat-to-worse while the index gained 45bp, so the index move carried no evidence either way about the complex. Two names improving is also not a resolution: the catalyst (chip-export regulatory plus memory cost, verified by web search at 14:20Z) has no resolution date, and trend-maturity leg (b) fails on an UNRESOLVED catalyst regardless of which way the tape ticked for 100 minutes.

The direction of the dispersion is measured; the ~60bp magnitude is one reading and carries no threshold. Do not derive a rule about how much dispersion widening constitutes a veto -- the point is only that the index reading is the WRONG denominator, not that 60bp is a number that means something.

_DENOMINATOR_B_OF_THE_200DAY_CUSHION_GAT.method: get_equity_historicals(day, 2026-08-11..2026-09-11) for the eight entered names + get_equity_technical_indicators(sma,200,day) last:20 each. _DENOMINATOR_B_OF_THE_200DAY_CUSHION_GAT.the_mechanism_which_is_the_transferable_: B divides the cushion by the decline rate measured over EXACTLY THE THREE SESSIONS THAT PRODUCED THE RSI2<10 PRINT. The Connors screen selects names for being at the steepest point of a short decline -- that IS the entry condition. So B is computed, by construction, on the steepest slope each candidate will ever show, and extrapolating it linearly forward assumes the mean reversion the entry exists to buy does not occur. The gate therefore cannot be satisfied by the kind of name the strategy is built to take, and a near-universal veto is indistinguishable from a working filter unless someone counts.
_DENOMINATOR_B_OF_THE_200DAY_CUSHION_GAT.this_is_the_MAGNITUDE_FLOOR_SHAPE_AGAIN: CLAUDE.md voided the magnitude floor 'not because it reasoned badly but because its premise was wrong: the exit banks ~0-1% of position value BY CONSTRUCTION, so a floor measured against the target can never be satisfied.' Identical here: the decline rate is steepest BY CONSTRUCTION at an RSI2<10 print, so a cushion measured against it can almost never survive the hold. Both are desk-invented heuristics layered on top of a written gate; both read as rigour; both veto the strategy's own setups. The detector for the class: when a self-invented filter declines nearly everything, test it against the entries the book ALREADY TOOK -- if it would have vetoed the winners, the premise is wrong, not the board.

WHAT_THIS_CHANGES.B_is_DEMOTED_not_deleted: B is no longer sufficient on its own to decline a candidate. Quote it, but a B-only failure is now an OBSERVATION, not a veto -- it must be paired with an independent objection (a still-falling sector complex, a broken thesis, a binary event inside the hold) that is stated separately. GD's single true positive is why this is a demotion rather than a repeal: an active, sustained decline into a thin cushion is a real risk, just not a 1-in-1 one.
WHAT_THIS_CHANGES.A_is_UNTOUCHED_and_still_binds: Denominator A -- cushion / the average's own upward drift, price frozen -- is a different claim and this finding says nothing against it. A is the LIN finding (2026-09-04) and the certification-expiry finding (2026-09-11): it measures whether the ENTRY GATE ITSELF survives the hold, which needs no assumption about price at all. SBUX (A 5.2 sessions) and RTX (A 9.7) are declined on A and those declines STAND unchanged.

THE_TRANSFERABLE_PART_and_it_is_why_FCX_.the_two_objections_are_one_measurement_r: 'The dip is still falling, so why NOW is unanswered' and 'the bounce already happened, so the entry is late' are NOT two independent objections to a mean-reversion entry. They are the SAME quantity -- distance travelled since the low -- evaluated at opposite ends. Dissolving one MANUFACTURES the other. A candidate is takeable only in the narrow window between them, and that window is a matter of hours, not sessions.

DEFECT_1_the_catalyst_was_mislabelled.why_the_distinction_is_load_bearing_and_: An export-control action is a POLICY BINARY: it has a decision-maker, a docket and a resolution date, so 'defer until it resolves' is a coherent instruction with an implicit expiry. A published essay has NONE of those. There is nothing scheduled to resolve, so the deferral the desk wrote had NO EXPIRY AND NO TRIGGER -- precisely the shape THE CAPITAL POLICY forbids for a cash hold ('an unexpiring waiting-for-something-better hold is the floor sneaking back and is FORBIDDEN'). The mislabel did not merely get a fact wrong; it manufactured an unbounded exclusion of six names and disguised it as a dated one.
DEFECT_1_the_catalyst_was_mislabelled.the_structural_gap_this_exposes_and_it_i: HARD RULE 7's news/thesis check is gated on PROPOSING a trade -- 'before proposing any alerted SELL or BUY'. So a name declined ON A CATALYST never has that catalyst verified, because the decline happens upstream of the gate that would check it. The error is therefore SELF-SEALING: the cheaper the decline, the less scrutiny the reason gets, and the label then propagates through the relay as settled fact. FIX: run the news check BEFORE a catalyst-based deferral, not only before an order. A deferral is a decision and costs real capital -- today it cost four runs' worth of a below-floor book sitting on $1,470 of deployable cash.

_A_RANGE_RELATIVE_ENTRY_GATE_INVERTS_WHE.headline: The FCX reopening condition written at 17:05Z is RANGE-RELATIVE ('trades back into the LOWER HALF of a session range ... re-derived not inherited') and has been re-derived and checked three times today. _A_RANGE_RELATIVE_ENTRY_GATE_INVERTS_WHE.why_it_survived_three_correct_checks: Because the gate's VALUE and the gate's FORM are different objects and only the value was ever tested. Each run re-derived the band honestly, computed the percentage correctly, and reported NOT MET correctly. A gate returning the right answer supplies no evidence about whether it would return the right answer at a different price -- this file's most-repeated defect, a check that passes for the wrong reason, arriving in a condition that has never yet been wrong.

the_conflict_with_the_standing_rule_and_.the_two_rules_collide: The standing rule is unambiguous: 'any trigger written with numbers in it must state the window those numbers came from, and every run must re-derive them before testing it' (2026-08-25T17:22Z, the stale-box finding). The 17:05Z key obeyed it explicitly -- '~68.5 on today's 67.01-70.06 band, RE-DERIVED NOT INHERITED'. For THIS quantity, obedience is what introduces the defect.
the_conflict_with_the_standing_rule_and_.why_the_rules_differ_and_it_is_not_arbit: Re-derivation is mandatory for a quantity that is a RATE or a LEVEL the market is genuinely re-setting -- a trailing volume baseline, a moving average, a live session box being tested for a break. It is WRONG for a quantity whose denominator RATCHETS: the session range's low is non-increasing and its high non-decreasing, so the midpoint is dragged upward by exactly the price action the gate exists to disqualify. Re-deriving a ratcheting denominator does not refresh the test, it relaxes it.
the_conflict_with_the_standing_rule_and_.the_rule_to_carry: BEFORE RE-DERIVING A TRIGGER, ASK WHICH DIRECTION THE RE-DERIVATION MOVES THE BAR. If a re-derived trigger becomes EASIER to satisfy in the direction the setup is supposed to be disqualified for, it is ratcheting and must be PINNED to an absolute level at the moment it is written -- with the anchor stated, so a later run can tell a pin from a stale number. Stale and pinned look identical in the file and are opposite in kind; only the stated anchor distinguishes them.
the_conflict_with_the_standing_rule_and_.family: Fourth denominator-direction defect in this repo, and the first outside the volume clause. Prior three: session-average baseline too STRICT (08-25), trailing-local too EASY in a decaying tape (08-26), closing-auction too EASY in absolute terms (08-27), post-flush trailing window too STRICT (08-28). Same shape, different instrument: a denominator that moves for reasons unrelated to the question being asked.

_A_REPORT_CYCLE_CAN_MINT_A_WHOLE_NEW_RSI.claim: A SINGLE MID-SESSION REPORT CYCLE CAN MINT AN ENTIRE NEW RSI2 COHORT OUT OF A SECTOR BREAK THAT IS STILL IN PROGRESS -- AND THOSE NAMES ARE AT THEIR LEAST ENTRY-ABLE AT THE EXACT MOMENT THEY FIRST APPEAR. The screen does not find names that HAVE fallen; between two cycles it finds names that ARE falling. So the newest cohort on any board is systematically the worst, and its novelty reads as opportunity precisely because no prior run has declined it.

_A_REPORT_CYCLE_CAN_MINT_A_WHOLE_NEW_RSI.the_detector: WHEN ONE REPORT CYCLE ADDS TWO OR MORE NAMES FROM A SINGLE SECTOR THAT WERE ABSENT FROM THE PRIOR CYCLE, DATE THE SECTOR'S BREAK BEFORE GRADING ANY MEMBER. One get_equity_historicals call on the sector ETF and the two largest members answers it. If the break is same-session and still extending, the cohort is distribution and not opportunity, and the correct output is a decline that says so. Test the cohort against the INDEX, never against its own sector ETF -- a cap-weighted ETF whose non-bank majority is flat will understate a bank de-rate by 5x, as XLF did here (2.83x vs a 12.9x cohort mean).
_A_REPORT_CYCLE_CAN_MINT_A_WHOLE_NEW_RSI.why_this_is_the_mirror_of_the_tension_fi: _TAPE_CONFIRMATION_AND_THE_RSI2_SCREEN_ARE_IN_TENSION establishes that a name which visibly CONFIRMS disqualifies itself from the screen that found it, within about one report cycle. This establishes the entry side of the same mechanism: the screen ADMITS names at the moment of maximum distribution. Together they say the RSI2 board is biased at BOTH ends -- it drops names as they turn up and adds them as they break down -- so recency on the board is a hazard signal, not a freshness merit.
_A_REPORT_CYCLE_CAN_MINT_A_WHOLE_NEW_RSI.honest_scope: This changed no decision that a correct application of the existing rules would not also have reached, and it licensed no trade -- which is the only condition under which an entry filter can be audited credibly. n=1 board turnover on one sector. The claim is about the MECHANISM (a mid-session screen samples in-progress moves), which is structural and does not depend on this cohort's outcome. It is explicitly NOT a claim that these four names will keep falling; a sharp one-day repricing in a mega-cap bank is a legitimate Connors setup in the abstract, and if the FOMC resolves and the tape stabilizes these are worth re-grading FROM SCRATCH on post-event numbers, never on today's grade.

THE_FINDING_STATED_PRECISELY_AND_NOT_OVE.what_IS_true: That conjunction is far narrower than either gate looks on its own, and nobody has written it down. Applied jointly, the desk's live entry criterion for an RSI2 name is: 'in the lower half of the session range AND already turning up against the index' -- buy the bounce after it starts but before it travels. Each gate as WRITTEN contains only one of those two clauses, so FCX is being judged with no trajectory test and RTX with no position test.
THE_FINDING_STATED_PRECISELY_AND_NOT_OVE.why_that_matters_more_than_it_looks: A gate that states one clause of a two-clause criterion will decline correctly and hand forward a reopening condition that is INSUFFICIENT. FCX's written gate is satisfiable by FCX simply falling -- which, on the day it happens, is precisely the 'still making session lows' condition that disqualifies RTX. So the FCX reopening condition, if met tomorrow and acted on literally, would license an entry the RTX standard forbids. The two names would be entered on incompatible standards, and neither key says so.
THE_FINDING_STATED_PRECISELY_AND_NOT_OVE.the_narrowness_is_also_a_cadence_problem: 'Lower half of range AND already turning' is a window that opens and shuts inside a session. This desk runs every ~15 minutes and, per the standing opening-deferral preference, takes its equity entry after ~14:15Z off a signal computed on the PREVIOUS close. A criterion this tight is not reliably observable at that cadence -- which is an argument for grading on the ENTRY STACK (thesis strength, setup quality, distance to target, the 200-day cushion) rather than on intraday range position at all.

_A_CASH_HOLDS_NAMED_OPPORTUNITY_WAS_REFU.THE_MECHANISM_which_is_the_transferable_: THE CAPITAL POLICY requires a hold to name (a) an opportunity, (b) a checkable trigger, (c) an expiry -- three parts, specifically so a later run can TEST the hold rather than inherit it. When (a) silently goes false, nothing errors: the hold still LOOKS three-part, a run checking it validates the trigger and the expiry (both still true), and the hold's real binding force quietly collapses onto the DATE alone. A three-part gate degraded to a one-part gate is indistinguishable from a healthy one unless someone re-reads the prose. This is the repo's most-repeated shape -- a check that passes for the wrong reason -- arriving inside the object the policy uses to prevent exactly this failure.
_A_CASH_HOLDS_NAMED_OPPORTUNITY_WAS_REFU.why_the_correcting_run_did_not_catch_it: It wrote a NEW key instead of editing the one carrying the refuted claim. That is the 2026-08-25 session-key lesson verbatim -- 'preserve the FINDING; do not preserve the CONTAINER... if your contribution narrows, corrects or supersedes an existing key, EDIT that key and say what changed'. The rule is written about proliferation (too many keys) and was never read as also being about STALENESS (the superseded key left standing). One additive correction leaves two objects disagreeing, and the relay inherits whichever it reads first.

So the semis component of the hold's opportunity resolves before the hold does, and after 09-15 the hold would be sitting on capital for a reason that had already been discharged. _A_CASH_HOLDS_NAMED_OPPORTUNITY_WAS_REFU.detector: Before crediting an inherited governance object -- a cash hold, a reopening condition, a deferral -- RE-READ ITS PREMISE, not just its trigger and expiry. Ask: has anything measured since this was written refuted the reason it exists? A dated trigger that still parses is not evidence the object is sound. Cheapest form: when a run refutes a claim, grep the ledger for the objects that assert it and edit them in the same pass -- the same discipline the lot-invariant rule applies to derived numeric fields, applied to derived PROSE.

RESULT_2_the_range_position_gate_is_an_A.THE_DETECTOR: Before letting a range-position gate decide anything, compute the session range AS A PERCENTAGE OF PRICE. If that percentage is small relative to the move the trade is sized for, the gate is resolving noise and its reading carries no information about the setup. Quote the range-as-%-of-price alongside the position figure, always -- the position figure alone is unreadable without it.
RESULT_2_the_range_position_gate_is_an_A.the_family_this_belongs_to: Same shape as this file's three recorded volume-denominator defects (session-average too strict, trailing-local too easy in a decaying tape, post-flush too strict), arriving in a PRICE gate rather than a volume one: a ratio whose denominator is itself a moving, regime-dependent quantity was read as though it were a fixed scale. The 09-17 row was written to the paper log and never mirrored here. *** WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC: `results` is the natural input to day_track.track_status(), and the two sources return OPPOSITE verdicts. Measured 2026-09-18 at equity $3,437.77: from the 3-row paper log -> {'paused': True, '3 consecutive losing days -- rest of week'}; from the 2-row `results` array -> {'paused': False, 'active'}. THE STALE SOURCE FAILS OPEN. A run that computed the pause from `results` would have taken a DAY TRACK signal that both pause conditions forbid (3 consecutive losers AND the week at -3.00R), and nothing would have errored -- the permissive answer is indistinguishable from a correct one. *** THE CLASS, which is this file's most-repeated shape arriving in a new place: two sources of truth for one fact, where the one that is easier to read is the one that goes stale, and the failure direction is PERMISSIVE. A safety interlock must be computed from the source that is WRITTEN on every event, not the one that is convenient to read. *** THE DURABLE RULE: day_track_paper.json is the authoritative history while status == PAPER; `results` mirrors it. Any run computing track_status() or graduate() MUST take max(len) of the two sources, or read the paper log directly while in PAPER, and MUST re-sync them in the same pass -- never read one and leave the other. Asserted, not eyeballed: len(_DAY_TRACK.results) == len(day_track_paper.json['rows']) while status == 'PAPER'. *** EXTENDED 2026-09-21T17:05Z, SAME SUBJECT, SECOND MECHANISM -- A MIRROR DESYNCS BY REBUILD JUST AS EASILY AS BY OMISSION, AND THE REBUILD IS THE ONE THAT PASSES THE LENGTH ASSERTION. The 09-18 incident was a MISSING row, which len(results) == len(rows) catches. This run closed paper day 4 by filtering the open 09-21 row OUT of `results` and appending a freshly-built closed summary -- length stayed 4 == 4, the assertion PASSED, and the row silently lost `decided_utc`, `decided_by`, `action`, `shares`, `r_usd` and `_mirror_of`, while setting `exit` to a FLOAT where the 09-15/16/17 rows all carry `exit` as the full OBJECT and the float in `exit_px`. Caught by reading `git diff --stat` and then the diff body before committing -- the whole-run assertion, exactly as _A_RUN_COMMITTED_ITS_STALE_CLONE_OVER_MASTER... prescribes -- and reverted with `git checkout origin/master -- holdings.json` and re-applied. *** THE DURABLE RULE, which is the specific form the 09-18 rule was missing: CLOSE A MIRROR ROW BY UPDATING IT IN PLACE. Never filter-and-append a rebuilt row into a mirror array; a rebuild preserves only the fields the author happened to think of, and the entry-decision fields are exactly the ones a closing run is not thinking about. *** STRENGTHEN THE ASSERTION ACCORDINGLY -- length is necessary and not sufficient. Assert FIELD AGREEMENT against the paper log, which this run now does and which would have failed on the rebuilt row: for each pair, trading_day_et, status, r_multiple and exit_px must all agree. *** THE CLASS, and it is this file's most-repeated shape arriving inside the safeguard written for it: a check that passes for the wrong reason. The 09-18 rule named the right invariant but encoded the CHEAP half of it, and the cheap half is blind to the failure mode that preserves count while destroying content.

_DAY_TRACK_BAR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH.severity: BLOCKING, and found on the ONE day it mattered -- the DAY TRACK's paper phase starts trading day 2026-09-15 and no run had ever called day_track.py against live data.
_DAY_TRACK_BAR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH.the_defect: day_track.opening_range() read b['high'] / b['low'] / b['open'] / b['close'] and atr() read cur['high'] / cur['low'] / prev['close'] -- five accessors, all terse-form. get_equity_historicals(interval='minute') returns 'open_price' / 'high_price' / 'low_price' / 'close_price' (plus begins_at, volume, session). EVERY accessor raises KeyError on a real bar. The first run at/after 09:35 ET would have thrown instead of writing the 09-15 paper row, and the track would have logged zero signals while looking merely quiet.
_DAY_TRACK_BAR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH.why_the_selftest_passed: _selftest() builds its fixtures by hand as dict(open=..., high=..., low=..., close=...) -- THE SAME ASSUMPTION AS THE BUG. The test and the code agreed with each other and neither agreed with the broker. This is the repo's most-documented failure class ('a check that passes for the wrong reason') arriving inside the one artifact whose whole job is to catch it: a fixture is only evidence about the schema it was copied FROM.
_DAY_TRACK_BAR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH.the_fix: Added _bf(bar, field) which tries '<field>_price' first, then '<field>', and raises a KeyError naming the bar's actual keys if neither is present. Both functions now go through it, so hand-built fixtures AND connector bars both work and a bar carrying both spellings is read the broker's way. Wire values arrive as STRINGS; _bf floats them.
_DAY_TRACK_BAR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH.the_guard_that_makes_it_stick: _selftest() now carries a CONNECTOR-SCHEMA case built from five verbatim get_equity_historicals QQQ bars (2026-09-14 13:30-13:34Z, string values preserved) plus a wire-schema ATR case. That case fails if _bf is ever removed; the terse fixtures cannot. VERIFIED end-to-end after the fix: OR high 703.99 / low 702.75 / open 703.33 / close 703.34, direction 'none' (body 0.01 < 10% of the 1.24 range), ATR14 14.0, plan_entry -> skip 'doji opening bar'.
_DAY_TRACK_BAR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH.transferable_lesson: WHEN A MODULE IS WRITTEN AHEAD OF ITS FIRST LIVE CALL, ITS TESTS ENCODE THE AUTHOR'S GUESS AT THE UPSTREAM SCHEMA, NOT THE SCHEMA. Pin at least one fixture to bytes actually returned by the upstream call, copied verbatim, before the module's first live use. Same family as 'the broker is the arbiter' -- applied to a data SHAPE rather than to a position or a price.
_DAY_TRACK_BAR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH.scope_and_honesty: This changed NO trading decision: the track is PAPER (no orders), the market was shut when the fix was made (13:25Z, bell 13:30Z), and yesterday's OR was a doji the track would have skipped anyway. It is a code repair, not a rule change -- it adds no gate, filter or screen to the DAY TRACK, which the spec forbids an unattended run from doing. graduate(), the parameters and the PAPER->LIVE conditions are untouched.
_DAY_TRACK_BAR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH.still_gating_live: Unchanged: LIVE needs (a) day_track.graduate() == go_live at a Monday calibration AND (b) a v11 stamp on the run's own invocation. This run was invoked with v10, so PAPER stands.

_DAY_TRACK_SHORT_SIDE_SIZED_IN_THE_WRONG.found_by: scheduled run 13:30Z 2026-09-15 (unattended, prompt v10), on the DAY TRACK's FIRST EVER SIGNAL
_DAY_TRACK_SHORT_SIDE_SIZED_IN_THE_WRONG.severity: BLOCKING for the short side. Caught in PAPER, which is what PAPER is for. Second day_track defect in 12 hours -- the 13:25Z run fixed the bar-schema KeyError this morning.
_DAY_TRACK_SHORT_SIDE_SIZED_IN_THE_WRONG.what_happened: The 09-15 opening range printed SHORT (OR open 708.79, close 707.88, body 70.3% of a 1.295-pt range), so the vehicle is PSQ, not QQQ. plan_entry() passed price_now -- the QQQ price, 708.10 -- straight into size(), and size() divides deployable cash by that price. It returned 2 SHARES / $1,416.20. The trade is in PSQ at $26.195, where $1,470.86 of deployable cash buys 56 SHARES / $1,466.92. Placing the returned number would have deployed $52.39 -- 3.6% of the intended position. risk_usd was equally meaningless: $1.51 computed from QQQ shares x a QQQ stop distance, against the true $1.56 on the PSQ leg.
_DAY_TRACK_SHORT_SIDE_SIZED_IN_THE_WRONG.second_defect_same_function: plan_entry's own note read: 'for PSQ translate as psq_stop = psq_entry * (1 + stop_dist_pct/100)'. stop_dist_pct is an absolute value, so that formula puts the stop ABOVE the entry -- and PSQ is held LONG. A stop-loss above a long entry is rejected by the broker or fills instantly. Under v11 (which grants this track stop-order authority) that note is the number a run types into the resting stop order, so it is the more dangerous of the two.
_DAY_TRACK_SHORT_SIDE_SIZED_IN_THE_WRONG.why_neither_was_caught_earlier: EVERY fixture in _selftest was a LONG. The long path is correct by coincidence -- for a long the vehicle IS the signal symbol, so price_now is the right price and the stop is already on the right side. A test suite that only exercises the side where two variables happen to coincide cannot distinguish them. Exactly the shape of this morning's schema bug, whose fixtures encoded the same assumption as the code; both are instances of the file's most-repeated defect, a check that passes for the wrong reason.
_DAY_TRACK_SHORT_SIDE_SIZED_IN_THE_WRONG.fix_applied: day_track.plan_entry now takes vehicle_px and sizes on the instrument actually bought; a new vehicle_stop() translates the signal stop onto the vehicle and returns a stop BELOW entry on BOTH sides (both vehicles are held long, so the sign is carried by which vehicle you bought, not by the formula); the output carries vehicle_px and stop_px_vehicle alongside stop_px_signal. A SHORT call with vehicle_px missing or equal to price_now now returns action='wait' rather than silently mis-sizing -- fail loud, since the wrong answer here looks perfectly plausible. A short-side self-test asserting 56 shares and a sub-entry stop is added. Selftest passes. NO parameter, gate, filter or threshold was touched: this is arithmetic, not a rule change, so it does not run into the DAY TRACK's bar on unattended runs adding gates.
_DAY_TRACK_SHORT_SIDE_SIZED_IN_THE_WRONG.transferable_lesson: A module with a LONG vehicle and a SHORT vehicle has two price scales, and every function that takes 'price' must say WHICH. The long side hides the bug because signal and vehicle are the same instrument there. When a strategy is asymmetric in its instruments, the asymmetric side needs its own test on day one -- not the first time the market happens to produce it.

_DAY_TRACK_VS_CASH_HOLD_UNSETTLED_2026-0.the_collision: _DAY_TRACK.capital_priority: 'The day trade claims deployable cash at its entry run; swing-book entries that day wait until it is flat or skipped.' THE CAPITAL POLICY: a _cash_hold parks capital against a named, dated catalyst until it expires. arithmetic_which_does_not_depend_on_samp.signal_stop_distance: QQQ entry 708.10 -> stop 708.855 = 0.755 points = 0.1066% of spot.

arithmetic_which_does_not_depend_on_samp.spread_as_a_fraction_of_R: PSQ quoted 26.15 x 26.16 at 13:45:59Z -> a 1-cent spread = 35.84% of the stop distance = 0.358R per crossing. QQQ quoted 709.05 x 709.09 -> a 4-cent spread = 5.30% of its stop distance = 0.053R. EXPRESSING THE IDENTICAL TRADE IN PSQ RATHER THAN QQQ MULTIPLIES THE SPREAD COST, IN R TERMS, BY 6.77x.
arithmetic_which_does_not_depend_on_samp.quantization: At 13:37Z QQQ traded 708.53, which implies PSQ 26.1791. PSQ actually printed 26.160-26.175, i.e. up to 2 ticks below the implied level. _DAY_TRACK_THE_PSQ_STOP_IS_2_79_TICKS_WI.what_this_is_and_is_not: IT IS NOT a claim that PSQ tracks QQQ badly: over the 10 minutes held, QQQ +0.1285% against PSQ -0.1718% (1.34x rather than 1.00x), but a 0.1285% move is only ~3.4 PSQ ticks, so price quantization alone accounts for the gap and no tracking failure is evidenced. IT IS a claim about RESOLUTION: a $26 instrument quoted in whole cents cannot express a 0.1066% stop with better than ~36% precision, so on the SHORT side the stop is decided by microstructure rather than by the QQQ signal the track is built on. The LONG side does not have this problem -- QQQ at $709 with a 4-cent spread resolves the same stop to ~5%.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_PSQ_STOP_IS_2_79_TICKS_WI.n_is_1_and_the_direction_of_the_error_is: One trade. A 2.79-tick stop is trivially easy to trip, which will show up as a LOW win rate and small losses -- but the same coarseness could equally hand back a favourable tick, and a stop that fires early on a losing day costs less than one that fires late. NOTHING here says the track is broken. It says the SHORT half of the sample will be noisier than the long half for a mechanical reason, and graduate() must not read that noise as edge.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_PSQ_STOP_IS_2_79_TICKS_WI.why_no_fix_is_being_applied_here: Every available fix -- a wider short-side stop, a minimum tick-count on the stop, QQQ puts, shorting QQQ directly, or a leveraged inverse -- is a CHANGE TO THE SPEC, and the spec is edited only by an interactive session with a real Ryan turn. _A_CASH_HOLD_THAT_CARRIES_A_DOLLAR_FIGUR.headline: _cash_hold states in its own text that it 'does NOT bar an entry' and is 'a disclosure with an expiry date, not a gate'. Three consecutive runs this session subtracted its amount_held_usd from deployable capital and declined on the remainder -- 15:20Z ('leaving $0.69 -- far under the $600 minimum'), 15:30Z ('leaving $0.68 ... dispositive'), 15:45Z ('leaving $0.57 ... _A_CASH_HOLD_THAT_CARRIES_A_DOLLAR_FIGUR.THE_MECHANISM_which_is_the_transferable_: A GOVERNANCE OBJECT THAT CARRIES A DOLLAR FIGURE WILL BE SUBTRACTED, WHATEVER ITS PROSE SAYS. `amount_held_usd: 1470.92` sits in the same record as a paragraph saying the hold is not a gate, and the number is the part that composes with the run's other arithmetic. A run computing capital reaches for the field, gets deployable 1471.55 - 1470.92 = $0.63, and that number LOOKS like a finished capital verdict -- it is specific, it is small, and it lands under a real policy floor ($600 minimum entry). Nothing errors, nothing contradicts, and the run never has occasion to read the prose field that voids the subtraction. The repo's most-repeated shape -- a check that passes for the wrong reason -- arriving through a DATA TYPE rather than through reasoning: prose disclaims, numbers compose, and composition wins.
_A_CASH_HOLD_THAT_CARRIES_A_DOLLAR_FIGUR.why_it_hardened_rather_than_self_correct: Each run inherited the previous run's why_flat sentence rather than the hold itself. 15:20Z hedged it ('leaving $0.69 -- far under'), 15:30Z promoted it to 'dispositive', 15:45Z to 'dispositive BEFORE grade'. The escalation is the tell: a claim that is re-derived each run does not gain confidence, and a claim that is copied forward does. 'Dispositive before grade' is the terminal form -- it says the capital arithmetic fires first and the grading never has to happen, which is precisely the gate the hold denies being.

_RSI2_EXIT_IS_INDETERMINATE_WHEN_THE_BID.status: NEW DURABLE FINDING. _RSI2_EXIT_IS_INDETERMINATE_WHEN_THE_BID.headline: The RSI2>=70 take-profit is evaluated on a PRICE, and when the bid/ask straddles the price at which RSI2 crosses 70, the trigger's answer depends on which side of the spread you quote. Measured live on UNP at 13:39Z: BID 285.51 -> RSI2 66.9, DOES NOT FIRE. ASK 286.61 -> RSI2 76.7, FIRES. The crossing price is 285.7746 and it sits INSIDE a $1.10 spread. Same instrument, same second, opposite verdicts.
_RSI2_EXIT_IS_INDETERMINATE_WHEN_THE_BID.THE_MECHANISM_which_is_the_transferable_: A 2-period RSI is a near-vertical function of the newest close, so a small price interval maps to a large RSI interval -- here $1.10 of spread spans 9.8 RSI points (66.9 to 76.7). Every other trigger this desk uses is evaluated on a SETTLED daily close, where there is exactly one number and the question does not arise. The RSI2 exit is the only one evaluated intraday against a LIVE price, and a live price is not a number -- it is an interval. The trigger silently assumes a point quote.
_RSI2_EXIT_IS_INDETERMINATE_WHEN_THE_BID.the_half_that_actually_bites__THE_TRIGGE: A long position is SOLD INTO THE BID. So the executable price is 285.51, at which RSI2 is 66.9 and the condition is FALSE. Firing off last (285.95) or ask (286.61) means banking on a print the sale will not receive. The asymmetry is directional and always points the same way: for a LONG take-profit the bid is the conservative side and the trigger's own input (last/mid) is optimistic. This is the repo's most-repeated shape -- a check that passes for the wrong reason -- arriving through the difference between the price a signal is COMPUTED on and the price a trade is FILLED at.
_RSI2_EXIT_IS_INDETERMINATE_WHEN_THE_BID.why_it_showed_up_today_and_not_before: Spread width. UNP's bid/ask was $1.10 (0.39% of spot) nine minutes after the bell; by mid-session it is typically a few cents, at which point the straddle is arithmetically almost impossible and the trigger is determinate. So this defect is concentrated in exactly the window the standing opening-auction rule already tells the desk to distrust -- the two rules are the same rule seen from different ends, and the existing one (re-quote >=5 min past 13:30Z) is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT: this quote was taken 9 minutes after the bell and complied with it fully.
_RSI2_EXIT_IS_INDETERMINATE_WHEN_THE_BID.the_detector_and_it_costs_nothing: You already have the bid and the ask. Compute RSI2 at BOTH. If they disagree across 70, the trigger is INDETERMINATE -- do not fire and do not declare it falsified; re-quote later in the session when the spread has tightened. If they agree, the trigger is determinate and the spread is not load-bearing. Quote the crossing PRICE (here 285.7746) alongside the RSI2 value, because a price threshold can be compared against a spread and an oscillator reading cannot.
_RSI2_EXIT_IS_INDETERMINATE_WHEN_THE_BID.relation_to_the_existing_ruling: _TIME_STOP_NEEDS_NO_REPORT_BUT_THE_RSI2_EXIT_NEEDS_A_LIVE_ONE (2026-09-03) established that competing RSI2 IMPLEMENTATIONS disagree by ~10 points near the 70 line. This is a SECOND, INDEPENDENT source of ~10 points of uncertainty at the same line, from the QUOTE rather than the formula. They compound: today the implementation gap (~3 points, measured against the published 09-15 report) and the spread gap (9.8 points) both sit on a 1.7-point margin. Neither alone would be decisive; together the trigger is not resolvable from this run's data.
_RSI2_EXIT_IS_INDETERMINATE_WHEN_THE_BID.what_it_does_NOT_license: It is NOT an argument for a magnitude floor, which is VOID and must not be re-derived -- the finding is about whether the trigger FIRED, never about whether the gain is big enough to bother with. It is also NOT a general licence to defer exits: where bid and ask agree, the trigger is determinate and HARD RULE 5 says TAKE IT, including for a gain of a few dollars. And it says nothing about the TIME STOP, which reads no price at all.

A paper sample mixing the two sides mixes two different friction regimes under one statistic. Flag to the Monday calibration; do NOT 'fix' it by adding a filter.
subject_1_the_long_side_buys_ONE_SHARE_a.the_root_cause_is_the_OR_stop_being_sub_: Both days the opening-range stop was a fraction of a percent of the signal -- 0.0805% today, 0.1066% on day 1. A stop that tight is inside ordinary microstructure noise on any vehicle, which is why R is measured in cents and why fill slippage is a large fraction of R. This is a SPEC-level property for Ryan and the calibration to consider, not something a run may adjust.

subject_2_todays_window_SPANS_the_FOMC_a.the_stale_claim: market_brief.json (built 2026-09-15) says, under WINDOW_SCOPING: 'A DAY TRACK position is flat by 15:30 ET TODAY and the decision is OUTSIDE its window -- do NOT cite FOMC against the day track.' That was TRUE on 09-15, when the decision was the next day. It is FALSE on 09-16: the decision lands 14:00 ET and the flat rule is 15:30 ET, so a day-track position is held ACROSS it by 1.5 hours.
subject_2_todays_window_SPANS_the_FOMC_a.why_this_is_the_documented_failure_shape: It is the 2026-08-25 stale-regime-label rule and the 2026-09-14 _A_STALE_CATALYST_WINDOW_BARRED_A_TRACK_FOR_A_SESSION_THAT_HAD_NO_CATALYST finding, running in the OPPOSITE direction: that one carried a catalyst objection forward to a day that had no catalyst; this one carries a no-catalyst ALL-CLEAR forward to a day that has one. A window claim is only true relative to the date it was computed on, and an all-clear inherited across a day boundary is as wrong as a veto inherited across one. Today's rebuilt brief states it correctly.
subject_2_todays_window_SPANS_the_FOMC_a.what_it_does_and_does_NOT_license: It does NOT veto the day trade and was NOT used to. The spec is explicit that no unattended run may add a gate, a filter or a 'why now' to this track, and the whole design lesson behind the DAY TRACK is that the retired TACTICAL track died under exactly this kind of accreted, individually reasonable veto. The signal was taken as computed. What it DOES do is record, before the LIVE phase inherits it, that the track's resting stop will at some point sit across a scheduled binary macro release -- where a stop_market can gap through its trigger price and fill arbitrarily far away. That is a real execution property for Ryan and the Monday calibration, and it is the day-track sibling of the already-recorded overnight-gap argument that killed TACTICAL's hold-over convention.
subject_2_todays_window_SPANS_the_FOMC_a.the_general_rule: Each track screens its own window (2026-08-28), and the window MOVES WITH THE DATE. Recompute the window's start and end every day and name what falls inside it -- never inherit yesterday's answer, in either direction.

_DAY_TRACK_A_SECOND_CONCURRENT_RUN_DECID.headline: THE DAY TRACK'S SIBLING-COLLISION DEFENCE DOES NOT FUNCTION IN PAPER PHASE, AND THIS RUN PROVED IT BY ALMOST WRITING A SECOND, CONTRADICTORY PAPER DAY-2 ROW. _DAY_TRACK_A_SECOND_CONCURRENT_RUN_DECID.the_mechanism_and_why_the_prescribed_che: Prompt v11's day-track rule is explicit and correct for LIVE: 'before the entry order re-read get_equity_orders for today. This run's get_equity_orders(>=2026-09-16) returned EMPTY -- correctly, because the sibling had placed nothing and never would. This is the 2026-08-28 commit-latency mechanism exactly -- 'the ledger lags a sibling's fill by that sibling's commit latency' -- but with the broker leg removed, latency is the ONLY signal, so there is no second line of defence at all.

WHAT_THIS_RUN_GOT_WRONG_AND_RETRACTS.the_retracted_claim: This run initially recorded a finding titled '_DAY_TRACK_PAPER_DAY_2_WAS_SKIPPED_BY_LATENCY_NOT_BY_THE_TAPE', asserting a '27-minute cadence gap' with 'runs at 13:05/13:15/13:18Z then NOTHING until 13:45Z', and blaming the missed entry partly on the cron and partly on this run's own sequencing.
WHAT_THIS_RUN_GOT_WRONG_AND_RETRACTS.why_it_was_wrong: THE CRON FIRED NORMALLY. A run fired at 13:30Z, inside the window, quoted QQQ at 13:35:30Z with the late-entry gate comfortably satisfied, and took the entry. There was no cadence gap. The 'gap' was an artifact of reading the journal before the sibling had committed -- i.e. the finding's evidence was the very latency it was trying to describe, pointed at the wrong conclusion.
WHAT_THIS_RUN_GOT_WRONG_AND_RETRACTS.what_survives_of_it: Only the narrow sequencing point, and it is now moot rather than wrong: a run firing inside the entry window should quote the signal FIRST, because the late-entry gate is a moving threshold against a moving price. That remains good practice. It did not cost anything today, because the day's decision was already correctly taken by the run whose job it was.
WHAT_THIS_RUN_GOT_WRONG_AND_RETRACTS.the_transferable_shape_and_it_is_the_rep: A RUN THAT CANNOT SEE A SIBLING WILL EXPLAIN THE SIBLING'S ABSENCE AS A FACT ABOUT THE WORLD. Absence of evidence in a latency-bound artifact is not evidence of absence, and the failure is self-confirming: the quieter the record looks, the more confident the wrong conclusion. This run wrote a plausible, numerate, well-evidenced finding about infrastructure that was working perfectly.

_DAY_TRACK_A_SECOND_CONCURRENT_RUN_DECID.why_it_matters_more_in_PAPER_than_it_wou: graduate() is the ONLY gate left between this track and real money -- the v11 stop-authority precondition is already satisfied -- and it reads the paper log. Its inputs are paper_days and the list of R-multiples. A duplicate day would have inflated paper_days toward the 10-day minimum with no extra information, and had BOTH rows been action='enter' with different prices, the R-multiple list would have carried two contradictory outcomes for one day. The corruption would have been invisible: both rows are individually well-formed and internally correct.
_DAY_TRACK_A_SECOND_CONCURRENT_RUN_DECID.the_defence_that_does_work_in_paper_and_: THE PAPER LOG ITSELF IS THE ARBITER WHEN THE BROKER CANNOT BE. Before writing any day-track row, re-fetch origin/master and check day_track_paper.json AND _DAY_TRACK.results for a row whose trading_day_et is today. If one exists, the day is DECIDED -- stand down and MANAGE it, which is what this run ultimately did. This is not a new gate on the strategy (the spec forbids a run adding one) -- it is a write-conflict check on the log, and it is the paper-phase analogue of the existing broker-first rule rather than an addition to it.
_DAY_TRACK_A_SECOND_CONCURRENT_RUN_DECID.residual_hole_this_run_CANNOT_close: The re-fetch narrows the window; it does not eliminate it. Two runs can still compute the day concurrently and both find a clean log, exactly as happened here. Only the trigger configuration can stop two runs racing the same slot, and that is Ryan's to change -- an agent can make the collision cheap and detectable, never impossible. Recorded with NO approval claimed or implied (HARD RULE 9).
_DAY_TRACK_A_SECOND_CONCURRENT_RUN_DECID.for_ryan_no_approval_implied: Before the day track goes LIVE, the 13:30Z/13:45Z pair racing the same opening-range slot is worth one look at the trigger config: in LIVE, the broker check catches it and the second run stands down, so this is a paper-phase measurement problem rather than a live-money one -- but the paper phase is what decides whether live money is ever committed.

_DAY_TRACK_EARLY_SESSION_ATR14_5MIN_IS_M.headline: EARLY IN A SESSION, ATR14(5-MINUTE) IS MOSTLY *YESTERDAY* -- SO THE DAY TRACK'S 2R TRAIL IS SET BY THE PRIOR AFTERNOON'S VOLATILITY, NOT TODAY'S. At 09:59 ET only 6 five-minute bars of today exist, so 9 of the 15 bars ATR14 consumes come from the previous session.
_DAY_TRACK_EARLY_SESSION_ATR14_5MIN_IS_M.status: NEW DURABLE FINDING. THE SPEC WAS FOLLOWED AS WRITTEN -- ATR14(5-min) was computed over the available series and the stop was set from it. No parameter was changed and no gate added; an unattended run may not edit this track. Recorded for the Monday calibration and for Ryan.

measured.ratio: Today's gap-free 5-minute ATR is 1.72x the ATR14 the spec actually uses.
measured.consequence_for_the_stop: Trail = session_high - 1.5 x ATR5. With 0.82 -> 710.18 - 1.23 = 708.95. With today's 1.412 -> 710.18 - 2.118 = 708.06, which is BELOW the breakeven stop 708.43, so breakeven would have governed and the stop would have been 708.43. The two inputs differ by 0.52 per share = 0.92R on this trade.

_DAY_TRACK_EARLY_SESSION_ATR14_5MIN_IS_M.THE_DIRECTION_IS_THE_SURPRISE_AND_IT_INV: The intuition is that including an overnight gap INFLATES ATR and loosens the stop. The opposite happened. 2026-09-15's final hour was exceptionally quiet -- five-minute ranges around 0.2-0.4 points -- while today is running 1.4, and one gap bar diluted across fourteen does not offset nine placid ones. So the stale bars DRAG ATR DOWN and make the trail TIGHTER, i.e. MORE aggressive, in a tape that is demonstrably moving faster than the average describes. A trail 0.885 under the session high on a name printing 1.4-point five-minute ranges is well inside noise.
_DAY_TRACK_EARLY_SESSION_ATR14_5MIN_IS_M.why_it_is_not_a_bug_and_must_not_be_patc: ATR14(5-min) is what the spec says, the code computes it correctly, and the formula is deliberately mechanical so that runs execute rather than judge -- which is the entire design lesson the track was built on after TACTICAL died of accreted judgment. A run that silently swapped in a gap-free intraday ATR because it preferred the number would be re-importing exactly that failure. The right move is to execute as written and report the measurement, which is what happened.
_DAY_TRACK_EARLY_SESSION_ATR14_5MIN_IS_M.quantified_pattern_rather_than_a_one_off: The composition problem decays predictably through the session: 9 of 15 bars are stale at 09:59 ET, 0 of 15 by roughly 10:45 ET. So the trail is most contaminated exactly when a fast trade reaches +2R earliest -- the tail of the distribution where the trail matters most. It is a systematic early-session bias, not a fluke of today's quiet prior close.
_DAY_TRACK_EARLY_SESSION_ATR14_5MIN_IS_M.for_the_monday_calibration: Worth a look, and NOT a self-granted change: whether the 2R trail should use ATR14(5-min) as written, or hold the initial/breakeven stop until 15 bars of the CURRENT session exist (~10:45 ET). Note the honest counter-argument -- a tighter trail banks more of a fast move and this paper trade would lock +0.92R instead of +0.00R, so the stale input is not obviously worse, merely unintended. Two paper days is no sample for settling it; the point is that the input is not measuring what its name implies.

_DAY_TRACK_IN_PAPER_manage_MUST_BE_FED_T.measured_by: scheduled run 14:00Z 2026-09-16 (unattended, prompt v11), after a merge conflict put two contradictory readings of the same paper position side by side.
_DAY_TRACK_IN_PAPER_manage_MUST_BE_FED_T.headline: day_track.manage() tests the stop against the price you HAND IT. In LIVE that is harmless because a resting broker stop_market fires on the intraday low whether or not the agent is looking. In PAPER there is no resting order, so a run that hands manage() the CURRENT quote cannot see a breach that happened between runs -- and the paper log silently converts a stopped-out loser into an open winner every time price recovers.

how_it_presented.the_position: DAY TRACK paper day 2: long QQQ 1 share, entry 708.43 at 13:35:30.133Z, initial stop 707.86 (the opposite OR edge).
how_it_presented.what_actually_happened: The 13:36 bar -- the first full minute after entry -- printed low 707.650, breaching by 0.21 points. Re-fetched twice ~5 min apart, byte-identical; 5-minute bucket reconciles exactly to its 1-minute sum; SPY clean at the same timestamps. Settled fact.
how_it_presented.what_the_13_45Z_run_did: Called manage(price=709.82, session_extreme=710.18, ...) at 14:00Z. manage()'s step 1 is `if price <= stop: close`, and 709.82 > 707.86, so it returned raise_stop 'ratchet at 2.44R' and the run recorded a +2.44R open position with the stop moved to 708.95.
how_it_presented.was_that_run_careless: NO, and this is the point. It checked feed integrity on all three buckets, caught and documented an in-progress bucket revision, deliberately used the BID rather than the last as the conservative executable price, cross-checked the session high against two intervals, and retracted an earlier wrong finding of its own. It did everything the playbook asks and still recorded the opposite of what happened, because the defect is in WHICH PRICE the function is asked about, not in the care taken measuring that price.

_DAY_TRACK_IN_PAPER_manage_MUST_BE_FED_T.why_it_is_the_DANGEROUS_direction: The error is not symmetric. A breach followed by a recovery is invisible and becomes an open winner; a breach followed by continuation is caught, because the current price is still through the stop. So the bias runs ONE WAY -- toward deleting losers -- and it feeds straight into day_track.graduate(), whose whole job is to decide whether this track goes LIVE with real money. An inflated paper sample is exactly the input that would push go_live true on an edge that is not there. Paper day 1 escaped it only by accident: that run happened to examine the bars explicitly rather than pass a quote.
_DAY_TRACK_IN_PAPER_manage_MUST_BE_FED_T.the_fix_and_it_changes_no_PARAMETER: In PAPER, feed manage() the ADVERSE EXTREME over the interval since the last management pass -- the minimum LOW on a long, the maximum HIGH on a short, from the 1-minute series -- and only then, if no breach, re-run it on the current quote for the ratchet decision. Two calls, one extra argument's worth of thought, no parameter touched and no gate added. The run cadence is 15 minutes and the bars are 1 minute, so between any two passes there are ~15 unexamined bars; asking about the 15th one only is not a stop check. In LIVE the broker covers this and the same discipline is still worth keeping, because the run must RECONCILE the stop order's fill rather than infer liveness from the quote.
_DAY_TRACK_IN_PAPER_manage_MUST_BE_FED_T.the_transferable_shape: A simulation inherits the guarantees of the thing it simulates ONLY where it reproduces the mechanism. PAPER reproduced the stop LEVEL but not the stop ORDER -- a resting order is continuous, a scheduled run is a sample every 15 minutes -- and the gap between those two facts is where the whole distortion lives. Whenever a paper mode stands in for a mechanism that runs while the agent is absent, ask what that mechanism does BETWEEN observations, not what it would do at one.
_DAY_TRACK_IN_PAPER_manage_MUST_BE_FED_T.honest_scope: One instance, caught only because two concurrent runs disagreed and the conflict forced a re-read. Without the collision this would have merged silently as a +2.44R open position. That is the uncomfortable part and it is stated rather than smoothed: the redundant-trigger collision the repo treats as a hazard is what caught this one.

_DAY_TRACK_BOTH_PAPER_SIGNALS_WERE_DIREC.the_outcome_independent_half_which_is_th: initial_stop() applies the MIN_STOP_ATR floor to the OPENING RANGE, not to the realized entry-to-stop distance. Day 2 makes it visible: floor = 0.1 x ATR14 7.7635 = 0.77635; OR range 0.93 clears it, so the floor never engaged; but the entry filled at 708.43, which is 0.57 above the OR low, so the actual risk distance was 0.57 -- 27% INSIDE the floor the parameter exists to enforce. The two coincide only when the fill lands exactly on the opposite edge, which a run firing minutes after the range closes will rarely do. This is arithmetic and would be worth recording even if both trades had won.
_DAY_TRACK_BOTH_PAPER_SIGNALS_WERE_DIREC.what_this_run_did_NOT_do_and_may_not_do: It changed no parameter (min_stop_atr, or_minutes, late_entry_frac, risk_pct) and added no filter, screen or 'why now'. docs/day-track-spec.md and CLAUDE.md both forbid an unattended run doing either, and that prohibition is precisely what keeps the retired TACTICAL track from being re-created by accretion. Measured, not asserted: graduate(2, [-1.0,-1.0]) -> go_live FALSE; track_status($3,855.93, [-1.0,-1.0], [-1.0,-1.0]) -> not paused (needs 3 consecutive losing days).
_DAY_TRACK_BOTH_PAPER_SIGNALS_WERE_DIREC.FOR_THE_MONDAY_CALIBRATION_AND_FOR_RYAN: If this shape holds across the paper sample, graduate() will correctly refuse to go live, and the honest conclusion is NOT 'widen the stop until it works'. A wider stop is not free: at fixed risk_pct it enlarges R in dollars, cuts share count, and worsens reward-to-risk on the same move. Three settable responses, all belonging to a Monday calibration or to Ryan and to NEITHER an unattended run: (a) raise min_stop_atr AND apply the floor to the entry-to-stop distance rather than the OR range; (b) lengthen or_minutes so the edge is less fragile; (c) accept the hit rate and let expectancy decide. (c) is the null and is a real option.

The bias is one-directional and points at entry -- an incomplete calendar always makes a name look SAFER than it is, never riskier.

_THE_RSI2_TRIGGER_IS_A_FIXED_PRICE_THRES.why_this_matters_beyond_convenience: The 13:39Z straddle finding correctly observed that a live price is an INTERVAL, not a number, and that a 2-period RSI maps a small price interval onto a large RSI interval. The consequence it did not draw: the inverse map is the useful one. Comparing a threshold PRICE to a bid/ask is trivially decidable -- you can see at a glance whether the spread straddles it -- whereas comparing an RSI VALUE to 70 requires recomputation on every quote and hides how far away the trigger actually is. Quoting the threshold also makes the distance to the trigger legible in dollars, which an oscillator reading never is.
_THE_RSI2_TRIGGER_IS_A_FIXED_PRICE_THRES.the_executable_side_rule_is_unchanged_an: A long is SOLD INTO THE BID, so the BID is the price the threshold is compared against. Firing off last or ask banks a print the sale will not receive. This finding does not soften that -- it just means the comparison is one subtraction instead of three RSI evaluations.

A straddle needs only that the threshold fall inside the spread, and a price parked ON the threshold straddles it at any spread width. Width governs how OFTEN, not whether.

The 16:20Z run read the event as grounds to defer with a clock. The 16:27Z run read sizing-down as the rule being applied as written, and entered at 18.3% of the account rather than the 30% cap. _TWO_CONCURRENT_RUNS_REACHED_OPPOSITE_VE.THE_MECHANISM_which_is_the_transferable_: THE 2026-08-28 BROKER-FIRST RULE DETECTS A SIBLING'S **FILL**, NOT A SIBLING'S **DECISION** -- and a run that DECLINES leaves no broker trace at all. That rule was written after two concurrent runs each took an entry, so it was aimed at the double-position case and it solves that case correctly. It is structurally blind to the mirror case: when a sibling's output is 'no trade', get_equity_orders is empty, the check passes, and the passing check means nothing. The git second line is blind for the documented reason -- the ledger lags a sibling's commit latency, here about four minutes. So the ONLY collision the system can see is the one where both runs trade, and the one where the runs DISAGREE is invisible by construction.
_TWO_CONCURRENT_RUNS_REACHED_OPPOSITE_VE.why_this_is_the_more_dangerous_shape_eve: A double fill is loud: it shows up as an over-sized book and a breached throttle, and any later run reconciling against the broker finds it immediately. A split verdict is SILENT. Whichever run traded writes the state, the other's reasoning survives only as prose in a superseded key, and no reconciliation anywhere can flag it -- because the book is arithmetically correct. Exactly one IBKR lot exists, the throttle reads a truthful 1 of 3, and both runs' records are individually honest.

_TWO_CONCURRENT_RUNS_REACHED_OPPOSITE_VE.FOR_RYAN__the_policy_question_no_unatten: Does a scheduled MACRO event (FOMC, CPI, payrolls) bar an equity entry, or only shrink it? v11 answers this for OPTIONS in as many words -- sizing input, not a bar -- and says NOTHING about the equity book, where CLAUDE.md makes only the single-name [ERN] flag absolute. Today that silence produced two defensible opposite answers four minutes apart, and on 12 of the last 12 sessions the same ambiguity has been cited against bank-cohort entries. One sentence in CLAUDE.md settles it permanently. Recorded as a QUESTION, not a recommendation dressed as one, and NO approval is claimed, quoted or implied -- HARD RULE 9 intact, this is an unattended run.
_TWO_CONCURRENT_RUNS_REACHED_OPPOSITE_VE.the_transferable_lesson: A SAFEGUARD BUILT FROM ONE INCIDENT WILL SEE ONLY THAT INCIDENT'S SIGNATURE. The broker-first rule was derived from a double-fill and therefore watches for fills; it cannot represent the state 'a sibling considered this and said no'. Same family as this file's most-repeated defect -- a check that passes for the wrong reason -- but arriving through the safeguard's OWN scope rather than through a run's reasoning. The practical mitigation available today is cheap and partial: on any run that is about to place a signal-sourced entry, re-fetch origin/master IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the order and grep the newest _last_entry_evaluation for the ticker. It would have caught this one with about four minutes to spare, and it catches nothing if the sibling has not yet committed.
_TWO_CONCURRENT_RUNS_REACHED_OPPOSITE_VE.AMENDED_2026-09-16T16:35Z__WHAT_A_SPLIT_: The 16:35Z run reconciled independently, reached this same incident from the other direction (it found the fill at the broker with master still showing no IBKR row), and DELETED its own near-duplicate finding in favour of this one -- per the standing rule that a contribution which narrows or extends an existing key EDITS that key rather than minting a rival. Cross-validation worth recording: the two runs independently derived the SAME entry_price 87.2999, shares 8.109516, target 96.14 and sizing arithmetic ($707.96 = 18.29% of account = deployable/2 at 2 open slots). No factual disagreement. WHAT IT ADDS, and it is the practical sting of a split verdict: THE WINNING RUN WRITES THE STATE, BUT IT WRITES ONLY THE HALF ITS OWN REASONING NEEDED. The 16:27Z run wrote a full entry provenance and correctly corrected the throttle to 1 of 3 -- and left the IBKR row with NO setup_invalidation and NO _current_state, while every other swing row carries both and prompt v11 requires a written exit plan on every entry. The deferring run's analysis, which is where the durable thesis WATCH lived (IBKR's two-sided FOMC sensitivity), survived only as prose in a superseded key and was attached to nothing. Both gaps are closed as of 16:35Z: the invalidation now carries that watch forward as a HELD-POSITION thesis duty for the first run after 18:00Z, explicitly not as an entry re-grade. GENERALISE IT: after any split verdict, do not only ask WHICH run was right -- audit the winner's ledger row against the schema the other positions use. A run that has just talked itself INTO a trade writes the entry case; the exit case is what goes missing, and nothing reconciles against the broker will ever flag a missing invalidation because the book is arithmetically perfect without one.

the_arithmetic_that_killed_it.the_general_form: An unstopped concentrated book with a 72% hit rate and a 1.02 payoff has per-trade expectancy that is SMALL relative to daily noise BY CONSTRUCTION. That is what a hit-rate engine IS. Comparing one-day volatility to per-trade expectancy therefore returns a large multiple for every candidate, always, and a filter that fires on every input carries no information.

_THE_VOL_TO_EXPECTANCY_VETO_DOES_NOT_DIS.the_transferable_lesson: BEFORE A RATIO VETOES A CANDIDATE, COMPUTE IT FOR THE POSITIONS ALREADY HELD. A risk metric that condemns the book you are already running is measuring the strategy, not the trade. This is the repo's most-repeated shape arriving in its most seductive form: the number was correctly computed, genuinely large, and pointed at the cautious answer -- which is exactly why nobody would have questioned it.

_A_CARRY_OVER_DECLINE_PRESERVES_ITS_VERD.THE_FINDING: A name declined once is carried forward as a CARRY-OVER on 'grounds unchanged'. That mechanism preserves the VERDICT faithfully and silently preserves the EVIDENTIARY STATUS of every component that produced it -- including components that were never established. FDX sat as a decline from 14:00Z through 16:45Z across roughly a dozen runs, each correctly declining to re-argue it on an unchanged board. Nobody had ever established its earnings date. The report's Earnings column was BLANK, and CLAUDE.md is explicit that blank means UNKNOWN, not clean.
_A_CARRY_OVER_DECLINE_PRESERVES_ITS_VERD.what_verification_cost_and_returned: TWO calls, under a minute. get_earnings_calendar(start 2026-09-16, days 15, high_market_cap) returns NO FDX print in the window. get_earnings_results('FDX') gives the only quarter with eps.actual == null as 2026-10-28 pm, verified=true -- OUTSIDE the 14-day time-stop window ending 2026-09-30. Two independent sources agree: FDX is earnings-CLEAN, and the [ERN] absolute bar does not apply to it.
_A_CARRY_OVER_DECLINE_PRESERVES_ITS_VERD.why_this_is_not_pedantry: [ERN] inside the hold window is an ABSOLUTE bar under the 2026-09-02 concentration policy -- at up to 30% of the account with NO price stop, one gap through a print is a ~4-5% account hit. So 'earnings unknown' and 'earnings clean' are not shades of the same status: one forbids the trade outright and the other removes the single hardest gate on the board. Carrying the first forward as though it were settled is the cheapest possible way to lose a legitimate A-grade entry, and it leaves no trace -- the name simply keeps appearing in the excluded list.
_A_CARRY_OVER_DECLINE_PRESERVES_ITS_VERD.THE_ASYMMETRY_THAT_MAKES_IT_INVISIBLE: An unverified ground can only ever make the desk MORE restrictive, never less. So the error never produces a bad fill, never shows up in P&L, and never trips a reconciliation -- it shows up as an entry that quietly never happened. This is the exact shape of the accreted-veto failure that killed the TACTICAL track (85 fully-evaluated triggers, 0 trades), arriving through the carry-over mechanism instead of through new rule text. It is this file's most-repeated defect once more: a check that passes for the wrong reason.
_A_CARRY_OVER_DECLINE_PRESERVES_ITS_VERD.THE_RULE: A carry-over decline is valid ONLY for grounds that were MEASURED when first written. Before inheriting one, ask which of its components were measured and which were assumed -- and VERIFY any assumed component that is cheap to check and capable of flipping the verdict. An earnings date, a sector classification, an ownership flag and a corporate action all cost one or two read-only calls. Re-deriving the full grade on an unchanged board is still correctly forbidden; establishing an unestablished FACT is not re-arguing, it is finishing the original grade.
_A_CARRY_OVER_DECLINE_PRESERVES_ITS_VERD.detector: When a name's exclusion cites a component the report left BLANK, the exclusion is provisional whatever its age or however many runs have repeated it. Repetition is not corroboration: twelve runs inheriting one unverified ground is still n=1. the_measurement.method: Quote ATM-nearest calls across consecutive expiries and read the IV term structure. A binary event sits between the last LOW board and the first HIGH one.
the_measurement.reading: Monotone DECLINE from the 2-DTE board to a 30-DTE trough at 28.87%, then a +8.79 vol-point JUMP to 37.66% at 44 DTE. Longer-dated vol is normally flat-to-lower; a ~9-point step UP on a later board is an event being priced between 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-30. That brackets 2026-10-28 exactly.
the_measurement.the_near_board_disconfirms_an_imminent_p: If FDX reported 09-17 or 09-18, the 2-DTE board could not sit at 35.93%. At that IV the implied move to expiry is only ~2.7% (0.3593 * sqrt(2/365) * 305 = $8.1); a FedEx print historically implies 6-9%, which over two days needs IV in the 70-110% range. The 35.93% front reading is ordinary short-date convexity plus tonight's FOMC -- NOT an earnings board.
the_measurement.verdict: FDX's next print is priced between 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-30, consistent with the 2026-10-28 field. The 14-day hold window on a today-dated entry ends 2026-09-30, clear by ~4 weeks. [ERN] DOES NOT BAR FDX -- now on market evidence rather than on a corrupt table.
