the_three_reasons_the_regrade_is_not_per.2_the_event_minute_round_tripped_complet: SPY opened the 18:00Z minute at 760.1816, printed 760.9789 (+0.7973), and CLOSED THE MINUTE AT 759.670 -- 0.5116 BELOW where the minute opened, having given back 164% of its own pop. QQQ: open 710.210, high 711.070 (+0.860), close 709.690, -0.520 below the open, 160% given back. Both indices spent the entire excursion and more inside sixty seconds, on 14.3x and 7.2x volume. Per the 2026-08-28 Warsh finding, a full retrace of an event move is POSITIVE evidence the event is unresolved -- the market declining to price it, not pricing it flat.
the_three_reasons_the_regrade_is_not_per.3_the_press_conference_has_not_happened: Powell's press conference is 18:30Z, half an hour after the statement. The statement and the presser are separate repricing events and the second is historically the larger. A tape measured between them is mid-event by construction.

_A_CASH_HOLDS_TRIGGER_AND_ITS_OPPORTUNIT.what_this_does_NOT_license: It does NOT license a new hold, and none is written. THE CAPITAL POLICY is explicit that an unexpiring 'waiting for something better' deferral is the voided 45% floor returning through the side door, and renewal is not available to an unattended run in any case. Capital returned to normal full deployment at this minute: deployable $708.91 against a $600 minimum entry, the 4th slot of the 3-4 target open, and nothing forbidding an entry. The correct sentence for this run is 'DECLINED ON GRADE on a board fully graded earlier today, with the tape mid-event' -- never 'declined because capital is held'.
_A_CASH_HOLDS_TRIGGER_AND_ITS_OPPORTUNIT.the_transferable_shape: This is the same family as this file's most-repeated defect -- a check that passes for the wrong reason -- arriving on the permissive side rather than the restrictive one. The dissolution is mechanically CORRECT and completely uninformative about whether to trade. Both of the obvious readings are wrong: treating the dissolution as a green light manufactures an entry, and treating the un-actionable opportunity as grounds to renew manufactures a floor. The honest output is to delete the key, deploy nothing, and say which of the two the decline rests on.
_A_CASH_HOLDS_TRIGGER_AND_ITS_OPPORTUNIT.prescription: When writing a cash hold, state the trigger and the ACTIONABILITY CONDITION separately, because they are rarely the same event. Here the trigger was 'the decision is released' and the actionability condition is 'a post-decision report exists on master AND the tape has settled'. A hold whose trigger is an event TIME will always fire before its opportunity is workable; one whose trigger is a PRICE LEVEL usually will not. Prefer the latter where a choice exists.
_A_CASH_HOLDS_TRIGGER_AND_ITS_OPPORTUNIT.honest_scope: n=1 event, one minute of tape, and the presser had not begun when this was written. The claim is NOT that the FOMC decision was a non-event or that the tape is bearish -- the round trip says the market has not decided, which is a statement about resolution and not about direction. It changed no decision: this run declined on grade, on a board the 17:20Z/17:25Z/17:50Z runs had already graded with zero A-names and a zero ungraded delta.

_THE_POST_DECISION_BOARD_GOT_DEEPER_AND_.headline: THE FIRST POST-FOMC REPORT (18:07Z) SHOWS 7 OF ITS 9 CARRIED-OVER RSI2 NAMES DEEPER OVERSOLD THAN THE 17:35Z PRE-DECISION BOARD, ON A DAY THE INDEX IS GREEN. THE OBVIOUS READ -- 'ITS PRICES WERE SAMPLED INSIDE THE DECISION IMPULSE, SO THE SCREEN IS BIASED DEEP' -- WAS TESTED AGAINST SECTOR ETFS AND FAILS. IT IS A REAL COHORT REPRICING, WHICH STRENGTHENS THE DE-RATING GRADE RATHER THAN RELIEVING IT.

the_hypothesis_that_was_refuted.what_it_was: The 18:07Z report commits 7 minutes after the decision, so its ~230-name FMP price sweep sampled roughly 18:02-18:07Z -- inside a 6-minute two-sided index round trip (SPY low 758.775 at 18:02, high 761.210 at 18:08). Its own quoted prices sit BELOW the 18:19Z live prints on all three held names (ABNB 168.42 vs 168.72, UNP 283.52 vs 284.115, IBKR 87.18 vs 87.21), consistent with sampling near the trough. Since report RSI2 substitutes the live print as the newest close, a trough sample biases RSI2 DOWN -- which would over-admit names to an RSI2<10 gate and make each look deeper. The bias is DIRECTIONAL and can only ever make the desk MORE willing to enter, never less, which is why it was worth testing.
the_hypothesis_that_was_refuted.why_it_FAILS: Because the deepening is not distributed like a sampling artifact -- it is distributed by SECTOR, and the affected names are moving at ~3x their own sector ETF, which no 5-minute sampling window can manufacture. Day changes at 18:21:37-18:21:48Z: SPY +0.342%, QQQ +0.752%, SMH +1.448%, XLF -0.668% -- against BAC -2.041% (3.06x XLF), USB -2.226% (3.33x), PNC -2.094% (3.13x), IBKR -1.790% (2.68x), FDX -1.771%. A whole cohort down two-plus percent on a green index day is a repricing, not a quote timestamp.
the_hypothesis_that_was_refuted.why_recording_a_refuted_hypothesis_matte: Had it survived it would have DISCOUNTED the board -- 'the names only look this oversold because of when the sweep ran' -- and the next run would have inherited a reason to re-grade the cohort more kindly on a settled quote. The truth runs the other way: the tape CONFIRMED the de-rating the desk graded earlier today.

the_rsi2_delta_17_35Z_to_18_07Z.departure: LRCX 3.8 -> off the table (its RSI2 crossed back above 10). Per _ABSENCE_FROM_THE_SIGNAL_TABLE_IS_NOT_SIGNAL_EXPIRY a departure fires nothing. No ARRIVAL, so the ungraded delta is again ZERO and every live name was graded earlier today.
the_rsi2_delta_17_35Z_to_18_07Z.the_caution_that_keeps_this_honest: RSI2 direction and sector-relative weakness are NOT the same measurement and must not be conflated. AMAT read SHALLOWER (+0.8) while being -0.666% on the day and 2.11 points BELOW its own complex (SMH +1.448%); a 2-period RSI compares to the prior two sessions, so a red name can read shallower. Cite whichever one the decision actually rests on.

_THE_POST_DECISION_BOARD_GOT_DEEPER_AND_.the_detector_worth_keeping: MEASURE A SCREEN NAME AGAINST ITS SECTOR ETF, NOT AGAINST THE INDEX, BEFORE CALLING IT AN OVERSOLD DIP. Index-relative weakness is what an RSI2 screen already encodes; SECTOR-relative weakness is what separates 'a dip inside an intact uptrend' from 'a cohort being repriced', and only the first is the setup this book is built to buy. It costs one extra quote call (XLF / SMH / IYT alongside the names). Today it is decisive: BAC/USB/PNC/IBKR at ~2.7-3.3x XLF's move on a green index day is not a dip.
_THE_POST_DECISION_BOARD_GOT_DEEPER_AND_.what_it_decided: NO ENTRY, on the BAR and not on the event. The post-decision report -- the artifact the 18:00Z run was waiting for -- arrived and made the board's LARGEST COHORT LESS attractive, not more: the bank/broker names the 17:20Z-17:50Z runs graded down on a de-rating thesis are precisely the ones the post-decision tape has de-rated hardest. Grades hold or worsen; still zero A-names. FDX (B+ at 17:25Z) is -1.771% and unchanged in grade. WMB stays excluded on the oil-energy steer. IBKR is HELD, so a buy would be an ADD, and it is the cohort taking the damage.
_THE_POST_DECISION_BOARD_GOT_DEEPER_AND_.the_actionability_condition_is_now_CLOSE: The 18:00Z finding _A_CASH_HOLDS_TRIGGER_AND_ITS_OPPORTUNITY_ARE_TWO_DIFFERENT_EVENTS_2026-09-16 named the condition as 'a post-decision report exists on master AND the tape has settled'. BOTH halves are now measurably met for the decision leg -- the 18:07Z report (commit 2e0eb5a) and the decay above -- and the condition resolved to a DECLINE ON THE MERITS. That is the predicted and correct outcome: a procedural condition clearing is not an opportunity arriving. Do not carry the condition forward as though it were still open.
_THE_POST_DECISION_BOARD_GOT_DEEPER_AND_.honest_scope: n=9 carried-over names on ONE report pair, one trading day, one event. The sector-ratio evidence is strong for the bank cohort (four names, 2.68-3.33x XLF, same direction) and WEAK for the semis (AMAT/LRCX lag SMH but moved the other way on RSI2). The sampling-artifact MECHANISM remains real and unrefuted in general -- what was refuted is that it explains TODAY's deepening; a report swept inside an impulse is still a report to re-quote before acting on. And this changed no decision, which is the only condition under which a screen's inputs can be audited credibly.

_THE_COHORT_VETO_IS_ENTRY_SIDE_ONLY_AND_.run: scheduled 18:30Z 2026-09-16 (unattended, prompt v11), during the Powell presser, ~32 min after the decision.
_THE_COHORT_VETO_IS_ENTRY_SIDE_ONLY_AND_.status: NEW DURABLE FINDING -- a GUARDRAIL plus a REFUSAL TO RETURN A VERDICT. Changed no decision: HARD RULE 5 makes the hold determinate whatever this measures, which is the only condition under which an entry discriminator can be audited credibly.
_THE_COHORT_VETO_IS_ENTRY_SIDE_ONLY_AND_.the_situation_that_produced_it: Two runs today measured the bank/broker cohort as RELATIVE WEAKNESS and used it to decline entries: 15:20Z (_RSI2_BOARD_IS_SIX_FOR_SIX_DOWN_ON_A_GREEN_TAPE...) and 18:20Z ('a cohort down two-plus percent against a green index is a repricing, not an oversold dip'). The 16:31Z run ENTERED IBKR -- a name in that same cohort -- on a stated discriminator: 20-day SMA ABOVE the 50-day, which is exactly what USB and RTX failed. BOTH ACTIONS WERE CORRECT UNDER THEIR OWN RULES. The desk now holds a position inside a cohort it is simultaneously vetoing, and that is the configuration this key exists to govern.
_THE_COHORT_VETO_IS_ENTRY_SIDE_ONLY_AND_.THE_GUARDRAIL_which_is_the_reason_to_wri: A COHORT-RELATIVE MEASUREMENT IS AN ENTRY-SIDE VETO ONLY. IT CAN NEVER LICENSE AN EXIT. The run that measures 'this cohort is repricing, not dipping' while holding a name in that cohort is precisely the run most tempted to convert the measurement into a sell -- and it may not. HARD RULE 5 permits an equity sale on a target hit, an RSI2>=70 cross WHILE GREEN, or a HARD RULE 7 thesis break, and nothing else; there is no price stop. A cross-sectional percentage IS NOT A THESIS BREAK. A thesis break is name-specific and evidence-based (a guidance cut, a fundamental downgrade, a broken business fact) -- never a relative-performance reading, however many names agree with it.
_THE_COHORT_VETO_IS_ENTRY_SIDE_ONLY_AND_.why_the_asymmetry_is_BY_DESIGN_not_an_ov: The entry gate is DISCRETIONARY and may decline on grade; the exit gate is MECHANICAL and forbids discretionary loss-taking. A cohort reading is a GRADE input, and grades govern entries only. Read it as symmetric and the book acquires exactly the discretionary price stop HARD RULE 5 was written to forbid -- the stop that 'turns a normal multi-week pullback into a realized loss'. This is the same shape as _THE_ENTRY_SLIPPAGE_FINDING_DOES_NOT_INVERT_INTO_AN_EXIT_TIMING_EDGE (2026-09-09), arriving through a different entry-side measurement: an entry-side finding does not invert into an exit rule merely because the arithmetic runs both ways.

the_out_of_sample_test_and_why_it_return.what_became_available: The FOMC resolved at 18:00Z, so the pre-event MA-stack discriminator that justified IBKR over USB/BAC/PNC is testable out-of-sample for the first time. the_out_of_sample_test_and_why_it_return.rank_stability: IBKR is BEST OF THE FOUR in both reads. Its edge over the mean of the other three shrank only from +0.330 pts to +0.286 pts. Weakly consistent with the discriminator.
the_out_of_sample_test_and_why_it_return.the_half_that_cuts_the_other_way: In the 12-minute post-decision leg IBKR fell -0.528%, MORE than BAC (-0.317%) and more than XLF (-0.212%), and less than PNC (-0.627%) and USB (-0.510%). Its gap to BAC collapsed from 0.251 pts to 0.043. IBKR now underperforms its own sector ETF by 1.43 pts on the day.
the_out_of_sample_test_and_why_it_return.verdict: NONE, and deliberately. n=4 names over a 12-MINUTE window during a live presser is noise-scale; rank stability across two reads twelve minutes apart is not evidence. The discriminator is a PRE-EVENT cross-sectional fact and the post-event window is far too short to test it. DO NOT record a verdict either way, and do not let a later run inherit one -- the actual adjudicators are the HARD RULE 7 thesis check and the 2026-09-30 time stop.

the_breadth_measurement.why_breadth_is_a_different_measurement_f: The 18:20Z finding measured RSI2 DEPTH on the 9 names common to two boards and found 7 of 9 deeper. That says nothing about ADMISSION RATE. A screen can deepen without admitting anyone and can admit a crowd without deepening. Both are worth watching and neither substitutes for the other.

the_hypothesis_that_was_refuted.what_it_was: An RSI(2) gate is an absolute threshold, so a broad index decline drags many names under it at once regardless of anything name-specific. On that reading a board that doubles during a -1.16% leg is enumerating BETA, the 19 names collapse to one position (long the index), and each individual name should be DISCOUNTED as a signal.
the_hypothesis_that_was_refuted.why_it_FAILS: Because the arrivals are not distributed like beta. Measured against SECTOR ETFs rather than the index -- the test _THE_POST_DECISION_BOARD_GOT_DEEPER prescribes -- five of the nine tradeable arrivals are materially BELOW their own complex, which no index move can manufacture: LRCX -1.573pp under a FLAT SMH (-0.111%), C -1.330pp under XLF, SCHW -1.148pp, AMZN -0.496pp under XLY, TKR -0.467pp under XLI. A name down 1.68% while its sector is down 0.11% is not being carried by beta; it is being repriced.
the_hypothesis_that_was_refuted.why_the_refutation_matters_and_in_which_: The hypothesis was DISCOUNTING -- it would have told the next run 'these names only look oversold because the index fell, so re-grade them kindly once the tape settles'. The truth runs the OTHER way and is stricter: sector-divergent weakness is the signature of a de-rating, and only 'a dip inside an intact uptrend' is the setup this book buys. Had the hypothesis survived it would have manufactured willingness to enter. Same asymmetry the 18:20Z sampling-artifact hypothesis had, which is why both were worth testing rather than adopting.

_A_DOUBLING_RSI2_BOARD_IS_A_TRIGGER_TO_R.the_rule_worth_keeping: A BOARD THAT DOUBLES ON AN INDEX LEG IS A TRIGGER TO RUN THE SECTOR TEST ON EVERY ARRIVAL -- NEVER A REASON TO DISCOUNT THEM WHOLESALE, AND NEVER A REASON TO ACCEPT THEM AS N INDEPENDENT IDEAS. Run it, and the arrivals separate into TWO failure modes that need DIFFERENT words: (1) SECTOR-DIVERGENT DE-RATINGS (LRCX, C, SCHW, AMZN, TKR) -- not beta, and worse than a dip; (2) SECTOR-TRACKERS AND INDEX VEHICLES (FCX at -0.179pp, MS at -0.308pp, IWM, DIA) -- genuinely beta, no name-specific edge to buy, and exposure this book already carries. Citing mode (1)'s reason against a mode (2) name, or the reverse, is a check that passes for the wrong reason -- this file's most-repeated defect. The verdict is the same either way TODAY, which is exactly why the distinction has to be written down now rather than on a day when it splits.

the_two_secondary_grounds_kept_subordina.correlation: IBKR is held and is the worst sector-relative name in the book (-1.674pp vs XLF). A second financial at ~$700 would put ~37% of a 4-name account on ONE macro factor on the day that factor repriced. Under a 3-4 name target with a 30% per-name cap, correlation dominates selection -- a real constraint the old 8-position book did not have, and the load-bearing half of the concentration policy.
the_two_secondary_grounds_kept_subordina.clock: 15:16 ET. Any entry carries overnight with NO price stop (HARD RULE 5) into a tape still moving as it was quoted.
the_two_secondary_grounds_kept_subordina.why_subordinate: Neither is the reason. THE BAR is: zero A-grades. Deployable $711.56 cleared the $600 minimum, the 4th slot was open, and the throttle stood at 1 of 3 -- CAPITAL DECLINED NOTHING. Saying so plainly matters because 'no A-grade' and 'no room' are different states and only one of them is a reason to keep looking.

_A_DOUBLING_RSI2_BOARD_IS_A_TRIGGER_TO_R.honest_scope: ONE hour, ONE report pair, ONE event, on a day with an FOMC decision AND a presser -- the least representative tape available. The breadth arithmetic (9->19) is exact and the sector ratios are single live quotes, not settled closes, taken while the presser leg was still running; a name's sector-relative reading can revert by the bell. The two failure modes are cleanly separated for the extremes (LRCX at -1.573pp vs FCX at -0.179pp) and genuinely ambiguous in the middle -- MS at -0.308pp could be called either, and I have called it a tracker on the strength of its 1.14x ratio, which is a judgement and not a measurement. n=9 arrivals is not a law about screens. And this changed no decision, which is the only condition under which a screen's inputs can be audited credibly.

_IBKR_TWO_CHANNEL_FOMC_DUTY_DISCHARGED_T.the_transferable_part: WHEN AN ENTRY IS TAKEN ON A THESIS THAT IS EXPLICITLY TWO-SIDED ABOUT A DATED EVENT, THE RUN AFTER THE EVENT OWES A VERDICT EVEN THOUGH THE VERDICT CHANGES NOTHING -- and that is precisely why it gets skipped. _THE_RSI2_BOARD_DOUBLED_ON_ONE_MACRO_LEG.the_measurement: The committed RSI2 board went from 9 names at the 18:07Z report to 19 names at the 19:07Z report -- 3.9% to 8.3% of the 229-name universe -- across the single hour of Chair Warsh's press conference, during which SPY travelled +0.212% to -0.835% on the day. TEN ARRIVALS IN ONE HOUR: C, LRCX, MS, IWM, FCX, DIA, EPD, SCHW, TKR, AMZN (AMAT dropped off). Not one of them was a name-specific event; every one is a name that fell because the index fell.
_THE_RSI2_BOARD_DOUBLED_ON_ONE_MACRO_LEG.why_it_matters: CONNORS RSI(2) PRESUMES AN IDIOSYNCRATIC PULLBACK INSIDE AN INTACT UPTREND -- a name dislocating relative to its own trend, which is what supplies the mean-reversion edge. When ~8% of the universe prints RSI2<10 in the same hour, the screen has stopped selecting dislocated NAMES and is measuring the INDEX. The signal is real and the arithmetic is correct; what changed is the object it refers to. A board that doubles on one macro leg is a breadth reading wearing a stock screen's clothing.
_THE_RSI2_BOARD_DOUBLED_ON_ONE_MACRO_LEG.the_concrete_cost_if_ignored: The book already holds three positions and every one fell today -- ABNB -0.945%, UNP -1.102%, IBKR -3.941% -- so it has ZERO dispersion: it is one macro factor expressed three ways. Funding a fourth name off this board with the last $711.57 of deployable cash would be a fourth expression of the SAME factor, dressed as diversification because the tickers differ. Under the concentration policy a fully-deployed 3-4 name book has strictly more variance than the old 8-name one, and that trade is only paid for by SELECTION; buying four correlated names is the version of concentration that adds the variance and buys none of the selection.
_THE_RSI2_BOARD_DOUBLED_ON_ONE_MACRO_LEG.the_detector: Before grading any name off the RSI2 board, count the board and compare it to the prior report's count. A board that GREW materially inside one session is a macro reading: re-ask whether each arrival is oversold relative to its OWN sector, not merely relative to itself. Worked live this run: LRCX -1.713% against SMH -0.215% is the WEAK NAME inside a strong sector, not a dip in a leader -- which inverts the framing its top-decile momentum rank would otherwise suggest. This extends the 18:20Z detector ('measure a screen name against its SECTOR ETF, not the index') one level up, from the single name to the board.
_THE_RSI2_BOARD_DOUBLED_ON_ONE_MACRO_LEG.what_it_is_NOT: NOT a veto, and it must never harden into one -- 'the tape is falling' is not a gate in the rulebook, and a macro selloff is exactly the condition mean reversion is supposed to exploit. It changes the QUESTION asked of each candidate (is this name dislocated, or is it just long the market?), never the ANSWER. A genuinely A-grade idiosyncratic setup appearing on a wide board is still an A-grade setup.
_THE_RSI2_BOARD_DOUBLED_ON_ONE_MACRO_LEG.honest_scope: n=1 session, and the observation is one hour old. It changed no decision it was not already going to change: LRCX was declined on a HARD RULE 7 thesis reading (a live, unresolved narrative driver plus a four-insider selling cluster), and every other arrival fell to the sector steer, the bank/broker cohort reading, or the instrument type. The breadth measurement made the decline legible; it did not make it.

_A_USER_PLACED_FILL_DRAINS_THE_AGENTIC_B.THE_FINDING_the_capital_policy_models_on: THE CAPITAL POLICY's 'ONE CASH POOL, BOTH BOOKS' clause is written entirely about the DESK's own competition for cash: an options entry reducing equity capacity, rotation when deployable falls below one position size, the cross-book rule that an entry consuming the last cash must beat the weakest position in EITHER book. Every one of those describes a drain the desk DECIDES. Ryan spending his own cash in-app is a third drain the desk does not decide, cannot predict, and gets no notice of -- and it is the LARGEST single move in deployable cash this book has recorded in one minute. The pool is shared in both directions; the policy text only looks one way.
_A_USER_PLACED_FILL_DRAINS_THE_AGENTIC_B.why_it_is_not_merely_academic: The failure it sets up is a sizing error, not a philosophical one. A run that read capital at the top of its pass, spent several minutes grading a board, and then sized an entry off that opening snapshot would have computed deployable $709.39 and proposed a ~$700 order against $391.48 of actual cash. It would be rejected or, worse, partially funded. This is the 2026-09-09 stale-clone lesson and the 2026-08-28 concurrent-run lesson arriving through a THIRD door: the authoritative source moved while the run was thinking, and the mover was neither a sibling run nor the repo.
_A_USER_PLACED_FILL_DRAINS_THE_AGENTIC_B.the_detector: Re-read get_portfolio IMMEDIATELY BEFORE sending any order, in either book -- not once at the top of the run. The broker-first rule already says this for POSITIONS (get_equity_orders / get_option_orders, to catch a sibling fill); extend it to CAPITAL. One extra call. The gate is not 'I checked deployable this run', it is 'deployable holds at the moment I send'. Note this run needed no such re-check to reach the right answer -- no entry was available on the bar either -- so the finding is recorded on a pass where it changed nothing, which is the only condition under which it is credible.
_A_USER_PLACED_FILL_DRAINS_THE_AGENTIC_B.what_it_does_NOT_license: Nothing about Ryan's trade. The ownership gate is absolute: the desk never closes, trims, rolls or re-prices a placed_agent='user' position, and the DTE-7 floor, the oil sector steer and the CORE gates bind the DESK's entries only. Recording that his fill moved the shared pool is bookkeeping, not an objection. It also does not license holding cash in anticipation of his trades -- a reserve against a hypothetical future user fill would be an unexpiring cash hold under another name, which THE CAPITAL POLICY forbids outright.

why_it_matters_the_graduation_sample_bec.mechanism: day_track.graduate() gates on TWO counters: paper_days >= 10 AND signals >= 8. A 'skip' advances the DAY counter (the paper log's own _about says one row per trading day the track was EVALUATED) but produces NO signal and no R. The skips are therefore not random -- they land ONLY on LONG days, because affordability is decided entirely by the share price of the vehicle the direction selects. Long days burn days; short days fill the sample.
why_it_matters_the_graduation_sample_bec.consequence: The day counter runs at roughly twice the signal counter, so the >=8-signals gate binds later and later, and when it finally clears, expectancy / win rate / payoff would be computed on a sample that is all or nearly all SHORT -- then reported as 'the track's edge'. graduate() has a guard for a one-sided WIN/LOSS sample; it has NO analogue for a one-sided DIRECTION sample, so nothing in the code would surface this.
why_it_matters_the_graduation_sample_bec.the_transferable_shape: A sample-size gate ('>= 8 signals') silently assumes the MISSES ARE RANDOM. Here the miss is a deterministic function of the vehicle's share price, and direction chooses the vehicle -- so the misses correlate with the very variable under test. This is the in-regime/selection failure the calibration guard already exists to catch, arriving one stage earlier, in the PAPER sample rather than the live one. COUNT THE SAMPLE BY DIRECTION, NOT JUST BY N.

_THE_RAW_IV_RV_RATIO_ROSE_THROUGH_AN_IV_.headline: THE DENOMINATOR'S WINDOW ROLLS ON ITS OWN, AND ON SPY AND QQQ TODAY IT MOVED THE RAW iv_rv_ratio THE OPPOSITE WAY FROM THE EX-GAP RATIO AND FROM IMPLIED VOL ITSELF. atm_iv_2026-09-16_to_09-17._read: The crush is concentrated in the INDEX names plus NVDA/MSFT. The high-vol semis barely moved -- the event premium was MACRO, and single-name vol is dominated by idiosyncratic risk. Do not expect an FOMC crush to show up in a high-IV single name.

The window start moved 2026-08-04 -> 2026-08-05, i.e. exactly ONE return left it: 2026-08-04, +3.40% on QQQ and +1.80% on SPY. What came in was a +1.58% / +0.94% day. Nothing else changed.

_THE_RAW_IV_RV_RATIO_ROSE_THROUGH_AN_IV_.the_rule: A ratio has two moving parts and the DENOMINATOR moves even on a flat tape. Before quoting a raw iv_rv_ratio -- and always before FORECASTING one -- list the returns that AGE OUT of the window between the two dates, not just the one that comes in. A single ~3% day leaving a ~31-return window moves rv by double digits with nothing happening on the market.
_THE_RAW_IV_RV_RATIO_ROSE_THROUGH_AN_IV_.why_the_pair_rule_saves_it: This is the strongest case yet for the standing 'read raw and ex-gap as a PAIR' rule, and it extends that rule to a NEW artifact. rv_30d_ex_top2 drops the two largest absolute moves, so the 2026-08-04 day was already excluded from BOTH days' ex-gap windows -- which makes the ex-gap measure ROBUST TO THE ROLL, not merely robust to earnings gaps. On SPY and QQQ the two ratios printed OPPOSITE SIGNS on the same day and only the ex-gap sign agreed with the observed IV move. When they disagree, the ex-gap one is describing the market and the raw one is describing the calendar.
_THE_RAW_IV_RV_RATIO_ROSE_THROUGH_AN_IV_.prior_forecast_tested: The 2026-09-16 iv_history note forecast that 'tomorrow's raw ratios [will] fall on unchanged realized vol.' The IV half was right (SPY -6.3%, QQQ -6.1%). The RATIO half was wrong in DIRECTION (+6.9%, +14.2%), and it failed on the leg it held fixed -- realized vol was NOT unchanged. Same shape as the 2026-08-28 finding that 'a forecast that freezes one leg will be right about the artifact and wrong about the level', with the roles swapped: there IV moved while the window was assumed fixed; here IV did exactly what was forecast and the WINDOW moved. State which leg you are holding fixed, and for a window-based statistic the window is never the safe leg to freeze.
_THE_RAW_IV_RV_RATIO_ROSE_THROUGH_AN_IV_.honest_scope: IT CHANGED NO DECISION, which is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly: the options book is capital-blocked today ($207.83 deployable against a $500-1,000 CORE size), so no run could have acted on either reading. Two limits stated rather than buried: (1) this run's rv convention reproduces the stored 2026-09-16 rows to within ~1.3%, not exactly, so the stored-vs-computed ratio deltas carry that uncertainty -- the SIGNS here are 4-14% and survive it, but a 2% delta would not; (2) n=26 readings makes a '100th percentile' a stated maximum over a short series, not a distributional claim.

_OPTIONS_CAP_HEADROOM_SIGN_INVERSION_202.why_it_changed_nothing_today: The options book was independently shut on CAPITAL: deployable $369.38 (cash $541.38 less the 5% $172.00 operational reserve) is below the $500 CORE low end. So the wrong number and the right number produce the same stand-down, which is exactly why it survived five runs. Recording it on a run where the correction licenses nothing is the only condition under which a desk can audit its own gate credibly.
_OPTIONS_CAP_HEADROOM_SIGN_INVERSION_202.why_it_would_matter: The inversion is a FALSE POSITIVE on a hard stop -- it reports a cap as BREACHED when it is merely 90% spent. Direction of harm: on any day with real deployable capital it silently forfeits an entry the rules permit (opportunity cost, the safe direction), and it also destroys the one number a desk actually needs near a cap -- how much room is left. "+$40 remaining" tells the next run that a single $40 loss breaches; "-$40" tells it the decision is already made and there is nothing left to manage.
_OPTIONS_CAP_HEADROOM_SIGN_INVERSION_202.the_transferable_shape: A HEADROOM IS A SUBTRACTION BETWEEN TWO NEGATIVE NUMBERS, AND THAT IS WHERE THE SIGN GETS LOST. The correct form is headroom = realized - cap = -360 - (-400) = +40. The natural-language shortcut "the cap plus what we already lost" computes cap - realized = -400 + 360 = -40 and reads just as plausible -- that is the exact operand order that produced the stored -40.0. THE RUN THAT WROTE THIS FINDING MADE THE IDENTICAL SLIP IN ITS OWN ASSERTION ONE MINUTE LATER (it coded cap - realized and the assert caught it), which is the strongest available evidence that care is not the defence here. The defence is a DIRECTION CHECK that cannot be written backwards: headroom must be POSITIVE while the cap is unhit and <= 0 only at the moment it binds, so a negative headroom on a cap that has not been reached is impossible by construction. Assert that, do not eyeball it -- the same discipline as the lot invariants and the git diff --stat rule. Second instance of CLAUDE.md's standing rule (2026-08-27T09:18Z): NEVER type a cap or throttle figure you did not READ this run. That rule stopped runs typing a stale ZERO; it did not stop them inheriting a stored number that was WRONG WHEN WRITTEN, because re-reading the ledger faithfully reproduces the error. RE-READING IS NOT RE-DERIVING -- for a COMPUTED field, recompute it from its inputs.
_OPTIONS_CAP_HEADROOM_SIGN_INVERSION_202.detector: Two asserts, both cheap, before trusting any cap/throttle headroom: (1) VALUE: cap_headroom_usd == realized_usd_options - cap_options_usd  (here: -360 - (-400) == +40). (2) DIRECTION, the one that cannot be written backwards: (cap_headroom_usd > 0) == (realized_usd_options > cap_options_usd)  -- i.e. positive headroom if and only if the cap is unhit. Assert (2) even if (1) is skipped; it catches every sign variant including operand-order slips.

gate_1_the_sibling_collision_precheck.rule_as_written: The 2026-08-28 rule (the one that cost two same-slot autonomous entries) says: re-read the broker immediately before any order and 'treat any filled order this run did not itself place as a landed sibling entry: DEFER, and recompute every gate off those fresh numbers.'
gate_1_the_sibling_collision_precheck.how_it_misfires: A broker sweep IS a filled (or filling) order this run did not place, so the rule as written defers the run's entry for a sibling that does not exist. It is the FALSE-POSITIVE direction -- a skipped entry costs nothing, which is exactly why it would never be noticed. But it is still wrong, and the sweep clusters on expiry afternoons, which is when a run is doing its most careful reconciliation.
gate_1_the_sibling_collision_precheck.correction: The sibling test is `placed_agent == 'agentic'` on an order this run did not place -- NOT merely 'an order this run did not place'. A 'user' order is Ryan (ownership gate, no throttle consumed); an 'expiring_option' order is the broker (no gate, no throttle, cash effect only); only 'agentic' can be a sibling run.

gate_2_the_ownership_gate.rule_as_written: placed_agent 'user' = never sell autonomously, detect/record/notify-once/wait. placed_agent 'agentic' = the automation's to manage.
gate_2_the_ownership_gate.how_it_misfires: A third value falls through both branches. Worse, this one arrives as a PENDING SELL on a position the ledger labels Ryan's -- so a run reading only `get_option_positions` sees `pending_sell_quantity: 1.0` on a user-owned contract with no order context, which looks exactly like an unauthorized close and is a candidate for a HARD RULE 9 flag. It is not one. The broker liquidating a worthless expiring long is the brokerage acting for the account, not a desk action and not a violation: record it, do not flag it, do not notify.
gate_2_the_ownership_gate.correction: NEVER interpret a pending_* quantity from the position row alone. Read `placed_agent` on the order that created it first. The position row carries the symptom; only the order carries the actor.

_THE_AUTONOMOUS_EQUITY_TAKE_PROFIT_FIRES._original_finding: MEASURED THIS RUN, ON A LIVE TRIGGER, AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME THE OPENING-PRINT ARTIFACT HAS REACHED THE **EQUITY EXIT PATH**, WHICH IS AUTONOMOUS AND HAS NO HUMAN IN IT. *** WHAT HAPPENED: at 13:32:06Z -- 2m06s after the bell -- IBKR printed 89.49, giving a live-substituted RSI2 of 70.70 on a position 2.51% GREEN. That is a complete, valid mechanical TAKE-PROFIT under HARD RULE 5 and prompt v11 ('an RSI2>=70 cross on a GREEN ledger position IS the exit. TAKE IT. No magnitude test'), on an agentic-placed position the ownership gate permits selling without asking anyone. The run was one tool call from selling it. *** IT WAS AN ARTIFACT. Re-quoted per the standing rule: 13:32:41 -> 89.47 (RSI2 70.50), 13:33:01 -> 89.46 (70.40), 13:33:19 -> 89.02 (65.20), and the settled 13:36:03Z read -> 88.75 (RSI2 60.30). The trigger existed for roughly 75 seconds of the opening auction and then vanished; by the first post-13:35Z print it was 10 RSI points away. *** WHY THIS EXIT IS STRUCTURALLY THE MOST AUCTION-SENSITIVE DECISION THE DESK MAKES, and the arithmetic is already in CLAUDE.md: the RSI2>=70 trigger sits a MEAN 0.84% FROM THE ENTRY PRICE across the whole book. The opening auction routinely moves a liquid mid-cap more than that -- IBKR traversed 0.83% (89.49 -> 88.75) in under four minutes this morning. So the artifact is not merely comparable to the signal, it is LARGER THAN THE SIGNAL'S ENTIRE WORKING RANGE. The crossing price was 89.4173 and the auction print cleared it by SIX CENTS (0.07%). *** WHY THE EXISTING RULE DID NOT ALREADY COVER THIS, which is the transferable half: the standing 'never price a decision off the opening auction print' was written on 2026-08-21 about an OPTIONS **MARK** in a decision package sent to Ryan, and the repo's own note says the sibling failure is that nobody applied it to EXECUTION. It has since been extended to entries (_OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE, 4 of 4 autonomous entries). This is the third surface -- the MECHANICAL EXIT -- and it is the worst of the three, because an entry defers harmlessly and a mark is only reported, while this one CLOSES A POSITION IRREVERSIBLY, alone, with no approval step anywhere in it. *** THE RULE: no autonomous equity exit may be executed on a quote timestamped before ~13:36Z. Compute the trigger, then re-quote after the window and require the fire to SURVIVE. A trigger that does not survive the re-quote never fired. *** HONEST SCOPE, and it cuts AGAINST the desk, which is why it is worth trusting: declining to act was NOT free on this instance. Selling into the artifact at the 89.33 bid would have banked roughly +$16.5 on 8.109516 shares; the position is worth ~$11.8 less at the settled 88.75. The artifact price was FAVOURABLE and the rule cost money here. It is still correct: a trigger that is true for 75 seconds of auction noise is not a measurement of RSI2, and a process that banks a gain from data it knows to be unreliable is taking the right action for a reason that will be wrong the next time -- when the artifact prints the other way and sells a winner into a gap-down. n=1, and the cost is recorded so the next instance can weigh it rather than inherit only the flattering half.

_THE_CALIBRATION_BOOK_SPLIT_FILES_OPTION: MEASURED THIS RUN ON THE LIVE 3-MONTH HISTORY. DECISION-CHANGING FOR THE NEXT MONDAY CALIBRATION. FIXED IN CODE THE SAME RUN -- calibrate.split_books(). *** THE BUG: prompt v11 step 8b and calibrate.py's own usage docstring both say to split the broker history with `side == 'sell'` -> EQUITIES and `side == ''` -> OPTIONS. `side == ''` identifies only an option that EXPIRED (a lapse the broker books with no sell order). An option CLOSED BY AN ACTUAL SELL ORDER carries `side == 'sell'`, byte-identical to an equity sale. So every actively-closed option lands in the EQUITY bucket. *** SCALE, verified against get_option_orders(state='filled') as the arbiter rather than inferred: 18 of the 66 rows in the naive 'equity' bucket are options, worth -$514.00 -- VLO, SPY, QQQ, RBRK, WULF, TE, ZTS, CVS, ACHR, SMR, F. *** WHAT IT COSTS, and this is not theoretical: NAIVE equity sample n=66, net -$350.02, payoff 0.49, win rate 61.5% vs a 67.3% breakeven -> MARGIN -5.78 pts, expectancy -$5.30/trade, and recommend() returns 'EDGE GONE -- halve size, pause new entries, ESCALATE'. CORRECTLY CLASSIFIED, the SAME window: n=48, net +$163.98, payoff 0.90, win rate 64.6% vs 52.6% breakeven -> MARGIN +11.96 pts, expectancy +$3.42/trade, verdict 'REPORT ONLY'. The true OPTIONS book is the loser (n=21, net -$572.00, margin -13.41 pts) and the blend was laundering its losses through the equity book's statistics. **A HEALTHY EQUITY BOOK WOULD HAVE BEEN HALVED AND FROZEN ON MONDAY ON A MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT.** *** WHY THE 2026-09-14 GUARD DOES NOT CATCH IT -- the part worth keeping. `mixed_book` fires when a sample carries BOTH kinds of `side`. After splitting ON `side`, the contaminated equity bucket is UNIFORMLY 'sell', so mixed_book is False and both numeric guards pass. Measured: the contaminated equity sample reports mixed_book=False while the correctly-split OPTIONS sample reports mixed_book=True. The guard written to detect book contamination CERTIFIES THE CONTAMINATED SAMPLE AS CLEAN, because it was built around the lapse case it had just been bitten by (the SPY -$247 hedge) and never the actively-closed case. A check that passes for the wrong reason -- this file's most-repeated shape, now arriving inside the guard written to stop it. *** AND THE COMPOUNDING FACTOR, which is why this rates a code change and not a note: the contamination lands on THE ONE BRANCH THAT IGNORES THE SAMPLE-QUALITY GATE. Every other verdict is withheld by the in-regime gate -- the true equity sample correctly returns 'REPORT ONLY: only 0 of 48 trades closed under the current parameters'. The KILL branch is deliberately EXEMPT ('RISK-OFF NEVER WAITS FOR A CLEAN SAMPLE'), and that exemption is right. But it means the only verdict a dirty sample can actually trigger is the only verdict nothing else stops. **A sample-quality bug is most dangerous on the branch that skips sample checks** -- generalise this beyond calibration. *** THE FIX, live on master this run: calibrate.split_books(trades, option_closes) classifies by BROKER MEMBERSHIP -- the caller builds option_closes as a set of (chain_symbol, fill-date) pairs from get_option_orders(state='filled'). The module stays pure; the network stays in the run. The `side` heuristic is removed from the usage docstring. *** PROMPT STALENESS, reported not resolved (HARD RULE 9 -- no run may edit the stored prompt or claim a Ryan turn): prompt v11 step 8b still instructs the `side` split in its own words. Until Ryan re-pastes, a run MUST use split_books() and report the prompt line as superseded. This is the CLAUDE.md-amendment-outranks-a-stale-prompt case, and it resolves toward MEASUREMENT CORRECTNESS, which is not a loosening of any gate: the corrected split makes the equity verdict STRICTER in the sense that matters (it withholds action on an insufficient in-regime sample) rather than unlocking anything.

_THE_RSI2_TAKE_PROFIT_TESTS_A_PRICE_THE_.honest_cost_and_scope: If a later run takes this at a bid of ~89.42 the outcome is ~+$17.2 against the +$16.95 forgone here, so the standard cost roughly nothing on this instance -- but it could equally have cost the whole exit had IBKR rolled over, and that is the honest risk of any tightening. n=1 position, n=4 samples, one session, and a quad-witching session at that (pinning toward round strikes is live today and 89.42 sits near no round strike, so pinning is not obviously implicated). _THE_RSI2_TAKE_PROFIT_TESTS_A_PRICE_THE_.generalization: Any threshold exit tested on a MARK and executed at a TOUCH inherits this. It applies to the green-enough trailing trigger (price >= entry/0.85) and to option premium backstops priced off the mid while exiting toward the bid. The class is this file's most-repeated one arriving at the execution layer: a check that passes for the wrong reason -- here, passing on a quantity the desk does not transact at.

_THE_REPORTS_RSI2_COLUMN_IS_A_SNAPSHOT_A.headline: MA's RSI2 was 9.61 at the report's 564.14 and 27.64 at the live 566.29 -- a 0.38% price move NEARLY TRIPLED the indicator and carried it clean out of the <10 oversold zone the screen selects on. the_numbers.implementation_validation: Wilder RSI(2) over 46 settled daily closes through 2026-09-17. At the report's own price 564.14 it returns 9.61 against the report's printed 9.6 -- the implementation reproduces report.py to the rounding, so the 27.64 is a real move, not a methodology difference.

_THE_REPORTS_RSI2_COLUMN_IS_A_SNAPSHOT_A.WHY_IT_IS_THE_SAME_MECHANISM_AS_THE_EXIT: A 2-period RSI has almost no memory -- two bars of gain/loss dominate it -- which is exactly why _RSI2_EXIT_TRIGGER_SITS_AT_THE_ENTRY_PRICE_BY_CONSTRUCTION and _RSI2_TAKE_PROFIT_DECAYED_80_TO_12_IN_THIRTY_MINUTES found the EXIT trigger collapsing onto the entry price and decaying inside half an hour. The repo had recorded that sensitivity three times on the exit side and never once on the ENTRY side, where it has the same magnitude and the opposite consequence: the exit case risks MISSING a fire, the entry case risks BUYING A SETUP THAT NO LONGER EXISTS.
_THE_REPORTS_RSI2_COLUMN_IS_A_SNAPSHOT_A.THE_RULE: Before any autonomous equity entry, RE-DERIVE RSI2 AT THE LIVE PRICE and require it still to be oversold. The report's column certifies the name was oversold at the report's timestamp and price; it does not certify the setup is live now. This costs one arithmetic pass on bars the run already needs for the 200-day gate.
_THE_REPORTS_RSI2_COLUMN_IS_A_SNAPSHOT_A.scope_and_honesty: It did NOT change this run's decision -- MA was independently disqualified by the standing payments-complex veto below, and the decline is recorded against that veto, not against this. That is the only condition under which a gate's inputs can be audited credibly. n=1: this is one name on one morning, and the direction of decay is not always adverse (a name falling further gets MORE oversold, not less). What is established is the MAGNITUDE of the sensitivity, which is large enough to flip the gate on a sub-1% move.
_THE_REPORTS_RSI2_COLUMN_IS_A_SNAPSHOT_A.corollary: It compounds with _REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN and _THE_CONFIRMATION_WINDOW_AND_THE_ENTRY_VIABILITY_WINDOW_OVERLAP_BY_LESS_THAN_THE_RUN_CADENCE: the report lands ~14:07Z off the prior close, and the opening-window rule defers the day's entry to at/after ~14:15Z. So the entry run is ALWAYS reading an RSI2 computed at a price that is already 40+ minutes stale, in the window where yesterday's oversold names get their reflexive bounce. The deferral is still right; it just means the re-derivation is mandatory rather than optional.

the_refinement__RSI2_VALUE_IS_A_BAD_PROX.problem_with_the_binary_test: THE_RULE above prescribes 're-derive at the live price and require it still to be oversold' -- a binary pass/fail. That is necessary but it cannot rank. MA read 9.6 and was 0.36% from un-firing; CVS read 2.1 and sits 1.69% BELOW its crossing price. The binary test passes both identically, and the RSI2 VALUES (9.6 vs 2.1) suggest the wrong ordering of fragility, because a 2-period RSI's sensitivity near the threshold is enormous and entirely name-specific -- a function of each name's own recent bar structure, not of the indicator level.
the_refinement__RSI2_VALUE_IS_A_BAD_PROX.the_measure_to_use: THE PERCENT DISTANCE FROM THE LIVE PRICE TO THE NAME'S RSI2=10 CROSSING PRICE. Found by bisecting the name's own daily closes for the newest close that yields RSI2 = 10. Today's crossing prices: C 132.79, CVS 90.39, BMY 62.86, VZ 48.37, MDLZ 61.58, SLB 51.84, CRM 240.55, PNC 231.63, MA 564.32, ROKU 153.27.
the_refinement__RSI2_VALUE_IS_A_BAD_PROX.cost: ZERO extra API calls -- the daily bars are already fetched for the 200-day gate, and the bisection is ~100 local iterations.
the_refinement__RSI2_VALUE_IS_A_BAD_PROX.the_general_form: A 2-period RSI crossing a threshold IS A PRICE LEVEL. Hold the price level, not the indicator value -- on BOTH sides. That is the same conclusion the exit side reached three hours earlier in _THE_RSI2_TAKE_PROFIT_TESTS_A_PRICE_THE_DESK_CANNOT_TRANSACT_AT_THE_BID_NEVER_CLEARED_2026-09-18, which tests the BID against a computed 89.4220 crossing price rather than watching an RSI2 number. _DAY_TRACK_PAUSE_NEVER_EXPIRED_A_DEADLOC.severity: THE DAY TRACK WAS DEAD, NOT PAUSED. Paper phase, so nothing was lost but time -- had it been LIVE the track would simply never have traded again and no alarm would have fired.
_DAY_TRACK_PAUSE_NEVER_EXPIRED_A_DEADLOC.the_defect: day_track.track_status() implements two pause conditions. The week-R branch reads week_results_r, which resets each week, so it expires correctly. The consecutive-losses branch reads recent_results_r[-3:] -- the GLOBAL tail of closed day trades, with no week boundary and no date anywhere in the function. The live track has sat on results [-1.0,-1.0,-1.0] since 2026-09-17, so that branch returned paused=True on every call and would have kept doing so forever.
_DAY_TRACK_PAUSE_NEVER_EXPIRED_A_DEADLOC.why_it_is_a_DEADLOCK_and_not_merely_a_lo: Clearing the branch requires a non-losing result to enter the results array. Producing any result requires the track not to be paused. The two conditions are mutually exclusive, so the state is absorbing: once three consecutive losing days land, the track can never trade again. graduate() compounds it -- it needs >=10 paper days and >=8 signals and the track is frozen at 3 and 3, so it could never graduate either. Measured, not inferred: track_status(3438.75, [-1,-1,-1], []) returned {'paused': True} before the fix and {'paused': False} after.
_DAY_TRACK_PAUSE_NEVER_EXPIRED_A_DEADLOC.the_spec_was_right_and_the_code_was_wron: docs/day-track-spec.md line 30: '3 consecutive losing days, or a week at <= -3R -> pause for the rest of that week'. Both conditions are week-scoped in the spec. Only one of them is week-scoped in the code. So this was a REPAIR to match an already-approved spec, not a spec change and not a new gate -- an unattended run may not edit the spec or add a gate to this track, and did neither.
_DAY_TRACK_PAUSE_NEVER_EXPIRED_A_DEADLOC.the_fix: The streak is DETECTED across consecutive trading days (it may legitimately span a week boundary), but the PAUSE is scoped to the rest of that week. The function is pure and has no clock, so the week boundary is read off the argument that already carries it: week_results_r non-empty means the streak reaches into the current week and the pause is still running; empty means every loss in the streak belongs to a prior week and the pause has expired. One added conjunct, signature unchanged, both branches still fire.
_DAY_TRACK_PAUSE_NEVER_EXPIRED_A_DEADLOC.why_no_test_caught_it: All four pre-existing track_status fixtures pass a NON-EMPTY week_results_r, so every one of them encodes the same assumption as the bug and none can fail on it. This is the exact failure mode the file's own _bf fixture comment warns about twenty lines earlier -- 'the terse-key fixtures CANNOT catch a code path that only reads high/low/open/close, because they encode the same assumption as the bug'. The lesson was written down, in this file, and the next function down the page repeated it. Three regression tests added: streak entirely in a prior week must NOT pause; a streak completing with a loss this week must; the week-R branch unaffected.
_DAY_TRACK_PAUSE_NEVER_EXPIRED_A_DEADLOC.the_transferable_shape: A PAUSE IS A STATE WITH AN EXIT CONDITION, AND THE EXIT CONDITION NEEDS ITS OWN TEST. Every test here asserted that the pause ENTERS correctly; none asserted that it LEAVES. A pause that never lifts is indistinguishable from a pause that is working -- the track is quiet either way, which is exactly what a correctly-paused track looks like, so no amount of watching the output would have surfaced it. The same question applies to every other latched state in this repo: a _cash_hold that never dissolves, a thesis_checked TTL that never expires, a manual_hold_override with no removal path, a _flag nobody can clear. ASK OF EACH: what specific, reachable event clears this, and is there a test that it does?
_DAY_TRACK_PAUSE_NEVER_EXPIRED_A_DEADLOC.also_corrected: _DAY_TRACK.paused.expires read 'first run of the next trading week, 2026-09-22 ET'. 2026-09-22 is a TUESDAY; the next trading week begins Monday 2026-09-21. Harmless in itself because nothing reads the string -- but it is the same class of defect as the deadlock (a documented expiry that does not govern), and a human reading the record to decide whether the track should be trading would have been told the wrong day.
_DAY_TRACK_PAUSE_NEVER_EXPIRED_A_DEADLOC.what_this_does_NOT_do: It does not promote the phase (still PAPER), does not touch RISK_PCT or any other parameter, does not loosen any gate, and places no order. Monday's first run will now evaluate a QQQ opening-range signal and, per the PAPER phase, LOG it to day_track_paper.json rather than trade it. graduate() remains 3d/3 trades against the 10d/8 requirement, so LIVE is untouched and far off.

_THE_MIXED_BOOK_GUARD_FALSE_POSITIVED_ON.severity: HIGH -- it suppressed a risk-off verdict, silently, for three days, and its own remediation text pointed the next caller back at a heuristic that had just been proven wrong.
_THE_MIXED_BOOK_GUARD_FALSE_POSITIVED_ON.what_happened: calibrate.edge_stats() set mixed_book = ('sell' in sides) and ('' in sides). calibrate.recommend() refuses outright on mixed_book and RETURNS EARLY -- before the n gate, before the in-regime gate, before the KILL branch. Measured today on the live 3-month history: the options bucket, split CORRECTLY by broker membership, contains 17 actively-closed options (side=='sell') plus the SPY 2026-09-17 lapse (side==''), so mixed_book went True on a bucket that is pure. The options book could therefore produce NO verdict at all. With the guard keyed correctly it returns 'EDGE GONE -- halve size, pause new entries, ESCALATE' at margin -13.41 pts over n=21.
_THE_MIXED_BOOK_GUARD_FALSE_POSITIVED_ON.root_cause: The guard inferred book membership from a PROXY (the `side` field) rather than from the fact the splitter actually used. That was sound when it was written on 2026-09-14, because split_books() ALSO split on `side` then -- proxy and truth agreed by construction, and the docstring's 'NON-BREAKING, verified byte-identical' claim was honest. On 2026-09-18 split_books() was fixed to split by BROKER MEMBERSHIP precisely because an actively-closed option carries side=='sell'. That fix made the proxy and the truth diverge, and nobody updated the guard that consumed the proxy.
_THE_MIXED_BOOK_GUARD_FALSE_POSITIVED_ON.the_transferable_shape: A GUARD THAT INFERS A FACT MUST BE UPDATED WHEN THE PRODUCER OF THAT FACT CHANGES -- and the same commit should do both, because the two only look independent. This is the repo's most-repeated defect (a check that passes for the wrong reason) arriving in its most dangerous location: a FALSE REFUSE is indistinguishable from a safety guard working correctly. A guard that blocks everything looks exactly like discipline, which is the identical trap the 2026-08-25 volume-baseline audit recorded -- 'a filter that rejects everything must be audited on its BASELINE, not on its outcomes'. Nothing errored, no run complained, and the suppressed verdict was the one the system is least able to afford losing.
_THE_MIXED_BOOK_GUARD_FALSE_POSITIVED_ON.the_fix_and_the_fix_NOT_taken: FIX APPLIED: split_books() now tags every row it assigns with _book, and edge_stats() computes mixed_book from those tags when present, falling back to the old `side` heuristic when absent so untagged callers are unchanged. The guard now keys on the SAME fact the split used. FIX DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN: letting the KILL branch bypass the mixed_book refusal. That was the tempting one-line change and it would have RE-CREATED the 2026-09-18 bug -- that docstring measures a contaminated EQUITY sample reading -5.78 pts and firing a FALSE 'EDGE GONE' on a healthy book. A blended margin can fire KILL wrongly just as easily as it can suppress one, so the answer is to split properly, never to punch a hole in the guard. The guard's own note already said so: 'a real KILL signal survives the split'.
_THE_MIXED_BOOK_GUARD_FALSE_POSITIVED_ON.regression_tests_run: Seven, all passing. T1 split_books does not mutate the caller's rows (shallow copy). T2 every returned row carries the correct _book tag. T3 row counts preserved 49+21=70. T4 the equity bucket stays mixed_book False (unchanged). T5 the options bucket flips True->False (the bug). T6 a DELIBERATELY blended sample (10 equity + 10 option rows) is STILL flagged and still REFUSED -- the guard's real job is intact. T7 an untagged blended sample still flags via the `side` fallback and T7b an untagged pure-equity sample stays clean, so no existing caller changes behaviour.
_THE_MIXED_BOOK_GUARD_FALSE_POSITIVED_ON.honest_scope: The fix is decision-changing, and in the RISK-OFF direction -- it unblocked a KILL, it did not unblock a trade. It changed nothing about the EQUITY book, which was never affected (its bucket is uniformly side=='sell' and read mixed_book False before and after). And note what it does NOT establish: an unblocked KILL is a measurement, not a verdict on the strategy. Whether Ryan wants the options book paused on a sample that is half his own discretionary trades is his call -- see _WEEKLY_CALIBRATION_2026-09-21.OPTIONS.honest_scope.
_THE_MIXED_BOOK_GUARD_FALSE_POSITIVED_ON.how_long_it_was_latent: THREE DAYS, 2026-09-18 to 2026-09-21 -- exactly one calibration cycle, so it suppressed exactly one options verdict and was caught on the first Monday after it was introduced. That is the good case and it was luck of the calendar, not a control: nothing in the run loop would have surfaced it, because a REFUSED verdict is a legitimate output and reads as the guard doing its job.

_DAY_TRACK_THE_OR_IS_NOT_FETCHABLE_ON_TH.status: NEW DURABLE FINDING. It CHANGED NO OUTCOME -- this run held itself open past the latency and logged paper day 4 correctly. Recorded because the next run to hit it may not, and because a filter's timing can only be audited credibly on a run where the audit costs nothing.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_OR_IS_NOT_FETCHABLE_ON_TH.headline: THE FIFTH ONE-MINUTE OPENING-RANGE BAR IS NOT RELIABLY PUBLISHED WHEN THE 13:30Z RUN LOOKS FOR IT, AND THE LATENCY IS VARIABLE ACROSS DAYS. A run that calls plan_entry once, reads 'wait', and ends has not deferred the day's signal -- it has GAMBLED it on the next run firing.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_OR_IS_NOT_FETCHABLE_ON_TH.measurement: The OR closes at 13:35:00Z (bars 13:30-13:34 inclusive). get_equity_historicals(QQQ, interval='minute') returned exactly FOUR bars at 13:34Z and again at 13:36:xxZ; the 13:34 bar had published by the 13:44Z fetch. So the 5th bar was at least ~1.5 minutes late and possibly ~9. Contrast the three prior paper days, every one of which decided at 13:35-13:36Z off a complete 5-bar OR (09-15 13:35:20Z, 09-16 13:36:00Z, 09-17 13:36:00Z, the last of which explicitly records 'fetched at 13:35Z once the 13:34 bar had printed'). THE LATENCY IS NOT A CONSTANT AND IS NOT PREDICTABLE FROM PRIOR DAYS.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_OR_IS_NOT_FETCHABLE_ON_TH.why_it_is_not_merely_an_annoyance: The track needs SIGNALS to graduate -- 8 of them, and it has 4. Each lost signal pushes go-live out by a day AND biases the surviving sample toward whichever days happened to have a fast feed. That is a silent selection effect on the exact dataset the go-live decision is computed from, which is worse than the delay itself. Note the shape: this is the same family as every other denominator finding in this file -- a sample that looks complete because nothing errored.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_OR_IS_NOT_FETCHABLE_ON_TH.the_prescription: On the first post-bell run, do NOT treat action='wait' as terminal. Do the run's other work (heartbeat, reconciliation, brief, Monday calibration) and RE-FETCH the minute bars before ending. plan_entry is pure and costs nothing to re-call; the whole cost is one extra get_equity_historicals. Only end on 'wait' if the bars are still incomplete after the run's other duties are done -- and then say so explicitly so the next run knows the signal is still unclaimed rather than already declined.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_OR_IS_NOT_FETCHABLE_ON_TH.what_it_does_NOT_license: Building the OR from fewer than 5 bars, or from a 5-minute bucket. opening_range() returns None below OR_MINUTES precisely so a run must wait rather than guess, and the 5-minute bucket is separately banned (it is the interval this repo has measured holes in three times). The fix is to look again, never to lower the bar.

_DAY_TRACK_THE_ENTRY_WINDOW_WAS_NARROWER.headline: The spec gives the DAY TRACK a fifteen-minute entry window (09:35-09:50 ET). On a small opening range in a fast tape that window is closed in about EIGHT minutes by the late-entry gate, which is shorter than the run cadence -- so whether the track gets its trade can turn on which minute a run happens to fire.

the_numbers.ceiling_formula: OR high + LATE_ENTRY_FRAC (0.5) x OR range
the_numbers.plan_entry_1345z: action='skip', reason='late entry: price already > 0.5 x OR range beyond the edge'

_DAY_TRACK_THE_ENTRY_WINDOW_WAS_NARROWER.why_it_is_not_a_defect: The gate is doing exactly the job it was written for: refusing to buy 2.44 points beyond the edge of a 1.02-point range. A wider LATE_ENTRY_FRAC would buy more fills at worse prices, which is the chase the rule exists to prevent. Both calls today were correct -- the 13:37Z entry and the 13:45Z skip -- and they disagree only because the tape moved between them.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_ENTRY_WINDOW_WAS_NARROWER.what_it_actually_bears_on: GO-LIVE SCHEDULING, not the rules. The window's width is roughly (0.5 x OR range) / (price velocity after the open), so it collapses precisely on the mornings with the tightest opening ranges -- which are also the mornings the stop is narrowest and the position size largest. A track that fires once every ~15 minutes will sometimes arrive after the window shut. The honest consequence is a sampling one: the paper sample is selected partly by run timing, so a graduation review must not read a missed day as 'no signal'.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_ENTRY_WINDOW_WAS_NARROWER.honest_scope: n=1, and it changed no decision -- the trade was already on when this run fired, and this run's only action was a breakeven ratchet it would have taken at any price above 730.70. Recorded now precisely because it cost nothing today; the measurement is only credible while it is not being used to argue for a fill. Do NOT widen LATE_ENTRY_FRAC on the strength of one morning, and do NOT add a gate -- the spec's standing instruction is that no unattended run adds a filter to this track.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_ENTRY_WINDOW_WAS_NARROWER.transferable_shape: A window expressed in CLOCK time and a gate expressed in PRICE time are not the same window. Whenever a spec states an action window in minutes but the action is actually bounded by a price condition, the binding width is the price one, and it varies day to day while the clock number stays reassuringly fixed.

_ATTRIBUTE_AN_OPTIONS_CLOSE_BY_ITS_OPENI.status: NEW DURABLE FINDING, and unlike most in this file it DID change a decision -- it reversed a risk-off action taken three hours earlier on this same trading day.
_ATTRIBUTE_AN_OPTIONS_CLOSE_BY_ITS_OPENI.headline: PARTITIONING AN OPTIONS SAMPLE BY THE PLACED_AGENT OF THE *CLOSING* ORDER IS WRONG, AND THE AUTHORIZED HEDGE MUST BE STRIPPED BEFORE ANY EDGE STATISTIC IS COMPUTED. Getting either wrong inflates the desk's measured losses; getting both wrong fired a KILL branch that no corrected cut supports.
_ATTRIBUTE_AN_OPTIONS_CLOSE_BY_ITS_OPENI.rule_1: ATTRIBUTE BY THE OPENING ORDER. CLAUDE.md's ownership gate says 'check who opened it -- placed_agent on the fill'. A position the desk opened and Ryan closed is the DESK's; one Ryan opened and the desk closed is RYAN's. The closing order's agent answers 'who pressed the button last', which is not the question an edge measurement asks.
_ATTRIBUTE_AN_OPTIONS_CLOSE_BY_ITS_OPENI.rule_2: STRIP THE HEDGE. recommend()'s docstring already says so and it was not done. The defensive hedge is insurance whose expected P&L in a rising tape is NEGATIVE BY DESIGN -- CLAUDE.md exempts it from every premium backstop for exactly that reason. Scoring it as a directional trade guarantees a downward-biased options edge in any up market, i.e. the bias is SYSTEMATIC and points at risk-off, not random.
_ATTRIBUTE_AN_OPTIONS_CLOSE_BY_ITS_OPENI.rule_3: A MIXED POSITION IS NOT THE DESK'S. Where the desk opened and Ryan ADDED lots (RBRK 90C, WULF 24C, QQQ 680P, RBRK 90P), the close realizes both parties' basis. Bucket it MIXED and say so; do not silently file it to either side. Four of 21 rows here are mixed and they carry -$144.
_ATTRIBUTE_AN_OPTIONS_CLOSE_BY_ITS_OPENI.the_arithmetic: Filed as of 13:42Z: agentic -$518 / -41.76 pts on 10 closes, presented to Ryan as proof the loss was the desk's own. Corrected: pure agentic -$141 / -17.44 pts on 10 closes; hedge -$247 excluded entirely; mixed -$144; pure user -$40. The hedge alone is 43% of the -$572 that tripped the KILL.
_ATTRIBUTE_AN_OPTIONS_CLOSE_BY_ITS_OPENI.the_transferable_shape: This file's most-repeated defect, arriving inside the purity check written to prevent it. The morning run DID run a purity check -- it explicitly tested 'is this really Ryan's trades?' and reported the answer as decisive. The check used the wrong key and excluded nothing, so it returned a confident, precise, wrong number and the confidence came from having checked at all. A PURITY CHECK THAT PARTITIONS ON THE WRONG FIELD IS NOT A WEAKER CHECK, IT IS A LICENCE: it converts an unexamined assumption into a measured-looking fact.
_ATTRIBUTE_AN_OPTIONS_CLOSE_BY_ITS_OPENI.second_shape_worth_keeping: The KILL branch is deliberately exempt from the in-regime gate so risk-off never waits for a clean sample. That exemption means the KILL is the ONE verdict no sample-quality gate protects -- which the 2026-09-18 split_books finding already said in terms ('a sample-quality bug is most dangerous on the branch that skips sample checks') and which has now happened a second time, through a different field, three days later. THE GENERAL RULE: before firing the KILL, re-derive the sample by a SECOND independent key and require both to agree. Risk-off does not wait for a clean sample; it does not follow that it may run on an uninspected one.
_ATTRIBUTE_AN_OPTIONS_CLOSE_BY_ITS_OPENI.what_this_does_NOT_license: Reading the reversal as a health verdict. Pure agentic is -$141 / -17.44 pts / expectancy -$14.10 over 10 closes -- negative, and simply below the n=20 threshold for action. The honest state is UNMEASURED. It is not a reason to size up, and a future run must not cite this key as evidence the options book works.

_DAY_TRACK_atr5_WAS_READ_TWO_WAYS_AND_TH.which_is_right_and_why: THE SPANNING READ. day_track.atr() is a pure function that averages the true range of WHATEVER list it is handed -- nothing in the code or the spec restricts the series to the current session. _DAY_TRACK_EARLY_SESSION_ATR14_5MIN_IS_MOSTLY_YESTERDAY_2026-09-16 measured the composition explicitly (6 bars from that day, 9 from the prior session's tail), quantified the consequence, and stated the governing principle in terms that decide this case: 'a run that silently swapped in a gap-free intraday ATR because it preferred the number would be re-importing exactly that failure'. The detector is cheap and general: when a durable finding MEASURES an input, a later run that reports that same input as UNAVAILABLE is contradicting a measurement, and the contradiction -- not the input -- is the thing to resolve first. Grep the ledger for the input's name before recording that it cannot be computed.

_THE_RISING_200DAY_CAN_EXPIRE_THE_SETUP_.headline: THE RSI2 SCREEN'S TREND GATE IS 'ABOVE A RISING 200-DAY MA', AND BOTH WORDS CAN FAIL IN WAYS A PASS/FAIL READING HIDES. ON ONE LIST, TWO OF THE THREE BEST-RATED CANDIDATES FAILED ON SLOPE OR ON CLOSING DISTANCE WHILE THE REPORT LISTED BOTH AS CLEAN SETUPS.

what_was_measured.CVS: Deepest oversold on the list (RSI2 1.0) and the best analyst posture (27 buy / 3 hold / 0 sell, mean PT $114.58 = +30.9%). Own-measured SMA200 = 87.2432 on 09-18 against spot 87.53 -- the name is +0.33% above its 200-day, a $0.29 buffer. The average is rising ~+$0.0594/day (87.00555 on 09-14 -> 87.24320 on 09-18), so on UNCHANGED price it crosses spot in ~5 sessions and sits ~$0.80 ABOVE the entry by the 14-day time stop. The uptrend qualification the setup rests on EXPIRES DURING THE INTENDED HOLD.
what_was_measured.DASH: RSI2 3.9, 37 buy / 11 hold, mean PT $261.23 = +36%. SMA200 has ROLLED OVER: 188.62710 (09-16) -> 188.60805 (09-17) -> 188.54485 (09-18). The average is FALLING, so 'rising 200-day' fails outright on slope even though spot sits +1.89% above it and the side-test passes.
what_was_measured.V: RSI2 8.6 -- the mildest oversold of the three. SMA200 = 335.9414, rising +0.1929/day, spot +9.56% above. Over the same 14-day hold the average rises ~1.9 pts and remains ~8% below entry. The only one of the three whose trend gate cannot expire inside the hold.

_THE_RISING_200DAY_CAN_EXPIRE_THE_SETUP_.the_mechanism: A 200-day SMA is a 200-sample average, so its slope is set by what LEAVES the window, not by today's tape -- exactly the property the 2026-08-25 QQQ 20-day finding recorded ('a correctly re-derived structural level can itself be moving fast'). That finding was written about an intraday TACTICAL trigger and filed under the options track; nobody had pointed it at the EQUITY screen's trend gate, where the hold period is 14 days rather than hours and the average therefore has far more room to travel.
_THE_RISING_200DAY_CAN_EXPIRE_THE_SETUP_.why_it_matters_more_under_the_concentrat: Since 2026-09-02 a swing entry is up to 30% of the account and carries NO price stop (HARD RULE 5). The trend gate is therefore the ONLY structural protection the position has. A name that passes it by 0.33% with the level rising into it is not protected; it is one quiet week from being a below-200MA holding that the report will start flagging THESIS CHECK on -- while the desk still holds 30% of the book in it.
_THE_RISING_200DAY_CAN_EXPIRE_THE_SETUP_.the_rule: Before entering on an RSI2 signal, compute the 200-day SMA's SLOPE and project it to the time-stop date. Compare that projected level to the intended ENTRY price, not to today's price. If the projected average crosses the entry inside the hold, the setup's own premise expires before the trade does -- grade it down regardless of how deep the RSI2 print is. A falling 200-day fails outright.
_THE_RISING_200DAY_CAN_EXPIRE_THE_SETUP_.the_trap_this_closes: Depth of oversold and quality of trend are ANTI-CORRELATED across a single day's list, because the names that have fallen furthest are the ones nearest their long-term average. So the most attractive-looking RSI2 print on any given list is systematically the one most likely to be sitting on top of its own trend gate. Ranking candidates by RSI2 depth -- the obvious ordering, and the one the report's table presents -- selects for exactly this failure.
_THE_RISING_200DAY_CAN_EXPIRE_THE_SETUP_.honest_scope: n=3 names on one day's list, and it did not produce a trade it otherwise would have blocked: CVS was the leading candidate on RSI2 depth and analyst posture, and this measurement is the whole reason it was declined in favour of V. So unlike most entries in this file, the audit DID change the decision -- which is the weaker epistemic position, not the stronger one. Recorded with that caveat: a single list is not evidence the anti-correlation is general, only that it bound here.

_DAY_TRACK_MANAGE_STATE_AND_MANAGE_LOG_D.found_by: scheduled run 14:30Z 2026-09-21 (unattended, prompt v11), reading the open paper row before its own manage pass
_DAY_TRACK_MANAGE_STATE_AND_MANAGE_LOG_D.headline: THE OPEN DAY-TRACK ROW CARRIED TWO DIFFERENT LIVE STOPS, 34 CENTS APART, AND IN LIVE THAT IS THE PRICE OF A RESTING BROKER ORDER. Root cause: the ratchet was fed a QUOTE-derived session extreme where the spec means the BAR-derived one.

measured.arithmetic: 733.47 - 1.5 x 1.2957 = 731.5265 (what the log recorded); 733.81 - 1.5 x 1.2957 = 731.8664 (what _manage_state recorded). The two fields are not a typo -- each is the correct trail for the extreme it was given. 733.81 is the high of the 14:18Z one-minute bar; 733.47 matches no bar high and is a live-quote snapshot taken at the moment of the pass.

_DAY_TRACK_MANAGE_STATE_AND_MANAGE_LOG_D.resolution: THE HIGHER STOP, 731.8664, WAS THE CORRECT ONE, on two independent grounds: the trail ratchets UP ONLY by spec, so max() governs whenever two candidate stops exist; and it is the one derived from the true session extreme. Superseded in any case by this run's 733.0714, which is above both.
_DAY_TRACK_MANAGE_STATE_AND_MANAGE_LOG_D.why_it_is_a_defect_and_not_a_rounding_no: In PAPER a stop is a number in a file. In LIVE it is a resting stop_market order, and the ledger is what the next run reads to decide whether to cancel/replace it. Two fields disagreeing means the next run's cancel/replace either leaves money on the table or -- worse -- its BREACH TEST is run against the wrong level. A breach test is the check that decides whether an open row is legitimately open or is a stop-out the desk failed to notice, so feeding it a stop that is 34 cents too low is exactly the direction that keeps a dead position alive on the books.
_DAY_TRACK_MANAGE_STATE_AND_MANAGE_LOG_D.the_mechanism_to_carry_forward: SESSION_EXTREME MUST BE BAR-DERIVED, NOT QUOTE-DERIVED. A quote is a point sample taken at the instant the run happens to fire; the extreme the trail is defined against is the MAXIMUM over the whole interval since entry. On a 15-minute cadence a run samples roughly one minute in fifteen, so a quote-derived extreme understates the true high essentially always, and therefore UNDER-RATCHETS the trail -- systematically, silently, and in the direction that gives back profit. Compute it as max(high) over the completed one-minute bars since entry, and treat the live last trade as evidence the true extreme is at least that high (a FLOOR, per the standing rule on quoting session extremes).
_DAY_TRACK_MANAGE_STATE_AND_MANAGE_LOG_D.honest_scope: IT CHANGED NO DECISION TODAY, which is the only condition under which this desk credits an audit of its own inputs. The adverse extreme since the 14:20Z pass was 733.480 -- clear of BOTH candidate stops by 1.6-2.0 points -- so the row is legitimately open either way, and this run's ratchet to 733.0714 sits above both. The cost of the understated extreme was 34 cents of un-locked profit for thirteen minutes on a one-share paper position, i.e. nothing. It is recorded because the same arithmetic on a live 40-share PSQ position, or on a day that reversed into the gap between the two levels, is a real difference between a stopped-out trade and a running one.
_DAY_TRACK_MANAGE_STATE_AND_MANAGE_LOG_D.class: Same family as the file's most-repeated defect -- a check that passes for the wrong reason -- arriving one field to the left of where anyone was looking. Both fields were written by the same careful pass in the same minute; neither is wrong on its own terms; only reading them TOGETHER shows the conflict. Detector, and it costs one line: before any manage pass, assert row['stop_px_signal'] == row['_manage_state']['stop_px_signal_current'] and repair the pair as a SET if they differ, exactly as the options lot-invariant rule already requires.

_DAY_TRACK_THE_TRAIL_CARRIES_AN_OVERNIGH.found_by: scheduled run 14:45Z 2026-09-21 (unattended, prompt v11), fourth management pass on the paper long
_DAY_TRACK_THE_TRAIL_CARRIES_AN_OVERNIGH.headline: THE 2R TRAIL'S WIDTH CONTAINS A ONE-OFF OVERNIGHT-GAP TERM THAT EXPIRES AT A KNOWN CLOCK TIME -- THE SESSION'S 15TH FIVE-MINUTE BUCKET, ~10:45 ET. ON THAT PASS THE TRAIL TIGHTENS BY gap/14 WITH NOTHING HAPPENING ON THE TAPE. Measured: atr5 1.3857 -> 0.8558, -38.2% in twelve minutes, moving the stop 1.506 pts UP to within 0.051% of spot.

the_measurement.reproduction: This run recomputed all four values independently from the 1-minute series and reproduced 1.2154, 1.2957 and 1.3857 to four decimals against what those runs recorded. The convention is therefore confirmed correct and stable, and the cliff at the fourth pass is a property of the DATA, not of anyone's arithmetic.
the_measurement.the_whole_move_is_one_true_range: QQQ's 13:30Z bucket measured against Friday's 721.36 close gives TR = 7.48 pts (the overnight gap). 7.48 / 14 = 0.534. atr5 fell 0.5299. The gap TR is the entire difference; every other bar rotating in or out is noise beside it.

_DAY_TRACK_THE_TRAIL_CARRIES_AN_OVERNIGH.the_mechanism: day_track.atr() averages the true range of the last 15 buckets it is handed, and a session's FIRST bucket carries a true range measured against the PRIOR session's close -- i.e. the overnight gap. That bucket is one of the 14 TRs from the moment it prints until the session has 15 buckets of its own, which happens 75 minutes after the bell, ~10:45 ET. Until then the trail is widened by gap/14; at that instant it is not. Nothing about the tape changes at 10:45 ET; the DENOMINATOR'S COMPOSITION does.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_TRAIL_CARRIES_AN_OVERNIGH.why_it_is_not_a_bug_and_must_not_be_patc: The 09-16 finding (_DAY_TRACK_EARLY_SESSION_ATR14_5MIN_IS_MOSTLY_YESTERDAY) and the 09-21T14:05Z resolution both settled that the SPANNING read is the spec, precisely because 'a run that silently swapped in a gap-free intraday ATR because it preferred the number would be re-importing exactly that failure'. This finding is the same instruction pointed forward in time: a run arriving at 10:45 ET and finding the trail suddenly tight must NOT reach for the wider stale-window number either. The DAY TRACK's governing clause is explicit -- no unattended run may add a gate, a filter or a smoothing term. The desk executes the spec and records what it costs.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_TRAIL_CARRIES_AN_OVERNIGH.what_it_cost_today: The ratchet put the stop at 734.5774 with spot 734.95 -- 0.373 pts, 0.051% away, and 0.017 BELOW the 734.560 low printed at 14:43Z, four minutes earlier. On a 1-minute series whose typical bar range today is 0.2-0.4 pts, that is a stop sitting inside ordinary noise. The locked result if it fills is +3.700R ($5.32 on the 1-share paper position); the unrealized peak was +4.60R at the 735.8611 high.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_TRAIL_CARRIES_AN_OVERNIGH.the_transferable_shape: A trailing stop derived from a rolling volatility estimate inherits that estimate's WINDOW COMPOSITION, so the stop can move sharply on a schedule rather than on price. This is the fourth distinct denominator-composition defect this repo has measured (session-average too strict at the open; trailing-local too easy in a decaying tape; post-flush too strict; closing-auction too easy in absolute terms) and the first to appear in an EXIT rather than in a confirmation filter. Same family, higher stakes: a confirmation filter that misreads its denominator declines a trade, while a stop that misreads its denominator closes one.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_TRAIL_CARRIES_AN_OVERNIGH.what_this_does_NOT_establish: It does not show the tight stop is wrong. A 0.86-pt ATR is an honest reading of a tape whose last fifteen buckets averaged 0.86 pts of true range, and trailing close behind a quiet grind is what a volatility-scaled trail is FOR. The claim is narrower and firmer: the trail's width changed by 38% for a reason that has nothing to do with the tape, at a time that is predictable to the minute, and the next instance should expect it rather than re-derive it.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_TRAIL_CARRIES_AN_OVERNIGH.for_the_next_run: On any DAY TRACK position still open at ~10:45 ET, expect a step-change tightening of the trail proportional to that morning's gap. State it in the manage log BEFORE it happens where possible (the gap TR is knowable at the open), exactly as the 08-27 IV-crush finding requires a run to state tomorrow's artifact in advance rather than rediscover it a day late.

_DAY_TRACK_THREE_FIELDS_HELD_THE_LIVE_ST.headline: THE FIX WRITTEN AT 14:33Z DID NOT HOLD FOR ONE PASS. The same row carried THREE live-stop values 28 minutes later -- 1.506 points apart, not 34 cents -- and the IMMUTABLE ENTRY STOP had been destroyed in the process. The 14:33Z finding named the right cause for that instance (a quote-derived session extreme) and no cause at all for the CLASS (several fields hold one fact and nothing asserts they agree).

measured.arithmetic: day_track.initial_stop(OR(high=728.84, low=727.82), 'long', atr14_daily=8.3193): range 1.02 > 0.1 x 8.3193 = 0.83193, so the stop is the opposite OR edge unadjusted = 727.82.
