_DAY_TRACK_THREE_FIELDS_HELD_THE_LIVE_ST.mechanism: Through the 14:33Z pass, stop_px_signal WAS the live stop and was ratcheted in place. The 14:45Z pass stopped doing that -- correctly, since the 2026-09-17 closed row proves the closed-row schema reads stop_px_signal as the ENTRY stop (716.43 == that day's OR edge, never ratcheted) -- and introduced a new top-level `stop`. It did not migrate the old field back to the entry value, did not annotate the meaning change, and did not touch _manage_state. So a field silently changed meaning MID-ROW with no record, and two stale mirrors were left pointing at a level the trade had already ratcheted past twice.
_DAY_TRACK_THREE_FIELDS_HELD_THE_LIVE_ST.why_it_is_a_defect_and_not_a_bookkeeping: Two costs, and the second is the one that survives the day. (1) The BREACH TEST decides whether an open row is legitimately open or is a stop-out the desk failed to notice; run against 733.0714 instead of 734.5774 it passes 1.5 points too easily, which is precisely the direction that keeps a dead position alive on the books -- and in LIVE the cancel/replace would rest the broker order at the wrong level. (2) When this row CLOSES it mirrors into _DAY_TRACK.results, which is the graduation sample. A row whose entry stop reads 733.0714 instead of 727.82 reports a stop distance of $3.81 rather than $1.44, so every R-multiple computed from it is understated by a factor of 2.65. THE GRADUATION DECISION IS AN EXPECTANCY-IN-R DECISION, so a corrupted entry stop does not merely misreport the day -- it biases the statistic that decides whether the track goes live with real money.
_DAY_TRACK_THREE_FIELDS_HELD_THE_LIVE_ST.the_rule: ONE FACT, ONE FIELD, PLUS AN ASSERTION -- and the assertion is the part that actually works. The row now carries `_stop_field_contract`: `stop` is the ONLY live stop; `stop_px_signal`/`stop_px_vehicle` are the IMMUTABLE entry stop; `_manage_state.stop_px_signal_current` is a mirror every pass must rewrite. Before committing any day-track row, assert `stop == _manage_state.stop_px_signal_current == _manage_log[-1]['to']` and `round(entry_px_signal - stop_px_signal, 4) == stop_dist` (sign-flipped for a short). Three lines of arithmetic, run this pass, and they fail loudly on every variant of this bug including the ones not listed here.
_DAY_TRACK_THREE_FIELDS_HELD_THE_LIVE_ST.the_transferable_shape: THIS REPO ALREADY SOLVED THIS EXACT PROBLEM IN THE OPTIONS BOOK AND THE SOLUTION WAS NEVER CARRIED ACROSS. CLAUDE.md's lot-count rule says it in one line: a change to a primary value invalidates every derived field at once, so repair them as a SET and ASSERT the invariant rather than eyeballing it -- `sum(lots.qty) == contracts`, `sum(lots.cost) == total_cost_basis_usd`. Four careful runs missed the options version; two careful runs have now missed the day-track version, for the same reason: a stale field whose CONCLUSION is still roughly right is invisible to a check that only reads the conclusion. Both the 14:33Z and 14:45Z passes reported their stops correctly in prose and neither noticed the row disagreed with itself. The general form: WHEN A FIX CHANGES WHAT A FIELD MEANS, THE OLD FIELD IS NOT LEFT ALONE -- IT IS EITHER MIGRATED OR DELETED IN THE SAME PASS. A field that silently changes meaning is worse than a field that is wrong, because nothing downstream can detect it.
_DAY_TRACK_THREE_FIELDS_HELD_THE_LIVE_ST.honest_scope: IT CHANGED NO DECISION TODAY, which is the only condition under which this kind of audit is creditable. The 14:45Z and 15:01Z breach tests were both run against 734.5774, the highest and therefore governing value under the ratchet-up-only rule, and both passed on their merits (1.4886 pts and 0.0426 pts clear). The row is still open and still in PAPER, so no broker order and no real money was ever exposed to the stale fields. The graduation-sample corruption described above was PREVENTED, not suffered -- the row had not yet closed.

_DAY_TRACK_THE_ATR_TRAIL_CONVERGES_ON_PR._was: a prose string written by the 15:15Z run; promoted to an object by the UNION merge of PR #1847, which measured the SAME subject a second way. Kept as ONE key rather than two, per the ledger's own session-key-proliferation rule: preserve the finding, not the container.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_ATR_TRAIL_CONVERGES_ON_PR.finding_1_trail_vs_R_measured_15:15Z: MEASURED 2026-09-21T15:15Z on the track's best paper position. THE 1.5 x ATR14(5-min) TRAIL IS NOT A FIXED FRACTION OF R -- IT IS AN INDEPENDENT QUANTITY, AND WHEN INTRADAY VOLATILITY COMPRESSES IT CAN FALL BELOW 1R AND KEEP GOING. Numbers: R (stop_dist, fixed at entry from the opening range) = 1.4375 pts. 1.5 x atr5 across today's passes = 2.0786 (13:45Z) -> 1.2837 (14:45Z) -> 1.2525 (15:01Z) -> 1.0474 (15:15Z). It crossed BELOW 1R somewhere between 14:45Z and 15:01Z and is now 73% of R. Consequence: the stop now sits 1.007 pts under spot on a position carrying +4.96R, i.e. an ordinary 0.14% QQQ pullback closes the best trade the track has taken. *** THE MECHANISM, which is the transferable half: the opening range that sets R is measured in the session's MOST volatile five minutes, while the ATR trail tracks the PREVAILING volatility, which on a trend day that runs and then goes quiet is a fraction of it. The two numbers are sampled from different regimes by construction, so their ratio drifts all session and nothing in the spec pins it. *** WHAT THIS IS NOT: it is NOT a defect and NOT a reason to add a floor. A tightening trail on a decelerating tape is what an ATR trail is FOR, and the spec's whole premise (docs/day-track-spec.md) is that the day track is EXECUTED, not judged -- no unattended run may add a gate, a filter or a floor to it. Recorded so the GRADUATION REVIEW can see it, because it bears directly on how paper R-multiples should be read: a trail this tight will tend to convert large open R into a moderate closed R, so the track's realized payoff ratio will understate what its signal actually captured. If the Monday calibration ever wants to touch this, the honest lever is trail_atr_mult (currently 1.5), not an ad-hoc minimum -- and it needs in-regime evidence under calibrate.py's rules, which at n=3 closed paper trades does not exist.

finding_2_trail_vs_realized_pullbacks_me.mechanism_added: finding 1 explains WHY the ratio drifts (R is sampled from the session's most volatile five minutes, the trail from prevailing volatility). finding_3_the_room_can_WIDEN_while_ATR_k.the_arithmetic_so_nobody_re_derives_it: Room = price - (extreme - 1.5 x atr5). Net: +0.280 - 0.120 + 0.1152 = +0.0447. ROOM IS A THREE-TERM QUANTITY -- price advance, extreme advance, and ATR change -- and ATR is only one of them. A compressing ATR tightens the trail ONLY when price is not advancing faster than the extreme plus the ATR relief.

_DAY_TRACK_THE_ATR_TRAIL_CONVERGES_ON_PR.finding_5_the_series_TURNED_UP_and_a_ris: MEASURED 2026-09-21T16:31Z. THE atr5 SERIES ROSE FOR THE FIRST TIME TODAY -- 0.47099 -> 0.49173 (+4.4%) -- ending a monotonic six-step compression from 1.3857 at entry. Findings 1-4 all describe the trail tightening as volatility falls; this is the mirror leg and it is NOT symmetric, which is the point. *** THE ASYMMETRY: the stop is computed as max(current_stop, extreme - 1.5 x atr5) and the ratchet is UP-ONLY, so a RISING atr5 can never widen the room a position already has -- it can only SLOW or STALL the trail's advance. Quantified on this very pass: the bar-derived extreme advanced 0.605 pts (738.395 -> 739.000) while 1.5 x atr5 widened 0.0311 (0.70649 -> 0.73760), so the stop advanced 0.5739 rather than 0.605 -- the volatility expansion cost the ratchet 5.1% of the advance and nothing more. Had the extreme been FLAT, the computed trail would have fallen 0.0311 below the live stop and manage() would have returned hold: the stop simply stays put. *** WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE GRADUATION REVIEW, which is the only thing this is for: finding_1 warns that a compressing trail converts large open R into moderate closed R. This completes that picture -- the conversion is ONE-WAY. Volatility compression tightens the trail permanently, and a later expansion does not hand the room back. So the track's realized payoff ratio will understate what its signal captured by MORE than a symmetric reading of the ATR series would suggest. *** WHAT THIS IS NOT: not a defect, not a reason to add a floor, a cap, or a smoothing rule. An up-only ratchet is exactly what a trailing stop IS, and docs/day-track-spec.md forbids an unattended run adding anything to this track. If the Monday calibration ever wants a lever it remains trail_atr_mult (1.5), on in-regime evidence, which at 3 closed paper trades does not exist.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_ATR_TRAIL_CONVERGES_ON_PR.finding_5b_a_rising_atr_still_tightened_: REFINES finding_5, which the 16:31Z run wrote as 'because the ratchet is up-only a rising ATR can only STALL the trail, never loosen it'. That is true of the ATR LEG IN ISOLATION and is NOT true of the ratchet's output. Measured at 16:47Z: atr5 rose 0.49173 -> 0.54744 (+11.3%), so the trail's give-back leg widened 0.7376 -> 0.8212 (+0.0836) -- and the stop STILL TIGHTENED 0.3064 pts, from 738.2624 to 738.5688, because the session extreme rose further than the ATR did (739.000 -> 739.390, +0.390). *** THE ARITHMETIC, which is the transferable half: the trail is extreme - 1.5 x atr, so it moves by d(extreme) - 1.5 x d(atr). A rising ATR buys room at 1.5x its own increase and nothing more; on a tape making new highs the extreme leg routinely outruns it. 'Rising volatility stalls the trail' is therefore a statement about a TERM, not about the STOP, and reading it as the latter predicts the wrong sign. *** CONSEQUENCE, in the units that matter: room to stop fell 0.6676 -> 0.1912 pts (0.0259% of spot) on the very pass where volatility expanded, against a session pullback p90 of ~0.98 pts measured at 15:22Z. The stop now sits far inside this session's own realized noise band. *** WHAT THE RUN DID: NOTHING. manage() applied verbatim. v11 and CLAUDE.md forbid an unattended run adding a floor or a gate to this track; trail_atr_mult belongs to the Monday calibration or to Ryan. *** HONEST SCOPE: one pass, one trade, one session; it changed no decision, and it is an arithmetic correction to a claim, not a claim about expectancy.

_THE_UNP_SESSION_DECLINE_WAS_REPORTED_IN.headline: A units error inflated a single-name move 2.7x, flipped its diagnosis from 'sector' to 'idiosyncratic', and was pushed to Ryan's phone. The arithmetic that would have caught it is one division the run had every input for.
_THE_UNP_SESSION_DECLINE_WAS_REPORTED_IN.the_error: UNP._current_state.hard_rule_7_research.evidence_against, written 14:02-14:04Z, opens: '-6.20% on the session (279.37 -> 273.05)'. 273.05 / 279.37 - 1 = -2.262%. The -6.32 POINT decline was reported as a PERCENT. The same object's '-4.23% from entry' is computed correctly, so the run could do the arithmetic -- it just did not do it on this line.
_THE_UNP_SESSION_DECLINE_WAS_REPORTED_IN.what_it_changed_and_this_is_the_load_bea: The peer numbers in that same list were in genuine percent (NSC -1.34%, CSX -1.87%, IYT -1.11%), so the inflated UNP figure was compared against correctly-scaled peers. That comparison produced the conclusion 'IDIOSYNCRATIC, NOT SECTOR ... 4.3-4.9 points worse than its own merger counterparty' and the further inference that a deal-break would punish the target hardest and had not. On the CORRECT number UNP was 0.92 pts worse than NSC and 0.39 worse than CSX -- ordinary dispersion inside a weak rail complex. Re-measured at 16:18Z: UNP -2.66%, NSC -1.35%, CSX -2.31%, IYT -0.77%, spread 0.35 pts to CSX. THE RAILS ARE DOWN TOGETHER ON AN UP TAPE. There was never an unexplained idiosyncratic 6% print to explain.
_THE_UNP_SESSION_DECLINE_WAS_REPORTED_IN.the_honest_gap_dissolves_with_it: That research's 'the_honest_gap' section reasoned that 'a 6.2% single-session idiosyncratic move on a $170B mega-cap almost always has a cause' and, finding none in the feed, two web searches, the analyst tape or the peer complex, concluded the desk's information must be incomplete. That reasoning was sound GIVEN its input. A 2.3% move in a complex where the peer is also down 1.9% needs no special cause, and the searches came back empty because there was nothing to find. The epistemic humility was correct and correctly applied -- to a number that did not exist.
_THE_UNP_SESSION_DECLINE_WAS_REPORTED_IN.why_no_check_caught_it: Every surrounding figure was right, the conclusion was HOLD (which is also the correct conclusion), and HOLD is what the rules produce either way -- so nothing downstream diverged. A wrong number that does not change the decision leaves no trace in the outcome. It only became visible because a later run re-derived the session change from the quote instead of reading the prose forward.
_THE_UNP_SESSION_DECLINE_WAS_REPORTED_IN.the_detector: NEVER hand a percentage forward that you did not divide this run. Any figure of the form 'X% on the session' must be computed as price / adjusted_previous_close - 1 from the quote in hand, and a move and its peer comparison must be computed in the SAME pass so a unit mismatch cannot survive between them. Corollary with teeth: a number large enough to change a diagnosis from 'sector' to 'idiosyncratic' is large enough to re-derive before escalating -- and this one was escalated by push notification, which is the highest-cost channel the system has.
_THE_UNP_SESSION_DECLINE_WAS_REPORTED_IN.the_class: Same family as this file's most-repeated defect, arriving in the units rather than the logic: a check that passes for the wrong reason. The escalation was correct procedure (unexplained divergence SHOULD be surfaced) executed on a fabricated magnitude, and correct procedure is exactly what makes a bad input invisible.

_THE_STOP_FIELD_CONTRACT_WAS_PROSE_AND_T.headline: A contract that ends 'ASSERT BEFORE COMMITTING' was violated by the very next pass after it was written. It is now a function, day_track.assert_row_invariants(), with the two live defects as its regression tests.
_THE_STOP_FIELD_CONTRACT_WAS_PROSE_AND_T.what_happened: day_track_paper.json's _stop_field_contract (written earlier on 2026-09-21, after the 14:45Z pass overwrote the IMMUTABLE entry stop) states three equalities: stop == _manage_state.stop_px_signal_current == _manage_log[-1]['to'], plus entry - stop_px_signal == stop_dist. The 16:03Z ninth ratchet updated stop_px_signal_current to 737.1305 and wrote 900 words of justification, and left `stop` at 736.4524 with no log row appended. The 15:15Z pass had already skipped its log row (it is marked _reconstructed). So of the three passes after the contract was written, TWO broke it.
_THE_STOP_FIELD_CONTRACT_WAS_PROSE_AND_T.why_prose_fails_here_specifically: The omissions both landed on the most interesting pass of the day -- the one where the trail crossed above the market and the run spent its attention on whether to close the trade. A contract a run must REMEMBER to check gets checked when nothing is happening and skipped when something is. Three fields holding one number is a design that only survives an executable assertion.
_THE_STOP_FIELD_CONTRACT_WAS_PROSE_AND_T.the_consequence_if_it_had_been_live: The breach test and (in LIVE) the cancel/replace read `stop`. A stale-LOW stop fails OPEN -- it would have left a resting stop 0.68 pts below where the ratchet said it should be, giving back ~0.47R of locked profit on a stop-out. Not a catastrophe, and that is the point: it is exactly the size of error that survives review.
_THE_STOP_FIELD_CONTRACT_WAS_PROSE_AND_T.the_fix: day_track.assert_row_invariants(row) -- pure, raises AssertionError, called before committing any paper or live row. Its self-tests are the two real defects (stale `stop`, stale log row) plus the 14:45Z overwritten-entry-stop case and a short-side row. Also added day_track.stop_is_placeable(direction, stop, price): manage() ratchets on session_extreme -/+ 1.5 x atr5 with no guard against returning a stop on the wrong side of the market, which is what produced the 16:01Z near-close. BOTH ARE BOOKKEEPING: no gate, no filter, no spec change, and manage() is NOT wired to either. The spec is edited only by an interactive session with a real Ryan turn.
_THE_STOP_FIELD_CONTRACT_WAS_PROSE_AND_T.for_the_graduation_review: stop_is_placeable is the measurement, not the remedy. A trail that converges past spot in a volatility compression is a genuine property of a fixed 1.5x ATR trail on a decaying ATR, and whether the right answer is a floor on the trail, a minimum room, or simply closing the trade at that point is a SPEC question for Ryan. Measured today: atr5 fell 1.3857 -> 0.47099 (-66%) across one session and the trail crossed the market once.

_DAY_TRACK_THE_BREACH_WINDOW_MUST_BE_PAR.measured_by: scheduled run 16:18Z 2026-09-21 (unattended, prompt v11), concurrent with the 16:19Z run; resolved as a UNION, neither side discarded.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_BREACH_WINDOW_MUST_BE_PAR.headline: A RATCHET DECIDED AT TIME T OFF BARS ENDING AT T-k LEAVES A k-MINUTE ORPHAN WINDOW THAT BELONGS TO THE **OLD** STOP. Test that window against the NEW stop and you fabricate a stop-out; start the window at T and you never test it at all. Both shortcuts were live today, one in each concurrent run.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_BREACH_WINDOW_MUST_BE_PAR.the_mechanism: The 2026-09-16 rule says: in PAPER, feed manage() the adverse extreme over the interval SINCE THE LAST PASS. That rule is right and is not amended here. What it does not say is that a pass has TWO timestamps: the 16:03Z pass tested bars only up to 15:59Z and then set a new stop. The bars 16:00Z-16:02Z therefore traded under the OLD stop and were breach-tested by nobody. A window that SPANS a stop change cannot be tested against a single stop.

the_measurement.position: DAY TRACK paper day 4, long QQQ 1 share from 729.2575, stop_dist 1.4375.

orphan_window_16:00-16:02Z.vs_NEW_stop_737.1305: BREACHES by 0.1904 -- but that stop did not exist yet

the_measurement.naive_single_window: min low 16:00Z-16:17Z = 736.9401 vs 737.1305 -> manage() returns {'action':'close','reason':'stop level reached'} -> the row closes at +5.4769R.
the_measurement.what_the_16:19Z_run_did: Started its window at 16:03Z and cleared correctly -- the right answer, reached by using the pass TIMESTAMP as the boundary rather than the pass's DATA CUTOFF. That happens to be the correct partition boundary, but it drops the orphan bars silently, so a real breach of the OLD stop inside such a window would go unexamined. Correct today, unsafe as a general rule.
the_measurement.cost_of_the_naive_reading: 0.7R of open profit deleted and, worse, an exit row written with reason 'stop level reached' that never happened, feeding day_track.graduate() a fabricated close.

_DAY_TRACK_THE_BREACH_WINDOW_MUST_BE_PAR.the_rule: PARTITION THE NEVER-TESTED WINDOW AT EVERY STOP CHANGE INSIDE IT AND TEST EACH SUB-WINDOW AGAINST THE STOP THAT WAS LIVE DURING IT. The window starts where the last test ENDED, not where the last pass RAN; its threshold changes wherever the stop did. Neither shortcut is safe: testing the whole window against the new stop fabricates stop-outs, and starting at the pass timestamp leaves real breaches of the old stop unexamined -- the 2026-09-16 loser-deleting bias through a side door.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_BREACH_WINDOW_MUST_BE_PAR.when_it_can_bite: ONLY when a ratchet lands ABOVE a price traded in the orphan window -- exactly the condition the 16:03Z run flagged when the trail crossed above the live market for the first time, which is itself produced by the ATR-trail convergence in _DAY_TRACK_THE_ATR_TRAIL_CONVERGES_ON_PRICE_WHEN_VOLATILITY_COMPRESSES_2026-09-21. THREE FINDINGS CHAIN: the trail tightens toward prevailing volatility -> it prints above recently-traded prices -> the orphan window then contains prices below the new stop. On a normally-trailing position the new stop sits under everything in the orphan window and both shortcuts give the same answer, which is why this survived nine ratchets.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_BREACH_WINDOW_MUST_BE_PAR.the_bias_runs_OPPOSITE_to_the_2026-09-16: The 09-16 defect (handing manage() the current quote) deletes LOSERS -- a breach followed by a recovery becomes an open winner. This one deletes WINNERS' upside, converting a working trade into an early mechanical close. They do NOT cancel inside day_track.graduate(), which tests the win rate against the breakeven implied by the payoff ratio: one defect inflates the win rate, the other truncates the payoff. Distorting both legs of that comparison in opposite directions is worse than distorting either alone.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_BREACH_WINDOW_MUST_BE_PAR.read_with_its_sibling: _THE_STOP_FIELD_CONTRACT_WAS_PROSE_AND_THE_NEXT_PASS_BROKE_IT_2026-09-21 (the 16:19Z run) covers the other defect this run also found: day_track_paper.json's `stop` field still held the EIGHTH ratchet while _manage_state held the ninth. That run's fix -- day_track.assert_row_invariants(), executable rather than prose -- is the right one and is not duplicated here. WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE IT EXPLAINS WHY NEITHER WAS VISIBLE: THE TWO DEFECTS CANCELLED. A run obeying the prose contract reads the STALE 736.4524, tests the naive window's 736.9401 against it, and finds no breach -- the RIGHT answer from the WRONG stop. This repo's most-repeated shape, a check that passes for the wrong reason, arriving as two bugs that hid each other.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_BREACH_WINDOW_MUST_BE_PAR.what_this_run_did: NOTHING to the spec. day_track.manage() was applied exactly as written; no parameter, gate or filter was added or changed. The fix is to WHICH NUMBERS the function is asked about -- the same class of fix as the 2026-09-16 prescription, which v11 and CLAUDE.md permit an unattended run to make, unlike a rule change.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_BREACH_WINDOW_MUST_BE_PAR.for_the_graduation_review: manage() has no notion of WHEN its stop was placed, so the breach window has to be reconstructed by hand every pass and two concurrent runs reconstructed it two different ways. The cheapest honest fix is to carry the stop's placement timestamp alongside its level in _manage_log (the rows already have run_utc -- derive the boundary from it), making the partition mechanical. Code change, interactive session with a real Ryan turn, not an unattended run's to make.
_DAY_TRACK_THE_BREACH_WINDOW_MUST_BE_PAR.honest_scope: ONE instance. It did NOT change today's outcome -- the concurrent 16:19Z run reached the same no-breach verdict by a different route, and the union row stays open either way -- so this is an audit that cost nothing and licensed nothing. What it establishes is the general rule, which is arithmetic rather than judgement: 736.9401 printed at 16:00Z and the 737.1305 stop was not placed until 16:03Z.

The letter looks like a measurement and is actually a judgement wearing a measurement's clothes.
